The armored stone colossus was fearsome, emanating an almost palpable aura of dread and oppression. However, he was not the Great Titan Sunny had to destroy — he was merely the vessel that served as the confluence of the abomination’s titanic soul. The Titan's avatar.

The Jade Titan himself was embodied by all the fallen Stone Saints in the city. So, to defeat him... Sunny would have to wipe out every single one of the Tainted Saints, including the abominable colossus.

Luckily, Sunny himself was far more than what met the eye when one looked at him. The Shadow Legion was an extension of his soul, and so were his Shadows — in fact, the forces he controlled were many times more fearsome than the fallen Stone Saints the Jade Titan commanded.

It was just that Sunny was fighting a dozen battles in other places at the same time, so he could not unleash the full force of the Shadow Legion in the Underworld. He had to win this battle with what he had at hand. The good news was that with every tainted Stone Saint he destroyed, a part of the Jade Titan would die, making the abomination weaker — while, at the same time, Sunny's forces would grow. The bad news was that Saint and her army were fighting a losing battle against thousands of powerful Nightmare Creatures entrenched in formidable defensive fortifications.

So, it was difficult to predict which side would actually emerge victorious.

All Sunny could do was rely on Saint, knowing that she had never failed him before. His own job, meanwhile, was to confront the abominable colossus — the core of the Great Titan's power — and prevent him from reaching the battlefront. As for Nephis, she had to contend against the abyssal horror. Each of them had a role to play, and if any one failed, the rest would fall like dominoes.

That was if the situation did not change, of course. If something went wrong, then even with all three of them performing flawlessly, they would still be doomed.

‘Let's kill a Titan, then...’

Sunny eyes glinted darkly behind the visor of his helmet.

A Great Titan? Facing a creature like that was a deadly affair, sure. But Sunny also really, really wanted the shade of the Jade Titan to join the Shadow Legion — not only would that increase his overall power by quite a lot, but it would also allow Serpent to assume the same form. Currently, there were no shades among those Sunny ruled that Serpent could use to unleash its full potential.

Below, the Jade Titan had finally steadied himself and looked at Sunny, the darkness around him moving to devour all light. Sunny pursed his lips. The very nature of the enemy suppressed his powers, making the thought of fighting that thing seem suicidal. But then again, Sunny already had a solution for that particular problem.

Folding his wings, he plummeted toward the fractured floor of the great amphitheater. As Sunny fell, he turned into a shadow, and then released it from the narrow confines of a human form. The true extent of his lightless existence — vast and shapeless, deep like a sea — revealed itself, and then coalesced into a towering figure.

Just a few moments later, a second colossus landed on the shattered stones, making the whole immense stalagmite quake. He was just as towering as the Jade Titan, and wore a suit of fearsome black armor that looked almost exactly the same.

Two Jade Titans faced each other, looking like twin brothers. The only difference between them was that behind the visor of one, impenetrable darkness nestled. Behind the visor of another, though, there burned furious white flames, illuminating the ancient arena around them.

A colossal odachi formed in Sunny's hand, its blade glistening in the darkness. As if to answer, cold darkness flowed from beneath the Jade Titan's armor, coalescing into a menacing greatsword.

Raising the odachi, Sunny struck it twice against his right pauldron.

Instead of reciprocating the gesture, the Jade Titan moved forward like a walking mountain.

--- Chapter 3090 ---

Sunny clashed with the Jade Titan, feeling an ocean of malevolent Will bearing down on him like a crushing tide. Both of them were truly titanic in size, standing as tall as the great statues of the Forgotten Shore — nevertheless, they moved with speed and agility that beings of that size were not meant to possess, making the island-sized stalagmite beneath them quake and crumble.

The Jade Titan was a Nightmare Creature, but he seemed to possess a chilling, lethal battle skill — that was no surprise. If the armor he wore was indeed the same as the Jade Mantle, then he would have had to defeat thousands upon thousands of enemies to bond with it.

Their swords clashed, and before Sunny knew it, his odachi was caught in a bind and pushed down, the tip of the enemy's terrifying greatsword sliding across its spine toward his faceplate.

He turned his torso and slammed his palm into both blades, throwing the greatsword off course.

‘Crazy...’

Sunny had fought powerful Nightmare Creatures before, and he had also fought Nightmare Creatures that retained their sinister cunning and combat skill. However, abominations of higher Classes were usually too vast and inhuman to fight as a person would.

The Jade Titan, however, was both colossal and possessed the skill of a sword saint. That was a terrifying combination Sunny had not expected to witness, let alone be subjected to.

Worse than that, the shadow of the abominable colossus was hidden in the deep darkness. Sunny could not attack it, could not sense it, and therefore could not predict the enemy's next move.

With both swords temporarily out of the way, Sunny continued the motion and slammed his shoulder into the breastplate of the fearsome colossus, hoping to throw him off balance. There was a deafening thunderclap, and a devastating shockwave radiated outwards... however, the Jade Titan did not even flinch. Instead, it was Sunny who was thrown back.

It felt like he had slammed into something utterly, fundamentally immovable — as if his shoulder had struck the indomitable core of the Hollow Mountains.

His pauldron cracked, and his shoulder joint pulsed with sharp pain.

As Sunny staggered back, darkness surrounded him like a cold whirlpool, effortlessly suppressing the blinding radiance that spilled from the slit of his visor and from the seams of his armor. His light dimmed... but it wasn't extinguished. His Will wasn't shattered, either.

He was still ready to fight.

Somewhere far ahead, a bright flash tore apart the darkness for a fleeting moment, succumbing to the tide of lightlessness with unnatural swiftness. That was Nephis confronting the abyssal horror — Sunny could not discern what was happening there, but he doubted that things were going smoothly.

Far behind, Saint and her soldiers were besieging the soaring fangs of the ancient city.

Despite the superior numbers of the enemy, they were advancing. Saint had shattered the defensive formation on one of the aerial bridges, leading her centuria to slaughter the abominations. The Stone Saints were not ordinary soldiers, though.

In human battles, victory was achieved when the enemy's morale was broken, and the hostile soldiers turned to flee. It was during the disastrous rout that most casualties happened — the breaking point itself, meanwhile, happened after a relatively minor number of soldiers perished. Losing one in ten soldiers was often enough to make the rest surrender to panic and come undone.

Even Nightmare Creatures knew fear, and while they rarely retreated, overwhelming losses made most of them surrender to frenzy.

The Tainted Saints, however, did not break. They did not flinch or stagger, either. Instead, they continued to fight with the same disciplined, composed determination even when the casualties among them mounted — they continued to fight until every last one of them was wiped out.

Total annihilation... that seemed to be the only way to defeat the Stone Saints.

That was why even when Saint breached their formation, the battle on the aerial bridge did not end swiftly. It continued, with the warriors of the abominable legion stubbornly holding their ground as they were cut down one by one.

However, Saint herself did not stay to oversee their fall. Responding to her silent desire, Sunny pulled her into the shadows and brought her to a different bridge, where another centuria of her army was straining to push back the enemy. There, the Fire Saint was entangled in a devastating duel against two Great Demons of the enemy legion, dark flames boiling and spreading like waves.

Saint's arrival immediately shifted the balance, causing the abominable defenders to lose their advantage.

With two of the aerial bridges breached, the tide of the battle was turning. Soon enough, the centuriae that had conquered them would be able to attack other forces of the enemy from the rear, causing their defenses to collapse.

The battle above, meanwhile, was progressing slowly. The shadow of Absence led a smaller contingent of soldiers to conquer the stalactites, accompanied by two of the strongest Supreme lieutenants under Saint's control. Shattered corpses plummeted from great heights, disappearing in the billowing mist below, and fewer and fewer arrows struck the shields of the attacking shades.

There was progress... but it wasn't without cost.

At this point in the battle, Saint and her soldiers were still fighting at a great disadvantage. They slayed countless abominations, but their losses weren't insignificant either. For now, she was barely managing to keep the number of warriors under her command even — many of them were vanquished, while new shades took their place.

That was why Saint moved from one centuria to another, engaging the strongest champions of the enemy legion in fierce duels. She could not eradicate thousands of foes in an instant, but if she cut down their Great commanders, her own lieutenants would be able to turn the situation around. And those slain champions were becoming her lieutenants, too...

Pushed back by the Jade Titan and struggling to resist the suffocating tides of true darkness, Sunny could not help but feel a jolt of dark glee.

‘Look well, bastard... that is what a real champion looks like.'

As if to respond, the gargantuan greatsword shattered his defenses and left a deep dent on his breastplate.

At that moment, rattled and blinded by pain, Sunny learned what it felt like... to be hit by a mountain.

--- Chapter 3091 ---

Staggering back and reeling from pain, Sunny raised his odachi, deflecting the follow-up strike of the titanic greatsword — this one a vicious thrust aimed at the slit of his visor.

‘Oh, right... that's not the first time I've been hit by a mountain...’

In Antarctica, Goliath had given him a good kick. Sunny almost died that time — actually, he only survived because of the Undying Chain. This time, all the damage he received was a dent on his armor. That was progress, at least.

Actually, he was not much smaller than Goliath now. His Rank was superior, as well, so if one of them were to be destroyed by a kick from the other, it wouldn't be Sunny who ended up lying on the ground as a pile of shattered stone.

Sadly, the Jade Titan was far more powerful than Goliath, and far more harrowing as well. The Jade Titan was a Nightmare Creature, but before succumbing to Corruption, he had been a warrior on the frontlines of the Doom War. Sunny, meanwhile, was a seasoned veteran of the Age of the Nightmare Spell — both were supremely skilled and experienced, so their battle was like a clash between the champions of two epochs.

They were going to see which one was more skilled, which one was more lethal... and which one was luckier, as well.

There was a deafening, ear-piercing screech when their swords collided, the gigantic odachi pushing the titanic greatsword aside. The tip of the greatsword scraped across the side of Sunny's helmet, missing the visor — in the next moment, he growled and pushed forward, slamming the pommel of his odachi into the Jade Titan's faceplate. The force unleashed by the impact was harrowing enough to shatter the gates of a fortress, producing a devastating shockwave — however, the faceplate wasn't even bent. Before the shockwave could spread, Sunny already chained his next attack, delivering a lethal horizontal slash aimed at the adversary's neck.

The endless expanse of his immense blade raised a hurricane as it cut the winds apart, moving with such speed that its black surface began to glow, heated by air friction.

Come to think of it...

Sunny was already shadowing Neph's [Soul Flame] Ability, so what was stopping him from augmenting his weapon, just like she did? He was used to his ways, his power neatly divided among his seven shadows. But Nephis could spread her flame however she wished, making it more flexible.

So, now, even though this incarnation of Sunny only encompassed one-seventh of his soul, he sent half of the power the flames granted him into the black odachi. Instantly, the orange glow of the great blade swelled with blinding radiance, turning flawlessly white.

The darkness was pushed further back. Sunny aimed to behead the Jade Titan, but the detestable colossus raised a hand and blocked the blow with his impregnable vambrace. And yet, the incandescent blade cut the stonelike metal, biting deep into the creature's wrist.

Sunny smiled darkly and moved, avoiding the counterattack...

Or at least he tried to.

The Jade Titan ignored the waterfall of ruby dust escaping from the breach in his armor and turned his hand, catching the blade of the giant odachi in an iron grasp.

Sunny's smile faltered.

'Crap...'

In the next moment, the gigantic stalagmite quaked.

The two of them — a colossus wreathed in a billowing mantle of elemental darkness and a giant illuminated by the radiance of pure white light — clashed in a whirlwind of steel and destruction, sending deep cracks running through the mass of ancient stone. The fury of their battle was like a world-ending cataclysm, swiftly descending into utter mayhem. This was a battle between two titanic beings that were only one step away from becoming deities — a clash so ferocious and terrifying that no mortal could survive witnessing it, let alone being caught in its devastating storm.

And yet, there was no chaos or frenzied abandon in the way the two towering giants fought. Despite the utter mayhem unleashed by the dire forces of their clash, both moved with flawless precision and dreadful purpose, full of uncompromising killing intent. Their power was astounding, and their martial skill was sublime — put together, power and skill made for an unholy union.

The entire island-sized stalagmite shuddered and groaned, great slabs of stone sliding from its crumbling slopes and falling into the swirling white mist below.

The battle raged at a harrowing, frenetic pace. Creatures of this size were not meant to move with such awful speed, and yet they did, defying the universal laws of existence. Sunny pushed against the constricting limitations of the world with his Will, weaving it into his movements, while at the same time using the [Feather of Truth] trait of the Jade Mantle to precisely manipulate his weight.

The Jade Titan... he was not sure what means the harrowing creature used to break through the limits of the mundane, but the result was even more devastating. The Jade Titan was stronger than this lonely incarnation of his, and far more ancient. By all accounts, the detestable colossus should have swiftly gained the upper hand in their battle, but Sunny was stubbornly holding his ground, lashing out with vicious blows every time the titanic greatsword left a mark on his armor.

He could do so because of his skill and tenacity, because of his daemonic lineage and Divine Aspect... and because the Jade Titan had taken the brunt of Neph's fiery explosion earlier, as well.

The extensive damage dealt to his armor by the obliterating shockwave had already been mended, but the repaired swaths of the stonelike metal were still weaker than the rest of the fearsome carapace of black jade — and since Sunny remembered where the cracks had been located, he could aim his blows at the invisible seams.

Ruby dust was spilling on the fractured floor of the ancient amphitheater like a flood. At the same time, torrents of shadows were being consumed by the encroaching darkness — Sunny's titanic form did not escape the dreadful battle unscathed, either. With both giants suffering grievous harm and swiftly mending their broken bodies, the battle was deadlocked, with neither side managing to deliver a deadly blow.

And as the two of them fought, the battles on the edges of the magnificent city continued to rage, as well.

--- Chapter 3092 ---

At the southern outskirts of the ancient city, the battle between Saint's legion and the fallen defenders had turned into a vicious slaughter. The shades had conquered several aerial bridges and pushed forward, invading the neighboring stalagmites and attacking the enemy forces resisting other centuriae from the rear.

However, in the process, countless shades had been vanquished, and despite the casualties among the Tainted Saints, the scales of battle shifted in their favor. Especially so because the soldiers of the Jade Titan were not mindless abominations, either. Those of them who defended the stalactites above swiftly shifted their tactics, maneuvering to avoid Absence and his contingent while raining down death and destruction upon the warriors of the Shadow Legion down below.

Before, the shades Saint commanded could raise their shields to protect themselves from the enemy arrows and javelins. But once they engaged the enemy in melee, they couldn't maintain their turtle-like formations — of course, the archers could not shower them with projectiles, either, since doing so would mean destroying their own comrades.

However, when Saint cut down the enemy champions on the aerial bridges and the defensive lines of the Tainted Saints were breached, dooming them to be wiped out, the forces on the upper layer of the city drew the strings of their bows and unleashed a ruthless barrage, slaying both friend and foe.

Countless Tainted Saints were wiped out by the hail of arrows. Countless shades were vanquished, as well.

However, due to the fact that the defenders of Nether's magnificent city held a staggering numerical advantage, they could allow themselves to swallow these grievous losses. Saint's soldiers, on the other hand, were few in number compared to the enemy — so, the loss of each shade was felt much more.

Even the shades of the Great abominations Saint killed could not make up for the staggering casualties caused by the ranged barrage. For a few minutes, the tides of the battle turned against her and her soldiers. Then, however, there was another shift — that was because Saint led her warriors across the conquered stalagmites and used the enchanted elevator platforms to send two of her centuriae up, while the remaining two stayed below to defend the elevators.

Soon, the enemy forces above were pincered between different contingents of the Shadow Legion and besieged from two sides. The situation below, meanwhile, was reversed — the Tainted Saints attacked the remaining centuriae, while the Shadow Saints fought a dogged defensive battle. Sunny managed to contend against the Jade Titan in the center of the city, while on its outskirts, the Tainted Saints were being gradually ground to dust — so, he felt a feeble hope ignite in his heart. It was a hope that they would slay the Great Titan in time...

But, of course, things rarely went according to his hopes.

Just as the battle was reaching a breaking point, Neph's strained voice resounded in his mind:

“Sunny... I can't... fight it alone..."

His expression dimmed.

That was what he had been afraid of.

The Jade Titan and the Tainted Saints were fearsome foes, but they were also known. The abyssal horror Nephis faced, meanwhile, was a complete mystery — and more than that, it was far more powerful than even a Great Titan, at least of the Cursed Rank.

It was naive to expect that someone — even Nephis — would be able to defeat it alone. In fact, it was already a miracle that she had been able to contend against the eerie creature long enough for Sunny and Saint to make considerable progress.

Someone had to reinforce her, and there were not a lot of choices — it had to be either the incarnation of Sunny fighting the Jade Titan, or the incarnation of Sunny supporting Saint.

Both choices were a dead end, though.

If Sunny fled from the battle against the Jade Titan and joined Nephis, the abominable colossus would either follow him and put Nephis in even more danger, or rush toward the outskirts of the city to wipe out Saint and her soldiers.

If Sunny abandoned Saint, the situation would turn even worse. She would be robbed of his augmentation, diminishing the ability to slay the Great abominations among the defenders of the city — the balance of the battle would swing in favor of the Tainted Saints, and soon, the legion of shades would be destroyed.

That would allow thousands of Nightmare Creatures to rush to the center of the city, where they would aid the main vessel of the Jade Titan in the battle against Sunny — resulting in his defeat.

Something would have to be sacrificed no matter what he chose — and, more than that, chances were that the fall of one pillar of their forces would cause the rest of them to topple one after another, ending in complete defeat.

‘Damn it all...'

Barely managing to deflect another obliterating blow of the Jade Titan and feeling the stones beneath his feet shift, the colossal stalagmite swaying precariously, Sunny threw a dark gaze at his enemy.

The abominable colossus was just as fearsome and domineering as before, albeit far more battered. His armor was covered by a net of cracks, and ruby dust marred its surface. Even his breastplate was split by a deep fracture, a chilling darkness nestled between its jagged edges.

Despite his fractured state, however, the Jade Titan was far from being defeated — he wasn't even rattled. His power had diminished because of all the Tainted Saints slain by the Shadow Legion, but it was still terrifying and overflowing, drowning the ancient city like a lightless sea.

Even while channeling Soul Flame, Sunny was weakened and suppressed by that darkness. That was another reason why he had failed to destroy the abominable colossus, suffering countless wounds instead.

The pain washed over his mind, cleansing it of all unnecessary thoughts. It was a dreadful, pure state of being... of perceiving the world. Everything was sharp and clear, devoid of ambiguity and nuance. Everything was as it was, not as he would want it to be. The harsh edges of reality cut him, but they were also revealed in front of him in stark purity.

That was how Nephis saw the world, perhaps, and at the moment, Sunny saw it as well.

And so, he made a decision.

As the Jade Titan thrust his sword forward, the towering figure of his radiant enemy... Dissolved into shadows and disappeared from sight.

In the next moment, however, a dark lightning flashed through the air and crashed into his chest, causing the damaged breastplate to crack and sending the colossus staggering back.

That dark lightning was a round shield forged from stonelike metal — Saint's shield. It pierced the outer layers of the Jade Titan's armor, lodging itself in the epicenter of a vast web of cracks.

And before the Jade Titan could regain his balance, Saint herself fell from the darkness above, landing on the shield with a deafening thunderclap.

In the utter darkness that surrounded them, her black sword flashed like a guillotine's blade.

--- Chapter 3093 ---

Faced with a losing choice, Sunny could only decide which sacrifice would be the least painful. Among three threats facing them, the abyssal horror was the most perilous — so, helping Nephis hold it back was imperative.

Among the remaining two threats, the detestable colossus took priority. The most obvious solution would have been to send the incarnation augmenting Saint to Nephis, sacrificing the army of shades — they would not be destroyed immediately, at least, buying Sunny some time.

However, that would only extend the battle, not turn its tide.

So, Sunny decided on a riskier, more daring solution — he escaped the detestable colossus, while at the same time summoning Saint to take his place.

Without its commander, the army of shades would be wiped out far faster. However... would that even matter if the defenders of the city lost their commander, as well? Sunny had fought the Jade Titan to a stalemate, and that stalemate showed no signs of being broken any time soon. Saint, however, was an unknown variable. Sunny did not know how she would fare in a battle against the harrowing colossus, but he had a hope that she could perform better than he had alone.

Saint was a Supreme Devil, after all, only one step away from becoming a Tyrant. At the moment, she was enhanced both by the power of shadows and by Neph's flame. Most importantly, she wielded authority over true darkness — just like the Jade Titan — and over nothingness, as well.

And since true darkness was vulnerable to nothingness, Saint was actually better suited to fight the detestable colossus than Sunny was himself.

Granted... no matter how powerful Saint was, the gap between a Devil and a Titan was still vast. There was no guarantee that she would be able to leverage her unique affinity to defeat the colossal Nightmare Creature. It was a gamble.

But Sunny was willing to gamble — he had no other choice, considering that all other options felt like a delayed but assured defeat.

So, he shifted figures on the board, betting it all on Saint.

As Sunny rushed through the shadows to assist Nephis, her shield slammed into the Jade Titan's fractured breastplate, damaging it further and getting lodged in the stone-like metal. At the same time, the influence of the [Shield of Nothing] washed over the crumbling ruins, suppressing the profane powers of the towering colossus. Saint landed on the shield like a bolt of dark lightning, her sword flashing to widen the gap in the Jade Titan's armor. The two impacts followed each other so rapidly that the deafening roar they produced sounded like a single thunderclap.

[Nephis, recall your flame from Saint.]

It seemed like the worst possible moment to rob Saint of the powerful augmentation of Neph's flames, but Sunny had a good reason to do just that. Apart from the fact that Nephis needed all the power she could muster in the battle against the abyssal horror, there was also the issue of compatibility — while her flames were a boon for Saint, they did not empower all of her.

In fact, as far as those of Saint's powers that were rooted in elemental darkness went, they were actually weakened. Considering that she would have to challenge the Jade Titan's authority over true darkness, that was not something she could afford.

With one final blaze, the white flames dancing behind the visor of her helmet were extinguished, and the last feeble light shining in the boundless darkness disappeared without a trace. Darkness fully swallowed the crumbling arena, drowning the world like a tide.

Saint moved in the embrace of that darkness.

Her figure was graceful and towering, more than ten meters tall. However... considering the colossal size of the Jade Titan, Saint looked like a little mouse in front of the immense expanse of his gargantuan body. So, instead of trying to contend against the giant in a melee battle, Saint did something different.

She pushed off the vibrating surface of her shield... and plunged into the wide fracture in the Jade Titan's breastplate.

‘What?'

Even wrapped around Saint and sharing her senses, Sunny was surprised by her rapid action. But he had no time to dwell on that — because almost at the same time, he escaped from the shadows at the northern edge of the city, where Nephis had been fighting the abyssal horror.

As soon as he did, he saw a blinding meteor flash through the air and collide with the slope of the stalagmite behind him, shattering it with a deafening boom. A radiant figure rose from the billowing cloud of dust, its form torn and distorted. Two fierce eyes blazed with incinerating light, peering at something ahead.

Sunny glanced in that direction, as well. There, the immense tendril of flowing darkness rose from the abyss, looming above the world like a twisting spire. Its surface boiled as white flames danced across it, devouring vast swaths of the eerie darkness.

As Sunny watched, the entire upper length of the tendrils, hundreds of meters in length, broke from their base and plummeted down.

However, it did not disappear.

Instead, it struck the cobblestones of a wide plaza below and spread, turning into a perfectly circular pool of darkness.

The severed tendril collapsed back into the great chasm, disappearing in the boundless abyss below.

Here, the roar of the vast waterfall was much louder, chasing away the cold silence of the Underworld. White mist swirled below, higher than in the rest of the city, plunging into the deep chasm. The tendril seemed to be wary of the mist, so it retreated. The remains of the first one, which Nephis had torn apart with a devastating explosion, slithered back into the abyss as well.

But the pool of darkness remained.

Nephis levitated from the field of debris, hovering in the air near Sunny's giant helmet as they both glanced down at the inky-black circle. Her broken form was already restoring itself, her figure regaining its usual grace.

Sunny hesitated for a moment, then asked, his deep voice resounding like the roar of thunder:

"What is the situation?"

Nephis seemed to have frowned.

“I am not sure. That thing has not done this before — but it's immensely powerful. Its vitality is inexhaustible, and it's full of tricks. We should be careful."

Her tone was concerned.

"It's like... that thing is playing with us."

Just then, there was movement under the surface of the black pool. The darkness swelled, rising in two spots — as if two bubbles of air were escaping deep water. However, instead of bursting, they seemed to absorb all of the darkness.

At the same time, their form changed.

In mere seconds, two figures were standing on the shattered stones, looking at Sunny and Nephis with eerie smiles.

Sunny felt a cold shiver run down his spine.

‘Curse it.'

The first figure — the one facing Nephis — looked like a man wearing an intricate suit of plate armor.

The second, facing Sunny, was that of a tall woman with a graceful figure and breathtakingly gorgeous face. She wore a simple tunic, holding a longsword in her hand.

Both were perfectly black — their hair, their skin, their clothes, their weapons... their black eyes glistening like four bottomless oceans of cold darkness.

Sunny did not fail to recognize them, naturally.

The man facing Nephis was a dark copy of Sunny...

The gorgeous visage of darkness facing him was a dark copy of Nephis.

And the pressure they emanated was in no way lesser than that of two powerful Supremes.

“What kind of devilry is this?"

As Sunny spoke, the dark copy of Nephis moved. She unhurriedly raised her sword and pointed it at him, still wearing the eerie, frozen smile.

His eyes widened.

‘Oh, cr...’

In the next moment, a ray of abyssal darkness escaped from the tip of the black sword, reaching him in an instant. It struck his battered breastplate, easily piercing it — a moment later, an annihilating explosion of pure darkness tore the Jade Mantle from within, obliterating the towering colossus. His figure burst into a thousand jagged shards of stone-like metal, shooting in all directions like shrapnel. The world quaked. All surrounding buildings were severely damaged, some collapsing in a cloud of dust and debris. A moment later, the obliterating shockwave reached them, destroying the rest. Neph was pushed away by the shockwave, slamming into the ground a good kilometer away.

If Sunny had not turned into a shadow in time, he would have been utterly destroyed. Thanks to his quick reaction, though, he managed to escape the annihilating explosion while merely sustaining grievous wounds — his soul was torn to shreds and severely damaged, but retained its overall integrity thanks to Soul Weave.

The Jade Mantle was utterly ruined, what little remained of it retreating to hide under his skin.

Blinded by traumatic pain, Sunny rolled out of the shadows hundreds of meters away, hissing as he threw a gaze at the dark copy of Nephis.

The thing was still smiling, slowly turning her head in his direction.

His own copy, meanwhile, stepped into the darkness and instantly appeared near the real Nephis, a black odachi manifesting in his hands. A thousand chains forged of pure darkness exploded from the ground, melting in the light as they attempted to bind her limbs — at the same time, innumerable shapes surrounded her as a dark imitation of the Shadow Legion rose from the ground. Sunny’s heart turned cold.

He gritted his teeth, feeling both wary and indignant.

‘Damnation!’

--- Chapter 3094 ---

Nephis had yet to rise from the ground, and now, countless black chains shot from the darkness to pull her down, pressing her into the shattered stone with terrifying force. The cold chains melted and vanished like ghostly fog as soon as they touched her brilliant radiance, but there were simply too many of them — even as some were destroyed, more piled on, covering her like a dark tide.

At the same time, myriad figures rose from the dark spaces that her light couldn't reach, surrounding her like an army of monsters. They were the profane copy of the Shadow Legion — a swarm of twisted, ghastly apparitions born from elemental darkness. Their claws, stingers, and mandibles reached toward Nephis, aiming to sink into the pure white flames of her radiant body.

And most deadly of all, the dark expanse of a flawlessly black odachi was already falling, aimed at her neck.

That was the danger Nephis faced. However, if anything, she was better off than Sunny. Because while Nephis faced his dark copy, he was facing the dark copy of Nephis. And fighting Nephis — copy or not — was a truly terrifying prospect.

‘How is this even possible?’

As the tip of the pure-black version of the Blessing aimed at Sunny once again, he cursed and dove into the shadows. In the next moment, another ray of annihilating darkness pierced the world, followed by a devastating explosion. Instead of heat and flame, a wave of obliterating cold and elemental darkness washed over the ancient city, swallowing both light and the shadows it cast.

Sunny would have been expelled from their embrace, but he had already escaped it himself. Appearing behind the eerie facsimile of Nephis, he brandished his odachi, severing one of her arms at the shoulder. A split second later, the blade of his sword flashed again, cleaving deep into her torso.

Sunny swiftly disengaged, twisting the odachi as he pulled it free. The wounds he had dealt to the dark apparition were ghastly — more than enough to debilitate any enemy, if not outright kill them.

But the dark copy of Nephis did not seem to care at all. It turned, the eerie smile still playing on her lips. As she did, tendrils of impenetrable darkness shot from her severed shoulder, fusing with her falling arm; at the same time, the deep gash in her torso disappeared without a trace, washed away by the wave of dark flames.

A moment later, her flawlessly black body was whole and pristine once more, not a scratch on it. Even the rift on her tunic was gone.

Sunny stared at the black fabric, his expression dim.

‘Well that's just... cheating.'

He was suddenly covered in cold sweat — and it wasn't because of the aftershock of receiving soul damage.

It was simply because he knew what it meant to face Nephis on the battlefield. Nephis — Changing Star, the Star of Ruin — was a walking, breathing engine of mass destruction. Her powers were indescribably annihilating, capable of annihilating entire cities in one fell swoop. Worse than that, Sunny had personally armed her with a terrifying weapon that allowed her to focus that widespread destruction and channel it with pinpoint accuracy.

And if that was not enough, Nephis was also nearly indestructible, capable of recovering from any damage in a matter of moments. Her ability to heal herself was so potent that even she did not know its limits — nothing had managed to destroy her so far, at least. So how was Sunny supposed to fight that?

Actually, he knew perfectly well how. After all, in the past, he had spent countless hours thinking about that exact scenario — back when competing with Nephis had been an integral part of his world. And what he came up with was that if the two of them ever fought, trying to kill her would be a fool's errand. Instead, Nephis — like other beings who were functionally immortal or close to it — had to be restrained and contained, not destroyed.

Granted, he had imagined facing Nephis while wielding most, if not all, of his powers. But now, the Shadow Legion was engaged in a war against the Barrow Wraiths on the Forgotten Shore, while his other incarnations and Shadows were scattered across the Dream Realm, entangled in various conflicts to protect humanity against the encroaching apocalypse.

All he had was this one shadow.

‘That's... not good at all.'

At that moment, some distance away, a blinding flash illuminated the world. A roaring ring of white flame exploded from the real Nephis, consuming the chains that bound her and devastating the dark reflection of the Shadow Legion. The copy of Sunny, meanwhile, escaped destruction by stepping into the darkness.

A moment later, he reappeared, delivering a deadly strike. The dark blade of his odachi collided with the Blessing, and he was pushed back.

Before Nephis could counterattack, though, a second version of Sunny appeared from the dancing flames behind her, running her through with his sword.

The first one was already launching another attack.

‘There are only two.’

Lunging forward to prevent the dark copy of Nephis from unleashing another annihilation ray — and inwardly preparing to escape a wide-area explosion of black flames — Sunny frowned in concentration. His mind returned to the moment when the eerie thing mended her wounds. In particular, he remembered how the cut on her tunic had disappeared, as well.

That little detail was the most important, despite seeming like the most insignificant. That was because it revealed a hidden truth about these dark clones, as well as about the frightening being that had created them. It proved that these copies were merely approximations of what the creature believed Sunny and Nephis to be, not exact replicas.

Nephis could heal her body, but she could not repair her clothes. The Creature of Darkness did not seem to know that — in fact, it might not have understood the concept of clothes at all. Similarly, it must have observed Sunny manifesting two incarnations, but it did not know that he could summon seven of them.

Which meant that the dark clones it had created did not really possess the same powers Sunny and Nephis possessed. They merely wielded a facsimile of what they could do — it was the creature's own power shaped to resemble that of its enemies. That was, without a doubt, an important distinction.

Whether Sunny would be able to make use of it, though, was still a question.

--- Chapter 3095 ---

The dark copy of Nephis did not deflect, evade, or block Sunny's blow. She simply turned slightly, allowing his blade to pierce her shoulder instead of her neck — while, at the same time, delivering an attack of her own.

She had accounted for one of her arms being severely damaged, the muscles cut and the bone shattered, using only one hand to drive the black longsword forward. As a result, a split second after Sunny's odachi pierced her shoulder, her blade pierced his chest. He staggered back, barely saving his heart from being shredded.

A grim smile twisted Sunny’s lips.

‘It seems I've grown too accustomed to the Jade Mantle.'

If he was still wearing his armor, the dark copy of Nephis would not have been able to drive her sword through his breastplate with one hand. Well... she would have probably aimed for his armpit instead and dealt just as much damage — because he was one step behind.

He had already realized that the Creature of Darkness had created a facsimile of Nephis based on its flawed understanding of her, but he failed to realize that it fathomed Neph's battle art, too.

When Nephis was a Saint, she had woven her ability to mend herself into her battle style. That was why most pillars of combat collapsed when facing her. Any other opponent would attempt to defend themselves, which dictated their movements — Nephis simply chose which parts of her would be mangled while enduring the pain to deliver lethal attacks. People did not fight like that. Even Nightmare Creatures did not fight like that — while they did not necessarily possess a self-preservation instinct, they were overcome by a frenzied desire to destroy and devour remnants of the Flame, and being needlessly killed went against that overwhelming obsession.

But Nephis had all but liberated herself from the deeply ingrained need to avoid harm. That made most of the combat experience Sunny possessed nearly useless in this battle — in fact, it was not only useless, but actively worked against him.

He needed to rid himself of all preconceived notions and approach this fight as a blank page.

...But did he, really?

Clutching his chest, Sunny looked at the dark copy of Nephis.

Far away, the real Nephis calmly grasped the sword that impaled her and pulled it sideways, slicing her own fiery body to drag it out. At the same time, she flourished the Blessing, deflecting the attack of the second incarnation of the dark clone and unleashing a radial wave of immolating flame.

Sunny could not hear her voice, but her lips moved, no doubt invoking the Names of Fire and Destruction.

The incarnation assaulting her from the front managed to escape in time. The one who had pierced her with the sword, though, was a moment too late — after all, his sword was still in her grasp, and she was not letting go. The flames engulfed him, and a stifled scream drowned in their hungry roar.

Sunny faced the dark version of Nephis with a resolute expression.

At the same time, he thought:

'...To hell with this!'

Fighting a version of Nephis with only one incarnation? Sure, it was an exciting idea. He was very curious to see how their battle would go.

But he wasn't crazy... well, he wasn't that mad.

So, without a second thought, Sunny turned around and fled.

Restraining and containing Nephis? That was a good strategy. The best strategy, however, was not to fight her at all!

Before the dark copy of Nephis could fry him the same way the real Nephis had just fried a copy of him, Sunny dove into the shadows and escaped them near her — near the real Changing Star, that was.

For a moment, he was enveloped by unbearable heat. Then, Sunny turned into a shadow and wrapped himself around Nephis, augmenting her and fusing their two titanic Wills into one. The power of shadows fused with the power of purifying flames, and the resonance between the two increased Neph's strength explosively.

[That thing can only use those of our powers that we have shown in the Underworld. And it doesn't seem capable of Shaping.]

Nephis assumed a defensive stance, looking around warily. The remaining incarnation of the dark clone was yet to reveal itself, so an attack could come from any angle.

[I see.]

Her own copy, meanwhile, summoned a pair of magnificent black wings and was descending from the vast emptiness above like a dark comet.

[Get ready!]

The dark Blessing moved, and an annihilating ray of pure darkness shot from above. At the same time, a ray of blinding light shone from the ground. The two collided midair, and the fabric of reality itself seemed to part, space and time rippling as a wave of unfathomable destruction was unleashed upon the world. Everything was consumed by darkness. Then, everything was drowned by blinding light.

The world shook, and a deafening roar obliterated all notion of silence — its very concept was made meaningless, banished from Sunny's memory.

In that roaring inferno, Nephis moved, raising her sword. In the next moment, a black blade bit into its radiant surface, throwing Nephis back.

She slid across the shattered stones, looking ahead with a grim expression.

There, a winged spirit of darkness landed gracefully and took a step forward, a dark figure rising from the flames to fuse with her — instantly, the chilling pressure she exerted multiplied, crashing into Nephis like a devastating wave.

She pursed her lips, ready to attack.

Then, however, something about Nephis changed.

Sunny felt it — a brief moment of confusion, a hint of hesitation. A spark of recognition. And then, a deep, debilitating fear rose from the depths of her being, weakening her grip on her sword.

Nephis suppressed that fear, but its claws still left their mark on her resolve, making her voice sound shaken and low.

"I... I know you."

The dark copy of Nephis continued to smile as she walked forward, the black surface of her sword consuming all light.

Nephis gritted her teeth.

"I know you, don't I? We've met before."

She inhaled deeply, then slowly exhaled.

"In the depths of my Nightmare."

Sunny, who was confused and startled by her reaction, suddenly understood.

That creature — the abyssal horror that extended its tendrils from the boundless darkness — it was the same creature that Nephis had met in her Second Nightmare. Nephis believed it to be, at least. It was the horror that wiped out the settlement she had built, and made her kneel.

Slowly, Neph's fear receded, replaced by... a dark, frightening, scathing joy.

A cold smile slowly appeared on her bloodless lips.

"I begged you for mercy back then."

Grasping the hilt of the Blessing with both hands, she pointed it at the dark apparition.

“I've wanted to meet you again for a long, long time. But I won't be begging today."

A moment later, she lunged forward with a speed so dire that it seemed like she had simply blinked out of existence, appearing near her copy at the same time.

Two swords — one forged out of pure light, the other forged out of pure darkness — collided, sending a shock rippling through the entire Underworld.

--- Chapter 3096 ---

No matter how curious Sunny was about what would happen if he and Nephis woke up one day and decided to battle to the death, he had to admit that he was badly matched against her dark copy here in the Underworld.

If he was wielding all his powers... he honestly did not know what the outcome would be. Sunny was an immensely powerful being himself, but his true strength lay elsewhere. His Shadows were immensely powerful, and he commanded a deathless legion of shades. He was also a master of sorcery. Of course, if his Domain were to be included, then Neph's had to be included as well.

Which meant that the question wasn't really who would win in a fight, him or Nephis. The question was who would win in a war — Sunny and his legion or Nephis and all of humanity.

Sure, his Shadows were powerful... but so were the people who pledged their loyalty to Nephis. Kai, Effie, Cassie, Morgan, Seishan, and the rest of them — hundreds of Saints, all the Legacy Clans, countless Masters, billions of mundane humans. Was his Shadow Legion stronger than all of humanity?

Sunny wasn't sure.

Of course, he was tempted to believe that he would win. There were simply too many tools in his toolbox. While Nephis was a force to be reckoned with, given enough time, Sunny could probably weave something to defeat her. But then again, there were countless sorcerers serving her, as well, and human ingenuity was endless. So who was to say that she would not create something to deal with him, too?

At the end of the day... Sunny was still most likely poised to win, simply because of how insidious his Domain was. The longer a war continued, the stronger the Shadow Legion became. So, unless Nephis learned how to fully destroy shades, humanity would fall to the tide of shadows sooner or later.

Ah, but then...

After their trip to the Tomb of Ariel, Nephis possessed the Knowledge of Corruption. So wasn't she capable of turning Sunny into a Nightmare Creature by simply whispering a few secrets into his ear?

Luckily, Sunny did not need to find out, because they were one and the same now. A war between them was no different from the right hand trying to kill the left hand. And since he was limited in what he could unleash here in the Underworld, the best decision he could make was to augment Nephis and lend her his strength in the battle against the Creature of Darkness.

It was like two hands holding the hilt of a sword — no different from the first lesson in swordsmanship Nephis had given him. One hand pushed, the other pulled. That was how the blade could move with deadly speed, slaying the enemy before they could react.

So, now, Nephis was empowered by his embrace, facing the dark copy of herself... who was augmented by the remaining incarnation of his copy.

What was it that Nephis had said? That the Creature of Darkness was playing with them?

No matter how uncomfortable it made Sunny feel, he had to admit that she was probably right. After all, if that thing was powerful enough to create nearly flawless copies of two Supreme wielders of Divine Aspects — as well as make a puppet out of a Great Titan — then it most likely did not need to mimic them.

Had it created the dark copies simply for its own amusement?

If so... Nephis was going to make that thing take them seriously.

She had always been strong-willed and determined, facing each battle earnestly. How could she not, if for her, fighting meant burning herself alive? But now, Neph's resolve reached a truly frightening level. Her mind was focused and clear. Her Will was absolute. Her killing intent was scorching, burning in her eyes like a merciless inferno.

She thought she recognized the creature... the same creature who had haunted her nightmares ever since she became a Master. Facing it as a mere Sleeper had been the greatest shock and humiliation she had ever experienced. Nephis was strong, Nephis was proud... but out there in the depths of the Nightmare, she had been forced to kneel and beg.

It had taken her years to recover from that humbling defeat. She had only regained her confidence — and her flame — in the ruins of Twilight, facing the ghastly visage of the Soul Stealer. And even if the wound only made her stronger in the end, she had never forgotten the bitter pain of losing it all to the abyssal horror.

Now, the same abyssal horror — or a being eerily similar to it, at least — was right in front of her. She wasn't a powerless Sleeper anymore, either. Instead, she was Supreme — she was Changing Star of the Immortal Flame clan, the living goddess of humanity. The woman who had slain the Sovereigns and conquered the world despite coming from nothing.

The radiant blade of the Blessing flashed as it cut the world, scorching the terrifying darkness surrounding her. Her brilliance was like an endless tide, burning the very thought of defeat away. Her body moved with the grace of a dancer and the precision of a natural-born killer, and her heart was utterly ruthless — both to her enemy and to herself.

Sunny wanted to activate the [Dark Embrace] enchantment of the Curse to soothe her pain, but Nephis refused it. She did not mind the pain — she welcomed it. Pain was the purifying fire that cleansed her mind and fueled her Will, reminding her of what was at stake.

The battle between Nephis and her dark copy was chilling. Neither of them worried about preserving themselves, only caring about ensuring that the damage their bodies received did not hinder their movements. As a result, their clash was perhaps the most brutal Sunny had ever witnessed — their bodies were pierced, cut, and scorched, waves of white and black flames dancing across their figures and mending the damage, only for their healed flesh to be cut and mangled a moment later.

It was utterly inhuman, only made more disturbing by the fact that Neph's focused expression never changed, while her copy's smile never faltered.

The dire forces they unleashed wreaked havoc across the district of the ancient city where the battle was taking place, and the entire city quaked, enormous slabs of stone falling from the distant ceiling of the colossal cavern and plunging into the deep mist below.

And throughout all of that, Sunny was observing the dark copy of Nephis intently. Figuring out the ways in which it was inferior to the real deal.

--- Chapter 3097 ---

As Nephis fought her dark copy, on the opposite side of the city, the legion of Shadow Saints was slowly melting under the assault of their corrupted kin. Despite the devastating losses both armies had suffered, the abominations were still numerous, thousands of them swarming toward the elevator platforms that two hundred shades defended.

Far above, the shadow of Absence led the remains of five centuriae as they pincered at least a thousand of Tainted Saints — attacked from multiple directions, the battle formation of stalwart abominations was slowly shrinking as more and more of them fell.

However, scores of shades were being vanquished, as well. The remaining Supreme shades clashed with the Great champions of Jade Titan's fallen army, collapsing one after another — after all, even empowered by the Will of the Lord of Shadows, they were not a match for living creatures of the same Rank. But even as they were vanquished, the silent shades dragged their enemies with them into the cold embrace of death.

The Shadow Legion still persisted in its mission, slaughtering the Tainted Saints and melting in the harrowing carnage of battle. The two hundred shades below were soon reduced to a hundred, and then to just a few dozen — but even then, the last of them stubbornly held their ground. Once those last defenders fell, the enemy would scale the great stalactites above and encircle Absence and his warriors.

Then, the army of Shadow Saints would be truly and utterly obliterated.

But before that happened, their commander still had a chance to turn the tide.

In the heart of the city, Saint had dived into a crack in the Jade Titan's armor. The abominable colossus staggered, and then slammed his fist into the cracked breastplate. His blow was so powerful that, for a moment, a blinding flash illuminated the crumbling stalagmite, and the net of cracks marring the surface of the stonelike metal deepened.

It wasn't easy to damage armor that the Demon of Destiny himself had forged. Its battered state right now was the work of two Supreme Titans — Changing Star and Lost from Light. So, the shockwave produced by the thunderous blow was truly devastating, fracturing the ancient stones beneath the terrifying giant's feet and making the colossal stalactites above sway. The Jade Titan's body could withstand the impact, but could Saint do the same? Apparently, she could.

Before the thunderous ringing produced by the blow even grew quiet, the abominable colossus shuddered and bent over, a waterfall of ruby dust spilling from beneath his helmet. A deafening sound — not quite a growl, but not quite a groan either — resounded in the impenetrable darkness, and leaning on his greatsword, the Jade Titan ripped a piece of his breastplate away. It was as if he wanted to plunge his hand into his own chest and crush the vicious invader between his fingers.

But before he could, a strange shudder ran through his body.

The Jade Titan straightened and let out a horrid, deafening roar. The low thunder of his titanic voice reverberated across the entire city, making the ancient stones vibrate and sending the flowing currents of true darkness into a frenzy.

Then, his shattered breastplate exploded outward.

What escaped from the vast breach was not a torrent of ruby dust and stone shards, however, and neither was it Saint.

Instead, it was a vast, unfathomable, billowing flood of darkness.

The darkness rose above the colossal body of the Jade Titan like a boundless cloud, expanding and circling it like a whirlwind. It swallowed the lightless void above the ancient ruins, looming above them, seething as it spun.

A great maelstrom of elemental darkness was born in the void at the heart of the ancient city, churning as its vast current spun around the battered figure of the abominable colossus. Unlike the true darkness that drowned all of the Underworld, however, this terrifying mass of it was different.

It was far more malevolent, frenzied, and terrifying, permeated by the appalling scent of Corruption... it was alive, controlled by a terrifying will.

That boundless tempest of true darkness was the essence of the Jade Titan — the towering giant it had inhabited before, meanwhile, had merely been its shell.

And now, like an empty shell, the terrifying colossus collapsed.

Its battered armor fell, as if the force that had been keeping it whole vanished. The enormous gauntlets, the shredded vambraces, the hill-sized pauldrons, the cracked breastplate, the fearsome helmet... all of it rained down like fragments of a shattered mountain, crashing into the fractured ground with devastating force. Clouds of dust rose into the air, and the crumbling stalagmite shuddered, one of its slopes shattering and sliding into the swirling mist below.

Once the dust settled, nothing but a mountain of broken stone remained, rising above the broken arena of the ancient amphitheater like a solemn barrow. The shapes and intricate decorations of the fearsome armor could still be recognized in the debris, but just barely — then, another explosion tore the stonelike barrow apart, and a graceful figure slowly climbed to its peak.

It was a graceful stone knight, her own armor bent and broken. Rivers of ruby dust flowed down from countless breaches, and harrowing wounds marred her jade body. However, the furious crimson flames that burned in her jewel-like eyes were still as cold and aloof as always.

Saint's helmet was bent and fractured, so she raised her hands and removed it. Her hair spilled over her shoulders like a waterfall of sublime silk, and her inhumanly beautiful face was exposed to the cold winds of the Underworld.

She inhaled deeply, as if remembering the long-forgotten scent of home.

Then, she raised her head and looked up at the titanic maelstrom of malevolent darkness above with a silent challenge.

The darkness moved then.

It shot downward with unimaginable speed, forming into a colossal vortex. The vortex struck Saint in the blink of an eye, flowing into her body like a flood. In just a few seconds, the entire boundless cloud vanished, absorbed by her.

The Jade Titan had abandoned his main shell, after all.

Which meant that he needed a new, equally worthy vessel.

The force of the forceful invasion threw Saint into the air. She soared through the darkness, crashed into the fractured floor of the arena, and rolled a few times, leaving a shallow crater and long trench in her wake. Then, she moved slightly, pushing herself up to one knee.

Saint swayed, the crimson fire burning in her eyes dimming slightly. There, in its depths, a hint of appalling darkness was straining to swallow her flame and replace it.

However, even though Saint was merely a Devil, the Jade Titan was struggling to consume her.

She wielded authority over elemental darkness as well, after all. And since the true nature of the terrifying Great Titan was that of an ocean of darkness imbued with malevolent will, she could attempt to wrestle away control over that ocean, too. As two wills clashed for control, Saint raised her shield slowly.

And then, she used all of her terrifying strength to slam it down, into the fractured stones beneath.

With a deafening groan, a violent tremor spread through the ancient stalagmite.

It shuddered heavily... and crumbled entirely, its entire peak shattering and falling down.

Carried by the avalanche of broken stone, Saint plummeted into the swirling mist of nothingness below.

--- Chapter 3098 ---

‘Smart...'

Sharing senses of both Nephis and Saint, Sunny could not help but concentrate more on the battle against the abyssal horror — after all, that was where most of his Will was focused, and that was where the puzzle he had to solve to stave off defeat was hidden.

But, naturally, he kept an eye on Saint as well.

Her actions just now were both daringly bold and deeply intelligent. Nothing of what had happened was a coincidence — it all transpired as she intended it to.

Since Saint could not contend against the Jade Titan in a physical battle, she wanted to challenge him on a different battlefield — she wanted to challenge his authority over true darkness, and crush it with her own. So, she used means available to her as a wielder of darkness to deal a grievous wound to the dark heart of the abominable colossus, thus forcing the Jade Titan to abandon his damaged shell. Then, she allowed herself to be invaded by the ocean of elemental darkness and contained it within herself, struggling to remain in control.

If Saint established her authority over the ocean of elemental darkness that the Jade Titan was composed of, she would vanquish the adversary — not only that, she would consume him, reaping a tremendous boon. But if she failed to shatter the Will of the loathsome creature with her own, she would be erased from existence, becoming its new vessel.

Needless to say, that was a risky strategy — deadly, even. After all, Saint was not a match for an ancient Great Titan, even if it had been wounded in a battle against Sunny. She was weaker, and her Will carried far less weight. Even if they were of the same Rank, the gap between them was as vast as a boundless abyss.

The measure of authority the Jade Titan wielded was insurmountable.

Or it was supposed to be, at least.

Saint naturally knew her own limits. However, she also knew something else — something that gave her a unique advantage in a battle of Will against the harrowing Nightmare Creature. It was that she not only carried authority over elemental darkness, but also had an affinity to nothingness, which true darkness was vulnerable to.

So, Saint evaluated the structural integrity of the crumbling stalagmite and delivered one last, targeted blow to its peak, causing it to collapse...

Collapse into the clouds of white mist swirling above the great river, thus pulling herself — and the Jade Titan that had usurped her body — into the insidious embrace of nothingness.

There, the Jade Titan was suppressed while she was empowered. And so, the playing field was leveled, giving her a chance to emerge victorious from their clash.

Sunny did not know if Saint would truly be able to usurp the dark essence of the Jade Titan. Would she win the desperate struggle, or would she perish? He could only lend her support to his taciturn Shadow and wait, knowing that the battle would be over soon.

In the meantime, he had to focus on another, no less desperate battle — the battle against the abyssal horror. If he and Nephis were defeated by the dark copy, then whether Saint won or not wouldn't matter. Even if she did, the eerie being of the Abyss would finish the Jade Titan's job.

‘How is this thing so strong?’

Nephis and her dark reflection were entangled in a dreadfully ruthless battle, both straining to deal the adversary more damage than their powers could heal. They cut and burned each other's bodies, and they cut and burned each other's souls as well. White flame and black flame fused in a harrowing conflagration, incinerating the very air around them.

Even the stones of the ancient city, which had withstood the endless tides of true darkness, were melting and flowing into the white mist as rivers of incandescent lava. At the same time, a dreadful cold encased the surrounding districts, making the magnificent buildings crowding them brittle like glass.

At the moment, the two radiant spirits — one woven out of pure light, the other from impenetrable darkness — seemed evenly matched. Their devastating power, their transcendent skill, their razor-sharp intent, and their miraculous ability to recover from the most terrifying wounds were almost exactly the same, preventing one of them from gaining an upper hand.

As a force of utter destruction, Nephis possessed few means of debilitating and containing her enemies instead of simply obliterating them. So, facing an adversary who could not be destroyed, she was temporarily driven into a dead end. Even if the dark copy could not annihilate her in turn, prolonging the battle was not in Neph's favor — after all, she was still a human, while the abyssal horror was not.

Neph's resilience seemed inexhaustible, but it wasn't. And while she showed no signs of being tortured by the agony of her Flaw, the pain was still putting a strain on her spirit. Even her uncompromising Will had a limit. Her dark copy, though? Neither Sunny nor Nephis knew what it truly was, and therefore what its limits were. It might not have possessed any limits at all. So, fighting it forever and grinding it down in a battle of pure resilience did not seem like a good option.

In fact, the dark copy was already putting immense pressure on Nephis through the sheer endlessness of its ability to endure punishment. At the moment, the amount of damage it had shrugged off was harrowing enough to turn an entire continent into an ashen wasteland — and yet, it showed no sign of slowing down, let alone of being shaken.

Nephis was able to hold her own because of two reasons. One was her mastery of Shaping, which the creature did not seem capable of replicating, and the other was her resolve. Having met the creature of her nightmares, she was more determined than ever to triumph over the adversary.

As for her Shaping, Nephis was primarily using it in two ways. She was using it to empower her attacks by invoking the Names that had to do with flames and destruction, and she was also using the Names having to do with passion to ignite and embolden her Will. In that way, and due to being augmented by Sunny, she could fight on a level that no other Supreme could achieve. Still, time wasn't on her side...

But it also was.

Because the more she fought the eerie apparition, the more time Sunny had to observe it and contemplate a solution. The more time the two of them had to adapt.

In the end, Sunny came to a simple realization.

It was that the dark copy was merely pretending to be a Sovereign, but didn't really possess a Domain. That was why the copy of the Shadow Legion it had summoned was composed of ghastly monstrosities instead of Sunny's actual shades.

Therefore, the abyssal horror was not only fighting Nephis.

It was fighting Nephis and all of humanity. And humanity had won countless weapons to fight against the horrors of the Dream Realm, conquering vast territories from them in a relatively short span of time.

At that moment, Sunny's mind turned to one particular tool serving humanity. The idea he came up with was so diabolical that even he was taken aback for a moment, frightened by his own imagination.

But after a few seconds of startled hesitation, Sunny regained his composure.

‘There is... no reason why it shouldn't work. Right? I don't think there is. So why not? Let's show this horrid hellspawn that there are deeper, far more terrifying layers of hell.'

--- Chapter 3099 ---

[Nephis... I have an idea.]

Engaged in a dreadful battle against the abyssal horror's creation, the very fabric of reality bending and parting in front of their blades, Nephis invoked the Name of Decay as she plunged the Blessing into the impostor's flesh. The radiant surface of the sword blazed with a scorching radiance as it turned into a torrent of pure light, incinerating her adversary's body.

At the same time, more Names escaped from Neph's lips, echoing with primordial power and reshaping the world around her.

The Name of Withering, the Name of Erosion, the Name of Sundering...

Destruction took innumerable forms, after all, and she knew the Names of all of them.

The dark copy reeled and staggered back, her body disintegrating in a conflagration of radiant flames — only to be restored moments later. Her eerie smile remained the same, even if her lips had been turned to ash and made it into a grotesque grin.

Nephis pressed the attack, even as the adversary's sword cut her flesh in turn.

[What... kind of idea?]

Sunny collected his thoughts and then explained in a short and concise manner.

[You are going to have to split your attention...]

Once he was done talking, something cold and frightening flashed in Neph’s eyes. Her lips twisted into a faint smile then, too.

She dashed back, intending to buy herself a split second of respite.

[...Damn.]

Huh? Was that really Neph's reaction?

No, it couldn't have been. That was so unlike Nephis... Sunny must have heard wrong.

Nephis grasped her sword with both hands and lunged forward, meeting her dark copy in a shocking explosion of annihilating carnage.

[Can we even survive that ourselves? Actually, never mind. Let's do it anyway.]

Now that was Nephis he knew!

In the next moment, the tides of her Will shifted, and her soul began to exert a subtle pull on the world.

Forced to split her focus, Nephis suffered a harrowing wound just a moment later — unlike all the previous ghastly wounds she had received, that one went against her intent, weakening her too much and sending her staggering back. The dark copy did not miss the opportunity, pressing the advantage and gaining the initiative in their vicious clash.

The battle turned against Nephis then.

But even while being pushed back, she coldly calculated every painful loss, guiding her adversary into destroying the least vital parts of herself. Biding her time.

And all the while, the subtle pull her Will exerted slowly grew more forceful.

‘Come on, come on...’

Sharing her pain, Sunny gritted his teeth and counted heartbeats.

The solution he had come up with was not difficult to realize, but demanded a bit of time to implement. Usually, it would not have been a problem, but attempting it in the midst of a battle was immensely difficult — especially a battle as intense as this one, where even the slightest distraction could spell doom.

But this was the best chance to turn the tide against the abyssal horror.

When Sunny asked himself how the dark copy differed from the real Nephis, he found too many answers. The eerie creature was merely emulating her powers, after all — there were things it could only vaguely approximate, and other things it could not replicate at all.

The dark copy was not a carrier of the Nightmare Spell, for example. Its soul — if it had one — did not burn with the Flame of Divinity. It did not possess [The Fire], and its dark sword did not carry the [Blessing of the Fire] enchantment either — which made Nephis stronger the more her soul was damaged.

But among those distinctions, few could actually help Sunny and Nephis defeat the eerie Creature of Darkness. The most obvious choice would be to make use of the [Blessing of the Fire], asking Nephis to detonate her soul cores in order to harm her adversary and empower herself.

However, there was no guarantee that the abyssal horror could not replicate the effects of the [Blessing of the Fire] once it observed them. That was why Nephis had not resorted to that strategy herself yet. No... Sunny needed something more decisive, more final. Finding out a way to bend the rules of the game was not enough — he needed to break the gameboard completely, leaving the adversary no chance to respond.

That was why his thoughts turned to the Longing Domain. On paper, it did not grant Nephis any actionable benefits — except for an endless stream of spirit essence and the unfathomable weight billions of loyal souls added to her Will, naturally, which were both passive boons. On the contrary, it was Nephis who could actively help her subjects.

However, as a ruler of humanity, Nephis also ruled all the Transcendent humans. And with them came the ownership of all the Citadels they controlled, complete with various Components of those Citadels. Most Components only affected the Citadels themselves and the immediate areas around them, but there were exceptions. Those exceptions granted Nephis powers that she could use here and now, in the dark depths of the Underworld — while the abyssal horror couldn't.

So, what Sunny wanted her to do was make use of one of those Components.

And after suffering a dozen terrifying wounds that left marks both on her body and on her soul, Nephis finally accomplished what she had set out to do.

A vertical fissure suddenly split the fabric of reality apart, towering between her and the spirit of darkness that besieged her.

That immense fissure was the first manifestation of an opening Dream Gate. The Citadel Sunny had wanted her to make use of was the Night Garden, which possessed a Component that allowed Nephis to open her Dream Gate between two places in the same realm. However, opening a Gate could not be done in an instant — just like using a tether, it demanded a bit of time and a lot of concentration. The smallest distraction could interrupt the process, as well.

It was a testament to Neph's remarkable willpower and clarity of mind that she had managed to manifest a Dream Gate even while fighting an overwhelming opponent and being subjected to traumatic pain. Anyone else would have failed... but Nephis knew more about pain than any other human. She had taught herself how to remain focused even while suffering the most awful agony.

More than that, she had learned how to use the agony to sharpen her focus.

And now, her Dream Gate was about to manifest.

...Of course, not just any Gate could help them in their current predicament. Sunny had something truly special prepared for the abyssal horror.

The dark copy lingered for a moment, surprised by the sudden manifestation of the towering fissure. And before she could act, the nascent Dream Gate opened wide, exploding into a colossal, radiant portal.

Nephis froze, ceasing all movement.

In the next moment...

The world seemed to come to a violent end. Sunny did not have words to describe the apocalyptic devastation he and Nephis had summoned into existence. In fact, he did not even possess the capacity to fathom it. All he knew was that when the fierce light pouring from the radiant Dream Gate touched the elemental darkness flooding the Underworld, reality itself was torn apart.

All of existence quaked.

All of existence screamed in horror and pain.

There seemed to be a colossal and obliterating shockwave, but Sunny was not sure, since the very concepts of force and impact had lost all meaning in the jaws of the unimaginable cataclysm.

A deafening roar took away his hearing.

A blinding flash took away his sight.

An eerie cold took away his tactile sense. An immolating heart burned away his sense of smell.

All he could taste was ash and fear.

It was complete annihilation...

Annihilation in its purest form.

The Underworld itself groaned, the ground beneath their feet suddenly turning into a slope. Even the mist of nothingness below seemed to have been banished, revealing the rapid current of the great river for a brief moment.

The river boiled and evaporated, then was born anew.

And worse of all — the calamity was not instantaneous. It was still continuing to spread and rage, growing more annihilating with each passing moment.

‘H—hell...’

Indeed, it was hell. Sunny and Nephis had summoned hell into existence.

To be precise, they had summoned a very particular hell.

Because the Gate Nephis had manifested was not connecting just any two points in the Dream Realm...

Nothing as prosaic as that.

Instead, what Nephis had done was connect the dark depths of the Underworld...

To the merciless abyss of the radiant sky above Godgrave.

--- Chapter 3100 ---

The Dream Gate towered above the ancient city of the Demon of Destiny, emanating a blinding, incinerating brilliance. It was like an incandescent wound dealt to the world, radiant cracks spreading through the air around it — as if reality itself was about to come undone.

The merciless white abyss of a godless sky invaded the dark depths of the Underworld through it, annihilating the true darkness that had always dwelled in this lightless realm.

The annihilating light spread in all directions, reaching far and wide. Nephis had grown still just before the Dream Gate opened, so she wasn't immediately destroyed — in fact, she was one of the few beings in the world who could move in that harrowing light, albeit not for long and only if she was ready to pay a gruesome price. Sunny, however, was not. Now that his shadow had fused with Nephis, neither of them knew what would happen if she moved — but chances were, this incarnation of him would be burned off her graceful figure, turning into a cloud of ash.

It was not an abomination corrupted by the Void, but if it had been... then it would have been equal to those of them who were Unholy. To the most powerful and dreadful beings in existence, the hidden rulers of the Dream Realm.

And now...

They had made it angry.

Still... Godgrave was what remained of the Sun Realm. The white abyss above it was no different from the dead flesh of Sun God, the Lord of Light. Even in death, one of the great gods was far more fearsome than any Unholy Creature could be.

As the tide of darkness rushed forward, it was consumed by light, shrinking and slowing down. Countless tendrils were incinerated, and countless more were severely damaged, falling into the white mist below and disappearing from sight.

In the end, only a few of them remained. Two of them shielded the third, dissolving in the furious radiance of the Dream Gate... But the third one flashed forward, wrapping around the blinding fissure in the fabric of the world.

And then, as its coils tightened, the annihilating radiance was extinguished.

The Dream Gate shut close and collapsed, plunging the world into darkness once more.

It had been torn apart, shattered... completely destroyed.

--- Chapter 3101 ---

When the Dream Gate was forcefully closed and destroyed, Nephis was hit by a devastating backlash. Her Transcendent form collapsed, and she staggered, a torrent of blood exploded from her mouth. She fell to the ground, trembling, the white flames that burned in her eyes dancing erratically. Her mind was in tatters, temporarily plunged into a dazed state.

Sunny suddenly felt a deathly chill permeating his consciousness.

The situation was critical.

Even if the abyssal horror was severely wounded by the incinerating light of Sun God's lifeless shell, it was still strong enough to wipe them out. In fact, it would probably do that in just a few short moments.

[Your shadow grows stronger.]

Sunny's mind settled.

Somewhere far away, in the heart of the ancient city — where the radiance of Godgrave had not reached — hidden in the flowing mist of nothingness, Saint had usurped the darkness of the Jade Titan and destroyed him.

She was evolving.
