That thing was not the only danger they could face, either.

There were the Dark Drifters and other Creatures of Darkness that came to the Realm of Death to hunt the shadows. There were far more terrifying creatures here, as well.

Sunny had not forgotten the warning Eurys had given him once — the warning about harrowing beings that dwelled in the heart of the Shadow Realm. However, he understood that warning better now.

The last and most dreadful battle of the Doom War had happened right here, in this desolate land. The Void Gate had been opened here, as well, at its very center. What did it mean?

It meant that the strongest beings of both the Demon Legion and the Divine Host had been here when Corruption invaded the world. It spread from here across all of existence... which meant that the soldiers who had fought in that calamitous final battle were the first ones to be swallowed by Corruption.

The strongest champions of the Doom War and Corruption... were not a good mix. Sunny was suddenly very glad that he had listened to Eurys and abandoned his ambitions of exploring the depths of the Shadow Realm.

‘That bastard is not entirely useless, after all...’

And speaking of Eurys. Had he not mentioned reaching the Shadow Realm by traversing the Abyss?

Now that Sunny knew what dwelled in that bottomless well of elemental darkness, he could not help but feel a sense of grim astonishment.

‘How the hell did he get past both the abyssal horror and that ghastly thing?’

No wonder Eurys had been in such a pathetic state when Sunny stumbled on him, with many of his bones shattered, barely able to move.

The fact that there was anything left of him at all was already startling.

Sunny inhaled deeply, thinking back to the terrifying visage of the giant skeleton hidden in the Abyss.

What was that thing?

Was it a nephilim who had succumbed to Corruption? That was not supposed to be possible.

Or was it the corpse of one, reanimated by an endless mass of Corruption that used its bones as a shell?

Or was it the remains of an actual angel? What about the abyssal horror, then? What was it and why would it keep the Unholy One bound? Was it feeding on it, somehow? Had it been created by Nether instead, tasked with restraining a test subject? Had it been born before or after the Doom War? Sunny was not sure. What he was certain about, however, was that the metaphor that had come to his mind when he first beheld the prisoner of the Abyss was not entirely figurative. He could only describe the terrifying rot nestling within the ancient bones as a universe of appalling darkness... and he did not know if that was an exaggeration.

Sunny knew that the souls of Divine beings were vast. The entire Shadow Realm had been hidden inside Shadow God once... had been Shadow God. So, how vast was the rotten expanse of an Unholy abomination's soul?

The world inside Ariel's Tomb was fashioned from the soul of an Unholy Titan, whom the Demon of Dread had slain. If anything, Sunny now suspected that Ariel had only used a fraction of it to create his masterpiece.

He could not help but shiver.

When he read the story of how Ariel had slain the Stone Titan for the first time, it sounded quite epic. But now, having met an actual Unholy being, Sunny could only think of it as utterly terrifying.

‘Damn daemons...’

He inhaled deeply, trying to calm himself, and thought back to the moment of his death.

Only now that some time had passed did Sunny begin to realize how close to complete destruction he had come. It was as he told Nephis — all the prisoner of the Abyss had to do was point at his incarnation to destroy it.

Actually, that might have been a mercy.

Although that thing probably did not know it, it had done Sunny a favor. If the Unholy horror had not destroyed his incarnation, all of Sunny would have become a Nightmare Creature by now, all seven of his Shadow Cores consumed by Corruption.

‘I should count my blessings, I guess?'

Sunny smiled weakly.

The most terrifying part, however... was that they had gotten impossibly lucky. Sunny was a unique being because he was divided into seven incarnations, so he only lost one of them. If anyone else had happened to be in his place, however, they would have simply been killed in the blink of an eye.

Nephis, Mordret... Cassie, Ananke...

None of them would have survived that blow. The moment the prisoner of the Abyss pointed at them, they would have been erased from existence once and for all.

That, too, put the power of the Unholy Ones into perspective.

And that perspective was so stark that it was difficult not to fall to the ground in utter despair.

Sunny remained motionless for a long while, then grimaced.

‘That's nothing new.'

He had felt the same way when facing the Mountain King for the first time, watching the Spire Messenger fly above the Forgotten Shore, when Solvane tore the heart out of his chest in the Kingdom of Hope, when the Winter Beast wiped out the remains of the First Evacuation Army in the Antarctic Center, when he first witnessed a storm made of rustling swords obscure the sky...

All those threats, and countless others like them, had seemed insurmountable once — and yet, to the Sunny of today, they were nothing but trivial obstacles.

With enough time and effort, the prisoner of the Abyss and other Unholy horrors would be the same.

So, there was no point in wasting time on despair.

...That was what Sunny forced himself to believe, at least.

For now, he had more practical matters to attend to.

--- Chapter 3114 ---

Sunny’s soul had been dealt a severe blow, losing one of his Shadow Cores.

There were obvious consequences, like the dull pain he was experiencing and his diminished power. The craziest of his shadows was gone, making him feel sad and a little depressed... as if a part of him was gone. It was, quite literally.

‘I'll miss that guy...'

His feelings regarding the demise of a loyal shadow aside, there was also the fact that he was once again a Terror, meaning that there was less of him out there. He could be in fewer places at the same time, could empower fewer things, and if he wanted to focus all his power in one place, the augmentation would not be as potent as it had been before.

As for the soul wound... it wasn't as bad as it could have been. Losing a single core was not going to kill a Titan, and especially not Sunny — his soul was especially tenacious, after all, and would slowly recover if even a little piece of it remained intact.

However, there were also less obvious consequences of plummeting to a lesser Class.

Sunny would be unable to summon the full form of the Curse until his seventh Shadow Core was rebuilt, for example.

Much more importantly... one of his Shadows was homeless now.

Each of the Shadows dwelled in one of his Shadow Cores, drawing on its power and retreating into its nurturing dark flames to heal and recover. Now that Sunny was a Terror, he had seven Shadows, but only six cores, meaning that someone could not find shelter within his soul anymore.

That someone was Slayer.

Sunny had been afraid that this strange situation would result in the destruction of the bond between him and the murderous Shadow, but luckily, the situation was not that dire. Slayer was still his Shadow, and he still felt a connection to her... however, she could not be dismissed.

That meant that if Slayer was wounded, she could not be healed by the dark flames of his soul — which presented a problem, since she was in the middle of a vicious war against the Barrow Wraiths right now. Receiving ghastly wounds and being mangled by the enemy was not a rare occurrence, and if these wounds kept accumulating, Slayer would inevitably be destroyed.

Unknown complications could arise in the near future, as well. Sunny did not entirely understand how the connection between him and the Shadows functioned, but he knew that they depended on him. Where did the essence they used to fuel themselves come from? Would its current run dry without the dark cradle of a Shadow Core? Would they wither and fade as time went on?

Sunny did not know. And he would rather not find out.

Luckily for him...

Sunny looked around.

If he wanted to build a new Shadow Core and become a Titan again, he was in the right place. There was nowhere in the Dream Realm where he could accomplish that goal faster. The vast expanse of the Shadow Realm surrounded him, promising a thrilling hunt.

It was just that Sunny was not in the mood to wander the Realm of Death in search of powerful shadows to consume. He did not have the time, and there were all the threats he had just been thinking about, as well.

However...

Sunny's expression turned pensive.

Maybe he didn't need to.

After all, he had just attained Shadow Weave. Among various boons it granted him, there was one that could help him solve this particular issue. Perhaps it was time to test his new powers.

Sunny remained motionless for a few moments, then took a deep breath and dove into his Soul Sea.

‘Here goes nothing.'

Instantly, the familiar landscape revealed itself to his mind's eye. The dark waters of his soul were still and silent. The lightless sky above encompassed six tenebrous black spheres, a few of them covered in cracks and healing slowly. The Nameless Temple towered above the water, surrounded by a legion of shades.

There was a vast sea of silent shadows populating his soul now. Some were distinct, while some were vague and elusive — the former were whole, while the latter had been vanquished recently and were now being mended.

Sunny's gaze shifted to a particular direction, where the newest recruits of the Shadow Legion stood. Unlike the rest of the shades, these ones were assembled into neat battle formations, standing upon the still water like a disciplined army. They were six thousand Shadow Saints, commanded by dozens of Supreme officers...

The colossal shadow of the Prince of Darkness was also there, wreathed in nurturing black flames. The mighty shade had been utterly obliterated by the prisoner of the Abyss, but luckily, the Titan of Tainted Jade was merely vanquished, not destroyed. In a few days, he would be ready to be summoned again, adding his strength to the power of the Shadow Legion.

Beyond them, countless other shades stood, stretching toward the dark horizon — every living being Sunny had slain over the years, except for those who were summoned and fighting his enemies on various battlefields. Hundreds of thousands still remained, all looking at the steps of the Nameless Temple, where their Sovereign stood.

Sunny exhaled and sat down on one of the steps, looking at his shades intently. Slowly, his gaze focused on a particular one — a beast he had once slain on the Chained Isles, an eternity ago.

He could feel a deeper connection to that beast than before. It was as if his authority over the shades had expanded, becoming not necessarily greater, but broader in its implications.

There was no instruction manual to Shadow Weave — unless the cryptic conversation between Weaver and Oblivion could be considered one — but Sunny could vaguely sense a new kind of power slumbering somewhere deep within him. So, he reached toward that power and explored it carefully, trying to discern its functions. He felt like a blind man trying to guess the nature of an unknown mechanism by tracing its shape with his fingers — it was mysterious, unclear, and covered in darkness.

Eventually, though, his intuition gave him a hint of what he had to do, and how he could do it.

Sunny inhaled deeply and looked at the bestial shade, commanding it to... dissolve. For a few moments, nothing happened. Then, the black beast was suddenly enveloped by dark flames, its form slowly melting in their tenebrous embrace.

In a few moments, the shade vanished in a black blaze, disappearing without a trace.

Once the dark flames were dispelled, the Spell whispered in Sunny's ear:

[Your shadow grows stronger.]

Summoning the runes, Sunny looked at the string he had not paid attention to for a long, long while.

It read:

Shadow Fragments: [0/6000].

He grimaced.

He had clearly felt his soul being reinforced when the black beast was consumed. It was just that it did not offer him as many shadow fragments as a true shadow would — instead, it offered him as many as consuming an Ascended soul shard would grant a Supreme.

A fraction of a single shadow fragment... but not nothing.

Sunny exhaled slowly and looked down.

‘That works.'

When he raised his gaze again, his eyes glinted darkly.

And when they did, a vast inferno of dark flames suddenly enveloped the silent expanse of his soul. Thousands of shades burned in the cataclysmic blaze, chosen carefully to become sacrifices.

The runes shimmered and changed. Shadow Fragments: [3/6000].

Shadow Fragments: [23/6000].

Shadow Fragments: [194/6000].

Shadow Fragments: [447/6000].

Shadow Fragments: [1342/6000]...

The counter continued to climb and climb. Until, eventually, it reached completion.

‘Oh, hell!'

Focused on his new power, Sunny had forgotten what would follow.

A ghastly pain suddenly pierced his entire being...

The pain of a new Shadow Core forming in the depths of his soul.

--- Chapter 3115 ---

3115 Dark and Sinister

[Your shadow is complete.]

Sunny hissed, finally feeling that the pain rending his soul apart was subsiding. His new Shadow Core was fully formed, and he was a Titan again — already. It did not take him long to reclaim his Class at all. Of course, it had also cost him countless shades, weakening his Domain somewhat. But all in all, that loss was one he could easily cope with.

With the kind of battles he was fighting these days, those of his shades that were below the Ascended Rank rarely had an opportunity to do something useful. So, he had consumed many of those, as well as some that were more powerful, but were difficult to integrate into the Shadow Legion. In fact, it felt like he was doing a long-needed cleanup of his soul... it already felt less crowded.

In the future, he would have to explore this newfound ability more. Could he consolidate the Shadow Legion, perhaps, making those of his shades that were truly powerful even more so?

Somehow, Sunny doubted it. Shades were dead, after all, and therefore static. It was against their nature to change and grow. However, he could turn some of his shades into Shadows, and fuel those with the lesser shades. He would not need to hunt for Memories to feed them anymore — at least up to the Supreme Rank.

Beyond that, even he did not know how to help his Shadows conquer Apotheosis, or if it was even possible. The Spell, at least, was either refusing or incapable of offering assistance. Regardless, at the moment, Sunny could only shelve that idea. He already had seven Shadows, after all, and could not accommodate another.

Sunny felt that he would find a way to do just that sooner or later, though.

For now, he exhaled slowly and looked at Nephis.

She seemed to have recovered somewhat, looking at him silently. Sunny did not have to explain what had happened to him, since Nephis could read his runes just fine — she would know that he had completed the Weave, that he lost a Shadow Core, and that he managed to build a new one by sacrificing thousands of his shades.

A pale smile appeared on Sunny's lips.

"See? I'm as good as new. No need to worry."

Then, he groaned and spat a bit of blood. Nephis gave him a long look, then sighed and shook her head.

“Your shadow is staring at me."

Hearing that, Sunny turned his gaze to the shadow his body was casting onto the black sand. It was even darker than the obsidian dust it was lying on, motionless, gazing at Nephis intently instead of obediently copying his movements.

Sunny frowned.

He had not known what to expect from the new shadow, but hoped that it would be like the mad guy, reborn. However, the newcomer was quite different from his fallen predecessor.

The new shadow just seemed... dark. Far darker than it was supposed to be, and more than a little bit sinister as well.

In fact, Sunny felt a cold chill run down his spine when he looked at it.

He sighed.

"Welcome to the world of the living, new guy. Well, to the Realm of Death, I guess. I'll call you... wait, we already have a creepy shadow. Huh, what then?"

Sunny pondered for a moment, then opened his mouth with a glint in his eyes.

However, before he could speak, Nephis interrupted him:

“Do not name him Creepy Number Two."

The glint in Sunny's eyes dimmed.

He remained silent for a moment, then scoffed.

“Whatever. Let's go with eerie, then. That fits your sinister ambiance, too."

The eerie shadow slowly turned its head and stared at him silently.

All shadows were silent, but this shadow's subtle silence was strangely unsettling. Sunny coughed, took control of his new invaluable helper, and manifested him into an avatar. After doing that, he allowed his other incarnation to turn into a shadow instead.

Looking at Nephis, he sighed.

“Should we finish our expedition here?"

It was easy for him to leave the Shadow Realm. All he had to do was use one of his other incarnations to summon the Shadow Lantern, and escape the desolate land through its gate.

Nephis raised an eyebrow.

“You have a different idea?"

Sunny hesitated for a moment, then nodded.

"I think... before we go, we can visit an old friend."

Rising from the sand, Nephis nodded.

"Let's do that, then. I wanted to meet him for a long time, as well."

There was a lot they had to discuss, adjusting their plans in light of this new, harrowing experience. Cassie would have to participate in that discussion, as well... even Mordret, if he was willing, not to mention Ananke.

For example, they had to determine the probability of the prisoner of the Abyss escaping the Underworld. Sunny felt that the creature would not be able to leave, at least for now — the abyssal horror that had kept it bound was not dead, after all, just wounded. It would recover from the damage it had received soon. Most of all, however, there were the white mists that shrouded the Hollow Mountain.

Nothing could keep the Void from seeping into the world. Surely, a single Unholy being —a creature merely tainted by the Void, not born from it — would not be able to break through its flowing cage easily.

But since Sunny and Nephis were already in the Shadow Realm, they could visit Eurys first.

They did not walk to their destination, of course. Instead, Sunny used Shadow Step to carry them both through the desolate wasteland. After the suffocating darkness of the Underworld, being surrounded by the endless expanse of shadows felt like a breath of fresh air — soothing and liberating.

On top of that, he was not being eaten alive by the Shadow Realm... at least not as blatantly as before. So, Sunny actually enjoyed their swift journey across the sea of obsidian dunes.

He was moving with astonishing speed, but it was still going to take them a little time to reach Eurys.

So, not wishing to waste it, Sunny summoned his runes once again.

This time, he ignored the counter showing his shadow fragments and looked directly at a different string of runes.

The ones describing his Shadows... in particular, the one describing Saint.

Saint had almost finished her evolution, after all.

This time, she achieved it much faster than ever before — perhaps because she had already been halfway to reaching a higher Class, perhaps simply because the situation had demanded it.

The runes read:

Shadow: Jade Saint.

Shadow Rank: Supreme.

Shadow Class: Tyrant.

--- Chapter 3116 ---

3116 Princess of the Underworld

Shadow: Jade Saint.

Shadow Rank: Supreme.

Shadow Class: Tyrant.

Sunny looked at these runes for a short while, feeling deeply satisfied. Finally, after a long while, Saint had evolved to a new Class once more — this time reaching the coveted title of a Tyrant.

There was a qualitative jump in power between a Devil and a Tyrant, marking the latter as the first of the higher Classes, so he had high expectations for his oldest and most loyal Shadow.

Sunny continued to study the runes.

They read:

Shadow Attributes: [Princess of the Underworld], [Warmaster], [Stalwart], [Flame of Divinity], [Heart of Darkness], [Vessel of Nothing].

Shadow Abilities: [Royal Banner], [Weapon Sage], [Underworld Armament], [Mantle of Darkness], [Blade of Darkness], [Shield of Nothing].

There were two new additions — one Attribute and one Ability. Saint had absorbed a great deal of both true darkness and nothingness, as well, meaning that her elemental Abilities had grown far more potent.

The new Attribute had quite a catchy name. Sunny focused on it, reading the description.

Attribute: [Princess of the Underworld].

Attribute Description: [This Shadow has inherited the crown of the Underworld, and with it, the legacy of endless war.]

Sunny stared at the short description for a while, contemplating it.

‘The crown of the Underworld...’

It was not difficult to understand the hidden meaning of these words. A long time ago, Nether had bestowed seven suits of armor to his most flawless creations. However, those suits of armor — the Mantles of the Underworld — were both a gift and a trial. Sunny suspected that those of Nether's favorite children who had passed the trial would have been recognized as his heirs, the Princes of the Underworld — like the Titan of Tainted Jade, the Prince of Darkness.

After all, Sunny had completed that trial himself, and that was the name of the enchantment responsible for tallying his victories.

However, all of the Princes were dead now, having either been destroyed in the endless war their creator had started or consumed by Corruption. The last of the seven Princes had been slain by Saint — so, ironically enough, she was the one who proved herself worthy of Nether's inheritance in the end, not them.

Only Saint was not one of Nether's favored creations, and neither had she received a suit of armor from him. Instead, she had forged her armor herself and had chosen her own path, walking among the shadows through true darkness and nothingness.

It was quite fitting, actually, for someone created by the Demon of Choice.

Sadly...

The kingdom she was supposed to inherit was long gone. Her people were extinct, the cities of the Underworld lay in ruin, and even Nether himself was dead. So, this crown of his was an empty promise — a symbol of a long-forgotten past that carried great weight, but offered very little to its wearer.

Maybe that Attribute did grant Saint some benefit, like gaining recognition among the creatures of the Underworld or being able to control ancient sorceries left behind by Nether better. But mostly, it must have simply functioned as a symbol of her authority — a spiritual mark that proclaimed her status as a Tyrant.

The Ability she had gained was much more interesting.

Sunny shifted his gaze to the runes that described it.

Ability: [Royal Banner].

Ability Description: [Those who fight under this Shadow's stalwart banner are connected to her by the bond of loyalty, and are therefore bestowed the boon of her command. They are vessels of her will and conduits of her power, becoming living armaments for their commander to wield.]

Sunny's gaze grew sharper.

If he was not wrong... then the [Royal Banner] Ability allowed Saint to fulfill the role of a general. Those who followed her command would be connected to her by a mystical bond, and through her to each other. That would allow Saint to command her soldiers directly, and therefore any army she commanded would act with an extreme level of unity, cohesion, and tactical excellence.

She possessed the [Warmaster] Attribute, after all, which expressed her profound knowledge of all kinds of warfare.

That alone was a tremendous boon. However, the description implied much more... it implied that Saint's soldiers would be enhanced by the connection to their general, sharing in her might.

What did it mean?

It meant that they would be infused with her Will, as well as inherit a measure of her power.

Not all of her power, of course — at least Sunny did not think so. The [Underworld Armament], [Mantle of Darkness], [Blade of Darkness], and [Shield of Nothing] Abilities were too specific, after all, and could only function because of Saint's [Heart of Darkness] and [Vessel of Nothing] Attributes.

However, that left one Ability... perhaps the most important Ability of them all.

It was [Weapon Sage].

If all soldiers under Saint's banner inherited a lesser version of her sublime and varied martial skill — while already benefiting from the direct control of a Warmaster on a tactical level — then the army she commanded would be truly terrifying. It would be nearly impossible to defeat unless the enemy forces were utterly, overwhelmingly superior in terms of raw power.

Among soldiers, experience was more valuable than gold, as were ability and talent. Those who dwelled on the battlefield rarely lived long, so experience was difficult to come by — a seasoned veteran was worth ten inexperienced recruits, or maybe more. If that veteran was not only seasoned, but also competent and gifted, though, they were simply priceless.

What the combination of the [Warmaster] Attribute's influence and the lesser version of the [Weapon Sage] Ability did... was make every soldier under Saint's command equal to such a priceless veteran.

An army composed of only seasoned, indomitable elites... was an army Sunny never wanted to face on the battlefield.

He would rather be the commander of that army — or rather, the liege lord of that army's commander.

And now, it seemed that he was.

‘Damn.'

In short, Saint was now a force multiplier that could dramatically elevate the power of the entire Shadow Legion.

Sunny had gained a legion of Shadow Saints and the shadow of the Prince of Darkness, as well, not to mention Shadow Weave. Overall, the expedition to the Underworld had proven to be quite fruitful... despite its disastrous ending.

As Sunny rushed across the desolate expanse of the Shadow Realm, carrying Nephis with him, he could not help but feel a hint of dark exhilaration.

He did not know what the future held, but he knew one thing.

Now that Saint was a Tyrant...

Those damn Barrow Wraiths would learn what sorrow meant very, very soon.

--- Chapter 3117 ---

Eventually, they made it to the graveyard of Soul Serpents. Eurys was just where Sunny had left him — a dozen kilometers away, at the bottom of a tall dune.

It seemed that the ancient skeleton had not managed to crest it yet, rolling down its steep slope countless times.

At the moment, he was sprawled on the black sand, staring at the sky. A distant essence storm illuminated his shattered bones, painting an eerie picture — when Sunny and Nephis rose from the shadows, the white skull turned, staring at them with empty eye sockets.

Sunny had to suppress a shudder, remembering the abhorrent skeleton that lay hidden in the Abyss.

Eurys remained silent for a few moments, and then said in a creaky voice:

"My, oh my. It seems that I have guests. Ah, what to do? Please forgive me, children... the whole place is a mess..."

From his tone, it was hard to say what place he was talking about — the bottom of the tall dune, the Shadow Realm, or the entire world.

In any case, the description fit all three. Nephis approached the battered skeleton and looked down at it, expressionless. Eventually, she said:

“So you are alive, after all."

Eurys laughed.

“Alive? Oh, I wouldn't go that far... but it's good to see you too, abomination."

Sunny frowned.

“Hey, bastard. What did I say about using that word?"

The ancient skull turned slightly, staring at him.

Then, Eurys chuckled.

"Something about breaking my old bones? Salutations, boy. How many cities did you destroy this time?"

Sunny scoffed with an indignant expression, offended by that greeting. It was as if Eurys thought him to be some kind of walking calamity hellbent on sowing destruction everywhere he went.

“What? None! Why would you think..."

But then, he abruptly closed his mouth and just glared at the ancient skeleton silently for a few moments.

In the end, Sunny had to say through gritted teeth:

“One... and half."

He did... sort of... destroy Weave when he and the Thieving Bird fell from the sky and crashed into it during their battle. And while the nameless city in the heart of the Underworld ultimately survived, a couple of the great stalagmites did end up crumbling and falling into the white mist.

Eurys just stared at him silently. Despite the fact that the old skull could not express any emotions, Sunny could not help but feel that his gaze was mocking.

Eventually, the ancient skeleton cackled.

“Good job! You've been gone for so long, so I really thought that it'd be a bigger number. You have really restrained yourself well, it seems!"

Sunny let out a heavy sigh and sat down on the sand near Eurys. Nephis followed his example, and a few moments later, the ancient skeleton asked in a curious tone:

“So, what have you been up to since our last meeting?"

He seemed... more subdued than usual, somehow. Maybe Neph's presence made Eurys want to be on his best behavior, or maybe he was simply tired of endlessly trying and failing to scale the steep dune. Maybe the curse of Shadow God was finally catching up to him, and he was slowly losing himself.

Remembering the appalling end of Azarax, the King of Kings, Sunny felt his gaze turning somber.

He remained silent for a short while, then spoke in a reserved tone:

“What have I been up to? Well, let's see..."

Sunny thought back to everything that had happened since his last conversation with Eurys.

“I went to Ariel's Hell and took your old friend, Azarax, off the tree. The curse consumed him eventually, but he helped me get to the old tomb hidden in the heart of that dismal place. I climbed into the Tomb of Ariel, found the loathsome bird who had stolen my fate, and killed it. The vile thing did not stay dead for long, but I managed to reclaim what it had taken from me... even if, in the process, the damn bird absconded with more of my possessions.”

Sunny grimaced and then continued in a dark tone:

“After that, I sealed a terrible idea in a deep well to save humanity. Later... the world is ending, so I was quite busy trying to keep it from falling apart. I did go on a mountain trip with my girlfriend — one thing led to another, and we ended up making the sun rise in the Underworld. It was quite a sight."

Sunny chuckled joylessly.

"The view was simply to die for. And I did... and so, here I am, in the Land of Death.”

Eurys stared at him silently for a long while, not saying anything.

In the end, though, he spoke in a friendly tone:

“My, oh my! It is good that you took Azarax... that insufferable buffoon... off the tree. Your tale was quite amusing, as well. But, uh... I wasn't asking you, boy."

Sunny blinked a couple of times.

He threw a furtive glance at Nephis.

She smiled faintly.

"The last time we met, I was still Dormant, wasn't I?"

Eurys nodded.

“And look at you now! Already a mighty Supreme. Well, you nephilim were always an eerie kind."

He looked at Sunny and asked:

“Do you know what that abominable girl said when she found Azarax and me in the middle of hell, boy?"

Sunny silently shook his head.

Eurys laughed.

“I don't need two guides, she said. So, pick among yourselves whom I should free. My, oh my! Can you believe it?"

He did his best impression of Neph's dispassionate tone, then laughed again, as if finding the memory infinitely amusing. Sunny looked at Nephis.

Could he?

"Actually... I can believe it very easily."

She remained unperturbed and just shrugged casually.

"I picked well in the end, didn't I?"

‘I'd say.’

No matter what horrible crimes Eurys had committed in the ancient past, he did guide Nephis into the depths of the Underworld, to a Seed of Nightmare. If she had chosen Azarax, he would have lost his mind before they even left the Nightmare Desert — in fact, he might have turned on her immediately after being taken off the tree. Nephis sighed.

"Many things have happened since."

She remained silent for a few moments, then said quietly:

“I was broken in one Nightmare and rebuilt myself in another. I swore loyalty to the people who had betrayed and killed my father, then betrayed and killed them in turn. There was war, there were bitter losses... there were brief moments of peace and sweet triumphs, as well. I am still pursuing my goal. I have come so far, but I am still only halfway there."

Eurys did not answer immediately.

“I have come so far, but I am still only halfway there..."

His voice sounded low and wistful.

He turned his skull to the slope of the dune — in the direction where the heart of the Shadow Realm, and the death he was seeking, lay.

“Come to think of it, that describes my situation as well."

Eurys looked back at them.

"Unless, of course, that wicked shadow of yours keeps his promise and kills me. How about it, boy? Have you come to try again?"

Sunny remained motionless for a while, then slowly shook his head.

“Not today. There is no point. I have grown far more powerful than I used to be, and Nephis is here with me as well. But, still, we are not strong enough to undo what Shadow God did."

He paused for a few moments, and then added quietly:

"We may be gods ourselves soon, though. The next time we meet... if we meet... Nephis and I will be Sacred, at least. Then, I will fulfill my promise."

Eurys stared at him with his empty eye sockets.

“You are going to make use of Weaver's spell, then?"

Sunny nodded.

"Yes. We plan to challenge the Fifth Nightmare soon... as soon as possible."

Eurys remained silent for a long while, and then sighed.

“Go forth and conquer, then. I wish you luck — gods know, you'll need it.”

He paused, clacked his jaw, and added in a thoughtful tone:

"But then again, the gods are dead. So, really, they wouldn't know anything at all..."

His voice echoed in the darkness of the Realm of Death, wishing them a safe journey.

--- Chapter 3118 ---

A dying city sprawled under the dark sky, the sun obscured by billowing clouds of black smoke. The great river that had once flowed through it was gone, the sediment on its bottom littered with corpses and broken weapons. The proud walls of the city were covered in fractures and deep scars, some sections so battered that they seemed ready to crumble.

The streets of the city were like a vision of hell, or perhaps a scene from a monstrous nightmare. Closer to the wall, countless buildings had burned down, with only their skeletal remains rising from the ash like blackened gravestones. Other areas were still intact, but enveloped by a suffocating atmosphere of fear and desperation.

Here and there, rotting bodies lay on the cobblestones, with no one bothering to gather and burn them anymore. Those people who still clung to life were suffering from hunger, disease, and murderous thirst. Clean water was a rarity, so many resorted to drinking whatever kind they could find, ignoring the risk of sickness and death.

The wails of people dying from the plague had become background noise, with nobody paying them attention anymore.

The bay had become a graveyard of ships, their masts protruding from the waves like twisted branches. By now, it was all but impossible to bypass the complicated maze of shipwrecks to enter the harbor... or leave it.

The soldiers who defended the city were like pale shadows of their former selves. They suffered from the lack of food and drinking water, too. Disease was just as rampant among them as it was among the civilian population.

Most of all, the majority of them had already perished in the endless onslaught of war. There were very few people left in the city who had not been called upon to become soldiers, in fact, but their number was still greatly diminished. All men had long taken up weapons to defend the wall, and when too many of them died, women took their place. Even children were conscripted, gathering arrows from below the walls and helping with menial tasks.

Worst of all... the sole Supreme of the besieged city, the Mason King, was dying. Countless months of clashing with the tyrannical Will of Azarax, the Plague of Steel, had eroded his spirit and worn out his soul. Now, the old man was slowly fading away.

And yet, the city still stood.

Its battered walls were scarred and fractured, but they refused to crumble.

Its people were being consumed by disease and despair, but they had not given up.

The soldiers, who had sacrificed countless lives to defend the city, were not ready to surrender to death yet.

But everything came to an end, sooner or later.

Looking at the nightmarish vista of the dying city, Effie knew that their days were numbered.

There was simply a limit to what people could do, no matter how deep the well of their resolve was. The city had been besieged for so long... how long had it been, actually?

She frowned, trying to remember.

‘Two years? No, not yet. But only a few months shy.'

Almost two years had passed since she and her companions had entered the Nightmare — a little less since the Steel Horde established an encirclement around the city. There had been countless assaults, myriad battles, countless losses. Being able to halt the unstoppable expansion of Azarax's bloody empire for so long was a miraculous feat, but did it matter in the end?

The city was still going to fall. Its people were still going to be slaughtered. No matter how long they had managed to hold out, their valiant defiance was still going to end up being nothing but a short line in the glorious chronicle of the King of Kings... a paragraph, at best, no different from all his previous conquests.

Worst of all, time did not stay still while they were fighting for their lives in the Nightmare. The same number of months had passed in the real world, as well.

Effie's expression darkened.

Somewhere out there... by now, the world was probably ending. The Dream Realm was devouring the last refuge of mankind. Humanity was besieged on all sides. Sunny and Nephis were desperately trying to stem the endless tide of abominations, and Cassie was probably even busier than them.

Two years...

Her son had not seen her for that long. He was about to turn nine, meeting another birthday without his mother. Was he alright? Was he well?

What about his father?

She sighed heavily.

They probably missed her just as much as she missed them. Were they counting days, both hoping to hear news about her and feeling their hearts sink every time someone knocked on the door?

‘Two years, damn it.'

Effie had known that the Fourth Nightmare might take them a long time to conquer. But she had not expected it to take years, with no end in sight.

No, actually, the end was already near... it was just not the kind of end they wanted. The Mason was dying. The old man was still keeping Azarax at bay despite his broken spirit, but the spark of his life was growing feebler with each day. Once he was gone, no amount of valor would prevent the Plague of Steel from conquering the city — Effie and her companions would not be able to stop him, either.

She gazed at the nightmarish vista of the city one more time and then looked down at her calloused hand.

In the dim torchlight, her hand was trembling uncontrollably.

Effie stared at it for a while, and then slowly made a fist, willing it to settle. Finally, the tremors subsided.

She inhaled deeply.

‘The end... let's end it, then. Little Ling's birthday is in December — I should wrap up everything quickly and return just in time to light the candles on his birthday cake.’

Effie smiled wistfully.

‘Ah, cake... I haven't had cake in a while...'

With that, she turned around and descended the wall of the Stone Castle.

In the next few days, she was going to break the Steel Horde's back, win the war, and write the final line in the chronicle of the great and horrible Azarax, the King of Kings.

--- Chapter 3119 ---

Dawn was approaching, so the Stone Castle was slowly waking up. This gorgeous stronghold had been the Mason's original creation once — the city grew around it, eventually becoming what it was today. Or had been, at least.

The castle was a small city in and of itself. It couldn't compare to Bastion, of course, but countless people could find shelter behind its walls, still. The inner stronghold of the besieged city had its own walls, its own moat, its own layered defenses, all isolated from the greater urban sprawl beyond — as long as the drawbridge was raised, getting inside was as difficult as breaching the city wall.

More so, even, since building a highly defensible fortress was far easier than ensuring the safety of a thriving metropolis. It used to be that the Stone Castle was sparsely populated, with only the royal family, their servants, and their closest retainer inhabiting its courtyards and walls. Now, however, the situation had changed.

As Effie descended from the wall and made her way to the drawbridge, she had to carefully wade through a mass of people. The castle was overcrowded, with each courtyard and corridor becoming a makeshift shelter — the citizens were in the throes of nightmares, sleeping restlessly with nothing but flimsy straw mats between them and the ground.

They were mostly those who were too old to fight, too young to be of use, or already maimed and unable to wield a weapon. Most able-bodied people had already been conscripted to help defend the city, so there were few of them here, behind the last line of defense.

Some of these people slept, but most were awake, pressing themselves against the walls or hugging each other, covered with threadbare blankets and staring into the distance tiredly. The mass of them was like a furnace, generating almost palpable waves of heat — when Effie walked by, something ignited in their eyes, and for a short while, they seemed like proper humans again.

This was a recent arrangement. Before, the remains of the civilian population stayed in the city, scattered across its safer areas. It was better to keep them apart, since that made it harder for disease to spread. But now that the Mason was about to fall, there were no safe areas anymore. So, everyone... everyone who was still alive... was brought to the inner stronghold over the last few nights.

Despite how crowded the castle was, seeing it like that was sobering. Before, it would have never been able to accommodate the entire population of the city — but the population had shrunk so much that now, it was enough. So many people had died. More people had died than survived, really.

That made Effie question if the accomplishment of holding the city for all this time was even worth a damn.

‘Well, there were certainly benefits.'

All of them, those who had challenged the Nightmare, were far more powerful than they were at the start. How could they not be?

Close to two years of constant battles, almost always against an overwhelmingly powerful foe, had tempered them. They had already been the best and most seasoned warriors of humanity, and with the accumulating weight of experience, their skill and tenacity only grew.

Their skill was improving by leaps and bounds. Their soul arsenals were expanding. They were learning to wield their Aspects better and discovering new facets of their power... there were other, less conspicuous improvements, as well.

Tactics, strategy, logistics, civil engineering, leadership — and so much more. The task of running an embattled city, wringing every drop of usefulness out of the limited resources at their disposal, was teaching them things beyond martial excellence and personal valor.

A few of them were close to unlocking their Aspect Legacies, as well.

The Nightmares were always catalysts of explosive growth, and this one was no different. In fact, it was far greater in scope and intensity than all the previous Nightmares Effie had survived.

The problem, of course, was that she and the others would only get to enjoy the benefits of their growth if they survived this one, as well. And that was looking harder and harder to achieve with each passing day.

What was the point of all that improvement if all it ultimately granted them was a slower death?

Finally making her way through the crowded paths of the castle, Effie reached the drawbridge. It was lowered, and the last batches of people were crossing it to escape the vast desolation of the devastated city. Soldiers were showing them the way, explaining their new temporary arrangements. A young man in a luxurious tunic was overseeing the process.

The tunic was embroidered with golden thread, shimmering radiantly in the torchlight. It had seen better days, though, just like the people walking across the drawbridge and the city itself.

The young man was the prince of the dying city, the youngest son of the Mason. His older siblings had perished centuries ago, having failed to outlive their Supreme father... their great-grandchildren were long gone, as well. The family trees of powerful Awakened were a complete mess.

Effie glanced at the prince, wondering how her own family tree would look one day, if she survived the Nightmare and the apocalypse both.

‘Supremacy... it's a bit messed up, as far as human connections are concerned.'

That was the price of becoming a demigod, as well.

When the young prince noticed Effie, a pale smile illuminated his face. He left his post and headed her way.

The prince was a pleasant enough fellow. He was diligent, polite, and competent — even if his talents did not lie on the battlefield, just like his father's. He had also been able to maintain his optimism and decorum for a long while, helping Effie rally the citizens and keep them from losing hope.

It was just that now, there was a shadow of melancholy in his eyes. The plague had not spared the royal family, either, taking the lives of two of his three children. The smile never reached his eyes since then.

But just like the walls of the city, the prince had not crumbled.

Approaching Effie, he bowed.

"May the heavens smile upon you, Priestess."

Effie looked at him for a moment, then nodded.

“And you as well."

He hesitated, studying her, as if unsure what to say. So, Effie spoke instead.

"This should be the last of them, right? You only have a few hours left. Make sure that everyone is inside the castle."

The prince turned to the stream of gaunt, battered people entering through the gate.

"Yes... this is the last of them."

His voice was distant.

Effie sighed.

"How is your father? He didn't look too well yesterday."

The prince remained silent for a moment, then smiled wistfully.

"He is fading away. I think the era of the Mason will end soon — perhaps in a few days, maybe in a few weeks.”

He paused, then added in a soft tone:

“My father... among the great and terrible Supremes, he might not have been the most glorious, or one whose thrilling feats are sung about across the mortal realms. But, still... long centuries of peace, long centuries of prosperity. If I wanted to leave behind a legacy, I would have wanted to leave a legacy like his."

The prince glanced at Effie and chuckled.

“I am sorry, my lady. As a priestess of War, you must find my talk of peace distasteful.”

Effie glanced into the distance.

“Actually, I am quite fond of peace."

She hesitated for a moment, then turned to the prince and smiled.

“It is just that my fondness for peace is purely theoretical, since I've never known it. I don't think I'll recognize peace even if it hit me in the face."

As long as Effie could remember herself, she had been fighting for her life. And by the time she grew powerful enough to survive, she was fighting for the lives of others.

So, what was peace?

She did not know.

Effie sighed, then shook her head.

“The legacy of your father is not long centuries of peace and prosperity, though. It is you, your family — and all these people. So, as long as his people continue to live and remember him, his era will continue.”

The prince remained silent for a long while, then nodded.

“As long as we continue to live. As long as we remember."

With that, he looked across the drawbridge, at the desolate city.

“Stone breaks, but people endure. Thank you, Priestess."

He turned to her then and looked at her solemnly.

After a long stretch of silence, the prince said, his tone laden with meaning.

"We will remember you as well, my lady."

Effie inhaled deeply, then smiled and turned away.

Stepping onto the drawbridge to leave the castle, she left the prince behind.

This was most likely the last time they saw each other.

If so...

Effie wished for the young prince and his people to find peace and prosperity once more, one day.

--- Chapter 3120 ---

On the other side of the drawbridge, a crowd of people — the last of the citizens to be led into the inner keep — were waiting for their turn to cross. The elderly were holding the smallest of children, while those who were old enough to stand on their own were hugging their legs, looking around with curious eyes.

These kids had grown up while looking at the distant, magnificent palace of the Mason King, but few had ever been inside. The adults were broken by the horrors of war, but children were far more resilient — since they barely remembered anything else, this was simply how the world was for them.

So, the light in their eyes had not been extinguished yet, and they were excited to see the castle up close.

To the side of the bridge, a crowd of children surrounded an unlikely babysitter, clamoring for his attention.

“Uncle, uncle! Tell us about the living ship!"

“Is it true that you fought a god once?"

“Uncle... what does stardust taste like? Is it sweet?"

Nightwalker chuckled, looking around with a helpless expression.

“Why are you guys pestering me? I am supposed to keep watch! Go, shoo. Find your grandmas... and for the record, I can never fight a god. After all, Storm God is my grandma. How can I disrespect my elders?"

Effie shook her head.

Nightwalker had been in charge of an important task before — he had been the only one who could bypass the blockade, so he often sailed away and returned with supplies to feed the people of the besieged city.

Even with how the harbor was now, littered with shipwrecks and utterly impossible to navigate, he could still do it. The problem was that all the ships of his fleet had sunk, so there was nothing for him to sail on. Now that Nightwalker was grounded, all he could do was join the defenders of the city on the wall.

His strength was greatly appreciated there, but without his perilous voyages, the city had no food source anymore. So, people had been slowly starving for a long while.

Effie knew a thing or two about starvation, so she felt their pain.

Noticing her, Nightwalker shooed the giggling children away and rose to greet her.

"It's a nice morning, isn't it?"

Effie looked up.

The sky was still dark, barely painted pale lilac in the east.

"I'd say it's still the middle of the night."

She spared him a look.

"Are you ready?"

Nightwalker chuckled.

"Me? I should be asking you instead."

He fell silent, mirth draining from his face. A few moments later, he said quietly:

“You can still change your mind, you know. You don't have to do it yourself."

Effie smiled.

"It's a little bit too late for that, I think."

There was already no way back. There had not been for some time.

She chuckled.

"Ah, but don't get me wrong. I'd gladly trade places with you. Sadly, you're not the one Azarax has developed an unhealthy fixation on."

She paused for a moment.

“What can I say? I guess you are not charming enough."

Nightwalker stared at her, aghast.

"What are you talking about? My charm has never failed me. That bastard just didn't have the chance to get to know me, since I was busy hunting for supplies most of the time. Otherwise, he wouldn't even look your way."

Effie grinned.

“Whatever you say, grandpa.”

Nightwalker's expression was quite amusing.

She looked back to the bridge, then asked:

“Everything has been prepared?"

He hesitated for a moment, then nodded.

“The castle is secured. Kai and Morgan finished the preparations in the city, as well. Seishan... well, you'd know best. As for Soul Reaper, we won't know until it's done."

Effie sighed.

"I'll leave the civilians to you, then. Once the bridge rises... make sure that the keep stays safe."

Nightwalker remained silent for a short while.

Eventually, he nodded.

“The castle won't fall. I guarantee it.”

Effie left him behind, as well.

She passed through the crowd of civilians and reached the empty, desolate streets of the city. Since most of its inhabitants had been taken away to the stronghold, there were only soldiers left here, rushing as they made the last preparations before retreating into the keep, as well.

They stopped and bowed deeply when they saw Effie, an indescribable emotion hidden in the depths of their sunken, haunted eyes. Their expressions were solemn, and only grew more so when she greeted them with an easy smile.

At some point, however, her smile faltered.

‘What is that I'm seeing?’

Out there in front of her... were Morgan and Seishan.

The Princess of Valor and the Princess of Song were sitting on the ground among the rubble, having completely forgotten their sense of decorum.

They were... playing cards.

Effie blinked and rubbed her eyes, wondering if she was imagining things. But no, her eyes weren't lying to her. Morgan and Seishan were indeed sitting on the dusty cobblestones and playing cards, discussing something quietly amongst each other.

She could hear bits and pieces of their conversation.

“Another ace? How can this be?"

"That is called skill, Your Highness."

“Don't your highess me, wench. You're cheating!"

“How would I cheat? That doesn't even make sense."

“Five aces in a deck of cards is what doesn't make sense."

"Oh, so you have a pair of aces? Hmm... unfortunate."

“Of course I do. Or do I only want you to believe that I do?"

“I will believe anything you say, Your Highness. I wouldn't dare doubt your honesty."

"How are you so good at being infuriating?"

“It comes with practice."

“Stop practicing on me, then!"

Effie stared at them, dumbfounded.

“What are you doing, fools?"

Morgan and Seishan looked at her. Morgan shrugged.

“Waiting for you, obviously."

Seishan nodded.

“What, did you expect that we'll leave you all alone on this fine morning?"

Morgan threw one last glance at her cards, then grimaced and stood up.

"Let's go. We'll see you off to the gate."

Effie gave her a long look, then smiled.

“It's an honor... Your Highness."

Morgan's eye twitched, and she forced out a smile.

"Why, of course. Anything for our esteemed Steward of the East."

Seishan rose, then stretched and spoke in her husky, tantalizing voice.

“By the way, I always wanted to ask... in your case, wouldn't it be the Stewardess of the East? That would make more sense."

Effie could only stare at her blankly.

"Did the plague rot your brain?"

Seishan shrugged.

"Someone would have to split my skull open to find out."

Hearing that, Morgan livened up.

“If you want to, that can be arranged. I'll volunteer."

Ignoring them, Effie walked past.

“Fine, let's go. I appreciate it. Goodness gracious, it's still dark outside! A fine young lady like me shouldn't be walking the streets alone in the dark... who knows what terrible things might happen!"

To whoever was foolish enough to bother her, that was.

The three of them made their way to the city gate, sharing a lighthearted conversation. The mood was carefree and laidback, as if they were not passing through burned ruins and stepping over the blackened bones, circling around rotting corpses from time to time.

It was so carefree, in fact, that for a short while, Effie was distracted from the truth. From the fact that today, her life could very well come to an end.

--- Chapter 3121 ---

The city was dead and quiet as they walked toward the distant wall. The streets were empty, with not a soul around. An eerie silence suffused the world, as if they had taken a wrong turn somewhere and somehow ended up in hell... if hell did exist, then Effie imagined it looking similar to this.

She had seen all kinds of horrors in her life, and the blackened ruins — collapsed buildings, bodies scattered in the dust, the smell of rot and ash permeating the air — were nothing new to her. The devastation itself was not hell... the knowledge of all the human pain, despair, and broken dreams that lay hidden under the rubble was.

Effie was glad that Morgan and Seishan had chosen to accompany her on this dreary walk. Otherwise, it would have felt too lonesome.

As they approached the city gate, however, the situation changed.

She had ordered most of her soldiers to pull back, but somehow, a grand welcome was waiting for her. Countless soldiers — all gaunt and battered — had assembled to see their commander off, forming two human walls on both sides of the road.

They did not cheer, and neither did they say anything. However, as Effie approached, she could see everything they wished to say in their eyes.

The soldiers saluted her silently as she walked past, their reserved expressions betraying a storm of turbulent emotions. Sorrow, reverence, pain, courage — she could see all of it, and more.

But most of all, what she saw was strength. These people were all wounded, hungry, exhausted, sick, and losing hope. But none of them had broken — none of them was entertaining the thought of giving up.

So, she thought she'd give them a good show.

Straightening her spine, Effie met the gazes of her soldiers and smiled. It was a confident, easy smile — one that betrayed no hint of fear or hesitation. The same smile they had seen countless times.

If the young prince of the dying city had been honest when he said that they would remember her, Effie wanted them to remember her like this.

It was a strange wish, considering that all of them were mere phantoms conjured by the Spell, and would be gone once the Nightmare was over.

What meaning was there in being remembered by forgotten phantoms? Finally, they reached the gates of the city. There, a lone figure was waiting for them, standing in the middle of the road — barring their way.

It was Kai, of course.

Morgan and Seishan slowed down, allowing Effie to approach him alone.

As she did, she whistled quietly.

‘Uh-oh. Kai is not happy...’

Indeed, it was as clear as day. The others had tried to hide their emotions, but he did not bother to — his face was dark and somber... desperate, even. There were black circles under his eyes, and his gaze was scathing.

Bruised eyes, sunken cheeks, chapped lips...

‘Goodness.'

Kai had really let himself go. The world had to be ending.

“Effie...”

Stopping in front of him, Effie smiled.

“Why the long face?"

He stared at her for a moment, then frowned.

“There has to be another way. You don't have to... you must not. We can come up with another plan. Please, reconsider."

Effie studied him silently for a short while, then chuckled.

“You know me, buddy. I am not a very considerate person. It took me a lot of effort to consider this one plan... now, you expect me to reconsider the whole thing? Gods have mercy, I cannot."

He refused to be placated by her lighthearted tone, looking at her with dark intensity.

Effie sighed.

“It's a good plan, Kai... it's the only way. You know it. Each of us just needs to do their part. My part is a bit flashy, but it's not the most difficult. In fact, I might be getting off easier than the rest of you."

Kai gritted his teeth.

"He'll kill you!"

Effie remained silent for a moment, then shook her head and laughed.

"He might. But he won't kill me immediately — and that's good enough. So, step aside."

Kai glared at her for a while longer, then looked down.

Eventually, he moved to the side, allowing her to pass.

Effie lingered for a moment, then patted him on the shoulder and walked past him. Now, only the gates loomed above her.

She hesitated a little, then took a deep breath.

“Hey, Kai. Can you do me a favor?"

He did not answer, prompting Effie to turn and glance at him.

“Once I am out there... don't look."

She did not say anything else, and he did not respond, either.

In the end, however, Kai nodded slowly. Effie smiled and nodded, as well.

"I have an image to maintain, that's all. Well, you used to be an idol, so you should understand."

With that, everything that needed to be said had been said. Effie looked ahead once more and raised her voice:

"Open the gate!"

The towering main gate of the city, which had stayed shut since the beginning of the siege, refusing to be breached or broken, finally groaned and moved.

Opening that enormous gate was a complicated affair, since the Mason had constructed it himself. It weighed too much to be pushed by people or Awakened — even Ascended and Saints would struggle to force it open. So, a complex mechanism was involved, operated by a team of engineers. Now, that mechanism had been activated, pushing two titanic slabs of mystical stone apart.

The sun was already rising by then, chasing away the night — a new day had arrived, bringing with it a promise of a brighter tomorrow.

Or a darker one, maybe.

Effie was not sure which, but she knew that tomorrow would be entirely different from all the days before.

Once the gate was open wide enough for a person to pass through, she inhaled deeply and stepped forward.

Behind her, countless soldiers struck their fists against their armor, solemnly shouting her name. The sound of their voices rose to the sky like a deafening roar, making the heavens quake.

Effie smiled faintly.

‘Damn it.'

She was a little touched.

The irony of the situation, though, was that she was playing the role of the War Maiden in this Nightmare, so they weren't even shouting her real name.

‘Those fools...’

Passing through the gate, Effie entered the vast, terrifying killing field that stretched from the wall of the city to the horizon. If the city only resembled hell, then this was its true face. Corpses piled like mountains here, with fat crows waddling between broken weapons and remains of towering siege engines. The ground had turned into black sludge, soaked with blood and ash. The stench was unbearable, pillars of smoke rising into the pale sky.

She walked forward without looking back. Out there, on the horizon, a dark line contoured the world. That line was the vast, seemingly endless camp of the Steel Horde — at night, the fires its soldiers made looked like a boundless sea.

That was where Effie was headed...

Today, after a long and bitter siege, she was going to admit defeat and surrender the city to the King of Kings.

--- Chapter 3122 ---

It took Effie a while to cross the killing field. Behind her, the gates of the city stayed open, as if inviting the conquerors to come and claim their prize. The soldiers of the Steel Horde, of course, noticed the unusual movement.

They saw a lone figure walking across the black expanse of blood-soaked mud, as well.

By the time Effie reached the encampment of the conquering army, there was already a welcoming committee waiting for her. Hiding her emotions behind a composed expression, she looked around.

The Steel Horde was doing much better than the defenders of the city, who looked like walking corpses by now. However... its warriors didn't look too good, either.

It did not matter how numerous they were or how fearsome the power of the conquering horde was. These people had been stuck here, below the walls of the once-peaceful city, for almost two years now. The casualties they had suffered were far greater than the losses among its defenders — a truly terrifying amount, to the point that it was impossible to count how many had died.

And so, they had learned terror. Even with Azarax instilling them with confidence, their eventual victory assured, the warriors of the Steel Plague could not help but feel a deep and penetrating fear when looking at the distant walls of the city.

The casualties were not their only problem, either.

The empire of Azarax the Mighty was vast and powerful, but it was also young and vulnerable. His endless conquest left him with no time to consolidate his rulership and properly integrate the conquered lands, establishing a shared foundation of culture, laws, and economic interest that held empires together.

So, the longer his conquest stalled, and the longer he failed to deliver new spoils to feed his empire, the more internal tension there was.

Two fruitless years spent under the walls of a single, weak city-state... various regions of the Steel Empire were already sliding into turmoil and unrest. His generals, meanwhile, were growing uneasy about the fate of their families and noble houses back home.

As a result, not only were the soldiers becoming restless, but the supply chains that sustained the great and insatiable horde were also growing strained. It took an unfathomable amount of provisions to feed the endless ocean of soldiers — with an unstable situation in the rear, satiating their daily needs had long become a problem.

The warriors of the Steel Horde were not starving like the defenders of the city, but they weren't unfamiliar with hunger either. That was what Effie saw when she looked at the soldiers who left the encampment to meet her — gaunt faces, worn equipment, haunted looks. The long siege had been cruel to them, too.

Those were only the ordinary soldiers, of course. The Dread Warriors, Azarax's elites, were as hale and full of vigor as ever. Their tables never seemed to lack food, while their weapons and equipment were meticulously maintained.

Effie struggled to keep her expression steady as the familiar aura of dread they exerted washed over her. Nothing could compare to the crushing, suffocating presence of the man who stood in front of the soldiers, though, watching her approach with a dark grin.

Azarax looked like he always did. Years of bitter battles, countless lives lost, rivers of blood that spilled into the ground, all the hopes he had crushed and all the dreams he had broken — none of it seemed to matter to him. He was still just as confident as ever, just as indomitable as ever, just as amused and full of dark glee as he had always been. Under his dark gaze, Effie walked the last of the distance between them and stopped in front of the King of Kings, looking at him calmly.

The Dread Warriors watched her. The ordinary soldiers of the Steel Horde watched, as well. Far away on the walls of the city... if Kai had stayed true to his promise, he would not see, at least.

No one that mattered would witness her indignity.

“Ah, what a surprise. If it isn't the Priestess of War herself... welcome to my camp, War Maiden. To what do I owe the pleasure?"

Azarax sounded relaxed, as if he had already known what would happen — as if this outcome was all but inevitable, and the only thing he had not guessed was its timing. Effie inhaled deeply, gathering her courage. It was funny... she had not needed to be brave while walking alone toward the war camp of a murderous Sovereign, even knowing that he could easily kill her if he wished.

Speaking the words she had prepared to say, however, was as difficult as raising a mountain into the air.

She remained silent for a short while, then briefly glanced over her shoulder, at the distant city.

Finally, Effie was able to speak:

"You told me once that you would spare the women and the children if I surrendered to you of my own free will."

Azarax's smile widened a little.

“Did I? I don't really remember... but I must have if you are reminding me, priestess. What of it?"

Effie inhaled once more, forcing the air into her lungs, and lowered her head.

"I..."

Saying the words hurt her more than any physical wound ever had.

"I..."

She grimaced, and then pushed the whole sentence out of her mouth, feeling like each word was a razor that cut her throat and lips.

“I surrender."

Her voice was quiet.

Azarax studied her for a while, then laughed.

“What? I didn't quite hear it. My soldiers did not hear you, either."

Effie closed her eyes for a moment.

Then, raising her head, she looked at Azarax and said in a loud, clear voice.

"I surrender! The city... surrenders. I ask you to give its citizens three days to bury their dead. After that, my soldiers will lay down their arms, and allow the Steel Horde... the victorious Steel Horde... to enter the city unopposed."

Azarax stared at her for a few moments, his smile slowly turning darker.

Eventually, he spoke in an even tone:

"I guess the old man is done for, then. A pity. I wanted to rip off his head with my own hands... but as long as he dies, that is fine. However..."

His fearsome, suffocating gaze pierced Effie like a blade.

“You don't look like someone who has come to surrender and beg, War Maiden."

For a moment, Effie's expression turned ugly.

Then, she exhaled slowly and composed herself.

Well... he wasn't wrong.

She had come to admit her defeat and surrender herself to the mercy of the victor. It was not a negotiation — she was begging. She was begging him to give the city time to bury the dead, and she was also begging him to keep his promise and spare the women and the children.

Pride was not something that beggars could afford.

Dignity wasn't a privilege afforded to losers, either.

Effie remained motionless for a few moments.

Her hands began to tremble again.

In the end, she looked down, at the wet mud between them...

And slowly lowered herself to her knees. Her hands sank into the cold mud, and a few moments later, her forehead touched it, as well.

"I... surrender."

There she was, kneeling in the mud, having abandoned her pride, her dignity, and all hope.

Seeing her lowering herself before him, Azarax laughed.

“Good. Now that... that is humility. I guess your endless pride was not unbreakable after all, priestess."

He looked over her, at the distant city — at its gate, which was wide open.

Then, he spared a glance to his Dread Warriors.

“I am a man of my word, after all. So, I'll keep the women and the children alive... spare them, though? Well, there will be some of that. They'll survive, at least.”

As he spoke those words, his elite soldiers were already assembling, dark glint shimmering in their eyes, and the camp behind him was boiling with movement.

"However, as for waiting three days... there has already been enough waiting.”

His smile turned into a dark, hungry grin.

“It's time for this damn siege to end. Will you watch with me as your city falls, priestess? I'd appreciate it very much."

With that, Azarax laughed and pointed forward.

“Go, my warriors! Go forth and plunder! Destroy that city... leave no stone unturned!"

--- Chapter 3123 ---

As the Dread Warriors rushed forward like a river of hungry steel, Effie felt the ground tremble. She was still kneeling in the mud with her head lowered, an indescribable bitterness squeezing her heart. A moment later, someone's hand grabbed her by the hair and violently jerked her head upward. In terms of physical might, Effie was stronger than a dozen Saints... but all her strength suddenly felt meaningless under the weight of the iron hand that was pulling her upward.

Grabbed by Azarax, all she could do was grit her teeth and suppress a pained groan.

Suddenly, he was very close.

“You are facing the wrong way, priestess. Come, let us watch your city fall."

He threw her down as two soldiers grabbed her hands, binding them with enchanted shackles. A complicated weave of runes ignited on their steel surface, and she felt her essence draining quickly — soon enough, it would be completely exhausted, leaving her weak and vulnerable.

Too easy to kill.

Only...

Effie knew that Azarax was not going to kill her. Not today, at least.

As more soldiers arrived, carrying a fur-covered seat for their Sovereign, the King of Kings sat down and leaned back with an easy smile. Effie, who was sprawled in the mud at his feet, slowly picked herself up. She looked away, in the direction of the battered city.

The Dread Warriors and other elite legions of the Steel Horde were already halfway to its gates. The ordinary soldiers stayed back, though.

“Tell me, priestess, now that you betrayed your god, what should I call you? Then again, perhaps I'll ordain you as the priestess... of me. Should I establish a temple of my own?"

Azarax was grinning, but his eyes remained cold, peering at her with a dark, murderous hunger.

Effie looked down, avoiding his gaze.

‘Betrayed War God, huh?’

War Maidens gave an oath to never surrender without a fight. If Effie were truly one of them, she would have been breaking the covenant with War God by lowering herself in front of Azarax.

And that was precisely the reason why Azarax was not going to kill her just yet. Because he saw the act of breaking her as proof of being greater than the gods.

Far away, the Dread Warriors were nearing the open city gate.

Everything was...

Everything was going according to plan. Effie sighed quietly and raised a hand, trying to wipe the grime off her face.

“Breaking things is far easier than building them, King Azarax. Building a temple would be no different."

She had not spent these two years idly. Effie had fought myriad battles against the Steel Horde, true, but she was also learning her enemy patiently. The structure of Azarax's army, the customs of his people, the history of how his father had come to power, and how Azarax killed him to claim the throne.

And not only the Steel Horde. She had learned about other realms and other Domains of this ancient time, as well.

Most of all, however, she learned about Azarax.

What motivated him, what moved him. What his virtues were, and what his vices were as well.

And at the end of it all, she had to admit that Azarax... was not that complicated at all.

He was a genius warrior, yes. His Aspect was frighteningly powerful. He was a tyrant with a natural talent for leadership, as well — he was not the kind of enlightened and benevolent leader that people of her time usually imagined when thinking about an ideal ruler, but rather a king fit for his time. Someone who could crush people with his authority and keep them in line with an unshakeable fist until the very thought of defiance and disobedience was eradicated from their minds.

And he was quite charismatic, too.

But beneath it all, his character was a collection of vile and banal cliches, only unique because Azarax took them to an absolute, inhuman extreme.

Azarax was absolutely prideful, egomaniacal, conceited, and sadistic — but most of all, he was entirely overcome by insatiable lust for power. All of his other traits stemmed from this one overwhelming obsession, and everything he did only pursued two goals. It was all either to gain more power or affirm the power he already possessed, lest it weaken and disappear. His cruelty, his greed, his ruthless tyranny — it was all a means of obtaining power. So was his narcissistic self-assurance, since in the world Azarax inhabited, no one could be above him, and no one had a greater claim to power than he.

Naturally, that belief clashed with the existence of the gods, who were above all, above everyone. No matter how deftly Azarax refused to admit, even to himself, that there were those out there greater than him, he was not unaware of reality. The gods were like a thorn in his side.

Of course, he was not entirely unfounded in his confidence, even if it bordered on insanity. After all, Azarax had been Transcendent before becoming Supreme, and before that, he was Ascended, Awakened... Dormant. The path he walked was littered with the corpses of those who had been more powerful than him, and yet ended up dying by his hand.

Those who had survived, meanwhile, had all become his thralls.

Why would the gods be any different?

That was why Azarax was fixated on Effie. She was a conduit for his hatred of the gods, a way of diminishing them that was in his power to conquer.

And that was how she had known that he would not kill her immediately.

There were only two possible outcomes to her surrender. One was that Azarax would viciously beat her until she was on the threshold of death, and then make her his thrall. The other was that she would keep her free of the enthrallment, resorting to mental torture instead — to break her and make her surrender to him fully of her own free will.

Both outcomes were acceptable to Effie, since that was what she had planned for. Unless something completely unexpected happened, there was no way for her to lose... at this stage, at least.

She just had to redefine what losing meant. This was the first component of the plan. The second one had come from diligent study of this era, as well.

It had to do with what victory meant for the triumphant army.

--- Chapter 3124 ---

What did victory mean?

To Effie, victory had always meant getting to live another day — it meant staying alive and not having to starve. Later, that also included her family, and all of humanity as well.

But these were ancient times, and there was no Nightmare Spell here. There were no Nightmares, and no Dream Realm slowly devouring the world. So what were these people fighting for?

There were numerous reasons for war, but at its most fundamental level, wars were fought over resources. That was what Morgan had said, and she would know best.

In the case of Azarax and his Steel Horde, the purpose of war was rather simple. They were here to conquer land and plunder its riches. The land itself was a resource... the people that populated it were as well, meant to be sold as slaves. Their possessions, meanwhile — gold, fabrics, artworks, and various items of luxury — would change hands and become the property of the conquerors.

That was how militant empires, and their most privileged class — the soldiers — thrived.

Azarax knew it as well, and he also knew that his empire was only as strong as its army. As the commander of the Steel Horde, he would get the largest share of the spoils, but if he wanted his soldiers to stay content and loyal, he had to share his prize.

So, for the Steel Horde, victory meant plunder.

After an adversary stronghold fell, the soldiers were given time — usually a few days — to freely take whatever they wanted. These days were often the most harrowing and heartbreaking for the defeated people, and at the end of it, the soldiers of the Steel Horde were satiated and enriched.

Even if there was no legal text postulating the rules of plunder, it was a silent law. It was a quiet agreement between Azarax and his soldiers, and he would not break it easily — or at all.

There was a process to the slaughter, as well. Not all of the soldiers would get to share in the spoils of the war equally.

The elite forces, such as the Dread Warriors, would be allowed to enter the fallen city and take their pick first. Some time later, less prestigious legions would follow, taking whatever was left. And finally, the dregs of the Steel Horde would be sent forward, hoping to find something that their betters had missed.

By the end of it all, the city would be utterly ravaged, its population slaughtered, those who survived victimized and enslaved. The larger haul would be presented to Azarax, who would take his share and distribute the rest as rewards to his champions.

It was a barbaric, but highly efficient and motivating system...

And now, Effie was forced to watch that efficiency at work.
