“How does it feel, watching everything you cherish become dust?"

Azarax's voice was not malicious or mocking, just... curious.

He chuckled, then let out a sigh.

"I am asking because I don't know."

His words were ambiguous, making Effie wonder if he meant that he had never been defeated, and therefore never had to experience something like this, or if he meant that he had never cherished anything, and was unfamiliar with the feeling of loss as a result.

In any case, he was being too presumptuous.

Turning her head, Effie glanced up at the King of Kings for a few seconds. Eventually, she said evenly:

"I think you have the wrong idea about me."

Azarax raised an eyebrow.

"Do I?"

She hesitated, then nodded.

"Have you forgotten how I ended up here? I'm a mercenary. I was paid to defend this city, so I did. The things I cherish are not here."

Azarax stared at her for a bit, his smile turning a little sinister.

"Really. Well... let's put that to the test."

In the distance, the Dread Warriors entered the city gate, with other elites following. No one stopped them. There was no hail of arrows falling from the imposing wall, no devastation of thousands of Awakened Abilities unleashed at the same time. In fact, there was no movement on the wall at all. That was because the soldiers who had defended it retreated. They had only remained at the gate in the early morning to say farewell to their commander — as soon as Effie left, Kai led them toward the inner keep.

Now, the warriors of the Steel Horde were entering the city and spreading through its streets. They rushed past the burned districts, knowing that there was not much plunder there — the areas near the gate had not been affluent, to begin with.

Their true goal was the districts closer to the castle, and the castle itself. That was where true riches were... that was where the noblest people of the fallen city were supposed to be, as well.

Noble slaves were far more valuable, naturally.

If there was one peculiar thing about their advance, it was that the city was too empty — the soldiers of the Steel Horde knew that starvation, lack of water, and the plague had culled the population direly, but they were still surprised to see just how desolate the city looked.

Azarax, however, smiled. His eyes glinted with a vicious glee.

If Effie had to guess, she would say that it was because he felt his Domain expanding. The Mason was still alive, but he could not resist the Will of the King of Kings anymore — so, at Effie's request, he limited his influence to just the castle, surrendering the rest of the city to his foe.

Now that the Dread Warriors were advancing into the city unopposed, Azarax's Will was advancing, as well.

Most of them continued to move toward the castle. Some got distracted after reaching more affluent neighborhoods, breaking into abandoned homes to ransack them. The elites who were not a part of the Dread Warriors did not hope to get their hands on the treasures of the Stone Castle, so they did not even aim for it, making their way to the residential districts where the nobility had lived.

By then, the last of the soldiers of this first, most elite batch of plunderers had already entered the city. There was an ocean of the Steel Horde fighters inside the wall, moving like ants, all drunk on greed and dark desires.

Azarax frowned faintly.

“Isn't it too quiet, priestess? I would have expected to hear wails and begging by now."

Still sitting in the mud, suffering from the early symptoms of essence exhaustion, Effie let out a sigh.

“Yeah... about that..."

As she glanced ahead, her lips twisted into a faint, dark smile.

“You'll hear it soon."

At that moment, a deep, reverberating sound resounded above the killing field. Then, the titanic stone gate of the city suddenly moved...

And closed shut.

--- Chapter 3125 ---

As the gate of the city closed behind the elite forces of the Steel Horde, Azarax raised an eyebrow and glanced at Effie with a hint of cold displeasure in his eyes.

“Pristess... it seems that you weren't entirely honest with me. Or is it that your soldiers are not as obedient as you believed, and decided to disregard your orders?"

He meant her promise that the defenders of the city would lay down their arms and surrender their lives without a fight. Azarax's tone was deceptively calm, but dangerous... however, he did not seem concerned. And why would he be? After all, the greatest obstacle in his path was the walls of the city. Now that his soldiers were inside, the hardest part of the siege was over.

Even if the remaining defenders tried to mount a resistance, they would be easily slaughtered by the elites of the Steel Horde. Plus, he was here as well. Even if Azarax had not joined the Dread Warriors in plundering the city, he could reach them quite rapidly if he wanted to — so, even if something unexpected happened, he would have plenty of time to react.

Or so he believed.

Effie, however, had her own thoughts on the matter.

It was all premeditated. She had known that the Dread Warriors and other elites of the Steel Horde would enter the city first. She had also known that Azarax would not kill her... more than that, she had known that he would not follow his soldiers inside.

That was because Azarax would not be able to resist the temptation of staying with Effie as she watched the city fall. He would find a good vantage point and force her to watch, doing his best to break her spirit... reveling in her dishonor.

His cruelty, too, had been accounted for. Effie had come up with the general form of the plan. Morgan, their tactician, worked out its every detail, including innumerable branching contingencies to account for unexpected variables and make the plan flexible enough to survive colliding with reality. Seishan was the one who had made it all possible, while Kai, Nightwalker, and Jet were meant to play key roles in what was about to happen.

Effie smiled faintly, feeling her fear dissipate.

She knew very well that she might die here... in fact, her eventual death was highly probable. Before that, she was bound to experience things that would make her wish she was dead.

But that was alright, as well. Because the possibility of her eventual death had been accounted for, too. It was one of the variables, and not one of the important ones at that.

Because her own task would be completed whether she lived or not.

"They should be following my orders just fine, Plague of Steel. Ah, but I have to admit — I might have been a little bit dishonest. I am not the most honest person in the world, you see. Let alone in two worlds."

Azarax frowned, scrutinizing her with a displeased expression. Then, he turned to look at the distant city gate.

But it was already too late.

Effie and Morgan had known that it would not take Azarax long to reach the city and scale its walls. So, whatever they were going to visit upon the plunderers had to happen rapidly... it had to happen instantly.

And now, Effie was going to enjoy the show — even if it could be the last thing she would see in her life.

In fact, she had to thank Azarax for choosing such a wonderful vantage point.

‘I hope he appreciates my showmanship, as well...'

Far away, in the city, the Dread Warriors and numerous of the best soldiers of the Steel Horde were busy ransacking the affluent houses or advancing toward the castle.

None of them noticed that the city gate had closed yet — and, of course, none of them had learned that the complicated mechanism which moved the titanic slabs of stone was destroyed immediately after the gate shut close. This time, forever.

The people responsible for activating the mechanism one last time before sabotaging it were volunteers — those without families, slowly dying from the plague. They knew that this would be their last mission, but they also knew that their lives would be used as fuel to cause the Steel Horde great harm.

And since everyone in the city had lost friends and loved ones to the horrors of the siege, they were willing to trade their faltering lives for those of Azarax's best.

As they completed their mission, Kai was far away, standing on a tall bastion of the inner keep's wall. The Stone Castle had been built near the sea, so almost all of the city sprawled before him — countless streets, myriad homes. And dark rivers of the Steel Horde warriors spreading through the tangle of streets like poison.

There were several people behind him — Morgan, Seishan, Nightwalker, and the prince of the city. However, due to the distance, only he could see that the gate had already been closed, and that its mechanism had already been destroyed.

Kai inhaled deeply and then spoke in a low, emotionless tone:

"It's time."

Nightwalker sighed and nodded.

"That's my cue, then. I will go and prepare the Stone Castle for battle."

As he walked away, the prince looked ahead with a pale face, a storm of emotions raging in his eyes. However, he did not say anything — just clenched his fist, enduring the turmoil silently.

Morgan and Seishan were matter-of-factly preparing for battle, their expressions as mundane and business-like as on any other day.

Kai closed his eyes for a moment.

He knew what he was about to do.

He knew what the price of his actions would be, as well.

Just like the prince, his heart was bleeding... even if it was for a different reason.

He was worried about Effie. He was frightened for her.

But he also knew that she was right, and that this was the only way. If they were stronger, smarter, or luckier, there might have been a different path to conquering the Nightmare — but they weren't. They were weak, and in this cursed world, weakness was a sin.

But it was also the fuel that allowed those like them to grow and overcome impossible obstacles.

And so, Kai opened his eyes.

Looking at the dying city sprawled below him, he called upon his Aspect and spoke a single word:

"Burn."

And, responding to his command...

The city was swallowed by flames.

--- Chapter 3126 ---

Effie and her companions had been preparing for this day for a long while — in truth, she realized that the siege could only end in their defeat on the day the great river ran dry, and the Steel Horde entered the city by walking across its riverbed.

There had been more battles after that, and while they managed to repel Azarax and his army time after time, cementing the newly built barricades with blood, it was a losing game.

So, Effie had decided to change the rules. Since then, Seishan had been developing a secret weapon, while Morgan had been developing another. To achieve the goal, she conscripted the help of the Mason King and his family — who were not only the rulers of the city, but also knew all there was to know about stonework, mining, construction, and alchemy as well.

Additionally, she gathered all the sorcerers left in the city, most of whom were either disciples of the Mason King or descendants of his former students.

Their task was both simple and difficult to complete — under her guidance, they had to develop a highly incendiary concoction that blended alchemy and sorcery, produce great quantities of it, and hide it in secretly arranged underground caches throughout the city.

With Morgan's extensive knowledge of history, warfare, and weapons manufacturing, creating a superior analogue of the Greek fire was not a problem. The only problem was to source enough ingredients to produce it in the needed quantity in the harsh realities of a besieged city, with a naval blockade cutting it off from the world.

Still, they managed to achieve their goal in the end. They also created a limited supply of an explosive agent meant to serve as the detonator and delivery vehicle for the sorcerous inferno.

Now, thousands upon thousands of barrels full of highly flammable, unstable liquid were hidden in the tunnels beneath the city. Some were placed in the sewer junctions that had already existed before the siege, while some were placed in the secretly excavated chambers Morgan had created.

A vast runic array connected all the caches, meant to cause the detonators to activate simultaneously.

And so, when Kai ordered the world to burn, that array came alive.

Somewhere in the city, countless items followed his command and caught fire. Among them were the barrels of the flammable liquid and their detonators, as well — and when one of them produced a spark, the heat was transferred to all the rest, causing them all to detonate at the same time.

The result was both immediate and catastrophic.

Throughout the dying city, the earth opened in a deafening roar, spewing towering pillars of fire into the sky. These pillars then turned into swiftly expanding clouds, swallowing the entire expanse of streets between the outer wall and the castle. Fire was literally raining down upon the warriors of the Steel Horde caught in the middle... and it wasn't mundane fire, either.

Instead, it was a burning liquid that stuck to any surface it touched and could not be doused with water. The temperature at which it burned was utterly terrifying, as well, chewing through stone and steel in mere seconds.

There was no need to say what happened when it touched human flesh.

Instantly, the city was swallowed by a harrowing inferno, its vast expanse disappearing into a raging blaze. Countless streets, countless homes... all of it either burned or collapsed into the deep fissures that opened in the ground, the thunderous roar of utter devastation washing over Kai like a requiem.

The screams of the Steel Horde elites caught in the fire, however, were a far sweeter song.

In an instant, all those who had rushed into the city to plunder it were either swallowed or surrounded by flames. The whole city burned, melting and turning to ash like a great funeral pyre for the countless people who had died to defend it — even if there were pockets of safety among the intense flames, the fire was spreading, and they would not remain safe for long.

And if the invaders attempted to escape the inferno by retreating... the gate was already closed, its mechanism destroyed, turning the city into an inescapable trap.

In the face of such vast, callous destruction, the faces of every soldier manning the walls of the Stone Castle turned pale.

But even if they were watching their city being reduced to ash, they felt sorrow and joy in equal measure. Because their enemies were burning with it.

However...

It was not enough.

The Awakened warriors would perish. The Ascended officers might burn to death, as well. But the strongest of them, the Transcendent powerhouses, could potentially find their way out of the inferno. They could stay alive until their Sovereign arrived, at least.

Kai could not allow that to happen.

"I'm going."

His face was grim, the flames reflecting in his eyes.

Leaving Morgan, Seishan, and the pale-faced prince behind, he rose into the air... and then dove into the flames.

‘Slaughter...’

This trap had been set by paying such a high price. An unthinkable price.

So, he had to make sure that it was all worth it... as close to being worth it as he could.

‘I'll slaughter them all.'

The flames roared as they took him in their immolating embrace.

...Far away, across the vast inferno of the burning city and the great expanse of the killing field, Effie smiled as she watched flames rise above the towering wall, and heard the wind carry over screams of chilling agony.

She looked at Azarax, whose expression was contorted in rage.

Effie's faint smile widened a little, turning into a grin.

“Did you say that you were going to destroy my city, Azarax? Look — you failed. You will never be able to destroy it now. It was never yours to destroy."

A mad glint appeared in her eyes.

"I destroyed it. It was I who burned it, not you. All the time you wasted, and for what? To be outdone by a Transcendent mercenary?"

As Azarax's expression turned dark and dangerous, Effie could not help but laugh.

“What do you think the chronicles will say now? Azarax the Mighty, the King of Kings, wasted two years trying his hardest to conquer a peaceful city. But in the end, he could not."

She was still laughing when his fist connected with her head.

Effie was thrown to the ground. The pain was blinding, and she could feel something inside her head cracking as she fell.

But even then...

She still thought that it was pretty funny.

--- Chapter 3127 ---

Effie had been drained of essence, and now, she received a blow from a Supreme. Although Azarax had not meant to kill her, she was still dazed.

Even without her Aspect, Effie was quite hardy — more so than most Saints... unless they were of a Divine Lineage, naturally. However, getting smacked by the King of Kings was not something she could escape unscathed in her powerless state. Her eardrum had ruptured, and she was pretty sure that her skull had cracked.

Lying in the mud and tasting blood on her tongue, some flowing down her face as well, Effie watched flames dance above the wall of the city.

It was a pretty sight.

There were three parts to their plan of conquering the Nightmare. The first one was right in front of her: the most elite warriors of the Steel Horde being burned alive in an inescapable trap. She had sacrificed the city to kill them. All of the city except for the Stone Castle, at least, which now sheltered the remaining population — so their distant screams were like music to her ears.

However, this trap of hers was not good enough in and of itself.

The Dread Warriors would not be able to open the gate, and all ways to ascend the wall from the city had either been destroyed or walled off, with traps waiting for those who did scale it. So, those of them who survived the initial detonation had only one way left to go — toward the last remaining safe area, the castle.

It was Nightwalker's job to defend it. Kai, Morgan, and Seishan, meanwhile, were meant to hunt down the Dread Generals in the immolating inferno, making sure that these powerful Transcendent champions perished in the flame.

But there was no guarantee that they would succeed. The Steel Horde had already sustained calamitous losses, but how many more elites Azarax would lose depended on how soon he intervened personally.

Even with his power and speed, he would not be able to save all of his warriors... but he could save some.

And indeed, as Effie turned her head, she saw Azarax preparing to rush toward the burning city.

And that was where the second part of the plan came into play.

As Azarax took a step forward, there was the sound of hooves, and the soldiers crowding behind him, watching the distant blaze with stunned and frightened expressions, parted like a sea. A horse with foam on its bloodied lips galloped through their mass, and an exhausted rider jumped off its back, landing into the mud near Azarax and Effie.

He was in such a hurry that drops of mud splattered on the King of Kings, which would usually get the messenger killed. At the moment, however, Azarax did not seem in the mood to pay it any attention.

"M—my... my lord!"

The messenger's voice trembled, and his eyes were full of fear.

Azarax scowled.

“What is it?"

The man, still kneeling on the ground, drew a hoarse breath and then spoke in a tone of urgency:

"The... the supply caravan, my lord! It was attacked! So many are dead... the wraith took them!"

The King of Kings' expression changed, and he threw a furious look at Effie.

‘Here it comes.'

She prepared herself, but when his kick arrived, sending her flying like a rag doll, it still hurt like hell. As Effie rolled on the ground, failing to suppress a suffocated groan, she heard Azarax hissing a curse.

Jet was responsible for the second part of the plan. Several days ago, she had secretly left the city and journeyed behind the enemy lines, making her way to the road that the caravans supplying the Steel Horde with equipment and provisions traveled. These caravans arrived daily, with an especially large one coming once a month. These caravans were heavily protected, and the monthly one was especially so. In fact, it was no different from a legion in and of itself, defended by countless Awakened soldiers, Ascended officers, and Transcendent commanders.

Today was the day it was supposed to arrive — and it was not a coincidence that Effie had chosen the same day to act, naturally. The immense size of the Steel Horde was its main advantage, but it was also its weakness. It consumed an unfathomable amount of food and demanded a constant influx of weapons, garments, medicine, and other equipment.

Usually, a part of that burden would be alleviated by scavenging and plundering the conquered lands. However, ever since the Steel Horde had gotten stranded under the walls of the Mason's city, there were no new conquered lands — only the surrounding areas, which had long turned into a desolate wasteland. So, the great army of the King of Kings relied heavily on the supply caravans. Which was why Jet had attacked it at the same time as Effie surrendered herself, facing all its defenders alone.

Her task was not to eradicate the entire guard legion — it was to destroy the supplies. Without them, the Steel Horde would learn what starvation meant, as well... they would feel the same hunger that the people of the besieged city felt. Even if the next caravan could alleviate their hunger somewhat, the supply situation was already unstable because of the unrest in the neglected empire.

These provisions had not appeared out of thin air, either. They were the result of a heavy war tax that the farmers and artisans of the empire paid, often while not having enough to eat themselves. These people had just surrendered their grain and cattle to send off the great caravan... so what would happen if the authorities demanded the same amount of tax to be paid again only weeks later?

Nobody knew.

So, Azarax had a choice now.

A choice Effie had graciously given him.

He could rush toward the city and save as many of his Dread Warriors as he could, or rush toward where the supply caravan had been ambushed and save as many provisions as possible.

Spitting a mouthful of blood, Effie looked up at Azarax from the ground.

The King of Kings... looked blurry.

She was really not feeling well.

Still, she thought she saw his hesitation. Azarax treasured the Dread Warriors, and especially the Dread Generals — they were the greatest trophies of his conquest, after all, the prideful warriors who had once defied him, but who were now his obedient thralls.

However, he also understood that the Dread Warriors were merely one legion of his vast army. And without the supplies... his grasp on the entire Steel Horde might weaken. After all, what was the worth of a warlord who could not even feed his warriors? Azarax could not allow his soldiers to begin asking themselves that question — he refused to, rather.

And so, gritting his teeth, he turned his back to the burning city and disappeared, rushing in the direction of the ambushed caravan. Effie was finally able to draw air into her damaged lungs, drawing a hoarse breath.

‘Good... that's for the best. It's up to you now, Kai...’

--- Chapter 3128 ---

The dying city that had resembled hell was now in its final death throes, having truly become one. Fire was everywhere, greedily devouring the collapsing buildings. Thick smoke enveloped everything around, plunging the burning streets into an acrid darkness.

Most of the city had been built from stone, but the blaze consuming it was not of mundane nature. The liquid fire Morgan had developed with the help of the local sorcerers burned hot enough to melt stone, and it fed on it too. The flames swallowed one building after another, turning the corpses of those who had fallen to the plague into ash.

The flames were devouring the living, as well.

Everywhere in the burning city, the soldiers of the Steel Horde were screaming in harrowing agony, thrashing as their flesh was melting off their bones. Neither steel armor nor Awakened powers could protect them, and their tortured, terrified voices fused into a hellish litany.

But not all of them were burning... yet.

No matter how many barrels of the Stone Fire Morgan and her subordinates had created, it was not enough to cover every centimeter of the vast city. The fire was spreading, but it was not spreading fast enough.

Those who survived the initial explosion had the chance to save themselves, still. Some tried to save themselves by launching an assault on the Stone Castle, which was protected from the blaze both by Morgan's careful arrangements and by the withering Will of the Mason. The rest tried to flee through the city gate, and once they discovered that it had been sealed shut, turned their gazes to the wall.

All paths to the ramparts had been blocked or destroyed in advance, but humans, and especially Awakened, were resourceful. They would find a way to scale the city wall, overcome the traps waiting for them, and some — those of them who survived — would ultimately escape.

The rest might try to seek shelter in the harbor, instead. The Stone Fire burned atop the water, having turned it into a sea of flame, but if one could hold their breath long enough, they might reach salvation after all.

Kai could not allow that to happen. Nightwalker was holding the Stone Castle. Morgan and Seishan were meant to block off the harbor. So, it was his task to make sure that those who retreated to the city wall died — all of them, without exception. He rushed through the fire and smoke like a dark shadow.

The flames could not harm him today — he had earned the right to move through them by bathing in the scorching blood of a dragon. As he traversed the inferno with terrifying speed, he encountered pockets of surviving soldiers among the shadows.

The soldiers died before realizing what kind of monster lunged at them from the billowing flames. Awakened, Ascended... Kai did not pay them enough attention to determine their Rank. All he knew was that they were not the prey he was hunting for — they were not the Dread Generals, who had to die today at all costs.

Jet was somewhere behind enemy lines, destroying the supply lines of the Steel Horde all alone. Kai did not know what Azarax would choose — would he go after the elusive wraith that threatened to starve his army, or would he plunge into the flames devouring his best soldiers — so he had to hurry.

He slaughtered more soldiers on the way to the wall. At first, he killed them with his sword and his arrows. Then, judging it too slow, he assumed his draconic form, emerging from the fiery clouds of black smoke like a terrifying, towering visage of destruction and death.

Wreathed in fire and smoke, his midnight-blue scales looked almost entirely black.

Then, even that seemed like a waste of time. So, he simply commanded the flames to devour the soldiers of the Steel Horde in his place, using his Aspect to make the blaze move.

He felt it then, in the violent embrace of merciless slaughter...

The heartbeat of fire.

The blaze was like a living being — a giant, insatiable beast that longed to devour all of existence, to use all of existence as fuel for its fleeting radiance. It moved, it twisted, it churned... it grew, it withered. It wanted to be, it wanted to shine...

It wanted to burn.

Kai reached the city wall by then, and clashed with those two Dread Generals who had chosen it as their path to salvation. He burned their soldiers first, and then called upon the flames to attack the Transcendent thralls as well.

The champions of the Steel Horde could endure the flame... but they couldn't endure the fierce black dragon that emerged from the billowing sea of black smoke, wreathed in cinders and fire.

The three of them fought in the middle of hell, the dire force of their battle fueling the spreading inferno.

The Dread Generals were strong. They were heroic. They were seasoned and experienced, having survived innumerable campaigns.

But Kai was strong, heroic, and seasoned as well. In fact, he had survived far more horrifying things than these fallen heroes of annihilated kingdoms could ever imagine. So, he fought them fiercely.

He fought them earnestly.

And somewhere in the middle of that...

The Spell whispered in his ear.

It said:

[You have received an Aspect Legacy...]

At that moment, Kai felt something deep and profound take root in his mind — something that was as old as the world, or possibly even predated it. He recognized its form, as well. It was something that he had tried to master himself, but failed to fathom innumerable times.

It was the True Name of Fire.

There were those who were born with a talent for Shaping, and those who were born without it. Kai's case, however, was unique — his Transcendent form gave him a unique resonance with Shaping, making him believe that if he could invoke the Names, the result would be much more destructive than for any other sorcerer.

However, perhaps for that very reason, his mind had not been able to accommodate any Names. It was as if there was a powerful force blocking him from learning them. He did not merely lack the talent for Shaping... he was the opposite of talented, completely inept.

Until now.

Now, the Name of Fire — and a few more — lived in his mind, having fused with his very spirit, making it feel like invoking them was the most natural thing in the world... like it had been his power all along.

They were like songs, making him feel a familiar longing.

And so, Kai invoked it.

He invoked the Song of Fire.

In the next moment, a vast, roaring pillar of radiant silver flame escaped from his maw, swallowing the Dread Generals in an instant.

Enveloped by that beautiful flame, they only survived for a second.

Then, their figures dissolved into the silver radiance, turning to ash.

And then, the ash was annihilated as well. The pillar of silver flame crashed into the city and exploded, turning into a radiant sea of immolating fire, drowning the world in obliterating heat.

Kai was not done, though...

His hunt was only beginning.

No one was going to escape the burning city today.

--- Chapter 3129 ---

In the end, very few of the Dread Warriors had managed to escape the inferno. Most of them perished in the fire, while the rest were either slaughtered by Kai, Morgan, and Seishan or died while trying to storm the Stone Castle.

The castle itself, as well as the survivors of the city sheltered behind its walls, remained safe.

The Dread Generals were all gone, slain in the devastating chaos.

The city was no more.

From the outer wall to the moat of the inner keep, it was now an ashen wasteland. Piles of blackened rubble protruded from the ash like twisted gravestones, and clouds of smoke obscured the sky, making the day as dark as the night.

Years of calamitous siege had not managed to destroy the peaceful city of the Mason King, but the actions of Effie and her companions did.

It was not that great of a loss, though. After everything was over and done, Kai had a brief conversation with the young prince. The prince told him in a distant tone that the city was its people, not its buildings and walls. The people were still alive... some of them were... so the city was alive, as well.

Far away, Azarax had managed to secure the remains of the supply caravan. The army of soldiers tasked with protecting it had been decimated by Jet, their Transcendent commanders slaughtered, and most of the provisions were ruined. Only a small portion was still intact.

Soul Reaper herself had disappeared before Azarax arrived. He did not know how she knew when to flee... perhaps the vast swarms of crows circling the camp of the Steel Horde had warned her. She was known to communicate with them from time to time, after all.

Overall, it had been a devastating day for the King of Kings and his horde.

Needless to say, Azarax was in a foul mood by the time he returned to the vast encampment of the besieging army with the battered remains of the supply caravan. The Dread Warriors and other elite units of the Steel Horde had been wiped out. Most of his thralls were gone. His soldiers were going to starve for a while, and their morale had been dealt a severe blow.

And what had he gained in return?

His gaze landed on the beautiful, prideful woman chained to the post of his personal tent. The priestess of War God... the War Maiden.

That was his prize.

Now that she was covered in mud, bloodied and beaten, she did not look so arrogant anymore. However, he could still see it, there in the depths of her eyes — defiance. An infuriating lack of fear. An absence of submission.

The priestess was still unbroken.

That sight made Azarax's blood boil.

For a moment, he entertained the thought of turning her into a thrall. The idea was certainly alluring. Having a woman like that following his every command, wasn't it a tantalizing prospect? Plus, it would please him a great deal to send her into battle against her former comrades, watch them die by her hand, and see the city she had so desperately defended fall to her own blade. See the War Maiden witnessing her comrades die by her hand and her city fall to her blade, most of all.

But no... there was no sport in that.

Now that Azarax had grown truly powerful — far more powerful than any of the enemies he could allow himself to keep alive — he did not enjoy turning them into thralls that much anymore. The fight was over in an instant, and their resistance was as well. They did not really break, they were simply shattered.

This one, though...

This one, he wanted to break thoroughly. He wanted to see her submit to him of her own free will.

Looking at the priestess, who sat on the lush carpet and stared at him with a lack of emotion, Azarax sighed.

"What was the point of this stunt, priestess?"

Leaning down, he grabbed her chin and jerked her head upward.

“You managed to kill some of my men, and destroyed one supply caravan. And for what?"

Azarax scoffed, then shook his head.

"The walls of the city have still fallen. The last of your soldiers may have retreated to the old man’s castle, but how long can they hold out? Even without the Dread Warriors, my horde is still vast and unrivaled. Now that my soldiers can enter the city, they will conquer that last stronghold soon. Even before that, your people will probably fall to starvation. They are completely isolated in that castle, after all."

He smiled darkly.

"That is if the old man does not crumble entirely before that. So... nothing has changed. All you achieved is buying your people a bit of time and inconveniencing me slightly. And at what cost? It cost you the only shred of mercy I was willing to afford that pathetic city. Foolish priestess... don't blame me for being merciless now."

The War Maiden stared at him apathetically for a few long moments, and then moved her hands slightly, the chains rattling as she pushed against the shackles.

“What was it for?"

Her voice was weak, making Azarax wonder if he had struck her too forcefully before. She looked at him silently, and then twisted her bloodied lips into a smile.

“It was to kill you."

Her smile widened, and was then erased by his slap.

The priestess toppled, falling back to the ground. More blood flowed down her face, looking almost black in the dim light of the tent.

Azarax exhaled slowly and then looked at her with displeasure.

He remained silent for a while, then shook her head.

“Well, in that case, you failed. You did manage to spite me quite a bit, though, so... prepare to atone for that."

Effie had a feeling that she would not enjoy what was coming next, but she could only steel her heart and prepare.

She had not lied to Azarax, after all.

The first part of the plan was to trap and destroy the elite forces of the Steel Horde inside the city, spearheaded by Kai and Morgan.

The second part of the plan was to ambush the great supply caravan and leave Azarax's warriors stranded without food, achieved by Jet alone.

The third and final part of the plan...

Was to destroy the Steel Horde and kill Azarax.

That one was all up to Effie.

--- Chapter 3130 ---

The next few days were as ghastly as Effie had expected them to be. Azarax was boiling with rage, and he had myriad ways to take it out on her. Of course, he never really lost control — she'd be dead in a moment if he did — and while he wanted her to believe that his mind was overcome by rage, she could see that all his gruesome feats of cruelty were meticulously calculated.

Azarax never truly lost control. Hidden behind his arrogance and outwardly unabashed savagery was a cold, calculating mind. He was always shrewd, knowing exactly how much unrestrained wickedness he could allow himself.

Azarax's true goal was to break Effie's spirit. And to do that, he had wisely decided to break her physically first — the body and the spirit were inseparably connected, after all. But even then, Azarax was careful not to damage her too badly... not to ruin her altogether, since he wanted her to become a thrall after all of it was over and the Steel Horde moved on to its next conquest.

In fact, Effie had a feeling that he wanted her to become his second-in-command. He wanted her to lead the Steel Horde as he conquered the rest of the mortal realms — to become the first of the new Dread Generals, no less.

So, no matter how ghastly his torture was, she could still endure it... somewhat. It was monstrous and gruesome, but not nearly as terrifying as what she had experienced at the hands of the Dreamspawn. Azarax was not starving her, at least — he did not know what her Flaw was, after all — and he was not using her husband to turn the whole ordeal into a morbid nightmare.

In fact, he was not doing anything that would leave a permanent mark on her... after a good healer tended to her wounds, that was. There were plenty of powerful healers in the Steel Horde, sadly, so that allowed Azarax to do quite a lot.

His methods were both simple and effective. There were the utterly mundane forms of abuse and torture, such as beating, cutting, burning, breaking, and drowning. There were more esoteric ones, as well, such as twisting the channels through which soul essence flowed through her body and wreaking havoc in her soul.

The ancients knew far more about the fine art of torturing Awakened than her own people. In that regard, at least, Effie had to give credit where credit was due.

She thought that she was holding up well... at least as well as anyone could be expected to hold up while being tortured and maimed. But, at the same time, she found herself slowly being reduced to a bloodied, scared beast who shivered when it heard the footsteps of its captor.

Effie was still a person, after all. She was not immune to pain, nor was she immune to the fear of pain. So, Azarax's methods, while crude, could not be called ineffective.

Effie still refused to obey him, though. She remained steadfast in her defiant refusal... even if, after a while, he did manage to make her beg for mercy.

On that day, Azarax finally smiled. He was standing there, covered in her blood from head to toe, looking at her with an expression of content and satisfaction.

"There is progress after all, huh, priestess?"

Leaning closer, he studied her pale face and grinned.

“Good! To be honest, I was growing quite bored with this arrangement. Shall we come up with something new, then? There's a crowd of people outside this tent clamoring to get to know you better, priestess. Do help me bolster their morale."

Effie wanted to protest and say that she would actually prefer if he tortured her some more. But even if she didn't want to admit it, these past few days had taught her caution... fear, even. So, she held her tongue.

'Well... he's bored now. Nothing I could do about it, is there?'

Azarax was a very busy man, after all. He had already dedicated a lot of his time to her — a dubious honor, but an honor nonetheless. So, it was no surprise that he wanted to outsource tormenting her to someone else.

His soldiers were starting to feel the lack of provisions by now, and the ghastly fates of their comrades were still fresh in their minds. They also knew that Effie was to blame for all their woes, which probably motivated them to tear her apart a great deal.

For a moment, Effie thought that Azarax had finally decided to kill her. Dying did not seem like such a bad idea, after everything she had to experience as of late... but no, she still wanted to live. She wanted to live desperately. After all, there were people waiting for her to return. Her husband, her son — she couldn't die so easily, at least for their sake.

Plus, she doubted that Azarax would really allow her to die. Why would he do something like that after spending so much effort carefully keeping her alive?

And, in a sense, getting access to his soldiers was beneficial to her. So, she did not mind.

In the end, Effie ended up chained to a post in front of Azarax's tent, this time wearing a collar around her neck. She spent her time sitting in the mud, her back leaning against the post, observing the movements of the soldiers with bleak eyes. The tendons in her feet had been severed, so she couldn't stand up even if she wanted to. Her body was void of essence, making her as weak as a kitten. Well... a Transcendent kitten, at least.

The soldiers of the Steel Horde were free to do whatever they wished with her. However, they mostly stayed away, only glaring at her with hatred from afar.

That was because there were a dozen corpses lying in the mud around her, about as far as the length of the chain allowed her to move.

These were the corpses of the soldiers who had tried to lay their hands on the chained priestess of War, but ended up being killed by her instead.

--- Chapter 3131 ---

At first, Effie had believed that Azarax would order his soldiers to nail her to a cross and install it in front of the camp, in view of the city. That would have been quite ironic, considering his eventual fate. The ancients seemed to love crucifying people, as well — it was their favorite form of execution, by far, at least in this era.

However, in hindsight, that wouldn't be very fun for the warriors of the Steel Horde, since there was little they could do to her on a cross. Having their nemesis nailed to a pair of wooden planks would limit their actions, and she wouldn't be able to offer any resistance either — which was the most amusing part, as far as Azarax was concerned.

So, he had gone with a wooden post and a dog collar instead.

Wounded and shackled as she was, Effie couldn't do much. But when the first batch of soldiers rushed forward to get her, she still managed to kill them.

Did she need to be able to stand to kill these vermin? Did she need her essence? Did she need a weapon?

The answer was no, which the warriors of the Steel Horde learned very soon.

Effie used her legs to topple the warriors, crack their skulls, and break their necks. Those who managed to reach her, after all, learned how sharp her teeth were. One even bled to death as a result, crawling back and clutching his torn throat in horror.

Effie spat in disgust and glanced at the wary observers with a grin.

“Who's next?"

Actually, she would have preferred if the last soldier survived. He was of more use to her alive.

There were some who survived after that, but eventually, the soldiers ceased their attempts to punish her, frightened by the fates of their predecessors.

So, Effie enjoyed a few days of relative peace.

She was not sure how much time had passed since her surrender, having lost track of it during the torture, but the world was still in motion.

Judging by the movements of the Steel Horde, they were preparing for another assault. There had been rain recently, so even the most stubborn fires that still burned in the city would be all but extinguished by now — so, nothing prevented Azarax and his warriors from attacking the Stone Castle.

In fact, there were far fewer soldiers in the encampment than there used to be. That meant that many of them had already scaled the walls of the city and established forward bases there, clearing out the way for the main force to pass through.

Effie did not know if this would be the first major assault on the Stone Castle after the defending forces surrendered the city, or if her friends had been fighting for their lives all this time. She did, however, know that they had not been defeated yet — Azarax would not have missed the chance to throw their bodies to her feet otherwise.

Another mystery that Effie could not solve was what had happened to Jet. Her friend seemed to have escaped Azarax's rage on the day of the ambush, but there had been no news of her since. The soldiers of the horde seemed both hungry and frightened, though, hinting that Jet was still a threat.

In fact, Effie had surmised why they were so wary of Jet by hearing bits and pieces of conversations happening in the encampment. The cause of their fear was not the ambush on the supply caravan itself — rather, they were afraid that the eerie and elusive wraith would continue decimating their supply lines. But most of all, the soldiers were afraid that she would aim her dreadful gaze elsewhere.

They were afraid that Jet would leave the city and journey into the heart of the Steel Empire instead.

Why attack the supply caravans, after all, when she could attack the settlements producing the supplies?

With Azarax locked by the siege and the Dread Generals dead, there were few warriors in the empire who could kill that demon. If she decided to rain terror on its heartland, it was very possible that nobody would be able to prevent her from razing entire cities to the ground.

And while the soldiers of the Steel Horde were safe on the frontline, under Azarax's watchful gaze, their families back home weren't. All of that added to the tense and anxious atmosphere in the vast encampment. Ironically enough, Jet's absence was doing more damage to the morale of Azarax's army than her blade had ever done.

The Stone Castle still stood. The Mason was still clinging to life. Kai and the other members of the cohort were still holding the Steel Horde off, buying Effie time to complete her mission.

Her mission...

Throughout the days of abuse at the hands of Azarax, Effie had not made a good showing of her resilience and indomitable will. It was partially because of how skilled he was at visiting pain upon living things, and partially because she was weakened and drained of essence, stealing her powers away.

But in truth, there was another reason why Effie had ended up in such a pathetic state — and most of her efforts during the torture went into hiding that reason from Azarax. It was that she was being weakened by a far more sinister affliction than essence exhaustion.

Sitting in the mud and chained to a pole, her hands shackled behind her, Effie could feel them trembling uncontrollably. Acting as if nothing was the matter, she looked at her side, where a fresh wound had just scabbed over. A bit of blood was still seeping from the cut, mixing with the grime covering her skin.

Her blood had been turning darker and darker over these past few days. Soon enough, she won't be able to hide her condition anymore...

She would not be able to hide the fact that she was carrying the plague.

Back when Azarax had diverted the river and invaded the city for the first time, Effie realized that they would be defeated eventually. So, she gave Seishan a morbid task — she told her to make the plague stronger instead of learning how to destroy it.

The sorcerers of the Steel Horde had created the plague, so they surely knew how to combat it as well. Effie could not just toss diseased corpses over the wall and hope that the adversary soldiers would be consumed by the same curse that had been unleashed upon the peaceful city.

But she had something that Azarax did not possess... she had Seishan, the descendant of Beast God — the God of Blood. So, she told Seishan to take the plague that the Steel Horde had created and turn it into a much more dire, much more virulent, much more dreadful curse. A curse that Azarax and his sorcerers had no cure for.

After that, Effie and her companions had been patiently waiting for Seishan to nurture the superior strain of the mystical plague within herself. The daughter of Ki Song had almost perished while attempting it, but in the end, she succeeded.

What she created was a profane masterpiece of curses, a mystical pestilence so ghastly and grotesque that even a Supreme would not be able to escape its jaws.

The only obstacle in their path was actually delivering it to Azarax's doorstep. He was not a fool, after all, and he was especially ruthless. So, if they weren't cautious, the King of Kings could detect and destroy their carefully engineered plague before it could really spread among his soldiers.

Luckily, Effie had a perfect delivery system in mind.

It was her own body.

Azarax had a fixation on the War Maiden, after all. She was the only one whom he would not kill immediately and keep close to himself, trying to break her spirit down slowly. Effie herself was the tantalizing lure that Azarax could not resist, and therefore, she was the flawless trap to destroy him.

She had come to the camp of the Steel Horde to surrender, which turned out to be a distraction to lure its elites into a trap. But, in fact, Effie herself was the true trap. Even if she seemed like a human, what she truly was... was a guided warhead carrying a heavy load of a lethal, virulent bioweapon. She was a weapon of mass destruction disguised as a person, engaged in the ghastly act of biological warfare.

And with each day that Effie stayed alive, the plague she had brought with her was spreading wider and wider through the vast encampment of the Steel Horde.

Azarax had been exposed to it the most, since he had spent a lot of time with her alone and came into contact with her blood on countless occasions. The soldiers who had touched her, had been close to her, or survived trying to accost her were next. Everyone whom they had interacted with since were most likely infected by now, as well. All the people the secondary carriers of the plague had talked to must have caught it, too. It must have spread far and wide in the camp of the Steel Horde, claiming innumerable hosts.

The plague was in its incubation period, for now... but it would begin to reveal itself soon. If even Effie, a Saint, was starting to show symptoms, then mundane and Awakened soldiers would follow at any moment now.

Then...

Then, the third part of her plan would finally be complete.

--- Chapter 3132 ---

It began slowly.

Effie was still chained in the mud, with more dead soldiers scattered around her now. Azarax did not seem inclined to remove the corpses, perhaps as a way of making her already morbid existence even more oppressive, perhaps to instill a sense of competition into other warriors of the Steel Horde.

As if seeing their dead comrades would motivate them to try harder and succeed where others had failed. That was a questionable tactic, at best, but considering that a handful of fools inevitably attempted to attack Effie every day, it seemed to be working.

In the meantime, her wounds had healed, somewhat. When they did, Azarax personally arrived to disable her all over again. That was one of the only two times he had bothered to tend to her personally after expelling her from his tent — the second time was immediately after the first major assault on the Stone Castle had failed.

That time, Effie really thought that she would die.

But, in the end, she didn't.

The severity of the beating she received, however, helped mask her worsening condition. She had kept the plague under control for as long as he could, but by now, her body was finally beginning to surrender.

Effie was being consumed by persistent, harrowing pain. It was as if all her organs were devouring themselves. Her blood was turning thick and dark, almost black — luckily, when it dried, it was almost indistinguishable from the mud, and her condition had only worsened after the last visit from the King of Kings. So, no one had noticed the strange detail yet.

The soldiers simply attributed Effie's groans and weakened state to the consequences of the beating she had received from Azarax. It gave more of them the courage to try attacking her in a group... hence the increased number of corpses.

‘How the hell did Seishan endure it for so long...'

Effie had known that the daughter of Ki Song was not to be trifled with from their days on the Forgotten Shore. Still, experiencing the gruesome torment of the plague put things into perspective. Now, she could understand better how Seishan had survived a decade in that harrowing place... longer than any other Sleeper who escaped the Forgotten Shore in the end.

Effie's body... was slowly rotting from the inside. At the moment, her Transcendent physique was struggling to heal it faster than the plague was destroying it, locking her in a vicious cycle. For now, she was able to overcome the terrifying rate of virulent decay — but soon enough, the situation could change.

By the time gruesome sores opened on her body and blood began to seep from her pores, even a blind man would know that something was wrong with the captured War Maiden.

Effie knew that Azarax would know the truth far sooner, though.

That was because while she was still able to hide the symptoms, the soldiers of the Steel Horde could not.

Seishan had engineered her plague to have a long incubation period, so that it could spread wider before being detected. Now, that period was coming to an end.

Azarax himself would have been the first of the infected, but he probably had not felt the changes happening deep within his body yet. He was a Supreme, after all, and an especially powerful one at that. His body possessed an almost inexhaustible amount of vitality. So, even if he had been infected by the plague earlier, it would take longer for it to conquer him.

His soldiers, however, were much weaker. In fact, they were weaker now than ever, because many of them were subsisting on pitiful rations. Hunger, exhaustion, and the burdens of a long siege had made them look gaunt and diminished, which allowed the plague to remain hidden longer.

Its first symptoms were easy to miss, after all. The overall fatigue, the hand tremors... all of it was easy to attribute to exhaustion and starvation. Only Effie knew that there was a different, far more alarming reason why many of the soldiers around the camp seemed like they were on the verge of collapsing as of late.

Observing how widely the plague had already spread, she could not help but feel both horrified and full of dark, merciless joy.

She wondered if the people of the First Generation had felt the same eerie confusion when the Nightmare Spell descended into the world. It had been all but ignored for a long while, and by the time humanity began to pay attention, there was already no time to react.

The same happened with the plague Effie had brought to the encampment of the Steel Horde.

Some of the soldiers looked tired at first. But who wouldn't be, when they had to lay siege to an impregnable castle on an empty stomach?

Their hands were shaking. But whose wouldn't, when countless soldiers had already perished in this grueling campaign, and many more would die before it was over?

It was only when one of them bent over and vomited a torrent of viscous, black blood that the officers of the Steel Horde finally realized that something was wrong.

Sadly, Effie had not witnessed that incident, but she quickly learned of it from the frightened whispers of the soldiers.

Even then, though...

The Steel Horde was slow to react.

The plague had originated from its sorcerers, after all. So, when one soldier was discovered to be a carrier, Azarax wasn't too alarmed.

He might have expected it, even, considering that his soldiers were fighting inside the infected city now. Perhaps the inferno Effie and her cohort had unleashed did not destroy all pockets of the plague — so, he simply ordered his sorcerers to begin administering the cure.

It was only in the process of searching for all the infected soldiers that the healers of the Steel Horde began to feel alarmed. There were simply too many people showing the symptoms of the plague — and while it had not progressed to truly harrowing stages yet, it wasn't in its early days either.

That went against the notion that these first cases were the result of random soldiers being infected while traversing the burned city. So, the healers and the sorcerers began to treat them with uneasy hearts.

--- Chapter 3133 ---

A few more days passed just like that. The atmosphere in the encampment of the Steel Horde was turning more and more tense. It was as if dark clouds were gathering above it. The supply situation was growing more dire as the old provisions were consumed, while the new ones never arrived.

There were rumors that the War Maiden's wraith continued to attack the smaller supply caravans, but Effie had no way of knowing if Jet was truly continuing her sabotage campaign or if the soldiers were simply frightened and telling tall tales. Azarax was steadily preparing to launch another assault on the Stone Castle — this one, he meant to make the final one.

He was unhappy with the supply shortage as well, and, feeling the plummeting mood of the soldiers, knew that the best way to turn the situation around and keep his fearsome reputation as spotless as possible was to end the siege sooner rather than later.

The Mason had to be taking his last breaths by now... if Azarax truly pushed an assault, the Stone Castle could very well fall quickly. Consumed by pain and drowning in her own blood, chained in the mud in front of the King of King’s tent, Effie could feel the Steel Horde stirring like a hungry beast.

Now that the soldiers knew that they could taste victory soon, their compromised morale soared once more. Even if there was not a lot left to plunder in the burned city, simply leaving this cursed place was a blessed reward.

However... that last fateful assault was not destined to happen. Not in the way Azarax imagined, at least.

Because by the time Azarax was ready to lead his warriors into battle once more, the sorcerers finally realized that the cure they had developed to heal their own plague was not working.

That was when Effie saw the camp of the Steel Horde really descend into panic. Perhaps at any other time, the warriors of the conquering horde would have endured the harrowing fear of the plague. But now, after months of a bitter siege, having suffered incalculable casualties, with the elite core of the entire army having been completely wiped out only weeks earlier, hungry, and with the rumors of an eerie wraith haunting the empire...

Even those soldiers who were not infected by the plague — the majority of them — could not help but feel suffocated by fear and anxiety.

Effie laughed as she watched them squirm. Well, she tried to, at least, before bending over in a fit of wet coughing.

‘Serves you right, bastards... die here, under the walls of the city you wanted to destroy. Let your bones nourish the land you turned into a desert...’

Naturally, her hatred might have been misplaced. After all, these soldiers were mundane people. She doubted that when Azarax the Mighty ordered them to be conscripted into the Steel Horde, they could have said no... in fact, many of them, possibly even most of them, hailed from the lands the King of Kings had conquered in the past.

Having been conquered, they had no choice but to become cogs in the insatiable machine of the militant empire. Choice was not a luxury afforded to those who had been subjugated.

But this was the ancient past. Morality was different and far more primal here... so, Effie did not care about the difficult lives of these people. They were the conquering horde that had come to plunder and burn a peaceful city, so as far as she was concerned, they could all go to hell.

She only hoped that they would die sooner than she did.

That, however... could very well prove impossible.

Azarax and the remaining generals were not going to allow the Steel Horde to descend into a panic, after all. If the soldiers were terrified of the plague, they just needed to be reminded that their king was far more frightening.

It did not take Azarax a long time to restore discipline. After a round of vicious punishments and public executions, as well as a timely delivered, fearsome speech, order was restored — a semblance of it, at least. Indeed, the wrathful below of a Supreme was more frightening than a mystical plague.

And why wouldn't it be? If Azarax wanted to, he could wipe out every soldier of his army far faster than any plague could.

After he reminded his soldiers who they served, though, their fear had no choice but to turn into anger, and that anger had to be directed at someone.

So, while Azarax was busy conversing with his sorcerers to understand why the plague he had created was suddenly killing his own soldiers, the rank and file of the Steel Horde found a perfect target to pour their fear and anger on...

Naturally, it was Effie.

The witch who had brought the plague to their camp.

At that moment, no one had proof that it had indeed been her doing. However, an angry mob did not need proof to make someone its target... ironically enough, the warriors of the Steel Horde had stumbled onto truth in their blind search for a scapegoat.

Effie moved slowly as she saw a large crowd surrounding the circle of mud that had become her home in these past few... however long it had been. The soldiers were glaring at her with murderous hatred, murmuring something in perilous voices, their hands resting on the hilts of their swords. They were staying outside the range her chain allowed her to move... for now. But she could see that, today, they were serious about rending her to shreds.

When the soldiers tried to attack her before, they had never been that many of them. Usually, there was a handful... a dozen at most. That had already been the limit of what she could handle in her weakened state.

Now, though, there were hundreds of them. And their expressions were far darker and full of far greater malice than before.

Effie inhaled deeply.

‘Oops... it seems I'm in trouble.'

--- Chapter 3134 ---

Effie sighed and then pushed herself off the ground, where she had been lying in a fetal position. Her entire body was a sea of torment, and as she moved, a few of the sores hidden under the layer of mud broke, black blood seeping from them.

Leaning on the wooden post tiredly, she stretched her legs and stared at the crowd of soldiers expressionlessly.

‘They are really here to kill me, huh?’

But she wasn't ready to die yet. Despite everything, she still wanted to live... she wanted to live desperately, possibly more than even before.

Effie remained motionless for a few seconds, watching the soldiers working up the courage to lunge at her, and then smiled.

"What, are you waiting for an invitation?"

Her voice was creaky and weak, but they still heard her. Their eyes ignited with murderous fury.

But Effie only laughed.

“Bastards... you don't seem to understand the situation."

She leaned sideways and spat a mouthful of black blood into the mud.

“See that? That means that I am infected by the plague. I'll kill some of you... many of you... before the lucky ones manage to land a blow. But guess what? Even those who get lucky won't live long enough to enjoy their fortune, because they'll be infected by the plague, as well. Crowding around a carrier of a virulent disease is not the brightest idea, don't you think?"

The soldiers paled. Those who stood in the front row tried to step back, but failed, pushed forward by those behind them instead.

Looking at their struggles, Effie grinned.

“But that is not even your real problem. Do you want to know what your real problem is, fools?"

She fell silent for a few seconds, breathing laboriously, then offered in a hoarse voice:

“There must be three hundred of you in that crowd, at least. You morons. How many of the three hundred of you are already infected, do you think? How many will be infected by the time you are done dealing with me? Catching the plague from me is not even the real danger. Who you should really be afraid of... is the person standing next to you..."

That made the warriors of the Steel Horde shudder. Before, they had been looking at her with murderous malice... but now, they were suddenly looking at the soldiers around them, distrust and deep, dreadful fear written on their faces. Effie could not help but chuckle.

That was what she wanted to see... that was what she was aiming for even above the deaths caused by the plague. Mutual distrust, fear, doubt, hesitation — this was the true pestilence that could destroy the Steel Horde.

After all, if Azarax's soldiers feared their fellow warriors more than they feared the adversary, how could they ever win a war? This was the rot that had to consume the Steel Horde from within.

That was why Effie smiled even as awful pain consumed her insides.

‘That's right. Look at each other. See? That one doesn't look so good. Why is he so pale? The one behind him is suspicious, as well. Is that dirt on his clothes, or blood? And the one staring at him from afar, doesn't he seem too gaunt all of a sudden?'

Her smile widened.

She was still smiling when a javelin shot from the crowd, ripping through the air at astonishing speed.

‘Uh-oh...’

At that moment, Effie realized that she might have committed a tactical error. She had missed the fact that scaring the soldiers by saying that those who approached her could become infected... might give them the bright idea of killing from a distance.

It seems these idiots were not as idiotic as she had assumed.

Effie's hands were shackled behind her back, and she couldn't really stand up because her tendons had been cut. She dealt with the previous attacks by using her legs and teeth, but dodging a javelin was a problem — especially because the person who had thrown it was obviously an Awakened, or possibly even a Master...

Or possibly even a Saint. There were plenty of them left in the Steel Horde, and while most weren't as powerful as the Dread Generals had been, that didn't mean that they were foolish or incompetent. Azarax wanted to keep Effie alive, but these officers might have had other ideas.

If someone here wasn't blinded by the same kind of unhinged lust for power as Azarax, they would see her clearly for what she was... a threat.

They wouldn't dare to kill her openly, but a large crown of angry and scared soldiers was a great cover for a bit of murder... as well as a perfect tool for it, if the unseen assailant used their cards right.

It would be quite difficult for Effie to dodge the javelin...

She still tried, though, awkwardly pushing her aching body to the side.

The javelin failed to deal her a deadly wound, but she had not been quick enough, either — it left a jagged wound on her side, dark blood soaking the dirty rags her red garments had turned into.

‘Argh...'

More pain... honestly, she couldn't even be bothered to register this source of it, by now.

The worst part was that whoever had thrown the javelin was not done yet — and their actions might have given the rest of the soldiers an idea.

Effie had successfully infected them with doubt and fear, but while the warriors of the Steel Horde were indecisive and fearful, they realized that they could allow themselves to feel these emotions after killing their source.

She could practically see the gears turning in their heads, their wary gazes turning more and more perilous.

An angry crowd was a scary thing.

‘If only I had my essence.'

Chained and surrounded by hundreds of angry men, all of them thirsting for her blood, Effie glanced at the warriors of the Steel Horde tiredly.

If she had essence, she could have snapped her chains and ripped off her collar. She could have called upon her powers and decimated these cowards. Hell, she could have assumed her Transcendent form and squished them like bugs under her feet. Sure, her insides were being consumed by the rotting plague, and she was alone... but she still could have killed them all and avenged herself on the Steel Horde.

But, well.

Dreams didn't always come true.

More often than not, only nightmares did.

--- Chapter 3135 ---

Effie sighed deeply, waiting for the brief moment of stillness to end. Once it did, she would probably turn into a pincushion... surviving that would be a challenge.

She could almost see when the hesitation in the eyes of the soldiers was replaced by malice and willingness to act. Even their fear of the plague was drowned out by bloodlust at that moment.

But just before the soldiers could snap, a low voice reverberated above the crowd:

"Who the hell gave you mongrels the audacity to block the entrance to my tent?"

And almost immediately, that bloodlust was replaced by terror.

The crowd of soldiers parted, revealing the imposing figure of Azarax, the King of Kings. He wore a dark, perilous expression, and his eyes were seething with barely contained rage.

When he noticed the javelin sticking from the mud near Effie, that scathing gaze turned even more terrifying.

In a voice that sounded almost like a growl, Azarax asked his soldiers:

"Since when do I lead an army of cowards?"

The soldiers had already been tense and wary, and his visible fury made them pale. Seeing this, all Effie could do was suppress a dark smile.

What was Azarax trying to say? That he encouraged them to try and kill her, but only in an honest and aboveboard way? Like attacking a bound and wounded woman with their hands, not ranged weapons.

In all honesty, he was being hypocritical. He had chained her in the middle of the camp precisely because he wanted his soldiers to attempt killing her — or hurting her, at least. However, he had only done that because he didn't really believe that they would be able to. What he wanted was to humiliate and torment his prisoner, grounding her spirit down, not lose his priceless trophy entirely.

But, ironically enough, at that moment, it was the spirits of his soldiers that seemed to crack. The hypocrisy of their tyrannical commander was the last drop that defeated their resolve, turning them from a crowd of seasoned murderers into a crowd of frightened, tired, starving men.

“Disperse! We are taking that damn castle today, so prepare to march!"

As Azarax bellowed, the soldiers glanced at each other, hesitated for a moment, and then followed his command.

That brief moment of hesitation, however, would have never happened before. He noticed it, as well, his face darkening even further.

As the soldiers dispersed, he made his way toward Effie and silently jerked her upright. The radiant priestess of War was gone at that moment. Instead of her, a gaunt woman covered in dirt and dried blood was in front of him, her hair like a dirty rag, her face pale and sunken.

Her eyes, however, were still the same, even if they were clouded by pain.

Azarax snarled, then snapped her shackles with his bare hands and dragged her toward his tent.

“Unsightly... pathetic. At this rate, they will really kill you, priestess. We can't have that, though... no, that wouldn't be fun at all. Everything will be over too soon..."

Inside the tent, he threw her roughly to the floor and took off a leather cord from his belt, tying her hands tightly. Effie thought that a piece of leather was much better than enchanted shackles, but her joy was short-lived — a moment later, the cord moved like a living being and tightened around her wrist, betraying its mystical nature.

At least her hands were bound in front of her, this time.

Azarax studied her for a few moments, then snarled.

"Stay still if you want to live. I'll deal with you later."

With that, he stormed off from the tent. Effie was left alone.

And once she was left alone, resting on the lush carpet instead of cold mud, she finally had time to realize it...

That today, one way or another, it would all be over.

The siege might not end just yet. The fight her friends were fighting could continue for a while... but the ending of the Nightmare was going to be decided before the night fell.

And her part in all this would most likely be over, too.

When Azarax promised to deal with her later, he had not sounded too menacing... as far as a sadist whose hobby as of late had been torturing her could sound that way. However, it was only because he still failed to realize the magnitude of what she had done.

By the time he returned to the camp, numerous things would change.

Kai and the rest of her cohort only had to push a little bit more to make the defeat of the Steel Horde inevitable. Hopefully, they knew that as well. The Stone Castle had to withstand the assault — that way, the morale of the Steel Horde would be completely broken.

It would be even better if news of Jet attacking another convoy arrived at the same time. Hunger was quite a frightening thing as well, after all.

Hunger, disease, death, and war... the Steel Horde would soon learn to fear all four. Then, Azarax would not be able to deny the fact that salvaging the situation had become all but impossible.

He would soon find out that he was being consumed by the plague, as well. It would probably not kill him, but it would make killing him far easier. And when he realized all that... his anger would only have one way to escape. He could only vent it on Effie.

Lying on the opulent carpet covering the floor of his tent — plundered from some fallen palace, no doubt — she smiled weakly.

It would be quite ironic if he had saved her from a lynch mob, only to kill her with his own two hands on the same day.

There was a silver lining to all of it, though.

‘He'll only kill me if he completely loses control.'

And if he lost control, it would mean that his days were truly and utterly numbered. So, Effie's quiet smile turned into a grin.

‘Come back sooner, Azarax... come back quick. I am bored with this arrangement, as well...'

--- Chapter 3136 ---

Lying there without motion, Effie extended her senses inward and explored her body.

The mystical cord bound her hands tightly, and she felt like she wouldn't be able to rend it even if her strength returned. However, it was not enchanted to drain her, so her essence was trickling back little by little.

She was still in the negative, suffering from the symptoms of essence exhaustion, but that would change soon. Then, she would be able to use her Aspect again. Much more importantly, even before that, her flesh would be infused with essence once more, becoming stronger and more resilient.

That meant that she would be able to resist the plague better. That also meant that she would be able to recover from the wounds Azarax had dealt her, both internal and external, faster.

Effie's goal was to be able to stand by the time the Steel Horde returned from its assault on the Stone Castle. Then, even if she died, she would not have to die on her knees, at least.

Something so simple seemed like an insurmountable challenge now.

She sighed and concentrated on guiding her essence.

Time flowed, permeated by pain and anticipation.

After a while, drifting in the haze of half-consciousness, Effie heard screams and chilling wails rising like a wave from somewhere in the camp. She wondered what was happening, but couldn't quite bring herself to care.

Some time later, she thought she heard an echo of a distant, deafening roar penetrating the walls of the tent. She also heard the sounds of powerful explosions, and could smell a hint of smoke.

The air tasted like ash.

She didn't know the source of that smell, either.

Then, she was suddenly terribly cold.

By then, she still didn't have enough essence to summon even a single Memory. Her body was greedily drinking her essence, absorbing more and more of it — it was still far from being saturated, though. On the bright side, as a result, her wounds were healing faster.

Effie concentrated on controlling the flow of her essence, guiding it through the mangled channels permeating her body to the areas she wanted to be mended first. The essence veins themselves were being healed and straightened at the same time, too.

‘A little bit more... just a little bit more...’

She was still healing by the time the dim twilight of dusk swallowed the world, and Azarax entered the tent, smelling of blood and ash.

As he did, Effie caught a glimpse of the battered, shell-shocked soldiers. She heard a bit of their conversations, as well.

She had to suppress a laugh.

‘So that's why...’

Kai had indeed realized the importance of today's assault. Under his lead, the defenders of the Stone Castle — Nightwalker, Morgan, Seishan, and the rest of them — showed the Steel Horde hell.

Even better, Jet had not missed the chance to act. She was probably observing the situation with the help of her crow Echo, after all... only, this time, she did not choose to attack a supply caravan.

She wasn't somewhere far away, terrorizing the Steel Empire, either.

Instead, once Azarax and his warriors engaged the defenders of the castle inside the city, she infiltrated the encampment of the Steel Horde and attacked its supply stores directly, destroying what little provisions there were left.

So, now, the Steel Horde had failed to take the Stone Castle, was without food, and suffering from a swiftly spreading plague on top of that.

Azarax's expression was ugly.

He stared at Effie with a terrifying gaze, then reached down and pulled her roughly to her feet.

She could see it then, in his eyes, hidden behind murderous rage.

Azarax the Mighty, the Plague of Steel, the King of Kings... was rattled for the first time since she met him.

Staring at her furiously, he shook her violently and hissed:

“Was that your plan all along?!"

Powerless in his iron grip, all Effie could do was smile.

“It was a good plan, wasn't it?"

For a moment, there was astonishment in his eyes.

Then, he responded the only way he knew how — by slapping her with ferocious might.

Effie saw stars, her mind buzzing dazedly. However, Azarax was dazed more than she was.

Because, as she reeled from the blow, he was staring at his hand in shock.

His hand, which had struck her so roughly, was trembling.

Black blood was seeping from under his fingernails.

Slowly raising his gaze, Azarax looked at Effie and hissed:

“What did you do? What did you do, witch?!"

Effie felt that a few of her teeth were dislodged, and her tongue was cut by the sharp shards.

Nevertheless, she tried to give him as brilliant a smile as she could muster.

Her answer was simple.

"I killed you."

Azara looked utterly stunned for a moment. Then, something in his eyes unraveled, and he seemed to be completely consumed by fury.

He lowered his trembling hand, unsheathed a long dagger from his belt, and drove it into Effie's abdomen in one swift motion. As dark blood washed over his hand, she doubled over, blinded by pain.

A strange whine escaped from her lips, then gradually grew louder.

It seemed like she was groaning at first, but as Effie raised her head again, it became clear that she was laughing.
