She was laughing out loud, her whole weak, mangled body trembling from laughter. Hearing her laugh seemed to daze Azarax all over again. He froze for a moment, then growled and stabbed her again, and again, and again...

He stabbed her until the sound of her laughter grew quiet.

Finally dropping the priestess to the floor, Azarax turned and staggered out of the tent.

Out there, in front of him, his warriors were returning to the camp, falling to the ground to rest after a strenuous, bitter assault. They looked tired, weak, hungry, sick...

Defeated.

Azarax's face paled.

Behind him, meanwhile...

The bound hands of the priestess moved, rising slowly and wrapping around the hilt of the dagger still protruding from her chest.

She pulled it out of her body slowly and then turned its blade around, bringing its sharp edge to rest against the leather cord that bound her wrists.

--- Chapter 3137 ---

Effie did not feel too good.

But, at least, she was free.

A terrifying plague was devouring her from within, and a river of black blood was flowing from the brutal wounds delivered to her by Azarax. Effie felt like she was at the end of her rope.

But the rope that had bound her hands was now cut, and she managed to escape. Azarax had made a mistake when he left his dagger in her body. At first, Effie entertained the thought of turning its blade against him — the mighty King of Kings was distracted, after all, and had turned his back to her. One strike, and the Nightmare would be over...

Her mind was dim, and her thoughts moved slowly, but even in that foggy state, her sharp survival instinct told her that trying to kill Azarax was a fool's errand. She would never manage to bring him down — not in one strike, and not in her current state. Maybe when the plague had ravaged him more thoroughly, but not now.

So, Effie chose to escape instead.

Using the fact that Azarax was dazed and distracted, she crawled to the back of his palatial tent and used the dagger to cut its fabric.

Outside, the camp of the Steel Horde was like a disturbed anthill. The warriors returning from the city were pale and covered in soot. Those who had remained in camp were either dead or rattled. A whole swath of the encampment was completely destroyed and on fire, flames consuming what little was left of the Steel Horde's provisions.

That had to be Jet's doing.

The soldiers were running around trying to put out the flames, while some simply slumped on the ground in exhaustion. There were many wounded... and many of the wounded looked at their trembling hands in horror, dark blood seeping from beneath their bandages.

The air was thick with smoke and ash.

Effie used the chaos to make her way out of the camp.

In truth, she did not quite remember how she had managed to escape it. She seemed to have killed a few soldiers on the way, since the blade of the dagger she was still clutching in her hand was smeared with blood — red blood, not black, which meant that it wasn't her own.

But even if she had killed a few, the rest did not seem to have noticed her escape. Not immediately, at least... by now, they definitely had. Effie knew it because she was being pursued.

With her mind foggy, she couldn't quite understand where she was. She had found herself in a forest, surrounded by countless dead trees. The ground was barren, and the sun was setting, plunging the world into twilight. Effie leaned on a tree, breathing heavily, pressing one hand against her mangled torso.

But it was like trying to stem the flow of a river with a single stone. Azarax had not been miserly when stabbing her, so she received more wounds than what could be covered with one hand — the blood was still flowing, heavy drops falling into the black soil.

That wasn't ideal, since leaving a blood trail while being pursued seemed like a bad idea. And there was something weird going on, as well...

In the places where Effie's blood fell onto the barren soil, it seemed to bloom. Green grass, vines, and flowers sprouted from the earth, growing with astonishing speed. Even the dead trees nearby seemed to come to life, young buds swelling on their branches.

‘What... the hell is...'

Thoughts churned slowly in her head. She didn't understand what was happening, but was vaguely dismayed by it. A blood trail was already bad enough, and now there was an even more conspicuous trail of thriving greenery left in her wake. The forest was coming back to life wherever she passed, so one only had to follow the vivid green to find her.

And the pursuers, whoever they were, were already catching up. She could hear the sounds of movement in the distance.

Effie doubted that Azarax had chosen to pursue her personally — after all, he would have reached her in mere moments if he had. The King of Kings had to be busy trying to salvage the situation at the moment, reigning in the rattled Steel Horde.

Plus, he must have believed her to be as good as dead — if Effie was honest with herself, she would admit it, too — so the soldiers pursuing her were probably experienced trackers, seasoned veterans, and a Saint or two to make sure she would not escape.

Usually, she would have turned the situation around and made these hunters into her prey, but at the moment, Effie was not even sure that she could survive a few more minutes. Fighting seasoned warriors of the Steel Plague was out of the question.

And she still wanted to live... she was desperately resolved to survive, even if common sense dictated that she was too weak and compromised by the plague to survive her fatal wounds.

Who cared about common sense, anyway? Sense never survived collisions with reality when powerful Awakened were concerned, so Effie decided to ignore the glaring truth of her impending and inevitable death as well.

She groaned and pushed herself away from the tree, dropping the dagger and leaving a bloody handprint on it.

Step, step, another step...

With each one, more blood flowed from her wounds, and she felt a little weaker.

But she still took the next one, and the one after that, and the one after that, stumbling forward as the sounds of the pursuit grew louder behind her.

Something strange was happening to her faltering body, and to her tired soul as well. But Effie ignored it and focused only on what lay ahead, willing herself to keep walking even when all she could feel was the insurmountable imperative to fall and grow still.

Maybe the green saplings bursting from the ground were the result of her burning, overwhelming desire to live.

So, Effie continued to stumble forward, one agonizing step at a time.

Until there was nowhere left to go.

The forest disappeared abruptly, opening into a vast expanse of water. In the crimson glow of the blazing sunset, the water was painted vibrant red, glistening like a placid sea of freshly spilled blood.

Effie froze, a stifled laugh escaping from her lips.

‘...End of the road, I guess.'

She could not walk on water, and with the sounds of the pursuit right behind her, it seemed that her journey was coming to an end.

She still took a few steps forward, reaching the edge of the water, and stepped into it. The waves reached her knees soon, and she stumbled, falling.

‘Doesn't even make sense...’

Why was there a sea in front of her? It was supposed to be in the opposite direction, behind the burned city. Effie couldn't have gone that way, because that was where most of the Steel Horde had been returning from during her escape. So, she fled away from the city.

She pushed herself upright and sat in the cool water, staring numbly as her dark blood mixed with it. A belated realization arrived. This had to be the artificial lake Azarax had created to divert the river. It was quite scenic, considering its purpose.

Effie inhaled deeply and looked up, at the crimson sky.

Behind her, she could hear the sound of heavy boots striking the soil, as well as the sound of countless bowstrings being drawn. Her mind was empty, and somewhere beneath that emptiness, the cold and undeniable knowledge that she was about to die floated in the darkness.

The warriors of the Steel Horde let their arrows loose.

Effie was pretty tired. She was hurting horribly. Cold water washed her burning body, soothing her pain... so, for a moment, she thought that maybe it was alright, to lie down in the cold darkness and rest. Instead, she used what little essence she had regained and activated her Awakened Ability, turning her skin as hard as steel. The arrows bounced off it, some shattering into splinters. A couple managed to sink in, but even then, their tips didn't penetrate too deeply.

‘Penetrate too deeply, huh...’

Suddenly, Effie's lips twisted into a crooked smile.

‘To hell with this.'

Lying down to rest in the soothing cold darkness?

Who had time for that?

Effie had no patience for the peace offered by death. She did not need its solace.

So even while the plague was eating her from the inside and sharp arrows pierced her flesh, she decided to struggle a little more.

She was going to see how many of her pursuers she would be able to kill before they brought her down... no, why consider that? She was going to kill them all, so there was no need to count.

Suddenly, Effie remembered her Second Nightmare. She remembered the Temple of the Chalice, and the children she had trained side by side with, enduring the harsh cruelty of the War Maidens and the subtle insanity of the Kingdom of Hope together... until all of them were gone, and she alone remained.

Still struggling.

That was the path of War God, wasn't it? The eternal struggle of all living things — the struggle to stay alive, to live.

To thrive.

‘Oh, War...'

Effie groaned.

‘...rot forever in your grave, you damn god.’

She tried to push herself to her feet, but there was too little strength left in her body, so she barely managed to move.

She kept trying.

And as she did...

Something inside her seemed to reach critical mass.

Something seemed to have reached completion.

It rose, suffusing her entire being, overflowing like a wellspring.

And then, the Spell whispered into her ear.

[You have received an Aspect Legacy, Blessing of War.]

As Effie gasped, clutching her bleeding abdomen, the Spell continued to speak.

[You have received a fragment of Life's Domain.]

[Your soul has given birth to a lesser domain, Garden of Prosperity.]

[You have become the master of a Soul Garden.]

‘W—what?'

Flowing from beneath Effie's hand, her black blood suddenly grew brighter, gradually turning red.

And she finally felt the change that had been happening to her reaching its culmination.

Even if Effie could not see it at the moment, a profound transformation was happening within her soul. If she were to enter her Soul Sea, she would have witnessed the sea that rested under a clear blue sky, illuminated by the warm radiance of a brilliant sun, seething and roiling.

Then, something vast slowly rose from beneath the undulating waves — it was a great island, with tall mountains rising to the sky and clear rivers running along its plains and valleys. Green saplings sprouted from the rich soil, and the barren island was swiftly covered by forests, meadows, groves, and grasslands. Flowers bloomed, and the branches of the trees bent under the weight of ripening fruit.

The thriving abundance of this elysian island was brimming with exuberant and inexhaustible vitality, and that vitality infused Effie's entire being, clashing with the plague that consumed her in a vicious war.

'What... kind of nonsense is this?'

Effie wanted to laugh, but she couldn't because at that moment, more arrows fell on her, more than a few managing to pierce her skin.

She swayed, feeling more blood flowing down her body.

If only she could stand up... then...

Her essence was almost consumed now, and even if her newly unsealed Aspect Legacy had strengthened her, she would still lose the ability to use her Aspect soon.

Once that happened, those arrows would kill her all the same.

But before Effie could run out of essence, she suddenly felt terribly cold.

An icy mist obscured the shore of the lake, hiding her from the eyes of the archers. Terrified screams resounded from the mist, muffled by its cold embrace.

Effie exhaled slowly and finally allowed herself to fall.

Just before she plunged into the water, though, someone caught her.

She looked up, at the icy blue eyes looking down at her from the darkness.

Effie sighed.

"Big Sister... I feel like crap."

Jet, who was holding her, nodded silently.

“You look like crap."

Effie tried to chuckle and grimaced instead.

“There's a garden... blooming in my soul... a soul garden..."

Jet frowned.

"You appear to be delirious. That's fine, but do try to get a grip. At least until we get out of here."

Cradled in her arms, Effie looked up and grinned.

"Get a grip, huh? What do you want me to grip, exactly?"

Tracing her gaze, Jet scoffed.

"Looks like she's doing alright, after all. Good... now, let's run..."

--- Chapter 3138 ---

Time flowed, its slow and steady current eroding both hope and sorrow in equal measure.

The sky was bright, then dark, then bright again.

Its distant veil was blackened by smoke, then cleansed by the purifying fury of rolling stormclouds.

Inside the destroyed city, only the most stubborn cinders still glowed, hidden deep below the ruins.

Outside the city, a vast encampment of the conquering army rested under the ashen sky, drowned by a suffocating atmosphere of suffering, confusion, and fear.

When there was sun, there was dust. When there was rain, there was mud. The tents were dirty, damp, and battered. The people were covered in grime and soot, their grim eyes slowly turning lifeless.

The soldiers were hungry. Hunger was a nightmare that haunted their waking days, stalking them persistently wherever they went, whatever they did. It sunk its fangs into their flesh, sapping them of strength and tormenting them. It also gnawed on their minds, eroding their willpower. Hunger was not the only nightmare haunting the Steel Horde, either.

A vicious plague was preying on the soldiers, stealing their lives away. It was like an invisible monster that walked among them, unseen and silent, marking its victims and feasting on their flesh. There was no way to ward off the man-eating monster and no way to fight it. Once you were marked, all you could do was die.

The agony of those infected by the plague was gruesome. Their deaths were hideous. Long before they could experience the torment of being eaten alive by the plague, however, most perished to cold steel — the King of Kings had commanded to cull the infected, so countless were executed as soon as they started showing symptoms, their bodies burned in communal pyres.

The stench of burned flesh was inescapable. Even worse than the plague, however, was the fear of the plague. The fear was far more virulent than the disease itself, and often just as deadly. The plague only affected some of the soldiers, but the terror of infection affected all of them. A gnawing paranoia made the warriors of the Steel Horde wary of each other, turning their already bleak reality into an oppressive purgatory of suspicion and mistrust.

And on top of the hunger, the plague, the fear...

Was the mounting pressure of a long and brutal siege.

The Steel Horde had already been bruised and battered by the countless assaults on the stalwart city. Then, the Dread Warriors — the most fearsome legion of the horde — were entirely wiped out. And even now that hunger and disease were ravaging the remaining soldiers, the King of Kings was still throwing them at the walls of the Stone Castle over and over again.

To burn in the flames of the fearsome dragon protecting the ruins of the fallen city.

To drown in the river of severing steel that encircled the castle like a moat.

To vanish forever in the billowing clouds of chilling mist, their very souls devoured by the sinister wraith that haunted the ruins.

To see rivers of blood flowing from every little cut they received, sapping them of life in a matter of moments.

To be torn apart when space itself twisted and rippled around them.

Despite the fury of the King of Kings, his soldiers had failed to take the Stone Castle time after time.

So, now, all they could do was crawl tiredly into their dirty tents, enduring the hunger and shivering from the cold, praying that these shivers were not a symptom of the encroaching plague.

Waiting for the next battle to claim their lives.

The camp of the Steel Horde was consumed by fear, fatigue, and exhaustion. It was grey and silent, permeated by the stench of burning corpses.

At the same time, an entirely different scene was taking place not too far away, across the blackened expanse of the burned city.

A radiant island sprawled under an azure sky. Warm wind caressed the leaves of tall trees, making them sway and rustle. Clear brooks murmured as they flowed toward the gentle sea, permeating the air with a refreshing coolness. Everywhere one could look, the world was vibrant and full of life. The branches brimmed with fruit, the bushes were full of sweet berries.

Flowers bloomed on green meadows, emanating a soothing fragrance...

And among it all, the clear ringing of children laughing could be heard, spreading far and wide.

There were people populating the island. Most of them were either old or very young. They looked gaunt, but color was already returning to their faces. The elderly gathered to talk, rest, and prepare simple meals from the gifts of the island. The children ran around, played, or splashed in the clear brooks.

The island was entirely safe. There were no predators here, and no enemies either. Food was delicious and plentiful, and clean water was abundant.

This was the Garden of Prosperity, and the people it sheltered were the remaining population of the city — all of them except for the warriors who defended the Stone Castle from the faltering Steel Horde. However, the warriors benefited from the gifts of the Soul Garden, as well, since both the fruit and the water could be harvested and carried out into the outer world.

‘Feels weird.'

Sprawled on a soft bed in the Stone Castle, still too weak to fight and recovering from her grievous wounds, Effie stared at the ceiling.

It was a strange thing, to know that there were thousands of people currently residing inside of her — and yet, that was precisely the case.

The Garden of Prosperity — her lesser domain — could be described concisely with just a couple of sentences. It was a physical space residing within her soul. Her Soul Sea had become a miniature mortal realm.

That realm was the size of a large island at the moment, but if she became Supreme, it would most likely expand to the size of a continent.

Additionally, the fragment of the Life Domain she had inherited fused into that land, infusing it with boundless vitality. Effie could visit her Soul Garden and enjoy its gifts. She could also admit people inside or summon them back.

It was a miniature paradise she carried within herself.

--- Chapter 3139 ---

The reality of the situation was not entirely unfamiliar to Effie, since it resembled how her Supreme Memory, the Black Beast Locket, functioned — albeit on a far grander scale. The space within the locket was artificial, but the Soul Garden was entirely real... it just existed inside her soul.

What did it mean for Effie?

In the future, it meant that she would be able to shelter an entire nation inside herself.

‘Would that make me... like, a Great Citadel?’

There would be Bastion, Ravenheart, the Night Garden, NQSC... and Effie?

‘I do have some outstanding Components, if I do say so myself...'

She suppressed a giggle, knowing that it would hurt like hell.

On top of everything, residing in her Soul Garden would be much safer than living anywhere else in the Dream Realm, since no ordinary Nightmare Creature could get in.

‘So, what? One day, some guy would be asked where he's from, and he'll say — oh, I'm from Effie!'

Her expression became strange.

Effie remained silent for a few moments, then shook her head and sent a succulent grape into her mouth.

Alternatively, she would be able to carry an entire army, no different from the Steel Horde, within herself, and deploy it anywhere at a moment's notice.

So, people would scream:

"There, on the horizon! Effie is coming, shut the gates!"

She grimaced.

In any case, that was for the future.

At present, the reality of the Soul Garden served a far clearer purpose. It was basically a cheat in the time of a siege, supplying both the population of the Stone Castle and its defenders with an inexhaustible source of food and water. Even the royal family, which had forgotten the taste of luxury over the long siege, was enjoying abundance once more — and the people were, as well.

To be honest, Effie's plan had already been based on outlasting the Steel Horde. It was just that, initially, she had expected a bitter contest of endurance, with both sides suffering from thirst and starvation. The defenders were supposed to come out victorious in that contest due to possessing a vital advantage — due to the fact that Seishan of Clan Song, the heir of Beast God, was on their side.

In the end, however, it had turned out that the survivors of the fallen city possessed two vital advantages instead of one. They also had Effie and her Soul Garden, which solved all of their remaining problems except for one — the fighting itself.

But even then, a starving soldier could not compare to a soldier who fought on a full stomach. So their advantage shone during the battles for the walls of the Stone Castle, as well.

The strongest elites of the Steel Horde were gone, while Azarax himself was weakened by the plague. Additionally, with the number of his warriors diminishing day after day and the confidence in the King of Kings plummeting, his Domain was growing weaker as well. Even the great Steel Empire behind him was stirring in unrest, his authority over it slowly becoming tenuous.

If Azarax was less prideful, he would have retreated from the walls of the city, returned to his empire, and consolidated his rule. Then, he could return with fresh forces in a few years, finishing what he had started. In fact, that was what most of his remaining generals, who had families and things to lose back home, wanted.

But Azarax was the epitome of a Supreme — an individual so determined and obstinate that the world itself had no choice but to bend to his will. And he was an especially tyrannical one, at that, so his pride was absolute. He refused to admit defeat, or even tolerate a temporary setback that could be perceived as such... so, the Steel Horde remained locked in a bloody siege. Effie had a feeling that it would not last much longer, though.

Soon enough, one of the sides would reach its breaking point. There was a chance that it would be the Mason King and his people... but if Effie had to bet, she would bet against the Steel Horde.

Not that it mattered to her, at the moment, because she was on medical leave.

She might have survived the weeks of torture, the brutal burden of the plague, and being stabbed by an enraged Supreme. But it was not like she had miraculously recovered to full strength. Her body was still a wreck, and even with the Garden of Prosperity blooming in her soul, it was recovering slowly. The damage that had been dealt to it was simply too severe.

So, all there was to do was relax on a soft bed and savor delicious fruit.

The fruit was delicious...

‘But I sort of miss meat.'

She would have to go about getting some animals into her soul once she got out of the Nightmare. Did it sound weird? Probably, but Effie didn't care.

‘Some fish, as well.’

Actually, was there already fish in her Soul Garden? She hadn't explored it that much, so she wasn't sure. She seemed to see bees and other small critters there already, and she thought she had heard birds. Where had they come from? Effie had no idea.

Maybe they had come as a part of Life's Domain, or at least were born from it.

‘Isn't Earth War God's realm, though?’

She was a little confused.

As Effie enjoyed another grape, the door to her spacious chamber opened, and Kai walked in, bringing with him the smell of soot and ash. His face was grim and cold, but when he saw Effie, it was illuminated by a smile.

"You look better already. How do you feel?"

Not long after Kai arrived, Morgan stopped by as well. Seishan brought a deck of cards. Jet appeared, as if attracted by the smell of fruit.

Well, and when that many beautiful women gathered in one place, Nightwalker was bound to show up.

Effie's bed resting session had somehow devolved into a war council. She sighed.

‘Well... it isn't bad.'

Not too long ago, their meetings had been permeated by the suffocating atmosphere of anxiety and grim anticipation. Now, the mood felt almost... light. There were even chuckles and an occasional bout of laughter.

Observing her friends, Effie sighed again and ate another grape.

‘Well, that's food for you.'

The world seemed like a brighter place on a full stomach...

A few days later, a different war council took place across the ruined city, in the camp of the Steel Horde. Only this one was not graced by the sounds of laughter — instead, it was somber and tense, full of unspoken truths and boiling resentment.

That meeting was destined to decide the outcome of the long siege.

--- Chapter 3140 ---

In the heart of the vast encampment, a grand tent stood, surrounded by an open space. Tall mounds of human skulls, which had once belonged to the enemy soldiers, surrounded it like morbid decorations. Inside, the tent was adorned with horns and antlers of terrifying beasts the King of Kings had slain, and a grave silence suffused the air.

Azarax the Mighty, the Plague of Steel, was seated on an imposing throne cut from rough stone. Below him were the commanders of the numerous legions of the Steel Horde — those who still lived, at least. Dozens of Transcendent champions and a scattering of Ascended stood along the walls of the tent, their expressions grim and reserved.

Usually, there would scarcely be any Ascended invited to the war council, but with so many generals having died in the siege or contracted the plague, those who were below them had to assume command over the battered troops.

The positions closest to the King of Kings, where the seven Dread Generals had usually stood, were conspicuously empty.

In fact, this gathering was different from the previous ones, because there was a wide open space between Azarax and his officers, isolating him like a hollow moat.

That space was there because Azarax, too, was infected by the plague.

The merciless conqueror was still fearsome and mighty, his imposing figure instilling terror in the hearts of his subordinates, but he was also diminished. His posture was crooked, his complexion was deathly pale, and there were traces of black blood left in the corners of his mouth, under his fingernails, and below his nostrils.

In fact, blood continued to seep, filling the tent with the smell of iron.

The Plague of Steel, being consumed by the plague of blood... there was something both frightening and ironically poetic about that, making the gathered commanders feel a hint of sacred fear. It was as if the gods themselves were punishing their king. There were whispers across the camp, in fact, saying that the King of Kings had angered one god in particular — War God, the god of life, as well as of victory and conquest.

That was why a seemingly insignificant city had managed to resist Azarax for so long, and that was why the unstoppable conquest of the Steel Horde had come to a crushing halt.

That was why the soldiers of the horde had been punished by a deadly plague, and so many of them had perished in the jaws of war.

Of course, no one dared to say these things loudly, since doing so would get them killed. However, the fact that people dared to whisper was already telling. Before, the soldiers would have never been bold enough to voice their discontent, knowing to keep it to themselves.

But how could they remain silent now?

The Stone Castle still stood, the King of Kings was stricken by the plague, and more and more of them were dying every day. More than that, those most loyal to Azarax — his thralls — were all dead. The Dread Generals were gone, and their legion was gone with them. Other core forces of the Steel Horde had been wiped out or were severely diminished, as well.

Although their numbers had not been great enough to put a dent in the endless ranks of the Steel Horde, the horde itself was changed in their absence. That was because the Dread Warriors and other elite legions that had perished the day the city burned represented the core of the Steel Empire — the lands Azarax inherited from the father he had killed, and which therefore were his first conquest.

Most of the soldiers that remained hailed from the realms he had conquered later. Some realms had been a part of the Steel Empire for a few generations, while some had been swallowed by it only recently. The greatest champions of the fallen kingdoms had been chosen by the King of Kings, defeated by him in personal combat, and became his thralls... they were all dead now.

But not all talented warriors had been enthralled. Some had been judged too weak to receive the recognition of the King of Kings, while some had been born or risen to prominence after the conquest. Some simply did not strike his fancy due to their background or character.

They were the ones who eventually came to lead the lesser legions of the Steel Horde, and they were the ones who stood today in the great tent, having outlived their supposed betters.

Needless to say, their loyalty to Azarax was not as indomitable as that of the thralls and those elites who hailed from the core of the Steel Empire.

For many, it was simply predicated on the fact that his power was insurmountable, and going against him meant death for them, their families, and their people. Many were loyal due to a sense of honor and the weight of given oaths, but their devotion was not absolute.

And just like everything else about the Steel Horde, that devotion had been slowly eroding under the weight of mounting casualties, the plague, and their king's wrathful folly.

"My king..."

One of the generals spoke, his voice low and full of resigned caution.

“The soldiers are tired. The provisions delivered by the minor caravans are not enough to feed everyone... our people are hungry, and hunger has stolen their strength away. Many have perished to the plague, and more still are dying in battle."

He paused for a moment and threw a brief glance at a tall Transcendent man who stood silently among the generals, leaning on a spear. That man was younger than most people in the tent, with a reserved expression and a calm, heavy gaze. He was one of the strongest warriors left in the Steel Horde, as well as a descendant of a royal family from one of the conquered realms.

While not known for his martial feats, the man was steady and astute, famous among the lesser legions for having the lowest number of casualties among his soldiers. He spoke rarely, but his words were always measured. Therefore, they carried weight. The general sighed and added, turning his gaze back to the bent figure of Azarax.

"This cannot continue, my king. It must not. We must return home and replenish our forces. Most of all, we must find a cure for the plague... the siege cannot continue until we do."

Azarax, who was leaning on the handrest of his throne, threw a dark gaze at him and remained silent for a while. The force of his oppressive presence grew even more unbearable, making the Transcendent generals pale and those who were Ascended struggle to breathe.

Eventually, Azarax spoke in a low, chilling tone:

“Since when do I rule cowards?"

The general pursed his lips, hiding all traces of dismay from his eyes.

Azarax shifted slightly, forcing a sore that had scabbed over to tear and spill blood. His already grim expression turned a shade darker, making the generals shiver.

"Since when do my officers think that they can give me commands?"

He leaned forward a little, looking at the general who had spoken with dark intensity.

“Are you trying to challenge my authority, worm?"

The general flinched and shook his head.

"No! No, my king. It was not a command... it was council."

Azarax grinned and then grimaced, spitting a mouthful of blood. His voice sounded hoarse and menacing when he spoke:

"Council? I see... so you feel qualified to give me council now. I assume others share this coward's opinion?"

The generals glanced at each other, trying to hide their tension. In truth, they did — almost all of them were reluctant to continue the siege. Some were frightened by the plague, some were incensed after seeing their soldiers dying in senseless assaults. Some wanted to return home, where growing unrest threatened their families, status, and lands.

Some merely saw no reason to continue fighting, since the city had already been burned, and there was little left to plunder there even if they won. With only the castle still standing, most of them were not going to see a reward after taking it.

So, they all wanted the same thing. They wanted to convince Azarax to abandon the siege... it was just that none of them dared to speak. The one who had was already a brave enough fool, since their king was not known for patience. He was not known for being merciful to those who defied him, either, so the courageous messenger risked being killed on the spot.

Azarax let out a chuckle.

"Listen to me, wretches. I am Azarax the Mighty, the Plague of Steel, the King of Kings! I have never been defeated, and I have never failed to take what is rightfully mine, either. This city won't be any different. The siege will continue. The blood will continue to flow."

A frightening smile split his dark, pale face apart.

“It will continue to flow until the Stone Castle is taken apart stone by stone, all the people sheltered behind its walls are burned alive, and the Mason King dies by my hand! I will sever his head, fashion it into a cup, and use it to drink wine at the countless feasts to come. Then, people will laugh and say — look! This was a fool who had dared to defy Azarax, the King."

He took a laborious breath.

“This is my will! You... all of you... are nothing but tools I use to carry it out. So think long and think hard about what you say next. What use do I have for tools that fail to serve their purpose?"

An uneasy silence settled among the generals as they glanced at him.

In front of them, the mighty figure of Azarax was just as menacing as ever... but also changed. He sat crookedly on his stone throne, leaning on the handrest. Although his eyes burned with frightening intensity, his face was pale and gaunt. Black blood trickled from his mouth, dampening his beard, and there was a feverish, sickly glint to his skin.

His breathing was ragged.

So many people had died from the plague... but Azarax didn't. He wasn't going to, either. Mere mortals might be devoured by the ghastly disease, but his mighty body would eventually devour it instead. Days would pass, or maybe weeks, and he would return to his former glory. Many of them would be dead by then, or perhaps all of them.

But the King of Kings would persist. He would be alive when their grandchildren grew frail from old age, and when time turned their bones to dust, as well. That was the nature of a demigod — and not just any demigod, at that. Because Azarax was a Supreme who had defeated and slain countless others like him.

How could a creature like that understand them?

How could they persuade him to understand?

Shivering, full of dismay and resentment, the generals glanced at each other.

What could they say? What arguments could they conjure up? What words could they use to make their terrifying king listen?

Eventually, the gazes of many settled on the quiet Saint who stood among them, leaning on a spear. He was known for being insightful, calm under pressure, and using his words wisely, after all. So, they hoped that he would show them the way.

And he did.

The quiet general studied Azarax with a concerned, heavy gaze for a while, as if weighing something in his mind. Then, he seemed to come to a decision and stepped forward. He didn't use words, however.

He used his spear instead.

--- Chapter 3141 ---

A morning came when Effie was called back to the wall.

This time, however, it was not to defend it. Using a crutch, she limped her way across the castle with Jet. The halls and courtyards weren't crowded anymore, at least — the citizens who had found shelter inside were now safely protected in her Soul Garden, enjoying all its gifts. So, she did not have to carefully make her way through the mass of people.

Still, Effie could not help but grumble.

“Ugh... who made this crutch? It's so shoddy. Feels like it is disintegrating a little with each step."

Jet gave her a look.

“Be thankful, fool. Do you think it's easy to make a crutch in a besieged castle? There are no trees around, in case you didn't notice. Plus, people of your height are not exactly common."

She paused for a moment and then added:

"The royals offered to make one from stone, while Morgan had the bright idea of making one from steel. In the end, Nightwalker disassembled a bunch of priceless antique furniture to fashion this thing. In the real world, you could buy a city block with that."

Effie gave her crutch another look.

“A whole city block?"

Jet smiled faintly.

“Well, the world is ending. So real estate prices are suddenly very affordable."

Chuckling, they ascended the wall and pushed their way through the crowd of soldiers standing on the battlements in silence. Everyone was here — even those who had ended their shifts and were supposed to be resting.

All of them were looking across the burned city in a strange, transfixed silence.

The castle stood on elevated ground, so they could see past the city wall from here. As Effie and Jet made their way to where Kai, Morgan, Seishan, and Nightwalker stood, they looked into the distance too. Laughter died on their lips, and they found themselves drawn into the silence.

‘Ah...’

The sun was rising, its rays spilling over the horizon. They illuminated the blackened ruins of the city, the crumbling wall, the terrifying killing field below it... and there, beyond the killing field, in the distance, the vast encampment of the Steel Horde.

At this time, it would usually look like an ocean of shimmering light, with countless fires burning in the dim twilight of the early dawn. However, today, the siege camp was dark and quiet, with only pillars of smoke rising above it here and there.

Mundane people could not see, but Saints like Effie were able to discern more. Kai, meanwhile, saw it all.

Even without his magical eyes, though, she could tell at once glance what had happened.

Effie felt her breath turning slow and haggard. A sudden weakness permeated her body.

The Steel Horde... was gone.

Sometime during the night, the warriors of the King of Kings had abandoned the camp, retreating the way they came. They took what they could with them, but left countless tents and weapons behind. Many of them were dead, after all, and those who survived had a long and arduous march in front of them.

If they truly did retreat, of course.

Effie slowly turned to Morgan, struggling to find words.

In the end, she just asked in a hesitant tone:

“We won't find a big horse statue there, will we?"

Morgan lingered for a moment, then shrugged.

"There's only one way to find out."

The other members of the cohort nodded solemnly.

It took some time to organize a sortie. Only the strongest of the defenders were allowed to go, since the encampment of the Steel Horde was still infested by the plague. Seishan was with them, but it was better to be safe than sorry — so, nobody below the Ascended Rank left the castle.

Effie went, too, hoping that her precious crutch would survive the journey.

They passed the blackened streets of the destroyed city. As they traveled, Effie remembered various scenes from her time here. There was the restaurant she had often gone to, back when the city still had supplies. There, a square where she had once watched children enjoy a puppet show, missing her family. There, a street she had often used to travel from the castle to the wall.

All of it was gone now, turned into ash and cinders.

As they neared the wall, there were more memories. Rushing soldiers, endless battles, the joy of those who survived, the sorrow of those who had outlived their loved ones... countless scars, countless wounds.

The wounds had healed, and the scars had disappeared as well. But the memories remained.

The wall remained as well, even if it was crumbling. Effie felt that the only thing keeping it upright was the will of its builder, the Mason. But the old man was dying now... once he was gone, the wall would probably succumb as well. Then, the city she had come to know would be truly and utterly gone.

Finally, they crossed the killing field.

The last time Effie had walked across it, she had been on her way to surrender to Azarax. That had probably been the darkest day of her tumultuous time in this Nightmare. Only a few weeks had passed, and she was coming back... however, the circumstances were entirely different now.

Soon, Effie and the rest of the scouring force entered the eerily empty camp.

The tents still stood, but the soldiers were gone. Winds blew as they scattered smoke across the desolate expanse of the abandoned camp. Weapons and equipment lay discarded in the dirt, piles of rubbish littering the mud. Here and there, an unbearable stench emanated from the tents.

Lifting the fold of one of them, Effie grimaced and covered her nose. There, a decomposing corpse lay, wrapped in a blanket, bearing the familiar and ghastly signs of having died from the plague.

No one seemed to have bothered with collecting and burning the dead. The retreating soldiers had enough mercy to kill those infected who were still alive, at least, instead of leaving them to the slow and agonizing death from the plague.

It didn't make sense.

Why would the Steel Horde just leave? Had Azarax truly decided to retreat to save his remaining forces? Effie could not quite imagine him admitting defeat. She had always expected to fight one final, decisive battle against him... even if they did not manage to slay the King of Kings himself, they could at least destroy his army, ending the Nightmare that way.

But the Steel Horde was simply gone. There was no sign of Azarax, either. All that remained was silence and desolation, which made Effie feel a sense of eerie, confused unease.

The scouts spread throughout the camp, investigating the mysterious absence of people. Effie wandered it for a while, as well, looking around in confusion. The eerie sense of incongruity grew, but she also felt a powerful, overwhelming sense of relief.

Her enemy was gone, after all. The terrifying army that had been besieging the city for two years had retreated. It was almost unfamiliar not to feel the weight of the Steel Horde pressing down on her... but it was not unwelcome. Quite the opposite.

Finally, they found the answer to the question that had been plaguing their minds ever since they entered the camp. It was hidden in the great tent at the heart of the encampment, where Azarax and his generals used to hold council.

The tent was empty, as well, but the stench of blood was far more powerful here. There were puddles of it on the floor, which had almost, but not quite, dried — as if many people had died here recently.

There were no corpses... except one.

There, on the throne that towered above the vast expanse of the tent, a plague-ridden corpse sat, staring down at the uninvited guests with glassy eyes. Azarax was nearly unrecognizable.

The plague had changed him, somewhat, but it was more so because of the traumatic damage done to his body.

He was impaled through the chest with a spear, pinned to the backrest of the stone throne, with dozens of arrows and javelins striking out of his flesh. Every part of his body that had not been pierced had been hacked and torn apart by sharp blades, as if hundreds upon hundreds of blows descended upon him in quick succession, delivered by scores of hands.

All of him was painted black by the plague-ridden blood, making him look like a ghastly effigy of a human made from tar and mangled flesh.

He must have resisted fiercely after being struck for the first time... it had taken hundreds of blows to bring the fearsome Azarax down, and even then, Effie was not sure how many of his attackers had survived their mutinous ambush.

But in the end, he still died. Azarax the Mighty, the Plague of Steel, the King of Kings... had been weakened by the plague of his own making and slain by his own generals, becoming the greatest and final victim of the Steel Horde.

It was a fitting end for a bloody tyrant like him.

In fact, Effie thought that it was better than he had deserved.

‘I hope you die a thousand deaths, bastard.'

She inhaled deeply, remembering all the pain and humiliation she had endured at his hand.

The years of a bitter siege and all the soldiers she had lost to his ambition, as well. All the civilians who had perished because of him.

Reality was far more cruel than Effie, though.

Instead of dying a thousand deaths, Azarax had been robbed of the right to die, spending thousands of years nailed to a tree in a godforsaken desert before succumbing to the curse of Shadow God.

She used to think that such a fate was a bit too gruesome...

But now, Effie was glad for it. That much torment... was enough to make up for one-tenth of the sorrow he had caused, perhaps.

Looking at the imposing, monstrous corpse that sat on a bloodied throne, she inhaled deeply, and then let out a long sigh.

‘Goodbye, Azarax. You called yourself the King of Kings... but you died like a dog. A fate most fitting.'

Their Nightmare seemed to be coming to an end.

--- Chapter 3142 ---

A few days later, Effie found herself standing on the shore of the sea. In front of her, the people of the fallen city, who had left the safe harbor of her Soul Garden, were busy working. Some were clearing the bay, some were salvaging the wrecked ship that had been pulled from its depths.

Their work was hard, but they seemed cheerful enough. Haunted and unnaturally quiet, yes, but nevertheless full of vitality. And, most of all, undeniably alive.

The gaunt bodies had filled up somewhat, and they did not look like walking corpses anymore. The quiet despair had also disappeared from their eyes, replaced by tranquility... hope, even.

With anticipation of a brighter future.

Effie quite liked the sight.

There was activity boiling throughout the city, as well. However, it did not look like the citizens were trying to clear away the rubble. Instead, they were simply searching for anything that had survived the fire and could be of use.

Soon enough, the other members of the cohort joined her to observe them.

Effie raised an eyebrow.

"Where's the prince?"

The prince had called them out here to discuss something, but now, he was nowhere to be seen.

Kai remained silent for a moment, then sighed.

“His father had taken a turn for the worse. So, the prince is with him."

Effie lingered a bit before nodding. She turned back to the sea.

Despite everything that had happened in the past two years, the sea was clear and beautiful beyond the harbor. It stretched toward the horizon, glistening in the sun, its waves murmuring steadily, like they always did.

She let out a heavy breath.

"Did he mention what their plans are? Are they going to rebuild the city?"

Jet, who had approached quietly, shook her head.

“The prince said that the city — what remains of it — is a place of death and sorrow now. To them, it is a graveyard. So, they are planning to build ships and sail somewhere else... somewhere far from conquest and war, somewhere far away. To start anew."

Looking at the sea, Effie smiled.

"Well, I can't say I blame them. It must feel nice to have somewhere else to go.”

Back in the real world, there was nowhere far away from war. War was everywhere. That didn't mean that humanity couldn't start anew, though.

Turning to her friends and companions, Effie studied them for a few moments.

"I guess this is it, then. We won."

The others nodded in confirmation, even if their expression betrayed a hint of bewilderment.

Nightwalker shook his head.

“It's astonishing, really. I thought at least half of you would die... if any of us survived at all.”

Seishan smiled.

"Unlike you, most of us have no experience dying over and over again, so we thought we'd pass."

Morgan simply shrugged.

"I don't know what you are talking about, either. Look at us. Great Clan Valor, Great Clan Song, Great Clan Night... the best and the brightest of the Forgotten Shore, the most fearsome soldier of the government — if the six of us couldn't conquer the Nightmare, then who could?"

She paused for a moment, then looked to the sea and sighed.

“Although... I feel that this is it. There probably won't be new Supremes for a long, long while after us."

This one Nightmare had already gathered the best of what humanity had to offer. The next generations, if they would get to be born, were not going to experience a world as terrifying as the one the six of them had been raised and tempered by. New champions might rise from among the descendants of humanity eventually, but it would take a long time.

Jet studied them for a moment, then smiled.

"Still. We did well, didn't we?"

Effie could not help but agree. Leaning on her crutch, she grinned.

“I'd say."

With that, they fell into a relaxed, exhausted, peaceful silence.

There was not going to be a lot of peace after they returned to the real world, so they had to enjoy this precious moment as much as they could.

Soon, a strange, imperceptible change rippled through the world. It was as if the weight of the sky had changed, and the scent of the air had become a little colder. As if something old had come to an end, and something new was beginning.

A few moments later, a deafening, roaring crash resounded from the distance. Turning to look across the blackened ruin of the burned city, Effie and her companions saw the impregnable wall they had defended bitterly for two years crumbling into a cloud of dust. It collapsed entirely across its length, pulled down by its own battered weight and erased from existence. They all knew what that meant. Somewhere nearby, within the walls of the Stone Castle, its creator had finally breathed his last breath.

The Mason King had endured long enough to see his people to safety... but now, he was dead.

Effie looked at the beautiful walls of the distant castle, considering.

They had met two Supremes in this Nightmare, which couldn't have been more different from each other. In many senses, the Mason and Azarax were opposites of each other, both representing distinct extremes.

Azarax was powerful and ambitious, proud, and impossible to ignore. An epitome of a tyrant.

The Mason, on the contrary, was quiet and unassuming, so much so that his presence was almost imperceptible at times. He had not been a powerful warrior, but created beauty and prosperity wherever he went.

Effie was not sure which of them would have fared better in the Age of the Nightmare Spell, where abominations and dreadful perils besieged humanity on all sides... but she knew that she wanted to be a Supreme like the Mason. She wanted to inspire and protect her people instead of using them as fuel for her own benefit.

She smiled.

‘Rest well, old man.‘

With that, the beautiful view of the Stone Castle, contrasted sharply against the blackened ruins behind it, suddenly grew vague and indistinct.

Effie inhaled deeply, breathing in the bitter air of this forgotten city for the final time.

Their Nightmare had come to an end.

--- Chapter 3143 ---

Sunny had survived the expedition to the Underworld... and even if it was just barely, he had not returned from the journey empty-handed. The Weave was finally complete, Saint was a Supreme Tyrant now, the shadow of the Prince of Darkness rested in his soul, and a legion of fearsome shades joined the Shadow Legion.

However, the spoils of the expedition were overshadowed by its heavy implications. Sunny and Nephis had always known that they were no match for the fallen gods of the Dream Realm — the Unholy Nightmare Creatures who were its true masters. At least not yet. But facing one in battle, if their brief encounter with the Abyssal Prisoner could even be called that, put just how inadequate they were into perspective. There was only one conclusion — they had even less time to augment their strength than they had thought. That lit a fire under them, forcing them to accelerate their preparations for the Nightmare even further.

The plan had been to wait until Jet, Kai, Effie, and the rest attained Supremacy before departing, so that humanity could persist in their care. Now, however, Sunny and Nephis could not help but consider an earlier, and therefore much more dire, date. There were still many things they had to do before leaving in search of the Fifth Seed. Their plans of finding a place to harvest mystical stone in the Underworld had failed, for example, which meant that an alternative source had to be discovered. The apocalypse had not stopped on account of their busy schedule, either.

Humanity was besieged on all sides. In the Dream Realm, countless Citadels were struggling under an onslaught of abominations, while some had already been lost. The waking world, meanwhile, was slowly descending into a global crisis. All lands controlled by humanity were under threat.

Still... the next few months felt almost peaceful. Knowing that challenging the Fifth Nightmare would mean nearing the end of this terrifying race, Sunny felt like he needed to enjoy these last days of humanity.

Not of mankind, but rather, of the humanity he himself possessed. He was not sure how Apotheosis would change him, after all, but knew that he would not be the same after becoming a deity.

It was a strange thing, to know that he would not be human for much longer.

In truth, it was more than a little scary... almost as scary as death. More so, perhaps, since Sunny had died on several occasions and still remained himself. A transformation so profound that your previous self would seem a stranger felt far more frightening.

Would he still enjoy drinking coffee? Would he be able to become engrossed in a novel? Would he know how to treasure the touch of soft fabric and the refreshing feeling of a warm bath?

...Would he have any kind of human emotions left at all? Would he still experience the joy of spending time with friends, the tender attachment to his sister?

Sunny did not know, and the unknown frightened him.

It terrified him, really.

And yet, there was no other path but the path forward. None of these things would be there much longer if he failed to conquer Apotheosis, anyway... so, there was no point in hesitating.

The apocalypse continued.

Even as Sunny and Nephis frenetically prepared for the Nightmare, alarming news arrived from all corners of the world.

On the Forgotten Shore, the Shadow Legion was pushing back the Barrow Wraith under Saint's command... however, something was stirring in the depths of the Burning Forest, and even the primeval hunters seemed ill at ease now.

In the east, the eerie darkness continued to spread, swallowing more and more land. In the west, calamitous snowstorms were rolling from the frigid wasteland, bringing with them swarms of Nightmare Creatures. In the south, leviathans who had spent thousands of years in the lightless depths were now rising to the surface, as if chased by something.

On Earth, Nightmare Gates were opening almost every day now, and the abominations escaping from them were stronger. The mystical interference caused by the Call was wreaking havoc across all three remaining Quadrants, disrupting industry and infrastructure. More pieces of the waking world were being swallowed by the Dream Realm, allowing Nightmare Creatures to bypass the Gates.

Resettlement wasn't progressing fast enough.

Even with how strong humanity had become — with the Fire Keepers, the Blood Sisters, the River People — it was slowly losing ground.

Sunny knew that he and Nephis had no choice but to challenge the Nightmare. But, at the same time...

He didn't know if anything would be left by the time they returned.

The fact made him feel indignant.

It was already unfair to be born into a world like this one. But to strain against it for so long, achieving one unlikely victory after another, to accomplish so much and come so far... only to end up losing everything, after all?

That left a bitter taste in his mouth.

Just like that, in the blink of an eye — but also an eternity — time passed. The winter solstice was swiftly approaching, which meant that Effie, Kai, Jet, Morgan, Seishan, and Nightwalker had been gone for almost two years now.

The memories they had left behind were still intact, but there was no news of their fate.

Sunny and Nephis had almost steeled themselves for departing without learning what had happened to their friends...

But then, one day, the world shuddered.

It was as if an invisible ripple spread through the fabric of reality, changing it forever.

There was a remote monitoring station left in Antarctica, keeping watch over the three colossal Nightmare Gates towering above the vast battlefield. The signal barely reached the relays, though, so it was not very reliable. In theory, if one of the Gates disappeared, they were meant to learn about it almost immediately...

In practice, however, Sunny and Nephis knew that something had happened because the Longing Domain suddenly and inexplicably weakened.

The six Saints who had challenged the Fourth Nightmare had released control of the Citadels before delving into the Seed, but they were still widely renowned and venerated figures. So, their simultaneous rise to Supremacy had taken a big bite out of Neph's Domain.

At first, she and Sunny assumed that something terrible had happened — an unexpected calamity that had wiped out a great number of people in an instant, maybe, or some other emergency.

They scrambled to react, but before they could even leave the Ivory Tower, Cassie's voice resounded in their heads, informing them of the real reason the world seemed to have shaken.

The truth, for once, was not alarming.

It was astonishingly joyous, instead.

On that day, six of the greatest champions of humanity had conquered the Fourth Nightmare and became Supreme.

The world welcomed new Sovereigns — and this time, their arrival was met with exhilaration instead of bloodshed and fear.

--- Chapter 3144 ---

On a day unlike any other in the history of mankind, the Ivory Island descended from the sky and landed on the misty waters of the Stormsea. It had traveled far from its usual place above the Mirror Lake, moving halfway between Bastion and the rapidly growing city in the delta of the River of Tears.

Silver Web, the city of the River People, was not too far either. So was the Night Garden, moving among the waves like a towering wall on the horizon.

Two smaller ships could be seen, as well, sailing across the sky — they were the Chain Breaker and the Time Slayer, the storied vessels capable of braving the heavens. These ships were bringing exalted guests to the Tower of Hope. Today, the great pagoda was meant to serve as a meeting place for the demigods of humanity, so no mere mortal would find themselves under its roof.

The meeting had taken some time to arrange, but it was happening mere days after the new Sovereigns conquered their Nightmare. They had received time to reunite with their families and explore their new powers, albeit just barely.

Now, the demigods had to make arrangements among themselves, deciding which lands would be ruled by whom, how they would share the burdens of protecting humanity, how they would divide it among themselves so that their authorities did not clash.

How they would stave off the apocalypse until true deities were born from their ranks.

The vast meeting chamber was bathed in light, with a large wooden table occupying most of its great width.

The host of the meeting, the current ruler of humanity, entered first. With her alabaster skin and silver hair, sparks of white flame dancing in her eyes, she looked like a radiant spirit of light — a messenger sent by the heavens down to the mortal world. Her gaze was steadfast and heavy, though, giving her radiance a stark and awe-inspiring edge.

She was Changing Star, Nephis of Immortal Flame.

Next was her companion, a being so fearsome that even his existence was a forbidden secret. An exquisitely beautiful man with porcelain skin, raven-black hair, and eyes that were like onyx jewels rose from her shadow. It was as if a sea of darkness was given form. There was something serpentine about his elegant movements, and the shadows across the chamber grew deeper as he appeared.

He was Sunless, Lost from Light — the Lord of Shadows.

The third to arrive was the dreaded King of Nothing, Mordret of Nowhere. He came out of reflections, gazing upon the world with his strange, mirror-like eyes. The world reflected in them was the perfect copy of itself, and yet eerily different. Wearing an aloof expression, the King of Nothing spared his peers a curt nod in greeting and took a seat in silence.

A petite woman wearing a white tunic and a seawave cloak entered next, her delicate beauty so stunningly breathtaking that it escaped description. Her hair was like a waterfall of pale gold, and her eyes were hidden behind a blindfold. There was an air of solemn mystery about her, and her presence was easily forgotten.

She was Cassia, Song of the Fallen, the blind prophet who had broken fate.

Next came a young woman with tantalizing features, wearing a nebulous black mantle. She had an elegant figure and glistening ebony hair, her skin dusky, her eyes piercing blue. Illuminating the world with a captivating smile, she bowed gracefully to the others and took her seat, greeting them in a melodious voice.

She was Ananke, the Silk Weaver, the sorceress who ruled the River People and the Twilight Sea.

Not long after Ananke took her seat, finally, the new Supremes arrived.

The first to enter was a fetching man who looked younger than the others gathered in the chamber, but was actually older than all of them instead. He had strange, nebulous silver eyes that seemed to gleam with distant starlight, flawless dark skin, and a dashing smile.

When he appeared, a cold breeze seemed to blow from the sea, bringing with it the smell of salt, distant lands, and wanderlust.

He was Nightwalker, the last legend of the First Generation, and the founder of the House of Night. As for a regal title... he had only been Supreme for a few days, so people had not had the chance to come up with one yet.

Following Nightwalker, a woman of exotic and riveting beauty entered, her dress a darkly crimson hue. Her supple skin was grey like stormy clouds, smooth like silk, and devoid of any imperfections. That gave her an exotic and tantalizing, but outwardly inhuman look.

She was poised, reserved, graceful, and exquisite, like the embodiment of nobility and regal elegance. Her inhuman beauty was of the kind that put both longing and fear in a person's heart, and when she entered, everyone who looked at her felt soothed and at ease.

That ease, however, hid a darker side — it was the ease of prey bewitched into lowering its guard by a predator.

She was Seishan, the Lost Princess of Song, the most tenacious daughter of the Queen of Worms.

Following the princess of fallen Song, the princess of fallen Valor arrived. She was a striking woman with dark wavy hair and alabaster skin, her eyes as cold as the sharpest of swords. More arresting than their sharpness, however, was their vibrant color — they were as red as freshly spilled blood, the same as her scarlet lips.

With her pale skin, raven-black hair, and austere elegance, she looked both beautiful and daunting. When she entered, the world was suddenly permeated by a lethal sense of clarity and sharpness... unlike before, however, that sharpness did not radiate outward. Instead, it was reserved and focused inward, making it seem that she could cut the world with one graceful movement of her finger.

She was Morgan of Valor, the Princess of War... although now that she had become Supreme, calling her a queen would likely be more appropriate.

A man so handsome that his beauty could become a deadly weapon entered next, following Morgan closely. With auburn hair and sparks glinting in his green eyes, he greeted everyone with a radiant smile. Even demigods could not resist the devastating force of that smile — some responded with their own before knowing what they were doing, some looked away with strained expressions.

His presence was light and effervescent, but also carried a hint of melancholy, making every emotion seem more poignant and precious. His voice was pleasant and impossible to ignore, as well, making them want to listen to it forever.

He was Kai, also known as Nightingale — the Dragonslayer.

Soon after his radiant smile seemed to warm the world, a sense of chill permeated the air. A woman of ravishing beauty entered the chamber, her icy blue eyes glowing with cold light in the shadows of the doorway. Her figure was riveting, her flawless skin was smooth and white as snow, and her raven-black hair was cut short.

She carried herself with a relaxed grace, and her subtle presence filled the chamber with the feeling of otherworldly cold. Despite its subtlety, however, she was impossible to look away from.

She was Jet, the Soul Reaper — a woman who was neither dead nor alive, and who inspired fear and reverence in equal measure.

Finally, a tall woman with a stunning, alluring figure entered the chamber. She was tall and athletic, with perfectly defined, lean muscles rolling under her dewy olive skin and an air of infectious vitality about her. Everything about her screamed of strength and vigor, and it was hard not to feel your blood flowing faster in her presence.

That alluring presence filled the air with liveliness and energy, causing a certain primal intensity to permeate her surroundings, infusing them with stimulating, spirited force. Now that she was Supreme, that energy had only become stronger, threatening to feel overwhelming. She was Athena, Raised by Wolves, known by many as War Beast.

Since the others were already seated, Effie looked around with a confused expression, lingered for a few moments, and then asked:

“What? There are no snacks?"

Sunny sighed deeply and covered his face with a palm.

There was not one, not two, not three, but eleven — eleven! — Supremes in the room. More than there had ever been, and for once, they were not at each other's throats. Instead, by some miracle, they had all gathered together to discuss how they were going to coexist peacefully.

Sunny groaned inwardly and mumbled:

“Still, it's too many Sovereigns, damn it..."

Then, he looked at Effie, glared at her for a couple of moments, and said:

“Of course there will be snacks! Who do you take me for?"

--- Chapter 3145 ---

There were a lot of things to discuss, so the meeting was going to take a long time. It could even stretch over several days, considering that Sunny, Nephis, and the other three Supremes who had stayed behind did not even know the details of the Nightmare the rest conquered.

Those who returned were not fully familiar with their new powers, either. A lot of the decisions that needed to be made depended on that knowledge, so Sunny expected to spend some time helping the new Sovereigns make sense of their Supremacy.

‘What a novel idea.’

Sunny and Nephis had to figure out the powers of a Supreme all on their own, relying only on each other in exploring the nuances of the Will and Domain powers. Well, naturally they had — after all, they had ascended to Supremacy by killing their predecessors. So, there had been no one left to teach them.

These new Supremes, however, could enjoy the benefit of having more experienced comrades show them the way. They would have to do a lot of work on their own, naturally, but it was still a starkly different situation.

‘Must be nice.'

Sunny was not bitter at all.

Just as he expected, the meeting ended up consuming several days, and in the process, all of them learned more about what the new demigods could do. Needless to say, their Supreme powers were both extremely potent and, in several cases, exceedingly peculiar.

There was also a lot of confusion because to them, those born in the Age of the Nightmare Spell, the power of a Domain carried an innate duality.

There were two ways a Supreme could build a Domain — one natural, one provided by the Spell, with the latter overshadowing the former in most cases. So, finding the true mechanism of spreading one's authority far and wide wasn't even important for some of the new Supremes.

Still, it couldn't hurt to know.

The most straightforward power among the six new Supremes belonged to Nightwalker, and even that one was weird as hell. His Aspect Abilities had been enhanced across the board, with a couple standing out among the rest. His already fearsome Transcendent form, that of a cosmic starbeast, had grown numerous times greater — as if that giant creature had been merely a whelp before.

He had also become capable of manipulating space at a greater scale — and, more importantly, of twisting it permanently. That alone was a tremendous boon, since it allowed many others to enjoy the benefits of Nightwalker's Aspect freely. He could make a road that allowed people to traverse a week's worth of distance in just a day or two, for example — with some effort, but forever.

What else could he do with that versatile power? Only time could tell. Sunny could not help but imagine a network of teleportation platforms that would connect distant corners of the immensely vast Dream Realm one day in the future, though. Instant teleportation seemed like an unreachable goal, but then again, the Demon of Repose had been able to create the Night Garden.

Who was to say that, given time, Nightwalker would not be able to accomplish something similar?

His Domain would have to grow quite powerful for that, probably. And speaking of his Domain, the natural path to expanding it was somewhat unexpected — at least to Sunny, whose view of Supremes was twisted by the few examples he had.

Apart from conquering Citadels, Ki Song had expanded her Domain by creating puppets. Anvil expanded his by forging swords and bestowing them upon loyal warriors — Sunny was still unsure if the swords had been the core of the Domain, or the people wielding them.

Cassie's Domain consisted of those she remembered, while his own consisted of shadows of those he had killed. Neph's Longing Domain, meanwhile, consisted of people she had inspired to strive for something they longed to achieve.

Nightwalker's Domain had nothing to do with people, though, or any kind of living beings. It was land. He could expand his Domain by laying claim to land... but only land that had not been claimed before.

In other words, without the Spell, he would have had to dedicate his life to journeying and exploration, always striving to find the next frontier. Only that would allow his Domain to grow, and his people to flourish... the problem, naturally, was that all easily conquered lands in the Dream Realm had already been claimed, and all that remained was a collection of unexplored, increasingly harrowing hells.

Still, knowing Nightwalker, Sunny could imagine him having a swell time traveling to exotic, distant hells and meeting exciting, unusual eldritch horrors one day in the future.

What mattered now, however, was that he would be able to use the Components of the Night Garden better as a Supreme. With Nightwalker at the helm, the living ship would be able to serve as a connection between various cities of humanity even if it ceased to be a part of the Longing Domain.

Seishan's new powers were also quite straightforward. Just like the rest of the Supremes, all her Aspect Abilities had grown more potent or evolved. The core of her Supreme power, however, was founded in her unique Transcendent Ability, which allowed her to transform others instead of herself.

The surviving Handmaidens of the Bright Castle had been infused with her blood, thus undergoing the empowering transformation and becoming known as the Blood Sisters. Now, however, the power granted to them by Seishan's augmentation had grown tremendously, and they also gained access to lesser versions of her other Aspect Abilities — especially the ability to grow even stronger by spilling blood.

That was not all there was to it, though. The most far-reaching change in Seishan's powers was that the people she had granted the Blood Blessing could, in turn, bestow it upon others now. There was a hierarchical structure to the spread of her power, with each next generation of those chosen receiving a weaker version of it, but seemingly no limit.

None they had discovered yet, at least. For all Sunny knew, there could be seven possible degrees of separation to this Blood Blessing — or even some random number of them, like sixteen.

Naturally, Seishan could expand her Domain naturally by bestowing her Blood Blessing to chosen champions, and having those champions spread it further. The more people they took into the fold, the more spirit essence she would draw from them, and the more fearsome her Will would become. Blessing someone took a toll on Seishan, though, so she couldn't transform crowds of people...

But that was where the Spell could help. She could also expand her Domain greatly by controlling Citadels — in fact, that was a far easier and more efficient path. Nothing prevented her from doing both at the same time, either.

Everything seemed great on paper... it was just that those who received Seishan's blessing did not only inherit a lesser version of her powers, but also, seemingly, a fraction of her Flaw. In the grand scheme of things, though, that wasn't a big problem. Sunny was sure that nothing awful would come of it.

Next was Morgan, whose Supreme power had turned out to be the most versatile. Apart from her Aspect Abilities receiving an overall enhancement, she gained a deep affinity to runes and runic sorcery.

Her Ascended Ability had evolved in an astonishing way, as well.

Before, Morgan had been able to copy a number of enchantments and store them in her body, making her capable of adapting to almost any situation. Now, not only had this Ability become more expansive, but it had also transformed in quite an astounding manner.

Simply put, it allowed her to copy the enchantments stored in her body onto other living beings. There was a limit to how many enchantments a person could accommodate, and of what power — but if she wanted, she could greatly enhance the power of any human below the Supreme Rank.

A mundane person could accommodate an enchantment of the Dormant Rank, an Awakened person could accommodate two enchantments — one of the Dormant Rank, one of the Awakened Rank — and so on. Which meant that she could make mundane humans almost strong enough to contend with Awakened, and make Awakened capable of facing Fallen abominations on somewhat equal footing. The only limit was her imagination, the enchantments available to her, and the competence of the charmed person.

Those carrying her enchantments willingly would become members of her Domain, so she could only enchant beings below the Supreme Rank...

She could place her enchantments on her enemies as well, though, making her Supreme power a bit more sinister. And while doing so, if her Will was sharp enough, she could carve her sorcery into Nightmare Creatures of any Rank, not just those weaker than her. That would not make them her subjects, but could certainly help her kill them.

That was a potent and versatile power that could both assist Morgan in battle and benefit innumerable humans greatly. The only thing Sunny was not entirely clear on was what, exactly, Morgan's source element was. In the end, they tentatively theorized that it was... swordsmanship. Or rather, any kind of martial craft taken to an extreme.

That made a peculiar kind of sense. Morgan had been meant to become a weapon for her father to wield, but in her defiance, she became a sword that wielded herself instead. A sword sharp enough to cut the world.

So, while anyone could receive her enchantments, those who dedicated themselves to overcoming their nature and striving for the heights of martial arts answered to them better. They could draw more power out of them, and Morgan received more spirit essence in response as well.

Sunny could imagine her being called the Sword Queen in the future... which sounded almost like the title of her father, but was actually the opposite. Anvil had looked down on all people, chillingly regarding them as weapons to be used. Morgan, however, had the power to arm her subjects and help them pursue their lives with greater passion, reaching greater heights.

...Sunny found it a bit weird, though, that there were two Supremes who had come from the Valor family.

As far as he was concerned, Anvil was the epitome of an awful father. But both of his children had become Supreme, so if anyone unfamiliar with the King of Swords heard about the dynamic sibling duo — the King of Nothing and the Sword Queen — they'd probably assume that Anvil had been the greatest dad in history, setting the golden standard of parenting goals for all eternity.

That was a concerning thought.

But not as concerning as the fact that there was now a whole continent inside of Effie...

--- Chapter 3146 ---

Effie's Aspect Legacy had granted her a fragment of Life's Domain — which was not a fragment of Earth, interestingly enough — and helped her soul give birth to a lesser domain of her own, the Soul Garden, which was a domain of thriving and prosperity. Then, the fragment of the Divine Domain fused with her Soul Garden, imbuing it with exuberant, mystical vitality.

And when Effie attained Supremacy, her Aspect Abilities growing more potent or evolving, her lesser domain evolved as well. Now, there was nothing lesser about it anymore — it expanded, becoming the size of a continent. It was just that her Domain was located in her Soul Sea, not in the Dream Realm or the waking world.

As for her Supreme power, it was rather straightforward. It shared the augmentation of her Dormant and Awakened Abilities with all her subjects, albeit in a diminished capacity — similar to how her Ascended Ability functioned before for those of her warriors who saw her during a battle.

Now, however, the effect of her Ascended Ability was greatly enhanced for members of her Domain, making it far more profound and potent.

Those who resided and thrived in her Domain would naturally become its subjects. That actually was a great boon for the Human Domain as a whole, since far more people would be able to abandon the dying Earth now — it was as if humanity had suddenly gained a new Great Citadel.
