It was unclear just how large a population Effie's Domain could sustain yet, but it had to be substantial.

Effie was in a strange position, though, because her Aspect Legacy had suddenly interfered in the natural progression of her Aspect. It was quite possible that there would not have been a Soul Garden without it, and therefore, Effie would have possessed a different source element and would be able to naturally expand her Domain in a different manner.

In fact, it was quite possible that she still could, which would mean that she possessed a dual source element. They suspected that one of them was nurture and prosperity, while the other was warfare — the kind of warfare meant to protect what her Domain nurtured, that was.

So, it could very well be that those warriors who were inspired by her on the battlefield could also become a part of her Domain, even if they did not make their home in her Soul Garden.

That inner realm needed a name better than "the Soul Garden", by the way... and everyone unanimously agreed to forbid Effie from naming it herself. Otherwise, one of the most vital sanctuaries of humanity would have ended up being called something like "the Big Pantry", "Effie's Huge Soul Food Vault", or "Snack Quadrant", which would not be great for morale.

...Sunny thought that Effie's Huge Soul Food Vault was a pretty good name, actually, but for some reason, everyone had ignored his opinion.

Then there were Kai and Jet, whose Supreme powers were the strangest — which was not to say that they were weak. On the contrary, they were quite fearsome. Especially Jet's, whose power was probably the strangest and most frightening of them all.

Kai's source elements seemed to be... songs. Which was a bit confusing, considering that his Domain could not really be called the Song Domain, for obvious reasons. In any case, his Supreme power was a word. Kai was able to leave that word on a living being's soul as a mark... or a brand... thus making them a member of his Domain.

That could be done voluntarily or involuntarily, although Kai, of course, would never resort to the latter — even if it made it easier for him to bend those affected to his will, therefore opening an easier path to great power. The former, meanwhile, was more difficult to accomplish, since it demanded a certain quality from the person being infused with his Word.

Perhaps it was a natural affinity, or maybe simply talent. The point was, different people could draw different benefits from becoming a member of Kai's Domain.

The fundamental benefit they received was being able to share in Kai's Ascended Ability, which allowed him to reshape the world with his voice. Most people were incapable of achieving anything with that power, though — only those with the right predisposition could achieve more, even if it could not compare to the frightening extent of Kai's own Ability.

However, for whatever reason... that only worked when they sang. Simply speaking had no effect whatsoever, and coincidentally, people with musical and artistic inclinations had a better chance of being receptive to the Word and becoming powerful chanters.

Those especially talented could receive other boons, as well. Some chanters inherited enhanced vision from Kai's Awakened Ability. Some could even gain the ability to fly, although there were very few of those.

And to make things even weirder, the statement that most people could not achieve anything while chanting was only partially true. Yes, an average person would not be able to do much after becoming a member of Kai's Domain. But... for whatever reason... that was only true if they chanted alone.

If a large group of people did it together, though, their ineffective efforts fused, producing a powerful effect — the larger the choir, the more pronounced the changes. Sunny could not even find words to describe how bizarre that Domain and that Supreme power were.

He could somewhat accept an image of a talented singer augmenting their cohort with a good song, or disturbing the minds of their enemies with a terrible one.

However, imagining a whole army singing as they went into battle, and becoming stronger for it — that was a bit too much for him. Why couldn't people just get augmentations in the normal, natural way? Like being wrapped in living shadows, wreathed in radiant flames of someone's soul, or staring at the lavish figure of a hundred-meter-tall woman?

Actually, now that Effie was a Supreme, her Transcendent form would probably be taller than a hundred meters. Nightwalker's, Morgan's, and Kai's forms had become far greater, after all. Seishan's ability to transform people had grown more potent, while Jet could now turn into a far more voluminous wraith if she so wished. So, Effie would not be an exception either.

And speaking of Jet...

Her Supreme power was one all of them were still struggling to wrap their heads around. In fact, it remained largely unexplored, since it could only be truly uncovered in battle.

A few things were already clear, though. The most startling of them... was that Jet could not generate spirit essence. And, therefore, she did not really possess a Domain, either.

Instead, her titanic, shattered Soul Core served as a substitute for a Domain, its sheer size adding incredible weight to the tyranny of her Will. The larger it grew, the more potent her spirit became — and it had grown tremendously already.

Jet's Aspect Abilities must have grown more potent or evolved in some ways, as well. But without an army of Nightmare Creatures on the Ivory Island to test them, there was no way to truly find out how.

The only exception was her Transformation Ability, the change in which was evident enough, and her Awakened Ability — the one responsible for her being known as Soul Reaper, since it allowed her to attack the souls of living beings directly.

Now, however, it seemed to have changed in a mysterious way, allowing Jet to attack the spirit of her enemy, as well. Not only was she able to directly weaken the Will of her opponents, but she had become generally resistant to its effects, all but ignoring them at times.

Needless to say, that made her a harrowing enemy for those who had attained a high Rank and relied on the Will to defend themselves and destroy their foes. Just like even Saints were wary of Jet in the era when Supremes were merely a rumor, now, those of the Supreme and Great Ranks... as well as those above... had a reason to be scared of her, as well.

Jet was neither dead nor alive, but she was certainly a natural killer.

As for her source element, it was soul. There was no surprise there, albeit quite a lot of irony.

Observing the six new Sovereigns, Sunny could not help but sigh.

Such great and wondrous powers... but was it going to be enough?

He had a feeling that even if it were, it would be just barely.

--- Chapter 3147 ---

Having more or less determined the general scope of everyone's powers, albeit not in a detailed fashion, the eleven demigods could finally discuss the grave matter of humanity's survival from an informed position.

There were countless minute decisions they had to make — minute only in the grand scope of the apocalypse, of course. In truth, each of these issues could decide the fate of thousands, if not millions of people. Put all together, these minor choices could decide the fate of all humanity, as well.

Luckily, the eleven Supremes did not have to figure out every little detail — like the precise deployment of troops, the timing of each resettlement effort, the resource allocation for the refugees, and so on — themselves. They simply had to decide the general direction in which they wanted to move and entrust the rest to their subordinates, who were far more competent in the infinitely complex task of managing the day-to-day function of humanity.

There was also the fact that planning anything in too much detail was simply meaningless, since the situation across both worlds was highly unstable and changing unpredictably every day. So, the best anyone could do was prepare for the highest possible number of eventualities and pray that the worst projected scenarios would not come to pass.

Even if, deep down, that was pretty much exactly what everyone was expecting to happen.

If one disregarded this infinite number of minor decisions, though, it all boiled down to three profound choices.

The Supremes of humanity had to accomplish three global tasks.

Someone had to conquer the Fifth Nightmare. Someone had to keep the Dream Realm from being consumed by an endless tide of Nightmare Creatures. And, finally, someone had to make sure that billions of people did not perish while the waking world was falling apart.

So, the most important decision facing them was just that — they had to decide who would undertake each of the three tasks.

It was obvious that Sunny and Nephis would challenge the Nightmare. They were the most experienced Supremes among the rulers of humanity, after all, as well as the strongest. However, it was unclear if they would enter the Seed alone or in the company of trustworthy allies.

Sunny had somewhat expected Mordret to volunteer — he had mentioned considering doing just that, after all. In addition, although the Mordret of today was not the same as the Mordret of yesterday, he still wielded a Divine Aspect. Among the Sovereigns, only he could claim to be as powerful as Sunny and Nephis were.

The guy avoided committing to an answer, though, either still hesitating or preferring not to share his decision. This new Mordret was a strange guy... Sunny received an impression that he did not care whether humanity survived too much, extending his help only out of courtesy. Mordret had isolated himself from the rest of the world, maintaining contact with just a few select people, like Morgan, Rain, or Cassie.

He wasn't as invested in the apocalypse as the rest of them. However, it was precisely because Mordret still seemed to care about at least one person — his sister — that Sunny felt like he could very well choose the Nightmare, in the end.

While Mordret abstained from voicing an opinion, someone else surprised them, though.

It was Cassie, expressing her intent to challenge the Fifth Nightmare with them. She spoke the words in a steadfast tone, as if having made the decision a long time ago.

Sunny had a feeling that she might want to follow them into the Seed, but then again, Cassie had an established role in the vast machine of humanity. Many things depended on her, so her absence would be felt almost as much as that of Nephis.

For that reason, he had assumed that she would choose to stay.

Sunny was not sure how he felt about being proven wrong. On one hand, there was a sense of joy in his heart... relief, even. Cassie was their closest friend and confidant, after all — a companion unlike any other. Many years ago, it had all started with the three of them enduring the dire trials of the Forgotten Shore.

There was no need to mention how powerful and useful to have around Cassie was, either. In a battle, she might not have been the most fearsome of the Supremes, but her profound affinity to revelations had saved them almost as many times as cold steel. Her Aspect and Domain were also exceedingly unique, making her a priceless ally.

But it was precisely because of how deep the bond between them ran that Sunny felt uneasy and reluctant at the thought of Cassie joining them in the Nightmare. All Nightmares were deadly, after all, and the Fifth one promised to be more harrowing than the rest of them. Sunny knew that he might never return from it... but the thought of Cassie perishing in the depths of a Nightmare cut him deeper.

It was easy to risk your own life, after all. Putting the lives of those you cherished at risk, though? That was a far more bitter pill to swallow.

In the end, however, there was nothing he could do — not that he would, anyway. Cassie was a Supreme now, same as Sunny, so he could not dictate her decisions. He had no ground to stand on, and no desire to refuse her help either.

So, on that day, it was decided that the three of them — Changing Star, Lost from Light, and Song of the Fallen — would enter the Seed of a Fifth Nightmare and attempt to become the new deities of humanity. With the decision made, many plans had to be adjusted. The other Sovereigns had already come to terms with the thought that Sunny and Nephis would be absent for a long time — years, most likely, and judging by how long the others had spent in the Fourth Nightmare, it might not be only a couple of years either. Now, they had to contend with the fact that Cassie would be gone as well.

Without her, a lot of things would change. At any other time, the news that Song of the Fallen would disappear for an unknown number of years would have caused a shockwave among the people who depended on her knowledge, insight, and mental communication to survive. However, today, it was almost a footnote — because a far more staggering change was about to occur.

The Longing Domain, which had served as the supporting pillar of humanity in the dire years of the early apocalypse, would soon cease to exist.

--- Chapter 3148 ---

There was no way to avoid it, since Nephis had to make space to allow other Supremes to establish their Domains. More importantly, it was almost a given that she would not be able to assist her subjects from the depths of the Nightmare — so, clinging to her throne served no purpose. And lastly, there was the simple fact that no matter how their attempt to conquer the Fifth Nightmare ended, the Longing Domain would disappear anyway.

If Nephis perished in the Nightmare, there would be no more Changing Star to govern the sea of frail flames burning in the hearts of humanity. If she succeeded, though, she would not be a Sovereign anymore — she would be a Spirit. And Spirits did not govern Domains... not in the same way Supremes did, at least.

As a matter of fact, neither Sunny nor Nephis knew what exactly would happen to their Domains after the Apotheosis. However, they knew that a deity was meant to be one with his or her source element, not merely controlling a construct made with the help of it.

Perhaps they would still be able to exert influence over their Domains — or over what had once been their Domains, rather. Perhaps the scope of their influence would even increase. However, its nature would definitely change, and neither of them knew how.

They knew, however, that Spirits existed on a plane above the Supremes, and were not concerned with expressing their authority. Although Sunny and Nephis did not know what Apotheosis would mean for them, they did know what their absence, as well as the absence of the Longing Domain, would mean for the warriors of humanity. There would be no miraculous flames to heal their wounds and save their lives anymore. There would be no radiance to shine from beneath their skin and make them stronger. Some of them had grown accustomed to the caring support of their goddess, but now that support would be gone.

Apart from that, the nature of the relationship between mundane people and the Nightmare Spell would change, as well. At the moment, humans who resided in the Dream Realm had two ways of challenging the First Nightmare — they could either leave the confines of the Longing Domain or relay their desire to become Awakened to Nephis, thus prompting her to withdraw her protection and allow the seeds of Corruption hidden in their hearts to bloom.

The latter was an unreliable method, since Nephis could not pay attention to each of the billions of sparks composing her Domain at all times. The former, meanwhile, was somewhat difficult to accomplish — simply because the Longing Domain was so vast, encompassing all settled regions of the Dream Realm.

The swiftest and most reliable way to challenge the Nightmare, therefore, was to leave the Dream Realm altogether and return to Earth, either with the help of a Saint or through Neph's Dream Gate. Everything about that process was about to change.

First of all, Dream Gates were meant to be a one-way passage — they only allowed people to enter the Dream Realm from the waking world, not the other way around. It was because of Neph's [Dreamspawn] Attribute that her Gate was unique, functioning as a Nightmare Gate as well and allowing people to return. Without her, though, leaving Earth would carry the weight of finality for most settlers.

Leaving their Domain in the confines of the Dream Realm, on the contrary, would become easier — simply because the Human Domain would become a coalition of smaller Domains in the future instead of being synonymous with just one.

At the same time, people would have to learn how to petition their Sovereigns in order to escape from the protection of their Domains... instead of praying to Nephis. Sunny could not quite imagine any of the new Supremes being treated with the same type of religious reverence — not yet, at least — so the meditation halls and barely disguised prayers would probably have to be replaced by something new.

The transition would not be a swift or easy process... however, considering how desperately humanity needed more Awakened, Sunny imagined that accelerating it would become a priority. There were other matters to address, as well.

The remaining Supremes all had unique advantages and disadvantages when it came to building Domains. Some could do without the assistance of the Nightmare Spell, while some would be able to support humanity better if they controlled a large amount of Citadels... some, like Jet, would find no use in ruling a Citadel at all.

All of that had to be considered when deciding how to divide the Longing Domain, so that humanity attained as much strength as possible while it was being split between its Supreme protectors.

Sunny felt a bit of incongruity as he watched the ruler of the most powerful and expansive Domain in existence calmly discussing how to divide it among other Supremes. Godgrave had not been that long ago... after that bloody civil war, who would have thought that something this peaceful would be possible one day?

‘I'm almost speechless.'

The eleven demigods deliberated for a long time, eventually coming to a tentative outline of a decision.

According to their plan, out of the seven Sovereigns that were certain to stay behind, four would stand guard over Dream Realm, while three would defend the waking world and oversee the resettlement of its population.

If there was one unexpected benefit to the great number of Sovereigns War Realm had given birth to, it was that its inhospitable laws could not keep all of them away. Even if the waking world was actively pushing those who had attained Supreme power out, they could remain on Earth for several hours before truly feeling the strain.

That meant that they could take turns overseeing its expanse and make sure that at least one Supreme was always present in the waking world in case some kind of unexpected calamity befell it.

The three Sovereigns who took responsibility for the dying cradle of humanity were Jet, Kai, and Effie.

Neither of them particularly needed the assistance of the Spell to build their Domain. Jet would draw no benefit from ruling Citadels, Effie carried one within herself, making it easy to gain new subjects, while Kai was limited in whom he could effectively convert. So, by process of elimination, they were the best choice.

Additionally, Effie had to be present on Earth to hasten the evacuation of its people. Her Soul Garden would greatly boost the rate of resettlement, moving the whole timetable of the great exodus forward by a few years. That alone was reason enough to assign her the task of guarding the waking world.

While these three focused their attention on the waking world, the other four would have to stand their ground and defend the Dream Realm to the last drop of blood. They were Ananke, Morgan, and Seishan, with Nightwalker serving as the link between them.

Ananke would remain in Silver Web, overseeing the Stormsea and protecting the lands of humanity from things that hid in its depths.

Seishan would claim Ravenheart and the Citadel Cities located in the basin of the River of Tears... ironically enough, that meant that she would regain the lands that had been meant to be her birthright, assuming reign over the former territories of the Song Clan.

The same held true for Morgan, who would claim Bastion and the vast expanse of the former Sword Domain. She would return home, as well.

Nightwalker, meanwhile, would take the helm of the Night Garden and turn it into a wandering stronghold of humanity, responsible for keeping the three parts of the Human Domain connected and capable of supporting each other.

Once the plan was finalized, Sunny leaned back in his chair, looking around with a strange expression.

A scion of the Song family would once again rule Ravenheart. The Princess of Valor would return to Bastion. The Night Garden, meanwhile, would fall into the hands of the House of Night once more...

Almost as if it had been meant to be. Sunny was not sure if that was poetic... or upsetting.

‘How come after everything we did to destroy the Great Clans, nothing seems to have changed?'

But, of course... in truth, everything had changed. This peaceful meeting was the best proof that the world had been irrevocably altered.

All the blood they had spilled was to make this moment possible.

Sunny sighed.

‘At least no one laid claim to the Forgotten Shore...'

A troubled smile appeared on his lips. That, too, was a headache he would have to solve... but not today.

Today, they had to draft the speech announcing the tectonic changes awaiting humanity in the upcoming weeks.

--- Chapter 3149 ---

A few days later, Sunny stared into the distance, a contemplative expression on his face.

He remained silent for a long while, then sighed.

“Things... do not look great."

He hesitated a little, then shook his head.

“It used to be that humanity was conquering new lands every day. There was so much energy when Nephis first ascended to the throne, so much momentum... we were achieving one victory after another. Those times are behind us now. The world just had to go and end on us without a warning. We were so busy preparing for the end of days that it arrived without anyone noticing. One day, we simply looked around and found ourselves in the middle of the apocalypse."

Sunny smiled bitterly.

"These days, we are not conquering new lands. In fact, we can't even seem to hold onto the ones that were already conquered. It's a controlled retreat, for now... but the Human Domain is shrinking, little by little, every day instead. And do you know what really grinds my gears?"

His smile turned contemptuous.

"It is that because of that bastard, the Dreamspawn, most people don't even remember the good times that well. The Longing Domain is about to disappear, and its glory days are all but gone from everyone's memory. That seems quite unfair, don't you think?"

Sunny cursed.

“And don't even get me started on the waking world. That whole place is a mess — Nightmare Gates opening everywhere, chunks of it being swallowed by the Dream Realm, swarms of abominations besieging all three Quadrants. The Barrow Wraiths, the Black Millipedes, and every other kind of horror imaginable... gods, I really hate those."

He inhaled slowly.

"Well, at least things are looking up now because of Effie, Kai, Jet, Seishan, Morgan, and Nightwalker. South America has been evacuated, and the coastal areas are next. Ananke and the cities in the Stormsea have been a real lifeline for us in the past couple of years, and now that Effie and her Soul Garden are ready to enter the fray... I think we can get ahead of the apocalypse for once. At least for a little while."

Leaning back, he shook his head.

“Who knows? The world might still be in one piece by the time I become a god. I sure hope it will be. After all, it would be quite unfortunate to become a god at the same time as all of existence crumbles. There won't be anyone left for me to boast to... what even is the point of godhood if one cannot be smug about it in someone else's face?"

In response, there was a long stretch of silence.

Then, a heavy sigh dispelled it.

“Has not being a god ever stopped you from being smug?"

Sunny raised an eyebrow, then frowned in indignation.

The voice, meanwhile, added:

"And for the love of gods, why are you monologuing in my room? Listen, there is a legion of dead shadows in your soul. Can't you use one of them — any of them! — to ramble at instead?!"

Sunny was, of course, in Revel's room. The room was just as messy as ever, but at least the great and terrible Lightslayer was in a more presentable shape than her usual reclusive self — if being covered in sweat, grime, and blood could be considered an improvement. She had just returned from the battlefield, and had yet to shake off her fearsome image.

‘No, what am I talking about? Of course, it's an improvement!’

Anything was an improvement compared to her usual sloppy look.

Sunny did not have to be ashamed of how unprofessional his supposed top minion... that was to say, the esteemed elder of his Shadow Clan... looked.

He stared at Revel in confusion.

"Of course, I can. But where is the fun in that?"

Groaning, Revel threw an exasperated look his way.

“Why are you hiding in my room, anyway? Did you make Aiko angry again?"

Sunny coughed.

“Of course not. Why would I make her angry? I don't know what you mean."

She seemed unconvinced.

"Why are you here, then?"

Sunny cleared his throat.

“By the way, do you remember that time I mentioned hiring Aiko as my assistant, then disappearing for a few years, leaving her in charge of a crumbling business in the absence of its main asset?"

Revel nodded slowly.

Sunny stared at her with a vague smile for a few moments.

“Well, I am leaving for a few years! And I am leaving you in charge of the Shadow Clan! Congratulations, I guess!"

His smile was flawlessly innocent.

"That is why I am here. To deliver the news — and the congratulations — in person. Oh, and I also had a question..."

Revel looked around her room with a strange expression.

What was that emotion?

Sunny couldn't quite recognize, but thought that it looked strangely similar to... melancholy.

‘What is that about? I just handed her a promotion! Of sorts...’

Why were people so ungrateful?

She sighed.

"Can't say I didn't see it coming.”

Sunny raised an eyebrow.

“Oh, you did? Well, that simplifies things."

Revel nodded.

“You didn't make a secret of your intention to challenge the Nightmare, after all. Our people can only enter the Forgotten Shore with the help of your Dream Gate. The expedition to the Underworld did not produce a safe and reliable path connecting us to the rest of the Dream Realm under the Hollow Mountains, either. So... once you're gone, we will be either stuck here or forced to retreat. I was expecting this conversation for a while."

She remained silent for a few moments, then glared at Sunny.

“I just didn't expect it to happen in my private quarters, immediately after I returned from a battle against one of those damn Barrow Lords."

Revel's scowl deepened.

“And speaking of my private quarters — do you know what 'private' means, damn it?!"

Sunny was surprised by the question.

"Who do you take me for? Of course, I do!"

He let out a derisive scoff.

“It means that I have to enter through the shadows instead of opening the door!"

A book Revel had nearby flew in the direction of his head, and Sunny elegantly caught it in the air.

Turning it around to look at the cover, he blinked a few times.

"What? There's a sequel? But how... how does she keep accidentally seducing all these men..."

Revel growled.

"Focus! Anyway, you had a question?!"

Sunny tore his gaze away from the book, put it aside, and surreptitiously wiped his hand on his tunic.

“Oh, yes."

He leaned forward and asked in a friendly tone:

"Say... how do you feel about pets?"

Then, he leaned back and sighed.

"You see, I have this snake. It is a sweet little fellow — about a kilometer long, house-trained, loves eating people... uhm, did I say eating people? I mean people, it loves people!"

He paused for a moment.

“Anyway, I was hoping you could look after it while I'm gone, just for a little while..."

--- Chapter 3150 ---

Sunny wanted to use the Grace of Shadows Ability of Soul Serpent to bestow it upon Revel.

There were two reasons why he had chosen to make that decision, each of equal importance.

The first one was pretty obvious, and had already been touched upon by Revel. He had to make arrangements for the Shadow Clan before leaving, the main of which was the fate of the Forgotten Shore.

Sunny and his forces were entrenched there, holding their own against the Barrow Wraiths. With Saint becoming Supreme, he was able to push the abominations back to the border of the Burning Forest — but if Sunny went away, the line of defense would collapse. In fact, if he did not take some kind of measures, the line of defense would simply cease to exist.

The members of the Shadow Clan would find it difficult to travel between the Forgotten Shore and other lands of the Dream Realm, as well, not to mention between the Dream Realm and Earth. Since establishing a safe route through the Underworld seemed impossible at the moment, all they would be able to rely on were Revel and the Nameless Temple.

In any case, the simplest decision seemed to be to give up on the Forgotten Shore and relocate his forces somewhere else. Sunny was tempted to do just that, as well... but ultimately, he felt compelled to fight for his lightless demesne. He had invested too much effort into making it his stronghold, as well as a secret sanctuary for humanity. More than that, giving it up felt like the first domino in a vicious chain of defeat.

The Forgotten Shore was not just any region of the Dream Realm, after all — it was the entire northern frontline of humanity's fight against the encroaching Nightmare. If it fell, all other human lands would feel the pressure eventually, if not soon enough.

Both on a strategic and personal level, the Forgotten Shore was important to Sunny. So, he had chosen to make sure that it remained in human hands... which meant that he had to come up with a way for humans to defend it even in his absence. The question of how to go about that, however, was innately connected to the second reason he was leaving Serpent in Revel's hands.

It was the Fifth Nightmare itself.

No person of the waking world had ever conquered it, and even in history, there were few examples. Sunny only knew of one — of Ketzelkan and other rulers of Mictlan, who had managed to become deities, but seemed to have lost themselves in the process of Apotheosis and ended up destroying their own people.

He knew that people of the Storm Realm, the Twilight Sea, had never produced a Spirit. It was unknown how the scions of the Beast Realm and Heart Realm had fared, but none of them managed to survive the spreading Nightmare, so it was safe to say that their achievements had been ultimately proven insufficient.

In short, there was scarcely any information about what the Fifth Nightmare entailed. The only pieces of knowledge they did possess came from Eurys and, to a larger degree, from the Dreamspawn — and gods knew where he had unearthed that information.

According to the Dreamspawn, Sunny's very own Domain — as well as all his powers and tools — would be turned against him in the Fifth Nightmare. They would, or at least could, become an obstacle instead of helping him pass the trial.

So, even if it felt counterintuitive, Sunny's intuition was telling him that unburdening himself from as much power as possible would aid him in achieving Apotheosis, as well as maintaining a measure of control over who he would become as a result of it.

Apart from that, doing so felt oddly fitting. The Fifth Nightmare would most likely become the most dire trial of his entire perilous life. Stripping all superfluous advantages and facing it as close to his pure self as possible felt like the kind of resolve he needed in order to survive it.

That meant that Sunny had to leave some, if not all, of his Shadows behind. If it was possible, he also had to reduce the number of shades populating his soul.

As much as he hated the idea of parting with his loyal followers, that also lay in line with his overall goals. Sunny's true goal was not to conquer the Fifth Nightmare or become a deity, after all — those were merely measures he had to take in order to achieve it. What he really wanted was to make sure that humanity survived the apocalypse.

There was no point in becoming a god if all of mankind was gone by the time he did, and leaving his Shadows to guard the strongholds of humanity would diminish the possibility of all humans perishing. Those Supremes who were staying behind could certainly use all the help they could get — and Sunny’s powerful Shadows could be of immense help.

The question, however, was... would Sunny even be able to leave them in the real world? When his body, spirit, and soul entered the Seed of Nightmare, would the Spell graciously allow the inhabitants of his soul to stay?

Sunny did not know, but he suspected that it would. Others were able to leave their Memories behind, after all — so why couldn't he do the same with Shadows? The problem was that his Shadows could not exist without him. They drew their power from him, returned to the nurturing embrace of his soul to recover and heal from the wounds they received, and in some cases relied on him for sustenance.

So even if Sunny did leave them behind, their usefulness to the effort of preserving humanity would be limited, and there was a real possibility that they would be destroyed.

Because his Shadows were not independent beings. As Eurys had said once, they were not yet complete.

Sunny had not known how to make them complete before, but after venturing into the Underworld and recovering Shadow Weave, he had come up with a theory.

That theory had been developed further and tested in the month following that dreadful expedition, and now, finally, Sunny was ready to put it into practice.

On the eve of departing for a dreadful Nightmare...

He was preparing to grant his Shadows freedom.

--- Chapter 3151 ---

It was night on the Forgotten Shore.

Well, of course it was. It was always night here, with no stars and no moon in the perfectly black sky. Still, Sunny liked the idea that, at the moment, it was really nighttime — just like when he had encountered Saint for the first time.

The location was the same, as well. It was the vast square in the depths of the Dark City, not too far from the ruined cathedral... only the cathedral was not so ruined anymore.

In fact, it had been restored to flawless condition. The whole city had been over the years, with Sunny and his shades, as well as members of the Shadow Clan, working tirelessly to make it suitable for humans to live in.

Now, the Dark City stood pristine and empty. The wide streets had been cleared of rubble, the buildings either repaired or demolished and built anew. It was just that there were no citizens here, not really... at least not yet.

Now that Sunny was planning to entrust the Shadow Clan to Revel, that could change. At the moment, however, he had to make sure that the Forgotten Shore remained under human control first.

That was why he had come to the familiar square where Saint had once fought the Iron Spiders, was slain by Sunny, and became his Shadow. At the moment, the square was empty, with not a soul in sight — and not a shade, either.

Except for Sunny and his Shadows.

Saint towered above the square like a magnificent monument carved from flawlessly black jade. Nearby, Fiend stood like a hill of jagged swords. Nightmare was here as well, having risen from the shadows. Slayer stood motionlessly, her graceful figure like that of a dancer. Vile had assumed the form of Sunny, sitting on the ground with a bored, but alarmingly mischievous expression.

The shape of the Dark Castle could be seen in the distance, looming above the city. And finally, Serpent had assumed its titanic Soul Beast form and coiled around the entire square, its head resting on the stones a few dozen meters away from Sunny.

These were his Shadows, his most powerful and loyal followers. Some had been with him for many years, some had joined the Shadow Cohort only recently. All in all, Sunny had really had a blast wandering the harrowing expanse of the Dream Realm in their company. He could not have wished for better companions...

He scratched the back of his head.

‘No, what am I talking about? Of course I could have!'

Sunny looked at his Shadows with a scowl. Nightmare, Fiend, Mimic, Slayer, and Vile... those wretches had truly put him through the depths of hell before becoming his Shadows! Encountering them had been among the absolute worst times in his impossibly appalling collection of terrible experiences.

So while it was true that they were wonderful companions, there could have been Shadows just as fearsome and loyal, but who had not left him with permanent mental scars.

Like Saint and Serpent. Why couldn't every Shadow be like these two?

“Come to think of it... you're actually a bunch of wretched bastards!"

Sunny shook his head in dismay.

The Shadows ignored his outburst, as they usually did. Only Vile seemed to liven up and turned to him with a grin.

"Bastard!"

Sunny sighed and covered his face with a palm.

“Yeah, yeah...”

Hearing the youngest curse, Fiend shifted and looked at Vile with a hint of approval. Then, he turned to Sunny and breathed out a puff of infernal flame.

His grating voice resounded from above.

“Wretch."

Sunny laughed.

"Well, I'll admit it. You have all come around, eventually. Thank you all for tolerating me for these long years of excitement and adventure... I wouldn't have made it without you, guys. Truly."

He sighed.

“But everything must come to an end sometime. So... this is it. It's time for all of you to graduate. Well — most of you, at least. Was I a good master or a terrible one? I am not sure. But I did my best."

Sunny smiled wistfully, remembering the good old times.

Which, really, had been the absolute worst. But still, he missed those days a little.

All in all, his Shadows really had nothing to complain about. He had nurtured all of them, helping them walk the Path of Ascension in his wake. So, he hoped that they would remember him fondly one day, even if he wasn't there anymore... at least not in the same way.

Sunny inhaled deeply and then looked at Saint.

His voice was quiet.

“Alright, then. It's time to get this show on the road."

At the end, his voice shook slightly.

‘Ah... this is going to hurt terribly, won't it?’

As Saint walked forward at his command, her size changing to that of a human, Sunny's shadow split into six, surrounding him like an honor guard. When Saint approached, standing before him, Sunny offered her a pale smile.

"We... have been through a lot together, haven't we?"

Fighting Sovereigns and Titans, conquering impossible Nightmares, delving into the darkest corners of the Dream Realm...

Hell, Saint had even been his therapist for a short while.

Hearing his question, she tilted her head a little, and then nodded slowly.

Sunny chuckled.

"As taciturn as ever..."

With that, he exhaled and then raised his hand.

Then, using the same motion he used when weaving a soul shard into a Memory, he reached into his own soul and grasped one of his Shadow Cores — his very first one, which had served as Saint's cradle for almost fifteen years.

And feeling his soul tremble, he pulled.

He tore it out.

‘Aargh!’

It hurt like hell.

But also, strangely, it wasn't that bad — no worse than the pain of a new Shadow Core being born, at least.

Sunny had seen Mordret doing something similar to create his Reflections or purge cores that were tainted by Corruption, but had never been able to do it himself — until Shadow Weave, that was.

Of course, there was more to the process than simply tearing the Shadow Core out of his soul. Sunny possessed an instinctual understanding of how to proceed now, and the foundation of his being had become far more capable and malleable, thus allowing the whole thing.

Still, it had taken him months of torturous experimentation to figure out how to remove a Shadow Core from his soul without destroying it. His soul, meanwhile, was not damaged terribly due to being enhanced by Soul Weave.

But removing a Shadow Core was only half of the process. Now, he had to embed it into Saint's soul — or rather, into the shadow that served her as one.

That, Sunny had never attempted before. This was the moment of truth.

Grimacing slightly, he reached forward and drew on his vast experience as a sorcerer to carefully embed the Shadow Core into Saint's chest.

However...

He did not have to worry. Once his core entered the dark depths of her being, it was as if something within Saint responded to its presence.

And then, a wondrous transformation took place in front of his eyes.

As it did, the Spell whispered into his ear...

[You have lost a Shadow.]

--- Chapter 3152 ---

Within the vast and boundless shadow hiding inside Saint's mortal shell, five dark embers burned with lightlessness among the sea of darkness. Those embers were jagged and uneven, utterly lifeless — they functioned as a facsimile of true Shadow Cores, but weren't at all equal to one.

Now, however, that was changing.

As Sunny watched, his Shadow Core entered Saint's shadowy soul like a wandering comet. The moment it did, the depths of the vast shadow seemed to respond, and a dark whirlwind surrounded the nebulous sphere. Within the darkness, the edges of the Shadow Core seemed to blur. And then, a conflagration of black flame ignited in the shadow, blooming at the very heart of Saint's being like a tenebrous flower.

The flower had five petals, and those petals were drawn to each of the dark embers, nourishing and reforging them.

Making them complete.

The embers were being reborn in the nurturing dark flames. Their jagged edges slowly became smooth, and their lifeless coldness was replaced with flawless transparency.

Soon, they came to resemble perfect spheres, as well. Five oceans of dark flame burned inside them, making them look like lightless stars — no different from Sunny's own Shadow Cores. In fact, that was what they were now. And, infused with the power of these cores, a subtle change rippled through Saint's soul.

[You have lost a Shadow.]

The Spell announced the loss of a Shadow, but Saint was not destroyed. On the contrary, she was alive and well... as far as a Shadow Creature could be considered alive, of course.

‘A Shadow Creature...’

After following Sunny for nearly fifteen years as a Shadow, Saint had finally become a Shadow Creature. The difference between the two was subtle, but profound.

It was independence.

A Shadow was a subordinate being serving a master — it was a part of its master's soul, and therefore lacked true agency. A Shadow Creature, however, was a complete, self-sufficient individual. It had agency, free will, and the ability to choose its own path... whom to serve, whom to defy. Which battles to fight, and the reason to fight them.

Sunny was not sure which way of being was better. Being a Shadow or a Shadow Creature simply offered different things, as well as had different demands.

He did know one thing, though.

Being a Shadow, while beneficial in many ways, ultimately created a ceiling for one's growth.

There was a limit to how much one could grow while relying entirely on others, after all. To truly come into your power and become a person, you had to stand on your own two feet.

Well... or four, in the case of Nightmare. Or however many feet Mimic had.

Sunny looked at Saint, who seemed to be engrossed by her transformation. Most of the changes happening to her were invisible, transpiring on the mental and spiritual planes. The connection between them had been severed, and Sunny was not sure what Saint was experiencing... he suddenly felt lonely, as if a part of him had gone missing.

It did, quite literally.

Not only was Saint not a part of him anymore, but one of his shadows had disappeared, as well, becoming her shadow instead.

Now, finally, Saint was a complete being... a Shadow Creature in her own right. Sunny wondered what the future held for her. It used to be that humans coexisted with all kinds of creatures once, back when that word was not associated only with the Corrupted — but those noble creatures were long gone.

But now, there was Saint. She was the first and, for the moment, only Noble Creature in this dire era. As such, she was a natural ally of humanity — both humans and creatures were threatened by the spreading Nightmare, after all, and had to fight it together to survive.

But what would happen if the apocalypse was over one day, and the world still existed? Would people and creatures like Saint coexist once more?

Sunny truly hoped that they would.

Because if some bastard decided to bother Saint in the future... he wasn't going to hold back.

‘Just try it, bastards...’

But that was a matter for the far, vaguely possible future. For now, Sunny was more interested in the changes happening to Saint right here and now.

The most obvious one, of course, was that she did not depend on him anymore and had no need of his powers to continue existing. Sunny was also certain that Saint would become more powerful, since true independence and agency were bound to cause her Will to grow.

She might become more... personable, as well. Although Sunny had a feeling that being aloof and taciturn was simply in her nature.

There was one additional benefit, as well. Since Saint's shadow had once belonged to Sunny, she inherited some of his innate traits, such as the ability to augment herself and use the shadow as a scout. In short, she had her own invaluable helper now.

And more than that, since Saint was a Supreme Tyrant, her shadow had the capacity to contain shades. She could not create them, but she could command them — even if it was to a limited degree.

That limit was enough for Sunny to bestow the shades of Shadow Saints upon her, still. He did so without regret, knowing that Saint would make better use of them. She was the one who had slain most of them, anyway.

“Think of it as a bit of inheritance... a legacy, if you will..."

He smiled as Saint peered at him with her ruby eyes.

Then, his Shadow... his former Shadow... bent down, bowing deeply.

Startled, Sunny waved a hand.

“N—no, no! What are you doing? There's no need for that..."

He fell silent for a few moments, then grinned.

"You know it will go to my head."

Although Sunny was smiling, and felt greatly satisfied seeing Saint become a true living being, he also felt a bit of melancholy.

Saint was her own person now. One of his shadows was now her companion, not his. It was as if his children had left for the Awakened Academy... he could not help but feel both proud of them and worried for their future.

In truth, however, there was no reason to worry. It was Saint, after all — if he could trust that someone would do well, it was her.

The rest of them, though...

Sunny turned to look at his remaining Shadows.

He was planning to grant independence to Nightmare and Fiend, as well. The former was needed in Bastion to guard the Dreamscape — Sunny would entrust him to Morgan, and Morgan to him. Fiend, meanwhile, was uniquely suited to defend Ravenheart and its surrounding territories from the snow wraiths of the western wastelands. So, Sunny intended to make him Seishan's headache.

The Marvelous Mimic was the headquarters of the Shadow Clan, so Sunny was planning to leave it to Revel.

The same went for Serpent — however, Serpent was unique. Due to his [Grace of Shadows] Ability, it did not have to become independent, and neither was it in Serpent's nature.

That was why Sunny would only lend it to Revel, not part with it forever.

He wasn't going to grant independence to Slayer, either. The two of them had formed a working relationship after a while, but she was simply too dangerous to be unleashed upon the world... at least for now.

As for Vile...

Sunny had special plans for that brat.

--- Chapter 3153 ---

Sunny had granted independence to Saint. Then, he did the same with the other Shadows.

Once everything was done, he consumed a great number of his shades to restore the Shadow Cores he had lost in the process. A great number of them vanished, diminishing the power of his Domain... but innumerable shades remained, still.

Finally, dazed by the pain and with his vast soul in a pitiful state, he made his way to Revel's chamber.

And here he was, explaining to her what he intended to do.

"So, that's about it... quite a genius plan, isn't it? As expected of me, the Lord of Shadows!"

Sunny grinned.

Revel let out a heavy sigh and covered her face with a palm.

She remained silent for a long time, then said evenly:

“Well, I'll give it to you. Sending Lord Nightmare to Morgan is a good idea... with a Sovereign and a Supreme Terror protecting Bastion together, people there will be much safer. The same is true for Seishan and the Shadow Fiend. Thank you for that, by the way. I don't even care about how immensely powerful he is — his unbelievable luck alone is a great asset.”

She paused and then mumbled quietly:

“Plus, he will finally have a chance to learn a thing or two from someone sane... thank the gods, that poor Devil really needs another role model..."

Sunny blinked a couple of times.

“Huh? What was that?"

Revel threw a dark look at him.

“Never mind that. That is your plan for the Forgotten Shore? Have you completely lost your mind?"

Sunny chuckled.

“Oh... a long time ago."

Then, he shook his head with a smile.

"But my plan is very reasonable. Just think about it for a moment."

Indeed, what Sunny had in mind for the Forgotten Shore was the product of a long and careful consideration. There was some risk involved, but he had a feeling that it would work out well in the end.

He raised a finger.

“Let's go over it one by one. First... the Soul Serpent."

Due to the [Grace of Shadows] Ability of Serpent, Sunny could transfer it to someone else's shadow. He had already done so with Rain, back when she was facing the possibility of becoming infected by the Nightmare Spell. She had been a mundane person at that time, though, and because of that, she had not received any real benefits from Serpent's companionship.

Revel, however, was a Saint — and an immensely powerful one at that, one of the most fearsome Transcendent people in the world even. So, if Sunny left Serpent with her, they would be able to form a true partnership. Needless to say, that was going to be a great boon both for Revel and for the Shadow Clan as a whole.

First of all, Serpent was quite possibly the strongest Shadow Sunny possessed... had possessed... at least on a technical level. It was a Supreme Titan, after all. Granted, Revel did not have a legion of shades resting in her soul, so Serpent would not be able to assume innumerable shapes as her companion — but even its natural Soul Beast form was already a harrowing force on the battlefield.

That was not the real reason why Sunny wanted to leave Serpent with Revel, though. The real reason was the Shadow Clan.

The members of the Shadow Clan had become who they were by receiving the Mark of Shadows. They were part of Sunny's Doman... but only because Serpent was a part of Sunny. If it became someone else's companion, though, they would become connected to that person instead.

Revel would be able to command members of the Shadow Clan more effectively, as well as support them with her strength. More importantly, she would be able to initiate new members into the Shadow Clan, expanding it as needed. Even if Sunny was gone for many years, the hidden force he had created would not cease to exist.

On the contrary, it would receive a chance to flourish under a new leadership. He doubted that the existence of the Shadow Clan would ever be revealed to the masses, since secrecy was required for the important work they were doing on behalf of humanity. But it would not need to remain so utterly clandestine either.

And if Sunny returned and wanted to take Serpent back, Revel could simply continue to act as the front of the whole operation. He would be more than satisfied to quietly support her from the shadows... in fact, that was only fitting for a force calling itself the Shadow Clan.

"So, you see, it all makes perfect sense."

Revel stared at him for a few moments, then glanced at her forearm, where an intricate tattoo of a graceful snake was etched into her alabaster skin. That was her own Mark of Shadows — the strongest among Serpent's offspring — and if needed, it could become a deadly weapon as well.

She sighed.

“Well, what the hell. I guess I'll need to dust off my dual-wielding technique."

Then, she shook her head in dismay.

"Still, the Soul Serpent alone would not be enough to defend the Forgotten Shore. It was the other part of your plan that bothers me."

Sunny shrugged.

“The other part is what is so genius about it! You need a fortress, an army, and a fearsome general. And look at that — miraculously, I can grant you all three..."

Saint might not have been Sunny's servant anymore, but that did not mean that she ceased to exist. The bond of trust and camaraderie between them had not vanished, either. By losing a Shadow, Sunny had gained an ally... a loyal comrade, even. And as far as allies went, one could hardly do better than Saint.

She also commanded the legion of her fallen kin. So, he had requested that she remain on the Forgotten Shore and help Revel defend it as the field commander of the human forces here. The members of the Shadow Clan had been trained by her, after all — so who was better to lead them into battle?

The general was taken care of. She was a Supreme Tyrant, as well. With Serpent and Saint, Revel was already in charge of a greater force than any other Saint in history.

Except for Sunny himself, of course, and perhaps Mordret.

That left the issue of a fortress.

Naturally, there was Mimic to fill that role.

--- Chapter 3154 ---

Saint was Sunny's companion and ally, so convincing her to come to the Shadow Clan's aid had not been difficult. Mimic, however, was not quite that receptive to earnest communication... and yet, achieving an understanding with it had been even simpler.

After all, the Marvellous Mimic and the Shadow Clan existed in a state of symbiosis. The Mimic sheltered humans and produced soul coins for them, while humans made sure that it never went hungry by feeding it a steady stream of delicious abominations. So, it was in Mimic's own interest to keep the relationship going. Out there in the wild, he would have to risk its safety and work laboriously to deceive and hunt powerful prey.

Being domesticated, though, offered it a far more stable and leisurely existence.

Plus... Sunny had a feeling that the Marvelous Mimic had gotten used to being a home. It almost felt as if it liked being a shelter for countless people, and was quite fond of its current form — that of living, magnificent, carnivorous castle.

Sunny had significantly enhanced the Dark Castle, as well. Even if Mimic was a living being, that did not mean that he couldn't enchant it the same way he and Cassie had enchanted the key Citadels of humanity. So, although Mimic's Rank and Class had not increased, it was far more deadly and impregnable now.

Even if Sunny was absent, it would serve the Shadow Clan well.

Sunny grinned.

"See? Aren't I brilliant?"

Revel gave him a long look.

"Don't you think that if a man calling himself the Lord of Shadows was brilliant, that would be a problem?"

She scoffed and shook her head.

“Anyway, that is not what I am talking about. Your replacement! Do you really think that leaving that thing here won't cause any problems? If so... think again!"

Sunny coughed.

Admittedly, the last element of his plan was the most questionable. However, after considering it carefully, Sunny tended to believe that it would work.

That element was Vile.

Yes, Sunny was leaving many powerful tools to Revel. She would become Serpent's host, gain Saint's support, and control a fearsome moving stronghold. However, even that was not enough to make sure that the Forgotten Shore withstood the dreadful peril of the apocalypse.

And so... Sunny was leaving Vile behind, too. To be precise, he was leaving it behind as his replacement. Before entrusting the devilish creature to Saint and Revel, he convinced it to take a particular form — Sunny's own form, that was.

Vile could copy the powers of most beings whose essence it stole, and Sunny had been one of its victims. It had already showcased the ability to contain and command shades in the Tomb of Ariel, and beyond that... if it wanted to, it could create Dream Gates as well. Especially now that one of Sunny's shadows had become its own.

With its transformation into a fully fledged Shadow Creature complete, Vile was not a devil child anymore — it was a mischievous... and more than a little sinister... teenage Devil. So while Sunny indeed felt a bit hesitant to set that Devil free, he was not too worried.

That was because Saint would stay behind to keep an eye on Vile and make sure that it did not do anything too dreadful. Additionally...

Vile would spend almost all of its time on the Forgotten Shore. Sunny would have hesitated setting it loose in a place like Bastion or Ravenheart, but here? There were deadly frozen wastelands to the west, the even deadlier Nightmare Desert to the east, the Hollow Mountains and the Underworld to the south, and the haunted tangle of the Burned Forest to the north.

What was the worst Vile could do?

‘No, no... let's not think those words aloud...'

If it had been immediately after the Tomb of Ariel, Sunny might have hesitated more. But the vile spawn had lost a lot of its savage wildness over the few years it had spent in the embrace of human civilization, learning how to be more cautious.

So, Sunny had transferred half of his remaining shades to the brat, warned him sternly to be a good boy... girl... or whatever it was, and then had Saint give it a look.

For some unexplainable reason, the little wretch all but ignored his warnings, but suddenly grew demure and obedient as soon as Saint glanced at it with her cold, indifferent ruby eyes.

It was like a kid who knew that he could get away with a lot of things when dealing with his parents, but became the picture of good upbringing when staying at his strict, cool aunt's house.

‘I'm cool too, damn it...'

No, what was Sunny thinking? He wasn't and had never been that little devil's parent! He was just its temporary master!

In any case, Sunny had managed to both ensure the safety of the Forgotten Shore and further weaken his Domain with Vile's help. There were still thousands upon thousands of shades resting in his soul, many of them immensely powerful, but at least their number was not overwhelming anymore.

So...

There was only one thing left to do.

Sunny studied Revel for a bit, then smiled.

“Well? Are you ready?"

She sighed and nodded somberly.

"As ready as I'll ever be, I guess."

Sunny stood up and offered her his hand.

"Let's shake on it, then."

Revel stared at his hand for a while, then rose and took it.

As they shared a handshake, Sunny's serpent tattoo slivered down his arm and slowly slipped under Revel's sleeve. She shivered, her dark eyes widening slightly. And just like that, the bestowal was complete.

Sunny took a deep breath.

Revel would do well... he was sure she would. Saint would serve as her strength and command the legion of shades, both those hidden in her shadow and taken by Vile. Aiko, meanwhile, would handle the administrative side of running the Shadow Clan — and gods knew how capable she was.

The Forgotten Shore would endure the tides of apocalypse.

In fact, Sunny felt that even if the rest of humanity were to fall, this dark land would remain standing.

He felt a little wistful, but also content with his decisions.

‘It's for the best.'

His smile faltered a little, becoming faint.

"Hey..."

Revel's voice sounded full of some unknown, poignant emotion.

Turning his gaze back to her, Sunny raised an eyebrow in surprise.

"Yes?"

She stared at him silently for a second, then asked in the same deadpan tone:

“Can you perhaps let go now? We've been shaking hands for like half a minute..."

Sunny looked down, blinked a few times, and unhurriedly let go of Revel's hand.

His smile widened a little.

“Sure. Oh, and congratulations. I will leave these lands in your care... Lady of Shadows."

--- Chapter 3155 ---

Saint and her legion had settled in the area of the Dark City where the solemn square and the Dark Cathedral were located.

Vile made a home... a nest?... in the hidden chamber of the cathedral where Sunny had once lived for a few months.

Fiend was sent to Ravenheart, where he had built a lair in the furnace-like depths of the great volcano.

Nightmare had gone to Bastion to haunt its dreams.

Finally, Serpent coiled around the hill where the Bright Castle had once stood, its scales like a wall of black onyx. The Bright Castle was long gone, of course, and the Marvelous Mimic towered above the Dark City instead. On the vast platform in front of it, the Nameless Temple rested in the darkness. Its tall pillars and magnificent edifice were as black as the starless sky of the Forgotten Shore, and silence shrouded its spacious halls.

Things were a little different in the inner sanctum, though.

There, the sound of butter sizzling on a hot pan crackled loudly, and a dancing fire of a stove threw warm shadows on the stone walls. Someone was humming a lively melody.

Sunny was cooking.

His kitchen was quite a marvel of magical engineering by now, created with the help of three different kinds of sorcery. It had everything a person would need on the road to culinary perfection — which, as those enlightened knew, was no less perilous and insurmountable than the Path of Ascension itself.

Some of the items in the kitchen of the Nameless Temple had been forged by the King of Swords — his shadow, at least — enchanted by the Sovereign of Death, and burned with the radiant flames donated by the Star of Ruin.

Needless to say, there had only ever been a handful of mortals fortunate enough to taste the sublime food prepared by the owner of the Nameless Temple, the Lord of Shadows, Lost From Light. Rumors were that it was the most delicious thing one could taste in their lifetime... and after their death, as well.

Of course, the Lord of Shadows had spread that rumor himself.

Sadly, there were few people in the world who knew of his existence, so the rumor did not spread far.

"You know... I spent countless years searching for the ultimate truth. Pancakes or waffles? The question had haunted my dreams since before you Awakened."

Rain, who was sprawled comfortably on the cushions, gave him a lazy look.

"Oh, really?"

Sunny nodded.

"Indeed. But at the end of this calamitous search, having reached the very limits of comprehension, I finally attained enlightenment and understood that my question had been erroneous all along."

Flipping a piece of bread sizzling in the pan, Sunny smiled with the content tranquility of a living sage.

“French toast! French toast is the best. It is the undisputed king of breakfast foods. So, the competition between waffles and pancakes is entirely moot, to begin with."

He glanced at Rain and asked in a pleased tone:

“And do you know what the secret of a flawless French toast is? Be wary — the answer might shake the very foundation of what you know about the world."

Looking back at the pan, Sunny sighed.

"Stale bread. The bread has to be a little stale... that's the ultimate truth."

Rain, observing him from behind, said languidly:

"I sort of miss your pancakes, though."

Sunny froze.

His hand trembled, and his sagely smile cracked a little.

He remained silent for a few moments, and then asked in a forced tone:

"Well, why didn't you say so right away? No, no! It's fine... it's absolutely fine. I can make pancakes, as well!"

Soon, the two of them ascended to the ground floor of the Nameless Temple and entered its courtyard. There, beneath the branches of a towering tree, Sunny laid out an improvised picnic and set up a lantern.

A feast of a breakfast lay in front of Rain, with pancakes and French toast serving as the centerpiece. The delicious aroma permeated the air, and steam rose from a cup of fragrant tea, adding a refreshing note to it. She couldn't help but drool a little and wasted no time assaulting the generous spread with the ferocity of a starving abomination.

She had not forgotten her manners, of course.

“Thank you for the food!"

Sunny sat down on a cushion and watched her eat with a smile. This one wasn't sagely, but it was sincere.

When Rain was about done, he asked:

"How are Tamar and your friends doing?"

Rain leaned back in satisfaction, throwing a regretful look at the empty plates in front of her.

Her face was a little rosy.

"Shouldn't you know? Same as ever, I guess, only more so. Now that some time has passed since we all became Masters, the initial euphoria of having gained great power is mostly gone. The world is ending, though, and a Master is never idle. The work we do for the Shadow Clan keeps us busy."

Sunny was aware, since he had paid attention to all his mortal agents. Tamar and her cohort were not the only Masters in the Shadow Clan — there were quite a few now, actually — but they were his most elite team. So, the missions they received were all especially colorful.

Each one was worthy of being turned into a movie... a horror movie, possibly... but sadly, they were meant to remain unknown and hidden, so the public would never hear of their deeds.

Rain took a sip of tea and leaned on the trunk of the tree, looking up at its branches.

“Ah... that was nice. But you haven't cooked for me in a while. Is something the matter?"

Sunny remained silent, choosing his words. But before he could answer, she gave him a long look and sighed.

Looking away, Rain asked in a distant tone:

"You are leaving again, aren't you?"

Sunny hesitated for a moment, then nodded.

"Yes."

It was time to say goodbye.

--- Chapter 3156 ---

There was a long bout of silence. Then, Rain exhaled lightly and smiled.

Turning to Sunny, she shrugged.

"Well, it isn't the first time. You left to challenge the Second Nightmare, then to fight the Chain of Nightmares. You always return, though, don't you?"

Rain paused for a moment, and then added sullenly:

“Even if, sometimes, you do stuff like erasing yourself from everyone's memory and getting into my good graces again by pretending to be an eccentric immortal... who just happened to decide to become my teacher because of a fortuitous encounter..."

Her teasing was meant to lighten the mood, but Sunny did not respond.

Instead, he simply looked at her for a few long moments.

"I do tend to return. But, Rain... this time is different."

Her smile faltered.

Sunny looked down, brushing his fingers against the warm cup, then looked at the mighty tree Rain was leaning on. Finally, he spoke:

"I am going to be gone for a long while this time. But that... that is not all of it. The Fifth Nightmare is different from all the rest. Apotheosis is different from all other steps on the Path of Ascension. So, even if I do return... I might not be the same."

He felt something then. The painful sensation in his chest, grasping his heart like a vice — the undeniable reality that no matter what happened in the Nightmare, he was going to lose a part of himself. Perhaps an insignificant one... maybe a precious one, instead.

The person he had been all his life would be gone, replaced by a strange god.

Sunny inhaled deeply and looked at Rain.

‘Time really flies, doesn't it? But it also crawls like a snail.’

She wasn't the sweet toddler who used to follow him around their tiny apartment anymore. She wasn't an awkward teenager, either, or even a young woman tentatively coming to terms with her budding adulthood. Rain was in her mid-twenties now, having already become a Master. The little girl he remembered had blossomed into a real adult...

Somewhere in the middle of the apocalypse, Rain had outgrown his image of her. Having experienced both war and peace, she was now tall and strong — just like the tree behind her.

She was thriving.

Sunny smiled.

Rain didn't need to depend on him anymore. So, even if he was gone... even if he didn't return, or returned so direly changed that they would not recognize each other... she would be alright.

...That was a little painful, too.

He cradled the teacup in his hands.

"But it has to be done. What can I do? Your brother is just too awesome. So, there's no one else who can fill my shoes."

Rain tried to smile, but her eyes betrayed an inner turmoil.

She looked away, remained silent for a short while, and then spoke in a tone tinged with emotion.

“We keep missing each other, don't we?"

She took a deep breath.

"In this life... we were meant to spend it together, but instead, we spent most of it apart. And now, we are parting again. How is this fair?"

Sunny couldn't help but chuckle.

“There's no such thing as fair, so who knows?"

He paused for a moment.

"This world is so vast. It is so harsh, too. So many forces pulled us in different directions, but in the end, we still found each other, didn't we? Over and over again. To me... those times we spent together were more precious than you can ever imagine, Rain. And they always will be."

He took a deep breath, then exhaled slowly.

"So, I want you to know that even if I seem odd after I return... even if I am not who I used to be or treat you differently... I will always look over you. You say that we have spent most of our lives apart, but Awakened have long lives, Rain. There are countless years ahead of us. And yes, I might not be able to spend them all by your side, but I will always be there, somewhere. Thinking of you."

Sunny scratched the back of his head and added awkwardly:

"Well, unless I die, of course. But you know me — your brother is not easily killed. In fact, I pity the fool who tries to kill me."

Rain couldn't help but chuckle.

Afterward, she fell silent again and looked at him with a wry, bitter emotion hidden in her eyes.

She did not speak for a while, then asked:

"So, what? This is a goodbye?"

Sunny shook his head slightly.

“This... is a picnic. And a see you later — in a few years, hopefully. Before the world ends."

He reached forward and poured more tea into her cup.

His voice turned lower.

“Take care of yourself, Rain. Things are going to get worse before they get better. You are a Master now, but I know that you won't remain one for long... that means that in the years to come, you will be at the forefront of humanity's struggle to survive. I know that you will do well — that you will be exceptional. But, please, put yourself first. Remember that somewhere out there, someone is fighting to get back to you. So, for their sake as well, please put yourself above all else."

He looked at her and smiled.

"Oh... and this is for you."

Rain frowned in confusion.

“What is?"

Sunny gestured to the courtyard around them.

“This. The Nameless Temple — I am leaving it to you. Revel will take care of it until you become Transcendent, but it's all yours. This courtyard, this tree, the Citadel behind us. This, too, is your legacy."

He hesitated for a moment, then leaned forward and put a hand on her shoulder.

A spark of energy passed from his soul into hers, and the Nightmare Spell announced that he lost a Memory.

Sunny cleared his throat.

“And a small parting gift, as well."

Rain raised an eyebrow, then summoned the Memory and stared at it for a while.

Then, she asked in an incredulous tone:

“Your parting gift... is an ordinary rock?"

Sunny laughed.

“Believe me, there is nothing ordinary about it. It is a Memory that can record sounds. So... I left a few recordings for you to remember me by. If you ever feel like you miss me, you can summon this Memory and listen to one or two."

He paused for a moment, and then added:

“Then, you'll remember how obnoxious I was, and stop missing me immediately."

Looking at the Extraordinary Rock, Rain let out a quiet laugh.

"I see. Indeed. Okay then... thank you for the thoughtful gift, Brother."

She fell silent, stayed motionless for a while, and then gripped the rock tightly.

Raising her head, Rain looked Sunny in the eye and said:

"You... take care of yourself too, Sunny. I don't care what happens to you or how much you change. If becoming a god gives you a big head and you forget how to be human... how to be my brother... then I'll just remind you. I'll keep reminding you until you remember, so if you want to save yourself the trouble, come back whole."

Sunny met her gaze, lingered for a few moments, and then nodded.

There was nothing left to say.

"Goodbye, Rain."

The branches of the tree swayed above them, rustling under a lightless sky.

Just like the two of them, the tree had been born in the outskirts of NQSC. And just like the two of them, it was uprooted and thrown into a wide, perilous world. However, the tree did not perish — instead, it adapted. Now, against all odds, it was thriving in a land where there was no sun, offering its company to the ancient walls of a forgotten temple.

Its roots were robust and strong, penetrating deep into an unforgiving soil. There were three scars on its bark, left by a mischievous youth.

That youth was a man now, and he was leaving to face his Nightmare.

He was leaving many precious things behind in this pursuit, as well... things he was not willing to part with.

But he knew that he had to let them go if he wanted to protect them.

Maybe that was the difference between a youth and a man.

--- Chapter 3157 ---

The world had been rocked by astonishing news.

One stunning announcement followed another. Just a few years ago, Supremes had been singular beings, each no different from a cardinal direction — but now, six new Sovereigns rose to the throne of Supremacy at the same time. And they weren't just anybody, either. Each was a famed figure, either widely beloved or deeply feared, the stories of their various deeds having long become modern folklore.

The news caused a great uproar. People were stunned and rattled, feeling the foundations of the world shaking beneath them. They had many reasons to feel wary and alarmed, but strangely enough... most of all, they were elated.

In the brief period of time since the first Sovereigns revealed themselves, the very word became synonymous with strife and calamity. It wasn't long ago when most of the Supremes were known to have caused great harm to humanity — the Queen of Worms, the King of Swords, his son, the King of Nothing...

Even the Lord of Shadows, who had only lived a few minutes as a Supreme, immediately attempted to betray and kill his comrade and ally, Changing Star.

So, it would not be surprising if people were wary of the fact that six new Sovereigns were walking the earth now. However, the identity of these Sovereigns made all the difference.

Raised by Wolves and Nightingale were widely beloved. Soul Reaper Jet enjoyed the deep loyalty of all government soldiers, even if her reputation was chillingly fearsome. Nightwalker was a living legend, his image influenced by the goodwill people had towards the House of Night. And finally, there were Morgan of Valor and Song Seishan...

Even if the Song and Sword Domains were no more, countless people had lived and fought under their banners — quite recently, at that. A kingdom was more than its ruler, and while the King of Swords and the Queen of Worms were gone, their legacy remained. So, seeing Valor and Song rise from the ashes brought many people a sense of belonging, as well as an empowering feeling of stability.

Instead of being alarmed, people felt happy and more hopeful about the future because of the news of six new Sovereigns emerging. Supremes were the ultimate champions of humanity in the war against the Nightmare Creatures, after all, and in the span of a single day, their number had more than doubled.

The next news, however, was even more shocking.

Lady Nephis of Immortal Flame, the guiding star of humanity, announced that she would step down from her role as the ruler of the Human Domain and commander of its armies. Not only that, but she would also withdraw from the public entirely — going to face the Fifth Nightmare in the company of her trusted companion, Song of the Fallen.

If the previous news sent humanity into an uproar, then this one caused it to shake. Although Changing Star's reign had been brief, it had also been tectonic. The entire world had rallied around her, ignited with the passion and resolve to push back the encroaching Nightmare.

Humanity had won countless victories, broadened its territories in the Dream Realm, nurtured a great sea of new Awakened warriors, and begun migrating to a different world. It had achieved immense breakthroughs in both technology and sorcery, settling the vast expanse of untamed lands.

Its power to resist the endless tide of Nightmare Creatures had been greatly enhanced, and even with the advent of the apocalypse, humans were still fighting doggedly to survive and triumph.

It was Changing Star's conviction and leadership that had stopped the senseless bloodshed of a civil war, made all these advances possible, and preserved humanity in the early years of the apocalypse. Countless soldiers had been saved by her flames, and many more found hope and solace in her luminous light.

And now, their goddess was leaving, perhaps never to return.

Even if Nephis of Immortal Flame had made one miracle happen after another, there was no guarantee that she would survive the Fifth Nightmare. She had not spoken at length about the reason for her decision to challenge it, but people could deduce it themselves.

It was to ensure humanity's survival, since being merely Supreme — being a woman whose powers seemed deific and who was called a goddess, but wasn't a real deity — was not enough. It did not seem enough to Changing Star, at least.

People felt a wide range of emotions regarding her departure, but if there was one thing that united all of these feelings, it was that they were incredibly intense.

And while they were consumed by this emotional tempest, the next piece of news arrived.

Other things were changing, as well.

For two years, people in various parts of the Dream Realm had been expecting the return of their leaders, praying for their safety. The Steward of the West, the Steward of the East, the Steward of the South... people in Ravenheart, Bastion, and the Stormsea had grown used to their rulers, even if their reign had not been a long one.

But now that they had returned alive — and Supreme — it turned out that they would not be returning to their posts. Raised by Wolves, Nightingale, and Soul Reaper were going to take upon the duty of protecting Earth, instead, while Song Seishan, Morgan of Valor, Ananke of Weave, and Nightwalker would replace them as the rulers of the Dream Realm.

In short...
