Things had been changing swiftly in the apocalypse, but now, everything seemed to have changed in an instant.

And as people were reeling, the new Supremes arrived in the Great Citadels of humanity to establish their Domains.

Nightwalker climbed onto the deck of the Night Garden, where the members of his clan were waiting at the front of a crowd of people. He flashed them a smile and then raised a fist, inhaling the salty breeze that blew from the sea with a full chest.

In Ravenheart, where the influence of the Song clan had never truly waned due to the popularity of Ki Song's daughters, a sea of people gathered on the streets, cheering as Seishan, the new queen, walked through it and across the great bridge to the gates of the Jade Palace, followed by her sisters.

Even though most members of the Valor family had been eradicated by the King of Nothing and its influence was all but gone, Morgan was met with cheers and ovations as well, a torrent of vermillion flags billowing in the wind behind her as a column of Ascended knights followed her on mighty Echo mounts. The steel of their heavy armor glistened in the sun, resembling a river of steel that flowed toward the Mirror Lake.

...Sunny, Effie, Kai, and Jet watched the procession from the shore of the Ivory Island high above, sitting leisurely on the emerald grass and sharing a bottle.

None of them could really get drunk, but the taste of good wine was still pleasant on a warm day like today.

"Look at her go..."

Effie clicked her tongue and took a large sip, letting out a satisfied sigh afterward.

Then, she raised the bottle and said in a bright tone:

"To Morgan of Valor, long may she reign. Ah, say what you want about that woman... but she really knows how to throw a parade."

She paused for a moment, took another sip, and smiled.

"And to us. Let's drink together again, the four of us, after this whole Fifth Nightmare business is over."

--- Chapter 3158 ---

Sunny smiled and remained silent, taking the bottle from Effie.

He had gotten back from the Forgotten Shore only this morning, and in a few hours, he would be gone. Behind them, in the Ivory Tower, Nephis and Cassie were finishing the last of their preparation and addressing the Fire Keepers. His own farewells had already been said.

The three freshly baked Sovereigns, meanwhile, were in the strange interim period where their duties had already been decided, but did not become reality yet. An army of bureaucrats, administrators, and military officers were feverishly rearranging the whole framework of how humanity functioned at the moment. Until the logistical side of the leadership change caught up, Effie, Kai, and Jet had precious little to do.

It was all too sudden and not at all ideal, bound to cause damage across both worlds... but also a part of the process. If Sunny and Nephis wanted to ensure a flawless transition, they would have had to spend years arranging everything properly. That delay, however, would have caused even more harm.

Now that the apocalypse was in full swing, Sunny had to abandon the idea of doing things without suffering losses. Somewhere along the way, everything had become an issue of mitigating the damage, not avoiding it altogether. It was a shift in mentality that he did not want to accept, but also a necessary one.

So, this hasty transition was, in fact, a good trial run of the dire changes to come.

Once pieces of Earth started to fuse with the Dream Realm en masse and the situation worsened even further, with unexpected calamities striking without warning on a regular basis, humanity would have to learn how to function with utmost effectiveness despite the utter chaos. Taking a sip of the wine and appreciating its flavor, Sunny smiled wistfully and looked at the bottle.

This bottle, too, was a symbol of humanity's perseverance and adaptability. The grapes used to brew the wine were a strain developed in Ravenheart from Godgrave vines, then cultivated in the uniquely fertile soil of the Night Garden. The beautiful bottle itself was produced in the Glass Hell and was sturdy enough to be used as a weapon.

In fact, humanity had three superb bread baskets now. Ravenheart with its rich volcanic soil, the Night Garden with its mystical enchantments, and Effie's Domain that had been infused with a fragment of War God's own vitality. Silver Web was exceptionally productive due to Ananke's augmentation, as well. As long as these treasuries were still in human hands, people would not starve, at least.

Sunny looked at his friends and grinned.

“Wow... look at that. All three of my interns have become Supreme! That is, like, a one-hundred-percent satisfaction guarantee. Am I not the greatest mentor in history? Honestly, even I am amazed at myself."

The three of them looked at him wryly. Eventually, Jet chuckled.

“Yeah, way to go, genius. We conquered the Fourth Nightmare, but you still managed to make it sound like your personal achievement, somehow. That's real talent right there."

Effie nodded, while Kai simply smiled.

“But yes... thank you, Sunny. I don't think we would have returned if it wasn't for the experience of those three expeditions. Not all of us, at least.”

Sunny waved a hand. He passed the bottle to Jet, remained silent for a few moments, and then said:

"Azarax, huh?"

He looked into the distance.

"After hearing about your Nightmare... I really want to return to the Nightmare Desert, find the bastard, and put him back on that tree."

After that, Sunny shivered.

“Although I'd better wait until I am Sacred. Or Divine. Let me tell you, that place is called the Nightmare Desert for a reason."

Effie shook her head slowly, a shadow briefly running over her eyes.

"That guy has already received his punishment. Now, the Shadow God's curse swallowed him up... all that remains is a husk. He'll probably become a problem one day in the future, but someone else can deal with him. We don't have a monopoly on dealing with terrible crap, do we?"

She grinned and looked at Sunny with curiosity.

“Our Nightmare is in the past, though. But yours will begin soon. So, how do you feel?"

Sunny remained silent for a bit, then shrugged.

“Alright, I guess. If anything, I feel... unburdened. I basically got rid of all my earthly possessions, so it's all a bit weird."

He smiled faintly.

“Every time I entered a Nightmare before, I was wary of what awaited me in the Seed. But now, strangely enough, I am not that worried about the Nightmare itself. I am only worried about its aftermath — how much time will pass, how the world will fare without me... how much I will change."

Kai sighed.

“It feels strange to us, as well."

He looked at the procession of knights far below, which was now approaching the Mirror Lake. A sea of scarlet banners billowed in the wind, and around it, a vast city was boiling with life.

Kai's expression turned a little wistful. "We entered the Second Nightmare together. We went into the Third one together, as well. So, except for the First, you have never challenged a Nightmare without us... I can't help but worry."

Sunny chuckled.

"Now you know how I felt when you went into the Seed."

Jet took a sip of the wine, glanced at it, and passed the bottle to Kai.

"I haven't been with you three in the Second Nightmare, but I did watch over this guy during his First."

She paused and then smiled.

Of course, that was to kill him in case he failed... but, still. Kind of makes me sentimental to remember. And look at us now. We are literally on top of the world."

Sunny scratched the back of his head.

“Apart from the fact that it's the wrong world, everything seemed to have turned out great. Well, except for the fact that it's the apocalypse. So, there are two facts — we are on top of the wrong world, and that world is ending. Come to think of it, I take it back. Everything seems to have turned out terribly."

He laughed.

Eventually, Sunny's laughter died out. He lingered for a while, then sighed.

“From before I entered the Academy until now, I had suffered both great and terrible luck. Sometimes, it threw me into situations that seemed inescapable, and sometimes, it saved me from perils that felt insurmountable. But, looking back..."

He glanced at Effie, Kai, and Jet.

“It's clear to me now that my greatest fortune has always been somehow meeting the right people. There are so many people without whom I wouldn't have made it that far, and among them... meeting you three was truly my greatest blessing.”

Sunny smiled.

“Usually, after saying something so earnest, I would immediately follow it up with a joke to handle the aftermath. But, uh... you've just returned from your Nightmare, and I am leaving for mine. Who knows when we will get the chance to see each other again? So, I just wanted to say thank you. For tolerating me for all these years and helping me become who I am. For everything."

The three of them studied him for a few moments.

Then, Jet smiled and waved a hand.

"It's me who should be thanking you, Sunny. For coming with me to Antarctica. For surviving. For helping me become a Saint. And simply for being there for me... meeting you has been a great fortune for me, as well."

Effie nodded.

“Mine too. There is a lot I am thankful for... besides everything, you are also the reason I got to meet my husband and become Little Ling's mom. He would have died somewhere in Antarctica without you, along with countless others. So, don't sell yourself short."

She paused, and then added with a mischievous grin:

“Although you are short..."

Sunny threw a scathing glare her way.

Kai, meanwhile, simply nodded.

“I'd probably still be in that well in the Dark City if it wasn't for you. Well, my bones would be."

He fell silent for a moment before speaking with a smile.

“But let us stop here. This... this is starting to sound suspiciously like a goodbye. And I refuse to say goodbye to you, Sunny."

Kai finished the wine and shook his head.

“We will meet each other again. We will have countless years to enjoy each other's company. So, there's no need to rush... go into your Nightmare with an easy mind, Sunny. The world you are leaving behind will be fine. We'll take care of it."

As Sunny watched, Jet and Effie nodded. He sighed, feeling emotions swell in his chest.

This precious moment... was ending. It was already over, and now, he really had to leave.

"Well, then. In that case..."

Rising from the grass, Sunny dusted himself off and smiled.

"I guess it's time to go. Knowing all of you... has been an honor and a privilege. Until we meet again.”

With that, he vanished.

He had left the world behind.

--- Chapter 3159 ---

Sunny, Nephis, and Cassie entered the waking world together. It met them with the same kind of inhospitable pressure they had long grown accustomed to, straining to push them back into the depths of the Dream Realm — although now that Sunny's Domain was smaller, that pressure felt slightly less intense.

There was no fanfare. Everything that needed to be said had already been said, and everything that could have been done was already done. They did not need to pack anything or prepare equipment, either. Supremes did not need a lot to sustain themselves and could carry a lot in their Soul Seas. So, the three of them looked like they were going on a casual walk.

Even if they were leaving to challenge the most dire of Nightmares.

The manor of the Immortal Flame clan was quiet, since the Fire Keepers were in the Dream Realm at the moment. So was Smile of Heaven, who had long resided in the Ivory Tower — now that both Nephis and Cassie were going away, Effie was going to look after her.

It was not only Effie who would remain on the Ivory Island, either. Kai and Jet would be based there as well, taking turns watching over the waking world. The Fire Keepers would remain an independent force ready to assist any of the four Domains that spanned the Dream Realm now, while the Wolves and the Night Singers would return to Earth.

But these... these were not issues Sunny had to concern himself with anymore.

He used Shadow Step to bring Nephis and Cassie out of NQSC, into the depths of the toxic wasteland beyond. They had a long way to go and little time to waste, hurried by the need to reach their destination before the War Realm tossed them out.

Still, Sunny allowed himself a few moments of reflection while taking in the desolate landscape around them.

"Funny."

His voice was quiet.

“Outside used to mean death... especially to us, people from the outskirts, who lived closer to it than anyone else. The thought of leaving the city was no different from contemplating suicide. We were so scared of it that, most of the time, we forced ourselves to forget that it even existed."

He inhaled deeply and then grimaced.

“But now, it's like going on a picnic. I am not sure if that is because I am much more difficult to kill now, or because I have experienced countless places that were far worse than this."

As if responding to his comment, a chilling howl resounded somewhere in the distance, and he sensed numerous shadows converging on their location.

They were the shadows of the new masters of Earth — the Nightmare Creatures. People liked to believe that the waking world still belonged to them, but in truth, most of its surface had been populated by abominations for a long while now. Just like humans were settling the Dream Realm, the Nightmare Creatures were settling Earth... and they were far more successful colonizers than mankind.

Nephis looked around, too.

"This land will flourish again."

Her voice was even and resolute.

She bent down and picked up a handful of dry, lifeless soil. It spilled through her fingers like dust, flowing down in a dark stream.

“When it is all over, and the Nightmare Spell is no more, once we've won... there will be those who will bring it back to life.”

She paused for a moment, and then added:

“Maybe we will."

They moved on.

The desolate reaches of the Northern Quadrant were teeming with Nightmare Creatures, but none of them were powerful enough to cause three Supremes serious trouble. Sunny moved with startling speed, as well, carrying Nephis and Cassie through the shadows. It did not take them long to reach the edge of the continent, where a deep ocean washed over its shore.

From there, they took to the sky.

East, east...

Across the ocean.

As they flashed across the heavens, moving from the radiance of day into the dark shroud of the night, Sunny was somewhat surprised to see how swiftly they were devouring distance. He had rarely traveled this way in the waking world, and the Dream Realm was vast — far more spacious than Earth.

But then again, with how swiftly Awakened moved — especially those of higher Ranks — it had to be. The endless expanse of that alien world had seemed too daunting once, but now, it felt ordinary.

Long before the strain of remaining in the waking world became unbearable, they finally crossed the ocean and landed on an unfamiliar shore. Around them, the air was acrid with the smell of sulfur, and great pillars of smoke were rising into the sky on the horizon. Those were the volcanoes that had awakened in the aftermath of the Category Five Gate opening, blanketing the world with ash.

Sunny, Nephis, and Cassie stood on the outskirts of a dead city. The streets were empty and forlorn; the buildings had collapsed or were staring at them with empty windows. Everything was covered by ash, and rusted remains of destroyed ships protruded from the tumultuous water in the harbor.

The landscape — the vast expanse of ashen mounds, the colossal pillars of smoke supporting a dark plane of clouds that obscured the sky, the deteriorated ruins of a lifeless city — was alien and strange, as if they were still in the Dream Realm instead of on Earth.

This was America.

The first continent humanity had lost to the tide of Nightmare Creatures, as well as the place where Immortal Flame and Smile of Heaven had perished while trying to buy as many people as possible time to evacuate. Looking at the ruins, Sunny felt a dull ache in his chest.

All of it looked too familiar.

Ash replaced the snow, and the layout of the city was different. But it reminded him terribly of Falcon Scott — of the mournful devastation of Antarctica.

He sighed.

There, in the shadows of the vast ruin, something was already moving, awakening

due to their presence. Nightmare Creatures were crawling out of their lairs, attracted by the scent of human souls.

Glancing at Nephis, Sunny frowned and moved forward.

“Come. Let's not linger."

They had to find the Nightmare Gate that had killed this land.

--- Chapter 3160 ---

Sunny and Nephis could have eradicated the Nightmare Creatures that populated the slaughtered city. In truth, they could probably have slain every abomination in America. Even the unknown Cursed One who was presumed to dwell on this continent was not an insurmountable challenge — in fact, their track record of battling Cursed Creatures was quite spotless so far.

Perhaps Nephis wanted to avenge the destruction of her family, as well as too many other families to count.

But they had not come to America to fight this time.

Fighting a Cursed abomination on Earth could very well cause it irreparable damage. The planet itself would be fine, but billions of humans still populating it could perish.

Take America, for example... the massive volcanic eruption caused by the calamity that had happened here caused temperatures to drop across all Quadrants. The natural disasters that followed were devastating. If not for the fact that humans had caused several such cataclysmic events themselves in the past, and therefore knew how to survive them, they could have gone extinct by now.

New abominations would emerge from the Nightmare Gates eventually, anyway — if the whole continent wasn't swallowed by the Dream Realm even before that. Besides, slaying endless hordes of Nightmare Creatures and battling a Cursed One was going to take time they did not have. They had come here to find the Seed, not to hunt abominations. So, no matter how meaningful this place was to Nephis, they had to move stealthily instead of engaging in all-out slaughter.

She was looking at the ruins with a distant expression on her face, white sparks dancing in the depths of her eyes.

Sunny looked at her with concern and asked quietly:

“What are you thinking about?"

Nephis remained silent for a while, then sighed and pulled her gaze away from the lifeless remains of the city.

"..The price of failure.”

She paused for a moment and added in a deeper tone:

“And the merit of trying, anyway."

Immortal Flame and Smile of Heaven must have known that they would most likely die here. They had been mere Masters, after all. Even if no one had ever seen a Gate like the one that opened in America, they understood how terrifying the Nightmare Creatures that emerged from the apocalyptic Gate would be.

And yet, they still attempted to stall them so that more people could survive.

America still fell. Countless lives were still lost. But not quite as many as would have been without their efforts.

But would the world have been better off if Immortal Flame and Smile of Heaven had chosen to save themselves instead of helping the civilians?

There was no way to tell. Broken Sword might have been still alive. The Sovereigns might never have turned on each other. There could have been no Godgrave, no Dream Plague...

Nephis might not have grown up being hunted like an animal and watching her clan slowly wither and die.

The world would have definitely been different... unrecognizable, really. But better? Sunny was not sure.

He gripped her shoulder briefly and looked away.

“All I can say is that if I were in their place... I probably would have made the same choice."

The soldiers of the Evacuation Army had known that many of them — maybe most of them — would not return from Antarctica. But that did not stop them. An overwhelming enemy was nothing new in the Age of the Nightmare Spell. Humans faced insurmountable odds all the time, but they still had to continue fighting.

Cassie, who stood nearby with her hand resting on the hilt of the Quiet Dancer, turned her head slightly at that moment.

"It's strange."

She hesitated for a moment, then raised a hand and briefly touched her blindfold.

“The Cursed One... I cannot sense it."

The Nightmare Gate was hidden in the very heart of the continent, a thousand miles away. But to someone as sensitive as Cassie, such distance was not an obstacle. Even if she could not learn anything about the Gate Guardian, she should have been able to feel an echo of its presence, at least. Sunny frowned.

Come to think of it, he did not feel anything, either. America was that thing's territory... its influence on the world should have already begun interfering with his Will, by now.

But while the atmosphere of America was oppressive, there was nothing.

The three of them were suddenly uneasy. An enemy who instilled fear with its mere presence was a dangerous foe. A being who concealed itself so utterly that even its power could not be felt, though... that was a far more frightening adversary.

An ambush predator was meant to be weaker than a true hunter, but it was also far deadlier.

“Let's proceed cautiously."

Leaving the ruined city and all the Nightmare Creatures that populated it behind, they rushed inland. By now, the strain of remaining in the waking world was pressing on them heavily, and as they moved closer to the source of the unimaginable devastation, the Call of Nightmare grew louder and louder, almost impossible to resist.

The Call of the apocalyptic Gate that had opened in America decades ago was unlike anything Sunny had ever endured. It was powerful, magnetic, irresistible... if not for the harrowing experience of witnessing the true Tomb of Ariel, he would have been tempted to succumb to it entirely. But everything paled in comparison to that terror.

They saw more destroyed cities on the way. They saw wreckages of military machines and signs of a desperate struggle, as well. The forces of humanity seemed to have been instantly overwhelmed, having offered little resistance — how could they, when the enemy had been of a much higher Rank?

The whole continent was like a graveyard... an empty, desecrated graveyard drowning in ash and blackened ruins. It was the sight that sent chills running down Sunny's spine, as if he was looking at an ominous depiction of what all of the world would look like one day soon.

They crossed a desert and a grand canyon that split the earth like a festering wound. They crossed a rocky mountain chain, as well. Finally, descending into vast lowlands, they moved across them with as much speed as they could muster.

And then, they finally found the Nightmare Gate that had stolen this continent from humanity.

It towered above the world like a great pillar of darkness, visible from hundreds of kilometers away. But as they drew closer, its true width was revealed. The abhorrent fissure swallowed several kilometers of the desolate plain, its seething darkness moving eerily in the absence of light.

They found the Cursed abomination that guarded the Gate, as well.

It lay on the ground in front of the vast fissure, its flesh itself like a mountain. There were countless limbs, an endless expanse of pale flesh, and a terrible maw that could swallow entire Citadels...

And blood. There was a sea of black, fetid blood surrounding the ghastly behemoth, soaking the barren land and forming a dark and motionless lake.

"Its name was Desolation."

As Sunny, Nephis, and Cassie stared at the dead god in stunned silence, a voice resounded from their side.

Flinching, Sunny turned and saw a man sitting on a slab of broken concrete — even though there had not been anyone there a moment before.

The man was wiping his hands with a piece of cloth, the fabric soaked with black blood. There was a subtly revolted expression on his face, and a detached coldness in his eyes.

Sunny also saw his own reflection on their mirror-like surface.

He grimaced.

"Look who decided to show up. How the hell did you..."

“How did I manage to kill that thing without destroying half of the planet?"

Mordret shrugged with seeming indifference.

“It wasn't that difficult, really. I simply lured it into my Mirror Realm and killed it there."

He smiled darkly and threw the cloth away. Rising, Mordret inhaled deeply and massaged his shoulder with a hint of displeasure.

"Granted, it was merely the sparing the planet part that was easy. The killing itself was... ah, it was quite unpleasant."

He bowed slightly to Cassie and then turned to face Nephis.

“I would prefer it if we didn't linger. The smell is quite dreadful.”

She studied him for a moment.

“So, you've decided to join us in the Nightmare, after all?"

Mordret remained silent for a short while, then looked around and smiled slightly.

“Well... it seems to me that I have gotten here first. So, if anything, it is you who are joining me."

She tilted her head slightly, then nodded.

“In that case, we shall proceed. It's... good to have you with us."

Mordret seemed slightly surprised to hear those words.

The rest was easy. Far easier than Sunny had expected, which hinted that everything that followed would be impossibly hard. They simply crossed the realm boundary, attempting to return to the place where their tethers had been placed. However,

instead, they were pulled toward the Seed by the Call of Nightmare.

Thrown violently off course, Sunny found himself in an unfamiliar place.

The ground was white and as hard as stone. The sky... was black and jagged. Half of it was, at least — the other was blindingly white, suffused with incandescent glow. Light poured down like a waterfall, flakes of ash dancing in it like snowflakes.

And there was something else, as well.

A suffocating, animalistic feeling of fear that suddenly grasped Sunny’s heart. The same kind of fear he had felt in the Underworld, standing on the edge of the abyss and gazing into its depths.

As if he was in the presence of an Unholy Nightmare Creature.

Feeling a suffocating heat, Sunny froze. His intuition was telling him that if he moved, he would dearly regret it.

The Call of Nightmare was deafening here.

[Stay still, Sunny.]

The four of them had been separated while crossing the realm boundary, so Sunny could only hear Cassie, not see her.

He hesitated for a moment, then asked.

[Where are we?]

But even before she answered, he already put two and two together.

The strange texture of the ground beneath him, the irregular shape of the sky, and that name, Desolation...

Sunny suppressed an unbelieving chuckle. The jagged sky... was no sky at all. It was bone — the jagged edge was where the bone had been broken, and the blinding radiance spilling into the immense breach was one he was all too familiar with.

It was the incinerating sunlight of Godgrave.

After all this time, they had returned to this cursed place. In fact, they entered a part of it that even Anvil and Ki Song had not dared to disturb.

They were inside the titanic skull of the colossal skeleton.

And the Seed they were searching for... was right at its center, in the great Hollow where the dead god's brain would have been.

They were not alone here, either.

‘Another... damn... Unholy...’

Despite the suffocating heat, cold sweat flowed down Sunny's back.

[Sunny, listen to me carefully.]

He had no other choice, since moving meant being burned to ash by the sky of Godgrave.

Cassie seemed to take a deep breath.

[You should feel by now the direction the Call is coming from. That is where the Seed is... once I tell you, run toward it as fast as you can. That is the only way we will survive — if we reach the Seed faster than the thing that dwells here reaches us.]

Sunny cursed inwardly.

[When will that be?]

Cassie did not respond immediately.

[Once the clouds close... now!]

Sunny flinched.

‘Now? Is that an example, or...’

Even while thinking that, he was already flying through the shadows.

Faster, and faster, and faster still.

Feeling something vast and ancient stirring in the darkness behind him.

Sunny did not know where Nephis, Mordret, and Cassie were. They would have entered the Dream Realm somewhere in the vicinity of the Seed, as well, but the skull of the titanic skeleton was vast. At the moment, they were probably rushing toward the Seed just like he was, knowing that only by reaching it they could survive. But would they make it?

Would he make it?

Sunny did not know.

The transition from the feeling of being powerful and all but invincible to small and defenseless was too jarring.

Sensing that something malevolent had noticed him, Sunny attempted to accelerate even further.

'Faster, damn it!'

Who would have thought that he would run toward a Seed at full speed one day, praying to dive into a Nightmare sooner?

Sunny gritted his teeth and turned into a shadow.

[Cassie, what about...]

And there, finally, he saw the Seed.

It was vast and appalling, hanging in the

darkness like a pulsating tumor. Infecting the world with an endless stream of Corruption.

The grotesque sight made Sunny's heart skip a beat. The Call washed over him like a tide, throwing his mind into disarray.

He was so close.

Witnessing the great Seed, Sunny threw himself at it...

And, without ever slowing down, plunged into its vile depths.

There, he heard a vaguely familiar voice whispering into his ear.

[Welcome, Lost from Light!]

[Prepare for your Fifth Nightmare...]

[End of volume thirteen: Prelude to Apocalypse.]

--- Chapter 3161 ---

In the beginning, the world was vast.

The day sky shining upon it was the realm of Sun God. The night sky shrouding it in darkness was the realm of Storm God. The pale moon moving across the sky was the eye of Beast God, and it illuminated the mortal realms below.

The mortal realms sprawled far and wide, populated by all manner of beasts and creatures — as well as men.

Below the red dust of the mortal world lay the peaceful darkness of Shadow God's domain.

The realm of Heart God, meanwhile, existed in the souls of living things.

And in the heart of it all, imprisoned, was the Void.

...The world was vast, but the shadow was small.

And since the world was full of horrors, the shadow was afraid.

It crawled out of the water, hid in a dark place, and shook, feeling the ground around it quake and groan under the heavy footsteps of history.

No. The Demon of Desire, Hope, had not invented writing yet, so there was no history. The world groaned under the footsteps of the gods, who walked its surface — as well as others like them, who were more terrifying than fear itself.

For they were Creatures of the Void.

In the beginning, when the world was young, the gods still fought against those few of their kin who had escaped the cage of existence during its creation. The shadow clung to the cold stones of its dark cave, terrified.

For a long time, that was all it knew. It didn't even know itself.

Outside the cave, the world was changing.

One day, a harrowing, colossal form fell from the sky, impacting the earth like a dying planet. Its death cries shattered the heavens, and its fall broke the world. The ground splintered and rose in molten waves, forming towering ridges. The being's blood flowed into the dark depths like a sea, and before it could rise again, another shape plummeted from the fractured sky to press it down.

The first being was vast and harrowing. The second was beyond the concept of horror — bestial and ferocious, it was so great as to be entirely unfathomable.

The moon served as that being's eye.

Its infinite maw was full of fearsome fangs, and with those fangs, it tore into the fallen being, rending its flesh and spirit apart. The fangs cleaved the molten earth, as well, shaping it into tall and jagged mountains.

That was Beast God slaying a great Creature of the Void.

Once the creature was dead, Beast God devoured its endless expanse and slept for a while in the molten cradle. Centuries passed, and the world slowly cooled. The Hollow Mountains took shape, and the great caverns of the Underworld were formed below them. The blood of the slain creature became true darkness, and white mist seeped into existence through the fractures in the broken fabric of reality.

Finally, Beast God stirred awake, displeased by the cold, rose from the ground, and returned into the dark embrace of the night sky.

The shadow trembled.

Another day, a horror so terrifying that it defied description — defied being cognized or conceived of, let alone comprehended — rose from the depths. All six of the great gods fought it together, and it was only when the daemons joined them that they finally managed to drive the Void Being back down.

However, they couldn't kill it.

Instead, Sun God placed a prohibition on the absolute laws of existence, eliminating the concept of warmth and movement from the waters where the terrifying being of the everlasting Void dwelled. The ocean turned to ice, imprisoning the Void Creature in its depths. A vicious cold emanated from the frozen ocean, swallowing the lands around it and turning them into a frigid, lifeless wasteland.

The cold continued to seep into the world, spreading slowly.

Many other things happened, as well.

A small sapling turned into a great tree, its roots reaching the depths of the Shadow Realm while its branches supported the heavens.

A vast forest grew around it, becoming a blissful shelter for all living things. In time, however, rot and corruption spread under its branches, and it wasn't until the Demon of Repose created the seasons that its endless hunger for growth was confined.

Humans abandoned the cradle of the primordial forest and ventured into the vast expanse of the world.

The cage of existence was almost broken by the crushing strength of the Stone Titan, who was eventually destroyed by the Demon of Dread.

All memories of Dream God were erased from existence, leaving an echoing absence.

The divine syzygy splintered into myriad realms.

A nasty bird stole Weaver's eye.

Mirage, the Demon of Imagination, built a system of artificial lakes and created the concept of reflections. Because of her, the world was able to look upon itself for the first time.

Some were enamored by their reflections; some were dismayed...

The shadow didn't look.

Reflections did not exist in the darkness, and it was reluctant to abandon its lightless shelter.

It wasn't really interested in its appearance, anyway — however, because of that disinterest...

The shadow became aware of its own existence.

It had existed for a long time, but it had never been aware of itself. Now, the thought of being indifferent to its looks made the shadow realize that it had to exist in order to look like something.

And so, the shadow asked itself a question.

‘Who am I?'

It did not know.

It did not remember.

Or, rather, it remembered too much.

The shadow vaguely remembered living myriad lives, being myriad creatures. In one life, it had been a beast hunting powerless prey. In another, a hunter slaying the beast.

In one life, it had been a king.

In another... A slave.

All of its numerous lives had been different. Some had been short, some had been long. Some had been spent in the embrace of the Flame, some drowned by the rot of Corruption.

There was only one thing uniting them all — it was death.

The shadow might have lived myriad different lives, but they all ended the same way. Death was the only constant in its strange existence, so it was what the shadow knew best.

Death felt like home.

Death was familiar, soothing, and peaceful. Life, however, was violent and full of strife. The weight of myriad lives had been arduous and overwhelming, and so the shadow was tired.

After escaping the endless cycle of rebirth, the shadow had fallen into water, sought shelter in a dark cave, and forgotten itself. It hid in the darkness while the world was in the throes of the Age of Gods.

The shadow was still tired of life, but having rested for a long while, it didn't feel as exhausted anymore. And so, as the tribes of humans spread across the mortal realms, fighting against the Creatures of Corruption that dominated the world beyond the safe haven of the Divine Realms, it asked itself a second question.

‘What am I?'

The shadow's memories were endless, impossible to encompass, and contradictory. It didn't know a lot while at the same time knowing too much. However, one thing that the shadow did understand was that a creature like it was not supposed to exist.

All beings were meant to live for a while, then find eternal peace in the embrace of death. The shadow, however, remembered dying myriad times, but it was always forced to return to the harsh embrace of life.

It vaguely remembered living — and dying — thousands upon thousands of times. Hundreds of thousands?

The shadow was not entirely sure.

It repeated the cycle of life and death over and over, over and over, over and over again... eternal, ever-changing... until it was shaped into the being it was now.

In some lives, the world was similar to how it seemed — governed by the great gods and populated in equal measure by mortals and abominations. In some, the gods were distant and indifferent, with mortals reigning over myriad realms. In some, the gods were dead, and the world was swallowed by Corruption. There were strange cities with towering buildings made from metal and people who did not know who the gods had been.

The shadow remembered the bitter smell of gunpowder drifting over a towering alloy wall, the deafening thunder of firing turrets, soldiers, and MWPs fusing into a somber litany under the light of a crimson aurora...

It also remembered staying behind as the Demon of Dread laid siege to the Realm of Death in the final battle of a world-ending war, its siblings fighting against the endless legion of shadows as gods and daemons clashed in the boundless darkness above them.

The shadow remembered Hope straining to break free of its chains. It remembered spending thousands of years being devoured by a profane vine... it also remembered being killed, kneeling, as the vine first took hold within its body.

The memories were endless, and some of them contradicted each other. Some came from the past, while many came from the future... from various futures, each more fantastical than the previous one.

It all felt like a dream.

‘Ah... a dream.'

The shadow realized that it had been asleep for a long time. And so, it felt like this world... this beautiful, harrowing world... was nothing but a dream it dreamt.

‘No, not a dream.'

It was a nightmare.

The shadow dreamt a nightmare, and in that nightmare, it had been forced to relive the lives of all the creatures it had killed. Hundreds of thousands of them...

The number was an answer that seemed to hint at what kind of being the shadow had been.

It would have been appalled and terrified, but its feelings had long been numbed by the weight of myriad lives the shadows had lived. So, it accepted it with indifference.

The shadow felt like it was forgetting something... something important. Something vital, or perhaps even precious. But even if that was true, the shadow did not really care to remember what it was, either.

Its curiosity sated and feeling no desire to explore its murderous past, the shadow settled comfortably and prepared to return to its slumber.

However, at that moment, it was disturbed. Something was moving at the mouth of the cave...

Someone was making noise in its quiet shelter.

Displeased, the shadow stirred and sighed, directing its senses to the uninvited guest. It was greatly displeased.

A strange word surfaced from the depths of its calloused being...

‘Damnation.'

--- Chapter 3162 ---

During the awe and horror of the dawn of time, the shadow had confined its senses within the cave, trying to make itself blind to the world. It wanted to become as small as possible, so that the terrifying giants that walked the earth could not see it — could not sense it watching them, and therefore become aware of its existence.

Now, however, the shadow was forced to take a look outside.

In an instant, its senses spread across hundreds of miles, encompassing the movement and texture of every creature, insect, and blade of grass swaying in the wind in the lands that surrounded its shelter.

...The world had grown small while the shadow rested.

Its cave had ended up in one of the mortal realms. The boundary of the realm felt like a moving stream to the shadow's senses — easy enough to cross, if one didn't mind getting wet.

Not that the shadow wanted to do such a thing.

Its senses encompassed a region of the primal realm that was covered by craggy mountains, green valleys, and forests. The youthful world was pure and untamed, unsullied by the devastating splendor of civilization. Myriad beasts and creatures populated its wild expanse...

And abominations, too.

They hid in the dark corners of existence, just like the shadow did. They were the beings of the Flame who had been corrupted by the Void, driven mad by the insatiable need to destroy that which they had lost, all in a futile effort to reclaim it.

They roamed the world, hunting the children of the Flame in a tortured frenzy, and infected everything around them with the appalling rot of Corruption.

Where there was life, there was Corruption. And those Corrupted were the rulers of all lands that fell beyond the cleansing fury of the gods.

The gods were great and vast... the gods themselves were beings of the Void. So what did they care about these small abominations?

The shadow did not care, either.

However, now, there was a scent of blood drifting into the cave it had chosen as its shelter. Out there near the entrance, a human was crawling across the jagged stones, leaving a trail of blood in his wake. The man was dressed in crude garments made from fur and hide, his weathered face hidden by a bushy beard. His body was covered in gruesome wounds, and his eyes were full of pain and despair.

As a hoarse groan escaped from his mouth, a grating sound came from behind him. There, a towering abomination broke through the wall of tall trees, shattering them into splinters. It was tall and imposing, blood streaming down from between its bestial fangs, its vaguely humanoid shape both gaunt and menacing.

The abomination was wounded, too, but it was nowhere near the man’s grievous state. It fell on all fours, glaring at him with murderous fury. Its powerful hind legs tensed, ready to send the creature into a deadly lunge, and its long tail whipped like a bone spear.

The man was about to perish gruesomely in the creature's hideous maw.

The shadow did not care whether he lived or died.

It had experienced hundreds of thousands of deaths, after all, so what was one more? It was not worth the effort of feeling anything. All things died, in the end. Their passions, their aspirations, their pain, their despair — none of it held meaning to the shadow. The accumulated weight of its myriad lives made everything seem fleeting, and it had lost the desire to care about small things.

All that was left was indifference.

The shadow did, however, feel a strange impulse to intervene.

It was not because the shadow felt compassion toward the man or considered his life valuable. Rather, it was because at that moment, the shadow discovered a new fact about itself.

It disliked Corruption.

In the vague recollections of its previous lives, the shadow remembered being constantly haunted by the corrupting influence of the Void. In fact, most of its lives seemed to have been spent in the throes of Corruption.

Sometimes, the shadow was born as an abomination. Sometimes, the shadow was born as a child of the Flame, lived a life full of joys and sorrows, then underwent the torturous transformation of being tainted by the Void and spent myriad years roaming the world consumed by madness and agony.

And throughout all those lives, the shadow itself — the being dreaming the nightmare of myriad lives — had to arduously resist the Corruption, preventing its seeds from taking root in its soul. That was a reason why the shadow's dream was a nightmare, as well.

Some of the seeds were small and weak, some were vast and terrifyingly virulent. The shadow seemed to possess quite a powerful means of defense, though, so it had managed to destroy them all. Still, Corruption never stopped trying to claim it, persistently sending its dark tendrils into the shadow's soul. It was unpleasant.

Corruption... was a bully.

Not only was it a bully, but it also seemed to have made its life's mission to endlessly bother the shadow.

So, even though the shadow did not feel much, it felt a strong dislike toward Corruption and those who carried it.

It was fitting, in a sense. Death was a weapon that destroyed Corruption, after all, and since the shadow felt a strange sort of closeness to death, it was only natural that it despised Corruption as well.

That was why it decided to act.

As the towering abomination prepared to lunge at the bleeding man, the shadows around it suddenly moved, as though coming alive. Tentacles of darkness surged forward, entangling its arms and legs.

The mighty being struggled, trying to break free, but it was powerless in front of the shadow. The dark tendrils dragged it back, pulling in different directions. The creature opened its maw, as if wanting to howl...

Before it could, its body ruptured, torn apart into pieces. Blood, viscera, and severed limbs fell to the ground in a torrent — wherever its yellow blood touched the soil, the soil smoked and melted, as if corroded by a strong acid.

But it didn't matter much, because the loathsome creature was dead.

Unlike Beast God, the shadow did not devour the remains of its enemy. It had better manners, and a more refined palate at that.

The shadow was displeased, though. It shivered uncomfortably.

That was because the moment the abomination died, the shadow felt something slip inside its soul, and thought that it heard an echo of a vaguely familiar voice.

It wondered if it would be forced to relive that unfortunate life, as well.

The bleeding man, meanwhile, stared at the gruesome remains of the ruptured abomination in shock. Then, he turned slowly and peered into the deep darkness suffusing the entrance to the cave.

His face paled horribly, and he took a step back, trembling.

Then, finding the strength to run, the man turned around and fled.

The shadow was relieved.

‘Good. Good riddance...’

Content that its shelter was peaceful and quiet once more, the shadow settled into its resting place. It hoped that no one would bother it again.

These hopes, however, were soon shattered into pieces.

Some time had passed — days, maybe, or perhaps years — and the shadow felt someone moving at the mouth of its cave once more.

With a heavy sigh, it directed its senses outward.

Then, its face fell.

Well, the shadow did not really have a face. But if it did, there would have been an expression of stunned dismay on it at the moment.

That day, the shadow asked itself the third question.

‘What the actual hell?’

--- Chapter 3163 ---

The shadow expanded its senses outward when the abomination appeared on its doorstep, so it knew where the man hunted by the creature had come from.

Out there in a valley at the foot of a hill, not too far from where the shadow's cave was, a small tribe of humans had been setting up crude tents on that day. The shadow assumed that they were merely passing by — now, however, it knew that its assumption had been wrong.

These humans were trying to settle down. The initial scattering of fur tents had grown since then, and their frames seemed more substantial. There were tools and hunting implements scattered around, wooden fences, and half-domesticated wolves gnawing on old bones.

The men were busy hunting beasts and fishing in a nearby stream. The women gathered fruit and berries, while simultaneously dedicating time to small crafts and rearing children. The children ran around and engaged in all sorts of mischief. There were not a lot of elderly around, but those few who had lived to see old age observed them from afar with grumpy discontent.

The tribe seemed like a primitive one, with only a few Awakened champions to guard them against the Creatures of Corruption that dwelled in the forest. They seemed to be at peace, but in truth, their existence was a constant war — a war against hunger, a war against the harsh elements, and most of all, a war against the loathsome rulers of this vast, untamed world.

Humans were wary of the forest. They were wary of the darkness. And so, they fought against the forest and the darkness, slowly pushing both back.

From the looks of it, the tribesmen were just barely learning the basics of agriculture, which had given their nomadic tribe the courage to settle down.

‘It means that they have nowhere else to go.'

The shadow felt a hint of interest.

It knew that agriculture was not born from progress. Rather, it was born from necessity. Nomadic tribes were far less vulnerable to the vagaries of the world, so there was only one reason why they would compromise their established way of life in favor of being tied to a land — there was not enough space for them to move to.

After all, nomads could leave in search of kinder lands in case of drought or natural disaster. They could flee if a powerful Creature of Corruption set its sights on their tribe. Once they became dependent on the land, however, there was no escaping it. Unless they wanted to starve, all they could do was stand their ground and fight — and go extinct if the enemy was too powerful.

The shadow found it mildly interesting, but its interest was aloof. It would not have paid the people any attention... if not for the fact that a group of them was currently standing near the entrance to its cave.

The man it had inadvertently saved was there as well, his wounds mostly healed. The tribesmen weren't holding spears or torches, though, and neither were they trying to enter the cave.

Instead...

They were setting up an altar.

The shadow observed them from the depths of the cave, flabbergasted.

‘For the love of gods, what the hell are they doing?'

The men dragged a large flat stone from somewhere lower down the mountain and placed it near the entrance, using smaller rocks as supports. Then, they placed strange things — fruit, meat, and some kind of beverage that smelled suspiciously like honey — on the altar and stepped back.

They were all wearing very odd garments and headdresses, as well, throwing frightened glances at the cave from time to time. Their faces were pale, but determined. The shadow was focused on something else, though.

‘...Honey?’

It recoiled.

The shadow didn't know why, but it felt a strong animosity toward honey.

The shadow distrusted it.

The humans, meanwhile, lowered themselves to their knees and then sprawled on the ground, kowtowing toward the dark entrance of the cave. Their voices rose in a strange litany, and they kept making noise for a long while.

The shadow shifted uncomfortably. It didn't like what was happening one bit.

The humans continued their ritual for some time, then left. Their pitiful presents remained lying on the altar. In time, the fruit and the meat rotted, while the vessel containing the sweet beverage was knocked over by the wind and spilled.

The shadow, obviously, did not leave its cave to lay claim to these unwanted offerings. It wasn't happy to receive them, but it was rather relieved that the noisy humans were gone.

It settled back into its half-awake state, slumbering in the darkness. Its senses still encompassed the land, so it could feel the world changing as time flowed. The trees grew taller. Two colonies of ants waged a war against each other. Deep in the forest, an eerie abomination had killed a bear, the mighty beast's body hanging limply from the creature's maw.

The realm was teeming with life, and the shadow's placid consciousness seemed to fuse with it, sensing every little facet of the boundless land through the shadows. In that state, it was difficult to differentiate where the world ended and the shadow began; it wasn't keen on making that distinction, either.

Such existence was peaceful in its own way, and while the shadow could not say that it was enjoyable, it did not find the state unpleasant. Its sense of self dissolved into the movement of shadows, and since there was close to no self in that state of inner transparency, there was no joy or discomfort either. There was only the great, endlessly changing vastness of the world. The shadow sensed the tribe of humans, as well.

The tribesmen were busy living their lives. Their settlement slowly grew, and as more of them matured and formed families, new tents were raised on its outskirts. The old tents were being slowly replaced by wooden structures. The forest was pushed back, creating space for a modest field. Some elderly surrendered to old age. Young women gave birth to children. A few of the hunters formed their soul cores and Awakened.

From time to time, the tribesmen made their way to the shadow's cave and performed their rituals, leaving new offerings on the altar. They seemed to have mistakenly decided that the creature that dwelled in the darkness was the guardian spirit of their tribe — the shadow did not care what they believed, so it wasn't going to correct them.

For what it was worth, it seemed that its presence scared away the more discerning abominations, so the tribesmen were benefiting from the shadow's existence, even if the shadow itself had no say in it. These humans were also quite lucky, since no powerful Creature of Corruption had wandered through this land in a long, long while.

They seemed to attribute that luck to the shadow, as well.

In time, the offerings the tribesmen left on their stone altar grew more lavish.

The shadow ignored them, as always. In fact, it ignored the humans entirely, enduring their noisy hymns with a mild sense of exasperation.

That was until, one day, the nature of the sacrifice they brought changed.

--- Chapter 3164 ---

The small settlement of the tribe had become a small village by then. The number of humans populating it had increased, while the tents made from fur and hide were replaced by wooden huts. The offerings brought by the villagers were more generous now — by their standards, naturally.

But perhaps, they still felt that it was not enough. Or perhaps they had grown fearful and desperate, for some reason... the shadow did not know. It did not care to know, either. All it knew was that, one day, its peaceful state of slumber was disturbed by a new noise. It wasn't the usual mumbling the tribesmen engaged in when leaving sacrifices on their altar.

Instead, the shadow heard a child crying. Displeased, it let out a heavy sigh and slowly, laboriously pulled its consciousness from the state of non-existence, creating a distinction between itself and the world once more.

‘What now?'

Its neighbors were proving to be most frustrating.

Out there, at the mouth of the cave, the shadow saw a familiar figure — it was the man it had saved once from an abomination.

The man was old now, his figure gaunt and bent. His limbs, which had been mighty once, were now thin and wiry. His thick beard had turned white, and there was a determined, mournful expression on his wrinkly face.

His shadow, on the contrary, had become darker and deeper, as if his death was drawing near.

Such was the nature of mundane humans. Their lives were fragile and fleeting — they flashed beautifully and vanished, leaving no trace of themselves in the world. One blink, and you could miss their existence entirely. The shadow frowned.

The man had grown old, but there was still strength in his limbs. He had no trouble dragging a crying child to the mouth of the cave, at least, whispering something in a somber tone.

‘What is the meaning of this?'

The shadow found its ability to ask questions much improved.

Before it could form a theory about what was happening, the old man stopped and lowered himself to one knee. Looking at the child — a girl who looked young enough to be his great-granddaughter — he said something, hugged her, and looked into the impenetrable darkness of the cave with an expression of fear, sorrow, and desperate hope.

Then, the old man pushed the girl into the darkness.

The shadow was surprised.

It was dismayed.

As the girl tumbled down sharp stones, rolling into the depths of the cave, it considered the old man, exploring a strange impulse that rose from the deepest, darkest corners of its soul.

The shadow felt compelled to kill the man. Was that so surprising, though?

It had been a consummate killer once, after all. It still was. Death was not only the shadow's home, but also the language it was most familiar with. In fact, the shadow suspected that it could very well be a living embodiment of death... its avatar, perhaps. Perhaps it was not just any shadow, but the shadow of Death itself.

Nevertheless, in the end, it allowed the old man to leave — for no other reason than that dealing with him would be bothersome. With the man gone, the shadow felt relieved.

That left it with another problem, though... The old man was gone, but the child was not.

The girl rolled to the floor of the cave and stayed there, trembling. In the darkness, her small frame looked like a heap of trash someone had left at the shadow's doorstep... in fact, using the word “doorstep” was not entirely correct.

Despite its attempts to become as small as possible, the shadow was still vast and deep. Its lightless expanse occupied most of the cave, so when the girl was pushed into the darkness, she was pushed into the vastness of the shadow.

In other words, the heap of trash had been unceremoniously left inside the shadow itself.

It hesitated, not sure what to do.

‘Should I kill her?'

The girl would be gone in the blink of an eye, anyway, like all mundane people. Killing her painlessly was the simplest solution... however, the shadow did not want to.

It felt a strong reluctance.

That was not merely because doing so would encourage more living sacrifices from the tribesmen, either.

At that moment, the shadow learned another fact about itself. It seemed that, although its nature was that of a merciless slayer... and that the number of its victims was incalculable... the shadow disliked senseless killing. The shadow abhorred it, in fact.

At the mention of the word "slayer", something seemed to move in its soul, but the shadow did not pay it any attention. It was preoccupied with the child.

The girl, meanwhile, seemed to find a tiny bit of courage and gathered herself from the ground, sitting up.

She looked around with an expression of fear on her small face and, unable to see anything in the dark, began to tremble even more violently.

She was trembling so much that the shadow barely made out what she said.

"O—o—oh, D—dark One... p—please accept t —this... s—sacrifice..."

Her voice gradually grew quieter, and then fell silent.

The shadow remained silent for a long while, then sighed inwardly.

In the end, it was forced to speak for the first time since regaining its self-awareness. The confines of the primitive human language felt alien and constricting, far inferior to the boundless expanse of its thoughts, but the shadow still forced itself to make a sound.

A cold, deep voice resounded from the darkness, making the girl freeze.

"I refuse."

The girl opened her eyes wide, shocked. Her shock was so great, in fact, that it even defeated her fear.

She blinked.

"What? W—what... do you mean?"

Her little mind did not seem capable of comprehending the concept of a spirit — the fearsome guardian spirit of her tribe — refusing a sacrifice. That was not how the world she knew was meant to work.

The shadow did not have a head, but if it did, it would have shaken it disapprovingly.

“I never asked for such a sacrifice. Or any sacrifice, for that matter."

The girl drew a shaky breath.

She remained silent for a long while, and then asked in a high-pitched, tentative voice:

"So... you... you are not going to eat me?"

The shadow stirred.

‘Who does she think I am?'

Well... the shadow itself did not know who it was, So that was a moot question.

It answered patiently.

“No. I don't eat children."

Then, the shadow remembered its countless lives, and felt compelled to add:

"...Anymore."

The girl did not seem convinced.

In fact, she seemed to be in disbelief.

"Really?"

The shadow let out a heavy sigh.

“Really."

The girl still appeared to have doubts.

“Really, really?"

The shadow suppressed a groan.

It considered its words for a short while, unaware that its silence made the girl tremble even more.

Eventually, thinking that it had found a way to placate the child, the shadow spoke.

“Of course. You can trust me."

Then, following an impulse, it added:

"I am the most honest shadow in the world, after all. Two worlds, even."

--- Chapter 3165 ---

The shadow's words seemed to work - to a degree, at least, because the girl eventually stopped trembling. She still seemed frightened, trying to stay as motionless as possible... but a child was a child.

Soon enough, she grew bored and restless. Looking around with an expression of curiosity - a senseless gesture, since she could not see anything in the darkness, the girl spoke in a brighter tone.

"My name is Tatal. I'm this many years old." She raised a hand, proudly showing the darkness her five tiny fingers.

The shadow did not respond. What did it care what this human child was called, let alone how old she was?

The girl did not seem to understand its reluctance to engage in a conversation, though, and asked after growing uncomfortable with the silence.

"What is your name, Dark One?"

The shadow frowned.

It did not care what it was called, either. But since the girl asked, the shadow tried to remember.

Its names were as countless as its past lives, the sea of them vast and meaningless. Eventually, its cold voice resounded from the darkness once more:

"I've been called by countless names in the past, in countless places. None of them have any meaning anymore, so... you can simply call me Shadow."

The girl turned her head this way, then another, as if trying to determine where the shadow's voice was coming from. Her attempts were futile, though, since it came from all directions.

She scrunched her face in confusion, then asked tentatively:

"Are you... are you hiding somewhere in the darkness, Shadow?"

The shadow was amused.

"No"

It paused, then added a helpful explanation.

"I am the darkness."

The girl trembled again.

She remained silent for a long while, then suddenly asked in a curious tone:

"Shadow God's name is Shadow. Aren't you afraid that he will get angry at you for stealing his name?"

Hearing the question, the shadow felt something stir in the depths of its soul. It was an old, vague memory - a memory of a life it had lived once, a long time ago. Perhaps the very first it had been forced to endure in this cruel, never-ending nightmare.

The shadow remembered a chilling cold, the rattling of chains, and the pain of shackles biting into the tattered skin of its wrists. Step, step, another step... someone had asked something similar of it back then, all those many years ago - in the distant future.

What had it responded with?

The shadow stirred and spoke, its voice distant:

"Why should I be afraid of a half-forgotten, weakling god?"

Shadow God was dead, anyway.

All of them were, even if they were alive and well, terrifying the shadow with the unfathomable magnitude of their existence.

'Nothing makes sense...'

Feeling unpleasant, the shadow turned its thoughts away from the contradictory nature of its strange existence.

The girl seemed very impressed by its absent-minded statement.

"Because gods are scary!"

The shadow smiled in the darkness.

Of course, they were. There was nothing more terrifying than the gods, but it did not fear Shadow God's anger. If the God of Peace were to get angry over something, it wouldn't be something as trifling as the shadow using his name. The shadow was a far greater being than the tribesmen, but to one of the gods, its existence must have seemed just as fleeting and insignificant as theirs were to it.

The little girl, however, did not understand it. How could she? Even the shadow could not fathom the gods, so a mundane child - and the old man who had pushed her into the cave, as well, would not even understand what it was they were failing to imagine.

So, the tribesmen comprehended the gods in the only way they could muster, by projecting their own small and primitive way of existing on them. An unfathomable being was indescribably terrifying, but a being that was exactly like them, just far more powerful, was merely frightening.

Such a being could be reasoned with, after all, as far as the tribesmen were concerned. Ironically enough, the shadow itself had somehow ended up in the same category of beings as the gods. That was why the tribesmen had been trying to please it with presents, leaving the items they saw as desirable on the altar... fruit, meat, drinks - something that all humans would want, since all humans knew hunger and thirst.

The shadow did not quite understand the reason the old man had decided to sacrifice a small child to it. Or, rather, it did not want to understand... it had a feeling that understanding the reason would not bring it any joy.

Perhaps it was simply because the girl was precious to the old man, and so he decided that the thing he held most dear would please the shadow a great deal, as if it had an inherent value.

Or maybe he simply believed that the shadow was no different from the Creatures of Corruption and Awakened beasts populating the forests, and had a taste for human flesh.

It probably didn't occur to him that the shadow had not eaten or drunk anything since the world was created, since it simply had no need or desire to.

'What a bother.'

The shadow sighed.

It considered the girl for a while, pondering what to do with her.

Eventually, the cold voice resounded from the darkness once more, sounding a little different.

"Why did the old man bring you to my cave?"

The girl hesitated, then said quietly, her voice carrying a hint of both pride and sorrow that she could not quite understand yet - the sorrow of being betrayed by someone you trusted.

"Grandpa used to be the strongest hunter of our tribe. But now, there are too few Awakened among us, and he's old. He says that his journey to the Shadow Realm is drawing near... so, he has to make sure that you'll watch over the tribe once he's gone, Dark One. Uh, I mean... Shadow"

The shadow studied the girl with regret. One's childhood ended when they lost their trust in adults. For this human child, that moment had come far too soon.

The shadow did not know why, but it felt sad.

Eventually, it spoke from the darkness, sounding tired:

"Go home, child."

Its voice was as cold as before, but now, there was a hint of emotion in it.

"Go home and give your people my message."

Tatal blinked a few times.

"W-what message?"

The darkness around her stirred, and then the cold voice spoke again.

This time, it felt like it was resounding from somewhere closer.

"Tell them that if they bring me a human sacrifice again..."

Even though Tatal was sitting on cold stones, suddenly, it felt as if she was being embraced by the shadows... drowning in them.

The shadow's embrace felt peaceful.

As she sensed the world shifting around her, Tatal heard the last of its words.

"I will kill them all."

In the next moment, somehow, she was not in the vast cave anymore.

Instead, she was in the heart of the village, having appeared there in the blink of an eye.

The light of day was harsh and blinding, and her visit to the dark cave seemed like a strange, frightening dream.

--- Chapter 3166 ---

Having sent the child away, and hoping that the tribesmen would not disturb it again, the shadow returned to its usual state of half-slumber.

It had already thrown the little girl, as well as her grandfather, out of its mind... however, for some reason, the shadow felt restless.

The peaceful state of being one with the world was not coming.

Instead, the shadow kept returning to the moment when it remembered a fragment from one of its past lives - the life of the ignorant man who had spoken about Shadow God with contempt, only to leave for the Realm of Shadows hours later.

That man had been a child once, as well. The shadow remembered...

In that life, he had been fortunate.

He had been fortunate because he was born in the glorious Empire.

The Empire stretched across countless realms, encompassing myriad people. It did not need a name, because there had never been another one like it - and there would never be, since the Empire was eternal. It was eternal because it was not ruled by mortal monarchs or even Supreme demigods, but by the Dragon himself.

The Dragon, who was War.

From his throne at the heart of the Empire, a sea of red flowed across the mortal realms, bringing progress and prosperity to all... all who survived the death and destruction it carried.

It was an empire of war, of conquest, of life - and, most of all, glory.

Glory! Glory! Glory!

He remembered watching victorious soldiers return from war as a young child, held tightly in his mother's arms. The roar of the crowd was like a palpable force, and as it made the glass in the windows tremble, he felt his entire body vibrate with excitement.

He remembered awe.

And most of all, he remembered knowing that this awe would be directed at him one day, as well. That knowledge filled his young and inexperienced heart with an insatiable, untamed, wondrous longing.

Not all born in the Empire were equal. How could they be when there were gods walking among them? The Dragon sat on his towering throne, served by the Four Spirits - the Spirit of Victory, the Spirit of Beauty, the Spirit of Art, and the Spirit of Joy.

There used to be six Spirits watching over the Empire, but two had perished in the war against the Jade Court - the only war the Empire had ever lost - while the seventh was said to have not been born yet.

Below the pantheon of the Empire were the seven Supremes who managed its vast expanse and ruled over its provinces. Those who served the Supremes, as well as Transcendent champions of its unstoppable legions, held a noble status among the people - they were the aristocracy and priesthood of the Empire.

Below them were the citizens, among whom the warriors were the most privileged class. Those born in the outer provinces were not afforded citizenship, but still retained the lofty status of imperial subjects - and could elevate themselves with meritorious deeds.

And finally, below everyone, there were slaves.

The slaves were everywhere in the Empire, but had no rights or status - even the lowest of free men was a person, while the slaves were not.

The shadow had been born a citizen, which was already an enviable fate. More than that, his father was a soldier, just like his father's father before - as such, his family enjoyed many privileges. Of course, they were not Awakened, who were the true elites... still, theirs was a prosperous and comfortable life, full of delights and boons that only people of the Empire could enjoy. But even faced with a life of prosperity, he never felt satisfied.

That was because somewhere deep within his bones, that roar of the crowd was still echoing and reverberating, making his blood boil.

Glory! Glory! Glory!

He longed for glory.

And so, as soon as he was old enough, he followed in his father's footsteps and became a soldier.

A war soon followed, and in its bloody throes, drunk and blinded by the clangor of metal...

He stumbled on a horrifying truth.

There was no glory to war. There was no valor. There was no honor to be found, either.

There was only avarice, lust, and stagnation. There was only... plunder.

The realm he and his fellow soldiers had been sent to subjugate was a peaceful one. Its people tried to offer some resistance, but how could they resist the Empire? Their cities burned. Their temples burned as well. Their rulers - the royals and the oracles - were slaughtered.

Those who survived were sold as slaves. The riches of the peaceful realm were gathered and sent as tribute back to the heartland. The soldiers all received their share, too.

At the end of it all, he finally received what he had been dreaming of all his life. A triumph. The legions returned home and were met by a roaring crowd, the ground shaking from the deafening cheers.

But listening to it did not bring him pride or pleasure.

Instead, he only felt a bitter, scathing emptiness.

He had earned quite a sum during his long years of service, and was awarded even more after returning to the embrace of the empire and leaving the legion. It was enough to spend the rest of his life in comfort... if one lived sensibly.

But he did not, could not. He did not want to. Abandoning his devotion to the Spirit of Victory, he dedicated himself instead to pursuing the worship of the Spirit of Joy... the Spirit of Revelry.

Years passed in the haze of taverns, brothels, and gambling dens. His money slowly dwindled in the storm of debauchery, but he didn't care. He only cared about chasing the next thrill, the next pleasure, the next delight - anything at all, just to forget everything. Just to drown out the mocking call of glory that still lived there, somewhere, deep in his bones.

His pursuit of revelry continued until he had no coin left at all. In fact, he was deeply in debt, with no way to repay it.

And that was how he ended up being sold as a slave.

He was tall and broad-shouldered, and a former soldier at that. Years of debauchery had not managed to weaken his body one bit. So, his first master had a lofty goal of making him a gladiator and earning a small fortune in the arena.

He had performed well there, indeed. But while other gladiators were content with their lot in life - battle slaves led quite a privileged existence, after all, enjoying more boons and pleasures than many of the citizens - he did not care about it one bit. He did not care about himself.

So, after several fights, he beat his master black and blue, stopping short of killing the bastard only out of revulsion.

As it turned out, even slaves had somewhere lower to fall.

He changed several owners after that, acting disobediently and violently each time. In the end, that earned him the very worst fate - being sold as an imperial slave, to be used as cannon fodder in the next campaign. Only the worst of the worst, those who held no other value or had committed crimes worthy of execution, earned that gruesome fate.

He did not mind. In fact, he was a little glad, thinking that this entire farce would finally end soon.

As he was escorted across the empire in shackles, he remembered his childhood. He remembered his mother's arms, and the crowd welcoming the soldiers back with cries of glory.

He did not want glory anymore.

But, funnily enough...

Even after throwing his life away, shackled, half-dead from the cold, and being dragged to what would almost surely become his death...

He still wanted to live.

He was amused to realize that he still desperately wanted to survive. He was willing to cling to life with all his might, determined to never let go.

Perhaps that was why the Empire was eternal. Not because it was ruled by the God of War... but because the Dragon was also the god of Life.

He walked, shivering from the cold and hoping that the caravan would stop for the night somewhere protected from the wind. What were these bastards thinking, dragging the slaves onto the mountain? Every soldier worth a coin knew that marching in the cold without proper equipment was a death warrant. Did they not care how many slaves would actually make it to the destination?

As he looked ahead, at the jagged peak of a lonesome mountain that cut the sky with its sharp edges, the chain rattled. Someone suddenly shouted from behind him:

"You little shit! I'm going to kill you!"

He chuckled darkly.

The boy chained behind him was gaunt and weak, stumbling already. There was no need to waste air shouting at the poor waif.

He spoke, wishing for the loudmouth behind him to shut up.

"Why bother? The weakling will be dead by sunrise anyway. The mountain will kill him."

A few seconds later, he added:

"It'll kill you and me, too. Just a bit later. I really don't know what the Imperials are thinking, forcing us into this cold."

The loudmouth continued to spout rubbish, but a few moments later, a more composed voice resounded from behind:

"This mountain pass is usually much warmer this time of year. We just had really bad luck. Also, I would advise you against harming this boy."

He turned his head, mildly curious.

"Why is that?"

The older slave chained behind the loudmouth gestured forward.

"Haven't you seen the markings on his skin? He is not like us, who fell into slavery due to debts, crimes, or misfortune. He was born a slave. A temple slave, to be precise. Not long ago, the Imperials destroyed the last temple of the Shadow God. I suspect that this is how the boy ended up here."

Shadow God...

He hesitated, suddenly uncomfortable. There used to be a god like that... there still was, probably. People of the Empire served the greatest god of all, though - War God, so they had no reason to concern themselves with the rest of them. Especially one as weak and obscure as Shadow.

There were no temples of Shadow God left anywhere in the world, which spoke volumes about what kind of deity that god was.

He scoffed.

"So what? Why should we be afraid of a half-forgotten, weakling god? He couldn't even save his own temples."

The old man was worse than the loudmouth. His voice sounded intelligent, but he spoke foolish things.

The caravan continued climbing the mountain. The cold continued to torture them and bite into their bodies. The winds continued to howl.

Eventually, they made camp. He tried to get as close to the fire as he could, finding comfort in its warmth. He ate the pitiful morsels the soldiers gave them.

He was still alive.

But then, there was a deafening sound of a crash as something gargantuan fell from the cliffs and landed in the middle of the camp. When the snow settled, he saw that thing, his eyes widening in horror...

The creature had two stumpy legs, an emaciated, hunched torso, and disproportionately long, multi-jointed hands - two of them, each ending with a set of horrifying bone claws, and another two, these ones shorter, ending with almost human-like fingers. It was covered in fur, yellowish-grey and ragged, thick enough to stop arrows and swords.

On its head, five milky, white eyes regarded the slaves with insect-like indifference. Beneath them, a terrible maw crowded with razor-sharp teeth was half-open, as though in anticipation. Viscous drool was running down the creature's chin and dripping into the snow.

And there were strange shapes endlessly moving, worm-like, under the creature's skin.

He froze.

'N-no...'

A Creature of Corruption... it was a Creature of Corruption, and a powerful one at that.

It was death.

'Move! I must move!'
