"They burn so brightly, so desperately. They are so easily extinguished, and yet pursued with such passion. They are so pure. That, to me... is beauty.”

The smile drained slowly from her face.

"Isn't that your design? Isn't that why the Flame endlessly wanes, but is never extinguished?"

War laughed lightly and shook her head.

“We never created humans. But, yes — that is the nature of the Flame. To endlessly burn itself and be endlessly reborn from itself, never ending, created from its own destruction."

White Abyss sighed.

She lingered for a while, then slowly shook her head.

"To tell the truth, I... feel like I desired something as well, once — a long time ago. I longed for something so desperately that no amount of pain, no amount of adversity, no amount of bitter defeats and heartbreaking losses could douse my resolve to achieve it. But I don't quite remember what it was, and why I strived to accomplish it so fiercely."

She frowned.

“That was one of the reasons why I defeated Kanakht and usurped his throne. I pitied his people, yes... but I also thought that if I helped them achieve what they longed for, then perhaps I would remember what I desired myself.”

Her expression grew distant.

“But it's strange. The more I observe their desires and care for them, the less I remember. By now, I don't think I remember at all.”

War glanced at her with a smile.

“Maybe you should try building the First Kingdom of the Corrupted, instead. You are a nephilim, after all. Those of the Flame, those of the Void — both are your kin, even if no one wants to claim you."

She scrutinized White Abyss for a moment, then added:

“Although that might be difficult, with that soul of yours. Truly, you are an odd creature. Rarely have I seen anyone stranger than you."

She sighed and glanced away.

“But even if you are merely a half-baked god, you still seem to have stumbled into the same sad predicament we did. The more we want to help humans, these strange creatures born from the sparks of the Flame, the more we harm them. It took us a while to learn our lessons... but, by now, even the most stubborn of us are tired of hurting them. Of being hurt by them. Of suffocating the sparks of the Flame burning within them."

War lowered her gaze.

“That is why the Age of Gods is ending. Soon, the Age of Humans will come to replace it, instead."

She glanced at her spear, then brushed her calloused hand across its wooden shaft.

“I was full of pity for them once, as well. At the beginning of it all, I saw them struggling desperately to survive, to stave off hunger... and so, I gave one of those pitiful humans a spear to help him hunt."

A pale smile illuminated her old face.

“He took it and used it to kill another human, taking his food and his woman. I gave them fire, and they used fire to burn each other's homes. I gave them knowledge of how to work metals, hoping that they would create farming tools... but they forged weapons and tools of torture instead."

War shook her head lightly.

“Ever since I gave that first human a spear, I was their companion. I walked among them, living a life no different from theirs and watching them grow. The spear turned into a bow, a bow turned into a cannon. A cannon turned into cluster bombs and mustard gas. Until, eventually, I watched nuclear mushrooms rise above civilian cities, and meticulously engineered bioweapons cleanse entire continents of all life.”

White Abyss seemed to freeze, looking at War with a startled expression.

Now, for the first time, a strong emotion seemed to find its way into her voice.

“How... how do you know this? You were long dead by the time all these things happened. You couldn't have seen."

War simply chuckled.

Reaching forward to warm her hands by the fire, she asked:

"What is time to a god?"

--- Chapter 3183 ---

White Abyss seemed rattled.

Despite War's casual tone, she could not help but grow tense. A myriad of thoughts seemed to flash in her eyes.

Having experienced countless lives, myriad desires, she knew a lot... she knew too much. So much, in fact, that her own life and desire were lost in the vast sea of human passions she had endured.

But all of those lives belonged to people who would live in the distant future, in a world much different from this one. So, she was aware of what all of them knew. Eventually, she spoke:

"So... you are not dead?"

War simply shook her head, the same faint smile illuminating her weathered face.

"We are."

“Some paths are obscured by fog. Everything that has to do with Weaver is especially difficult to see... so while we knew a lot, we did not know all of it. We chose a path and followed it earnestly. Even if we knew that, one day, we must end... we did not surrender without a struggle. We were still fighting fiercely when we reached the end of the path — because like all living things, we too are children of the Flame. We too burn with the desire to be alive."

“Even if death is nothing more than change.”

“Ah, death... how I despise that cowardly shadow!"

White Abyss regarded her in silence, the fire casting harsh shadows on her face. Then, she leaned forward slightly:

“Then why didn't you win?"

Her voice sounded stark and severe.

War seemed a little offended by her remark, but in the end, she simply shrugged.

Her voice sounded pleased.

Returning the brilliant sword to its owner, she hesitated for a moment, and then placed her spear on the ground near White Abyss.

The beautiful nephilim looked at the flint spear in confusion.

Looking down at the seated nephilim, she smiled.

"Do you know what the saving grace of existence is, child? For us gods."

Not receiving an answer, she sighed.

"It's oblivion."

With that, War turned away from the fire and headed into the desert. As she walked, she threw over her shoulder:

"The next time we meet, I will be different. I might not remember this conversation, either. That will be the day when I kill you... so I hope that you'll remember it well."

Moments later, she was gone.

White Abyss was left alone in front of the fire.

Her soldiers and priests still stood in the distance, too afraid to move.

She remained motionless for a long while, then reached forward and picked up the spear.

A grim and chilling emotion shone in her radiant eyes.

White Abyss hesitated for a moment, then looked down and sighed.

“Then let us never meet again, War."

Somewhere far away, in a realm being consumed by Corruption...

A blind woman fell to her knees, breathing heavily.

A slender rapier hovered over her shoulder like a stinger, its long blade slick with blood.

The woman was covered in blood as well, her garments tattered and torn. Around her, countless corpses were strewn on the ground, most killed with one swift, precise blow. Some, however, were torn apart or crushed viciously, mauled and mutilated in a myriad of ghastly ways.

There were thousands of them... tens of thousands, stretching toward the horizon like a morbid carpet.

But the land was still seething with Corruption.

Everything here had been twisted and changed, becoming a perverse parody of itself. The trees were reaching forward with branches that gaped with countless maws, their leaves as sharp as blades. The riverbeds swelled with torrents of virulent rot. The blades of grass slithered like tendrils, greedily absorbing the blood of the battle. The corpses bloomed with beautiful, harrowing flowers. The air was full of acid-like pollen.

The soil itself was seeping with black, oily liquid, long vines sprouting from it and reaching toward the blind woman like snakes.

In the distance, more abominable beasts were rushing in her direction.

The woman drew a hoarse breath and rose shakily.

“Come out, come out... I remember you..."

Before the vines could envelop her, a deafening roar shattered the world. Then, a pillar of incandescent flame plummeted from the sky, incinerating the twisting vines, the blades of grass, the clouds of pollen, and the branches of the frenzied trees.

A radiant dragon with scales of pure ivory landed with a thunderous boom in front of the woman, shielding her from danger. Another billowing torrent of flame escaped from its maw, and it lunged forward, assaulting the world of Corruption.

He was the Ivory Lord, Sevirax — a memory of him, at least.

As the great dragon tore a path through the mass of Corruption, the woman advanced forward with unsteady steps.

She had only walked for a few minutes before her champion was brought down.

In the end, even the descendant of Sun God could not resist the hungry abundance of the abominable world. His flames were swallowed by the black liquid, his talons were shattered by the impenetrable hide of mutated beasts, his mighty body was enveloped by vines and pushed to the ground. A swarm of hideous insects crawled into his ghastly wounds, and the trapped dragon let out a chilling, haunting wail of pure agony.

He was defeated... only, unlike the rest of her champions, he did not die.

Because he was immortal.

Cassie raised a hand to grasp the hilt of the Quiet Dancer and lowered her head in exhaustion.

She dismissed the memory of Sevirax.

She was so spent, so tired... so utterly exhausted.

She was all but devoid of essence, as well. But she had not reached her goal yet.

She needed to manifest another champion, but her choices had grown limited.

So, instead, she slowly pulled her blindfold up, revealing the radiant azure depths of her sole remaining eye.

The world of Corruption reflected in it, teeming with harrowing abominations. Something else reflected in it, as well.

She sighed deeply.

“It's... time. I can't keep going any longer."

There was a moment of silence.

Then, the hidden reflection escaped from her eye and took the form of a tall man with raven-black hair and strange, mirror-like eyes.

He regarded the sea of Corruption surrounding them, then looked at Cassie with an indecipherable expression. Eventually, he said in an aloof tone:

"You always bring me to the most peculiar places."

With that, the King of Nothing turned to face the encroaching tide of abominations and raised a hand, summoning a somber spear.

“Rest a while, Lady Cassia. And remember the deal we made. After this, I will leave you.”

The Fifth Nightmare was an insidious trial. It was a deadly gauntlet, and if that was not enough, it was laden with countless fatal traps.

The first of the traps was the process of the unmaking. It was the Spell's way of giving its carriers a path to attaining Apotheosis — of reaching the state of mind needed to become a god, at least.

Eurys of the Nine had said once that Apotheosis could not be achieved swiftly. There was truth to his words.

One needed to live, to experience, to expand their perspective above the mundane first if they wanted to touch upon the divine. Few ever did, and those few needed hundreds of years of gradual growth and learning — thousands of years, sometimes.

But who had thousands of years to spare in a world that teetered on the brink of apocalypse?

And so, in the Fifth Nightmare, time was folded in on itself. Time here had little meaning.

The first part of the trial, which each of the challengers had to face alone, was meant to unmake them as humans and rebuild them in the image of deities. The process was quite simple... it forced them to face their own Domain.

Cassie was not sure what the others had experienced, but she could infer it from her own unmaking. Sunny had most likely been forced to experience the lives and deaths of all the shades populating his soul. Nephis had most likely been forced to experience all the lives and desires of countless people whom she had inspired... the infinite ocean of them.

Even with the new Supremes taking control of the human territories in the Dream Realm, there were still countless souls who worshiped Changing Star in the waking world, after all.

An eternity of emotions, of aspirations, of fears, of joy, of heartbreak — all folded into a single moment.

That was enough to destroy anyone. Or to change them, at least.

The unmaking itself was a trial that hid deadly traps.

The most obvious one was the threat of one's consciousness being destroyed by eternity. Of losing oneself entirely and dissolving in the endless torrent of lives and experiences forced upon them. One had to possess an incredibly strong will, an impossibly firm sense of self, an absolute resolve to stay true to their goals in order to survive that terrifying ordeal.

Even if they did, at the end of it all, they would not be the same — so by design. They would hardly remember who they had been... who they had wanted to be. Their previous self — that of a mortal human — would be made pale and faint in the face of eternity, dwarfed by the vast immensity of accumulated experience and the great scope of consciousness worthy of a deity. For Cassie, however, that ordeal had not been too difficult to endure.

At the start of the Nightmare, she had been forced to live the lives of everyone she remembered. That was a dire test, but while it was different from her past trials — remembering something was different from truly experiencing it, after all — it was not entirely unfamiliar.

So, she managed to maintain her sense of self rather well.

There was another hidden danger in the process of the unmaking, though, at least for her.

It was the threat of Corruption.

Cassie remembered countless Nightmare Creatures, after all. So, she had to endure their appalling lives too.

She suspected that many Sovereigns had endured the same. In fact, she believed that learning how to resist Corruption — to an extent, at least — was an integral part of Apotheosis.

Cassie's own ability to resist was not that formidable, but she could cheat the process. And so, she destroyed herself countless times and rebuilt herself countless times, erasing those memories that were too dangerous for her to contain within herself. At the end of it all, she emerged relatively unscathed.

She had been tempted to erase far more of her memories, in fact, to alleviate the burden... but, in the end, she decided to keep most of them.

That was because while possessing too vast a Domain could become one's undoing in the Fifth Nightmare, completely destroying their self and obliterating them, possessing too weak a Domain was a danger in and of itself.

There was a purpose to the change, after all. Escaping the unmaking too easily would make conquering the Nightmare all but impossible.

Still. In the end, Cassie had survived.

The second part of the Fifth Nightmare was a mystery. Cassie had an inkling of what the conflict they had to resolve was, but she was not sure just yet. She did, however, have a feeling that they had not entered the final trial at the same time.

Cassie herself appeared in the young and untamed world of the shared Nightmare in the later years of the Age of Gods. It took her a long time to regain her senses, gather her shattered mind, and compose herself. By then, she learned of the first trap of this trial — the threat of being swallowed by the world.

Those whose consciousness was vast enough to become a deity, but had not undergone Apotheosis yet, faced a unique danger — the danger of allowing themselves to be enthralled by the world and fusing with it, achieving the opposite of what they strived for. Of losing their personhood and becoming elemental forces instead of Spirits.

That was an insidious peril, indeed.

But for Cassie, who had always struggled to maintain her personhood in the tide of foreign senses, that trap did not pose much danger, either.

And so, she ventured on a journey.

A journey to find something that had been long lost and did not exist in the real world anymore, but could still be found in this Nightmare.

--- Chapter 3185 ---

The journey had been long, but it had not been easy.

During the dusk of the Age of Gods, the mortal realms were still ruled by the Creatures of Corruption. Humans had carved out a place for themselves under the sun, but they were still on the defensive, fighting fiercely to safeguard their settlements.

Even though humans were steadily growing stronger as time went by, they were not ready to challenge the abominations for dominion over the world just yet. That would only happen when the Age of Heroes arrived, prompted by the fall of the First Kingdom and the rise of Transcendent champions who had divine blood in their veins.

So, Cassie endured a fair share of daunting battles as she searched. Some she had escaped unscathed, while some left her wounded and battered. She sought refuge among humans while she recovered — she needed to learn what they knew to reach her goal, anyway.

News brought by merchants from distant realms, old legends, rumors of strange occurrences that happened far away... Pretending to be a wandering fortune teller, Cassie learned a lot.

She learned even more from her intuition and innate affinity to revelations and fate. However, the item she was searching for could not be discovered that way — it was as if all clues about it were hidden by fog, obscured from her senses.

She continued her search.

Sometimes, she traveled with merchant caravans and temporary companions. Sometimes, she traveled alone, accompanied only by her memories. The company of those she called upon was not unpleasant... but even if they were with her, she couldn't help but feel alone.

Time passed.

One day, Cassie found herself in a human city. It was quite large by the standards of this primitive time, perched precariously on the edge of a deep canyon. People were wary of strangers here, so she didn't want to attract attention.

She was too tired and wounded to put a lot of effort into avoiding a conflict, and she didn't want to subjugate the city if its rulers acted against her out of fear, arrogance, or greed — so, it was better to remain unnoticed.

Sitting on the ground near a fountain in the main square, wrapped in her tattered cloak, Cassie unfurled a small rug in front of her and placed a chipped bowl on it, laying a small pile of carved bones by its side.

Her hair was covered by the hood of her cloak, while her face was hidden behind a veil. Her wooden staff lay nearby. She looked unremarkable and shabby — a vagabond who made a living by fooling gullible people, no doubt, instead of a demigod powerful enough to destroy the entire city... and beautiful enough to make countless men spill blood.

Cassie's appearance had never caused her trouble in the real world, but here in the Nightmare, she had learned to hide it. She did not want to launch a thousand ships, after all.

Soon enough, the first client arrived.

“Huh. A fortune teller?"

A copper coin fell into her bowl.

"Come on then, tell me my fortune."

Cassie reached for the bones and scattered them across the carpet. There was no point in doing so, but people believed her more willingly that way.

‘A copper coin...’

She hesitated for a moment, then said:

"Praise be! What luck. Congratulations, your home will welcome the fourth child soon. This time, it will be a son."

There was a moment of silence, and then an excited shout.

“A son! Finally!"

Her client paused, then asked with suspicion:

"No, wait. Are you blind?! The bones fell in a circular pattern. That clearly means misfortune!"

Cassie tilted her head a little.

"I am indeed blind.”

The man scoffed.

“What can a blind fortune teller even see?"

Cassie smiled behind her veil.

“I can see a plump, healthy boy..."

The man cursed a few times, then stomped away.

Before that, however, he did not fail to look at her tentatively and take the coin out of the bowl without making any noise.

Cassie did not care. What use did she have for money?

But still.

‘Bastard. I was going to tell you that your handsome young neighbor is the boy's real father, but oh well!’

It was better that way, anyway. She had learned long ago that people only got angry and confrontational when she brought them bad news, accusing them of spreading lies no matter how truthful her words were. They only believed what they wanted to hear.

There were more clients after that. Cassie easily played the role of a downtrodden fortune teller.

“What luck! Your son will be promoted by the lord soon. He will even receive precious silk as a reward..."

“Heavens above. I can see only good omens in your future. Have you offered a sacrifice to the gods recently? The gods must have been pleased..."

“Don't fret. Fortune smiles upon you. Your younger sister will indeed be wed before you — however, you'll meet your future husband at her wedding. And he will be the most handsome man there, by far..."

While making predictions, she listened. And as people told her about their simple lives, she learned a great deal about the city, its citizens, and the realm.

The lord here was a mighty warrior who worshipped Beast God. There was a rivalry between him and the Transcendent Monster, a great tiger, who lived in the woods. The two often quarreled and fought, but defended the city against Creatures of Corruption side by side.

There was another city across the mountains from here, ruled by a priestess of Storm God. The priestess was old and nurturing a successor — the temple she ruled had been built many centuries ago, and its influence spread across the entire realm.

...A young shepherd had, apparently, witnessed a goddess bathing in the stream and became enamored. So enamored, in fact, that a stone he had sat upon in a daze split nine months later, revealing an infant — whose skin was so tough that no sword could pierce it.

Cassie was not sure how the locals had learned that the baby couldn't be pierced by a sword, but still made sure to file the rumor away into her endless memory. There were countless strange stories like that in there, already.

Soon enough, another client sat down in front of her, wearing a troubled expression.

“Say, fortune teller... how soon will my cow recover? No, really, I need to know! She has been taking it easy for an entire month. Does she have any shame?!"

Eventually, she spoke:

"I didn't expect to meet you here."

The man blinked a few times.

“Huh? Do I know you?"

Cassie sighed.

"It doesn't seem that you trust my words, though."

The man frowned.

"Hey! Stop stalling and tell me about my cow!"

Cassie turned slightly.

"I wasn't talking to you."

Before the man could answer, his eyes glinted strangely. In the next moment, a tall figure appeared beside him, looking down at Cassie with an inscrutable gaze.

The man flinched and reeled back, shocked and confused. Looking up, he paled and tried to crawl away.

"A... a daemon! Gods, save me!"

The man who had appeared out of nowhere frowned, turning his head slightly to watch him escape.

“Do I look like a daemon?"

The retreating figure reflected in the man's mirror-like eyes. He frowned.

“That fool has never seen a daemon, so how would he even know what they look like?"

Shaking his head, he turned back to Cassie.

“And yes, Lady Cassia. I do, indeed, doubt that you had no expectations of meeting me here. The world is vast, after all. What are the chances of us stumbling into each other by chance?"

Cassie smiled faintly.

“Well. I might have sought you out on purpose."

Mordret sat down in front of her and remained silent for a few moments.

He had spent countless years in the Nightmare, already. At first, he had remained with Mirage near the Mirror Lake, where this version of him had been born. Later, he escaped the reflections and went to explore the world, hiding in people's eyes and experiencing life after life as a silent witness.

He had been the reflection of countless men and women by now, having seen the heights of virtue and the depths of depravity, having accompanied slaves and kings, soldiers and farmers — numerous faces all fusing together, slowly driving him mad.

There was a simple reason why he had chosen such a strange existence.

It was because Mordret had no Domain. His brother had built himself a mighty Domain — millions of vessels carrying the fragments of his soul, all united under the banner of the King of Nothing. But all of them had either been destroyed in the war against the Dreamspawn or consumed in an attempt to conquer Apotheosis.

This Mordret, however, had never destroyed a soul to take possession of someone else's body. He felt no desire to, and found the very idea distasteful.

He had only ever created one Reflection — and left it behind in the real world, where it was desperately needed.

There was no Citadel that he ruled, either. So, Mordret entered the Nightmare with nothing... and, as a result, he had experienced no unmaking.

Which was both a blessing and a curse.

It was a blessing because he had not been destroyed by it. It was a curse because he had not been changed by it.

Reaching the second trial of the Nightmare, Mordret had been no closer to Apotheosis than before entering it. So, having deduced what should have transpired, he endeavored to correct that.

That was why he had spent centuries submerged in the lives of countless people — experiencing all their hopes and aspirations, heartbreaks and sorrows, trials and triumphs. Observing the world through countless reflections and trying to learn what it meant to be a god.

Mordret was not sure that he had learned a lot about godhood. However, he had never experienced mundane life before... so he learned quite a lot about what it meant to be human, instead.

He wasn't sure if he liked what he had learned.

“What purpose might you have in seeking me out?"

Mordret smiled faintly.

Years later, the two of them arrived in a realm infected by Corruption. It used to be peaceful once, with vast seas and a scattering of islands that brimmed with flowers and emerald grass. But now, peace was gone.

--- Chapter 3187 ---

The shadow's authority over his kingdom was absolute. There was nothing within its dark boundary that did not belong to him, so naturally, there was no one who drew breath. His land was a land of death, with only the shades under his control simulating the acts of the living.

And yet, he could not shake off the suspicion that something was hiding within the darkness, obscured even from his senses.

He could not sense any movement that could not be explained, and he could not hear any sounds that could not be traced to a predictable source. And yet, at times, he felt a faint, alien presence.

A presence that should not have existed in his dead kingdom — the presence of someone who was still alive.

‘How can this be?'

The shadow had killed everything in this land. Countless years had passed since then, and no one managed to enter the eternal darkness shrouding it. The humans who came to find out how the nation born from the Shadow Tribe had been wiped out turned back and fled in fear, while the Creatures of Corruption who dared to enter his domain were ruthlessly slain.

So, if there was a living being somewhere in his kingdom, it could only mean one of two things.

One was that someone had managed to sneak past his senses and was still hiding. The other was that someone had managed to survive his wrath and had been hiding from his gaze ever since.

Both possibilities left him displeased.

So, the shadow endeavored to find the source of the elusive presence. He explored every corner of his kingdom with special attention. He even ordered all the shades under his control to stop, wanting to eliminate the chance of their movements obscuring something he had failed to notice.

And yet, he failed to find anything.

‘Did I imagine the whole thing?’

If the shadow had a physical body, he would have frowned.

‘No, it was definitely here...'

He had learned some news from the conversations of people who sometimes arrived in hopes of solving the mystery of the eerie darkness, but inevitably retreated after witnessing its frightening depths.

The Age of Gods was ending.

In fact, it was already over. Somewhere far away, the strange creature known as the White Abyss had withdrawn her grace from the people of the First Kingdom, appearing in front of them less and less. The First Kingdom continued its existence for a few more generations, but eventually collapsed and splintered, thus ushering in a new age — the Age of Heroes.

All across existence, humans had become powerful enough to challenge the Creatures of Corruption openly. Instead of merely surviving in a hostile world, they were now fighting for dominion over it — led by exalted champions, of course. Strength was a question of accumulation, in most cases.

Throughout the Age of Gods, humans had been learning and accumulating knowledge — they went from hunting beasts with flint spears to forging intricate tools and weapons out of bronze. The copper knife that Tatal had treated with such awe would be seen as a common item now, an inferior and trifling blade no less.

Humans had learned how to work mystical and sublime materials, as well, which allowed them to create truly lethal weapons.

A new and previously unheard-of concept, writing, was slowly spreading among some people — it was a gift from Hope, the Demon of Desire.

Humans had learned more about the Path of Ascension, as well, solving its mysteries and slowly developing essence techniques to climb it. When Tatal became a Transcendent, that had been a legendary feat — something nearly unheard of, let alone witnessed by many. But now, there were far more Transcendents around, all of them brimming with fighting spirit and resolve.

There were descendants of the gods among them, as well — humans with divine blood in their veins.

Harnessing the power of progress, humans ventured to conquer the world.

So, the world was slowly changing under their footsteps.

At the same time, the gods seemed to become more distant. While their avatars still existed, they rarely left the Divine Realms to roam the lands populated by mortals. Most of the daemons, too, had become withdrawn.

Mirage was spending more and more of her time inside her Great Mirror. Rime was exploring distant skies aboard her living ship. Ariel was rumored to have become fascinated by a beautiful monster, for whom he had built a magnificent palace from pure white jade. Nether spent his time by Storm God's side...

None of them, except Hope, seemed to be interested in humans that much.

And so, the heroes of humanity could stand tall.

No troublesome hero had grown brazen enough to try bothering the shadow, though, which he was thankful for.

Even if he felt that encountering a fool or two was only a matter of time.

Before that happened, though, he finally managed to confirm his suspicion and find the source of the strange presence.

"...Snuggle?"

"So, silly doll, your attempts to hide from me are meaningless. After all, you are walking around inside my soul, illuminating it carelessly with your light."

The doll looked around, seeming a little distraught. Then, she coughed.

“So, then, this thing in front of me... is just a physical form you took for convenience?"

The shadow nodded.

Inwardly, he wondered why the doll was pretending to cough — she did not have a throat, after all. It seemed like a human habit.

Come to think of it, Snuggle did not even have a mouth — only an awkwardly stitched curve that served her as one. So how was she even speaking? What power moved her little body, and what gave her the strength to lift the silver bell?

He was not exactly curious... but, for a moment, he did feel a tiny pang of interest.

"It is."

Snuggle hesitated for a few moments, then asked in her squeaky voice:

“Then... do you mind turning into something less creepy? With all due respect, of course!"

After that...

She giggled awkwardly.

The shadow stared at the brazen doll, stunned for a moment.

‘The... the audacity?’

Did she not know fear?

The request to take a different shape did not bother him, but laughing in the solemn silence of his kingdom, standing directly in front of his physical manifestation...

Was it fearlessness or stupidity? Or both?

‘But probably the latter.'

He glared at the doll for a moment, then smiled pleasantly.

“I don't mind."

With that, the shadows swelled and billowed, surrounding him like a storm. A colossal, grotesque shape rose from them, dwarfing the buildings — the shape of a fearsome, hideous creature that seemed to have crawled out of the very depths of the Abyss.

As his myriad limbs obscured the dark heavens, Snuggle shuddered and pressed herself against the wall.

“Come to think of it, your previous form was very fitting! It was tasteful, comely, and full of grace! Ha, ha-ha... it was a joke, a joke, just a joke!"

The shadow stared at her from the great height of his current form, then scoffed quietly and dismissed it.

‘That's better. That will teach her manners.’

Then, he fell into contemplation for a moment.

Taking a less frightening form? He did not care either way, so he could as well do it.

As if remembering an old habit, the shadow made a little effort and appeared in front of trembling Snuggle again. This time, he looked like a human.

In front of her stood a young man with porcelain skin and eyes that were like onyx, his hair as black as the darkest depths of night. He wore a simple tunic of black silk, while his expression was cold and aloof, devoid of all emotion.

“There. Are you satisfied?"

The doll looked up cautiously, stared at him for a few moments with its beady eyes, and then nodded.

“Y—yeah... that's better! Much better!"

The corner of his mouth rose slightly, but the faint smile never reached his tenebrous eyes.

‘What am I supposed to do now?’

The shadow had never entertained guests in his kingdom. All who came here either fled or died — so, he wasn't entirely sure what to do next.

After remaining silent for a while, he bent, picked up the silver bell, and tied it to his belt. Then, he glanced at the little doll and asked:

"Shall I show you around my kingdom?"

And that was how he ended up escorting Snuggle along the dark streets, describing the past of the Shadow Tribe. It felt strange and unfamiliar... but not entirely unwelcome.

Perhaps he had missed having conversations with someone.

Perhaps he had simply grown tired of his monotonous existence, and wanted to brighten it with the sound of someone else's voice.

After some time, Snuggle rubbed her forehead.

“It seems that I've been trapped for a long time."

He looked at her with a hint of curiosity.

“How did a wandering soul like you end up being trapped inside that crystal and locked inside a box, to begin with?"

Snuggle let out a nervous laugh.

“Well... actually, only the box was a trap. I created the crystal myself.”

The shadow raised an eyebrow, prompting her to continue.

"It's a... enchantment of a sorcerous item I possess. It places something into a state of stasis for as long as its master can sustain the sorcery with their essence. A very useful thing! You can remove a powerful Nightmare Creature from battle and deal with its minions first, for example. Or keep a can of be... I mean, an amphora of wine cool for a long time."

Snuggle sighed, her shoulders dropping.

“But, well, after spending years in this nightmarish world, I ended up in big trouble. So, in order to survive, I cast the sorcery on myself. That created a paradox — the sorcery could only be sustained for as long as I had essence, but I was placed in stasis. So, the amount of essence I had became static, as well. Therefore... I actually have no idea how may years passed since that day."

She looked around in confusion.

“They must have failed to destroy the crystal and decided to lock me in that box instead. The item that creates it is very powerful, so I am not even sure what could have damaged the sorcery enough for the crystal to crack... but it did crack some time ago, and little by little, I regained my senses. However, I couldn't escape the box... until you opened it."

The shadow remained silent.

He wasn't sure what danger the wandering soul had found itself in, and who it was that put the crystal in the box. Had it been the High Priest of the Shadow Tribe temple, or the rulers of the city? The very people who had sacrificed a living soul to him?

Or had it been someone else, who then traded the sorcerous crystal away or surrendered it to an enemy as a spoil of war? How many hands had the box passed through before ending up in the inner sanctum of that temple?

The shadow did not know.

He knew two things, though.

The first one was that, no matter who had trapped the wandering soul in the box, they must have been quite a powerful being. Runic sorcery had not spread widely yet, after all, and Shaping did not function in the absence of a sorcerer. So, creating a soul trap was not an easy task.

The second thing... he had an inkling of what had damaged the sorcery keeping the stasis crystal intact.

Looking at the small doll that waddled by his side, he said:

“I think I know what put a crack in your crystal."

Snuggle seemed curious.

“Oh, really? What was it?"

Then, she waved a hand.

"By the way... sorry for earlier! Now that I got to know you a little better, you don't seem quite as scary anymore, Lord Titan. You are actually quite nice!"

The shadow shrugged.

Was he?

Glancing at the shades that surrounded them, he said:

“The crystal must have cracked when I swallowed this land and killed every living thing in it — the people, the beasts, the trees, the grass... I willed everything to die, but the crystal must have protected you. It is quite unexpected that something survived.

He looked down at Snuggle and smiled faintly.

“You are quite a fortunate little soul, aren't you? Oh, and thank you for saying that I am not at all scary and very nice... I agree.“

Snuggle tripped and fell down.

--- Chapter 3190 ---

The shadow showed the transient soul the rest of his silent city. However, she grew much quieter after learning the nature of the shades that surrounded them. He did not have much to say, anyway — most of his memories of this place belonged to a time when the city was a makeshift settlement, and its people were no more than hunters and gatherers who barely knew how to farm land.

Tatal, Stone Hand, and their children... he remembered them well, but he knew very little about the people who had become his shades.

Of course, if he wanted to, he could peer into each of the shadows that dwelled within his soul and glean their past. The strings of their fates all ended in a single point, after all — in him. So, it was easy to learn about them. He had already glimpsed some of it when creating his kingdom, though, and had no desire to delve deeper into the mess of human lives.

Eventually, the two of them reached a solemn square with a monument towering above its center. The monument depicted a lone human figure facing a great wyrm.

The shadow studied the monument for a while, then said in an aloof tone:

“This is a statue to the Great Shaman who saved the people of this land from a terrible monster. There were no Transcendents among humans back then, so a Transcendent Devil was like a world-ending calamity. The shaman was a mere Master, but she faced the berserk creature alone. In the end, she defeated it."

Snuggle studied the monument for a long while.

Eventually, she asked:

“And what happened to her after that? Is she somewhere here, among these shades?"

The little doll remained silent for a few moments, then sighed.

She paused for a moment, then glanced at the shadow. Her perpetually downturned mouth twisted into a little grin.

"Not yet, at least!"

He lingered for a bit, not sure what she meant, then nodded.

“This concludes the tour of my kingdom. As you can see, it is not at all a hell.”

Snuggle chuckled weakly.

“Indeed. It is more of a Limbo... or a purgatory, perhaps. If its master has any mercy."

She glanced at the shadow, hesitated a little, then asked:

"Can I ask you a question?"

The shadow stared at the tattered doll, impassive.

"You can."

She turned to face the silent shades, observing their meticulous pretense of life.

"Why did you kill all these people?"

The shadow straightened and glanced away. He did not say anything for a long while, then uttered in a cold tone:

"Because I was angry. Because it was easy."

The shadow paused, imagining what his kingdom looked like to the transient soul. Trying to see the world from a different point of view was not easy for him — it was a skill that he had seemingly possessed once, but lost somewhere along the way.

Eventually, he added:

“Even if I never wanted it, these people treated me like a deity. They prospered under my accidental protection, spared from the countless cruelties of this vast world. There was only one commandment I ever gave them — it was to never sacrifice a human life to me. I warned them that if they ever did, I would erase their tribe from existence.”

The shadow fell silent.

After a while, he spoke again, his voice sounding a little quieter:

"But they didn't listen. Human memory is short."

Snuggle studied the silent shades.

After a while, she sighed.

“This is all new to me. Life has spoiled me, you see... I am used to Nightmare Creatures slaughtering innocent people, but I never really faced the malice of those who are free of Corruption. I am quite fortunate, don't you think? To have only ever fought monsters."

The shadow glanced at her with surprise.

“What are you talking about, silly doll? Humans are the most monstrous creatures of them all."

He turned his gaze to his silent kingdom, populated by the shadows of those he had slain.

“Because only humans have a choice. The Creatures of Corruption know nothing but agony and the desire to consume the Flame — they simply act according to their nature. But every human who commits an act of evil does so by choice."

Snuggle stared at him for a moment, then asked:

“Doesn't that make you a human, Lord Titan? After all, you committed this evil act by choice, as well."

The shadow tilted his head a little, feeling vague memories rise from the depths of his mind at the sound of her words.

Choice...

He felt like he had fought desperately for the right to have a choice, a long time ago. He must have won that desperate struggle... and for what?

Was he making good choices? What had he done with the privilege of being able to choose, to have chosen?

He was not sure.

The shadow smiled.

“I was human once... I was human myriad times. But it's strange — the more lives you live as a human, the less humanity you have left. You are right, however. I did make a choice. And that choice... it does seem like an act of evil."

Snuggle stared at him in confusion for a short while, then shook her head.

"Well, anyway... what are you going to do with me? I, uh, I hope you are not planning to add me to your collection of dead souls?"

The little doll shifted uncomfortably and put her hands on her hips.

“Because I—let me tell you! I have not angered you, and I won't be easy to kill. More than that, I have never sacrificed anything to you, so there's no reason to kill me, to begin with!"

The shadow stared at her for a moment, then laughed.

“Who says that I am going to do anything to you? I have no such plans. Do what you want, little soul."

Snuggle stared at him some more.

"Really?"

He nodded.

“Really."

However, she did not seem convinced. After studying him some more, she asked again:

“Really, really?"

The shadow sighed.

"I never lie.”

The little doll hesitated for a few moments, then took a step back.

"So... I can just leave? And you won't pursue me?"

The shadow threw one last wistful glance at Snuggle — the last keepsake of Tatal he had left — and turned away.

"You can, and I won't."

With that, he started to walk away. Soon, his figure was swallowed by darkness.

The little doll was left alone in front of the monument. She remained motionless for a short while, then dashed toward the border of the city.

The shadow sensed her departure, but didn't do anything. Instead, he returned to the steps of the temple and sat down, staring into the darkness.

He could feel the little doll reaching the end of the city and escaping into the wilderness outside. She was moving fast, as if afraid that the frightening lord of this eerie place would reconsider... however, the radiant soul did not abandon its clumsy vessel, choosing to remain a doll.

Perhaps she had felt that the shadow was attached to the ugly thing, and would hesitate to destroy it. So, she remained inside Snuggle, using it as a good luck charm.

The shadow still didn’t move.

If the transient soul wanted to leave, he had no reason to stop it. He did not want to kill it, after all, and neither did he want to imprison her and keep her within the kingdom by force.

He felt a little wistful at the thought of losing Snuggle... but he did not feel like he had the right to keep it, either. The thing he had become was not the same shadow Tatal would call a friend.

So, the shadow simply observed as the doll crossed the lands of his kingdom, feeling a little forlorn.

Soon enough, she reached the edge of the eternal darkness that shrouded the land. She dove into the light without slowing down or hesitating.

The shadow lowered his head.

‘...She could have glanced back, at least.'

After all, he had been quite hospitable to the transient soul. He had even broken the crystal and allowed it to escape the box. But, oh well. He understood her reluctance to stay in his dark kingdom any longer.

‘Good luck, little soul. I hope your travels will be...'

The shadow frowned, failing to finish the thought.

It seemed that the little doll had not made it very far.

Humans avoided the terrifying land of darkness that hid in the heart of this distant realm, so the lands surrounding it were wild and untamed.

..They were also home to countless Creatures of Corruption — some who had always dwelled there, and some who had fled here after being displaced by the swiftly spreading human civilization.

In short, the lands around his kingdom were no different from the primal hell of the world in the Age of Gods.

And the little doll... almost as soon as she left the quiet darkness and escaped into the light, she stumbled into one of the more powerful abominations that dwelled there. The shadow sighed.

‘Does she have the best luck or the worst luck?'

He couldn't tell.

One thing he did know, however, was that it was dangerous for someone whose soul shone with the golden light of divinity to exist in a world drowning in the rot of Corruption.

Somewhere outside his kingdom, a brilliant flash illuminated the sky.

The ground quaked.

--- Chapter 3191 ---

The shadow's senses extended over a vast area... but all of that area was his kingdom. By extending himself across its lightless reach, he had turned himself all but blind to everything that happened beyond its borders.

Still, he felt compelled to watch over the small doll until she disappeared from his sight completely.

So, sitting on the steps of the temple, the shadow remained motionless as a flawless copy of him rose from the darkness.

The second incarnation, too, took the form of a human. It looked down at its human hands and slowly made them into fists.

“It feels strange, to become a human once more."

It was strange, but not alien. After all, the shadow remembered living countless human lives.

The incarnation tilted its head a little.

"Don't you think?"

The shadow smiled faintly and remained silent. He felt no desire to converse with himself.

Shaking its head, the second incarnation dissolved into the darkness. A moment later, he appeared at the very edge of his dark kingdom. Instantly, his senses spread outward, encompassing the untamed wilderness beyond.

All across the primal land of hills and forests, countless creatures shivered, as if feeling a gust of ghostly cold. All shadows seemed to grow a little deeper.

‘Ah... how blinding.’

Having spent many years in the lifeless refuge of his kingdom, the shadow was momentarily dazed by the infinitely dazzling mayhem of life. Its splendor, its multitude, its movement... the teeming revelry of it all was nothing short of violent, assaulting his tired heart.

It took him a few moments to find the little doll...

And the Nightmare Creature that had descended upon the doll, full of frenzied hunger.

The shadow frowned.

That Nightmare Creature... he knew it well. It had been a Supreme Beast once, at the dawn of time — an offspring of one of the first living beings to be created by the gods. However, somewhere along the way, its soul festered with the seeds of Corruption.

It fled to this distant realm and hid, making the depths of the forest its lair. The shadow had sensed the Great Beast prowling the edges of his senses on many occasions, but despite being driven by madness and hunger, the Nightmare Creature never dared to enter his domain. So, the shadow never bothered to eradicate it, either.

The Beast was not very talented — after all, it had failed to rise both in its Rank and its Class over the ages — but it was still one of the more powerful abominations that dwelled in this realm... among those who had survived being the shadow's neighbors, that was.

So, the transient soul had little chance of surviving an encounter with the monster.

It was wearing quite a pathetic shell, after all. Snuggle was not exactly created for battle: she had no armor, no weapons, no fangs, no claws. The shadow was not sure what kind of power allowed the radiant soul to move the tattered doll, but he knew that it did not grant her great strength.

Perhaps if it had chosen a more formidable vessel — a golem forged for battle or the body of a fearsome predator — she could have offered the Great Beast a tough fight. But, as things stood, his unexpected guest would soon be annihilated.

She was quite nimble, true, having escaped his pursuit for a few days. But that was only because the shadow had never aimed to destroy the dazzling soul — if he had wanted to kill her, there would not have been any pursuit at all.

The Great Beast had no such limitations. The shadow's frown deepened.

‘Should I intervene?’

There was no logical reason for him to interfere, and yet, he was reluctant to see the little doll be destroyed. At the same time, he had spent a long time searching for peace, finally finding it within the bounds of his tranquil kingdom. Stepping out of its silent shade felt like an imposition.

Torn, the shadow sighed.

Before he could make a decision, however, the situation suddenly changed.

There was a blinding flash of light, and the ground quaked. Far away, in the distance, the little doll had clashed with the Great Beast — and, to the surprise of the shadow, it was the Great Beast who staggered back, roaring in pain.

"Huh?"

The little doll did not possess weapons, tough armor, sharp claws, or vicious fangs. All it had was its blazing, radiant soul essence — soul essence that belonged to a Transcendent Beast, but was dazzling enough to be mistaken for that of a Supreme.

And, somehow, she had used that essence to make a Beast of higher Rank wail terribly, as if consumed by an unbearable agony. Looking into the distance, the shadow saw something he had never seen before. Something that made even his ancient mind stir in discomfort.

There, within the horrid soul of the Great Beast... the appalling darkness of Corruption was boiling and dissolving, dispelled by radiant streaks of dazzling golden light.

Corruption was being destroyed.

‘H—-how?'

That should not have been possible. In all his countless lives, the shadow had never seen Corruption let something that it had grasped with its claws go. It could be defeated before taking hold of a soul, but never after.

Still...

The soul of the Great Beast was being cleansed of Corruption. The golden light was too weak to purge it entirely, but it diminished the appalling darkness. And, as a result, the Nightmare Creature was weakened. But even if the Great Beast was weakened, it was still a Great Beast. It was an ancient Nightmare Creature that had survived eons of agony and divine persecution, honing its frenzy and deadly rage.

And the radiant soul was still hidden inside an old, tattered doll.

So, their battle ended in a predictable way. However, the shadow did not have to intervene — even if the little doll had failed to defeat the ancient horror, it managed to escape it, at least.

Some time later, a tattered figure flew into the darkness as if shot from a cannon, got tangled in the branches, and rolled lifelessly to the ground after breaking through the canopy.

There were a few moments of silence, and then a squeaky voice broke it weakly:

“Ouch... owie..."

The shadow walked over to where the doll had fallen and looked down at it, unimpressed.

Snuggle had seen better days. It had always been covered in clumsy stitches, having endured countless rips and tears from rough play, but now, it looked like a victim of a particularly vicious delinquent.

Its crude dress was singed. One of its arms was barely attached to the body, and the body itself was torn almost in half. There were many smaller tears, as well, and one of the beads that served as her eyes was missing. Its hair was a tangled mess, with leaves and small branches sticking out of it like a ruined nest.

The shadow sighed.

"Back already?"

Snuggle turned her head and looked at him, her mouth downturned. She remained silent for a short while, then said in a trembling voice:

"Yes, well... it suddenly struck me that I haven't thanked you properly for rescuing me from that crystal, Lord Titan! So, I thought about it and decided to return... in order to express my gratitude. After all, I would hate being seen as ungrateful!"

The shadow studied her pathetic state for a moment.

"Uh-huh."

The little doll tried to stand, but toppled after leaning on her torn leg.

A frenzied roar resounded from somewhere in the distance.

“And, uh... oh, would you look at that! It's already evening. Traveling in the dark is unwise, so I thought I'd stay until morning. Or, you know. A few days. How about that?"

The shadow did not answer immediately. There was no morning in his kingdom, so the question was meaningless. She might as well have asked to stay indefinitely.

At the moment, however, he did not care about that. Instead, he was looking into the depths of the torn doll, feeling a hint of concern. Snuggle had suffered some damage... but it was the transient soul itself that was truly hurt. It was in tatters, having received vicious wounds.

That thing truly possessed mysterious powers.

“Of course. I used to be very good at weaving."

“This one? Hm... well, if memory serves..."

The little doll trembled a little, then looked away.

"Nether, huh? So he's on a first-name basis with a daemon."

Her quiet mumbling sounded dejected.

--- Chapter 3192 ---

In the end, Snuggle stayed — for a few more days, according to her. She was recovering from the wounds received in the battle against the Great Beast splendidly, but somehow, she still seemed downcast.

“A Great Nightmare Creature back home. What a Nightmare!"

The shadow could hear her grumbling from time to time.

“How many of these horrors are out there, for me to slam into one right away? Brrr. Scary!"

Actually, a Great Beast was already a rarity in this era. The Age of Heroes was in full swing, after all. In fact, it had probably passed the halfway mark already, and the vague shape of the Golden Age — the Age of Humans — could already be seen far in the distance. The shadow wasn't quite sure, considering how rarely news of the outside world reached him.

There were still some Great abominations around, and even those who were far more powerful. But meeting one randomly was uncommon — it was just that the realm where the shadow dwelled was quite special in that regard, like a preserve for eldritch horrors.

That was because the heroes of the modern era had not gotten here yet, and the most powerful noble creature who resided in these lands — the shadow — did not feel inclined to go out of his way to battle these abominations. As long as they knew their place, he simply left them alone.

However, he did not feel the need to explain that to the downcast doll.

“What about you, Shadow? Do you clash with Great abominations often? Well... they would scare a Supreme Titan, I suppose.”

The shadow nodded.

“Not that often. And they don't scare me, indeed."

He remained silent for a moment, then added, wanting to appear more relatable:

"It's not like I don't get scared, though. One time, I watched Beast God kill and devour a Void Creature. That gave me a fright."

Snuggle hiccuped.

Somehow, the shadow got a sense that his attempt to seem relatable had not worked. Some time later, Snuggle asked in a timid tone:

"A—anyway. What do you do here for fun?"

The shadow had to contemplate her question.

'What is fun?'

Was it something he enjoyed doing? Eventually, he said:

"I like to sleep."

The little doll stared at him with her beady eyes. Then, she giggled.

“So we have something in common, after all!"

Since Snuggle was going to stay... for a few days... the shadow decided that she needed a place to rest. He didn't want to return to the temple, so he led her to the largest and most opulent structure in the city — the manor where its former lord had lived.

As they entered, Snuggle looked around.

"Is this your house?"

The shadow shrugged.

"All houses in this city are mine."

Around them, the shades of the servants and slaves were busy dusting the floors and performing other tasks needed for the upkeep of the large manor. Their presence seemed to make the little doll uncomfortable, so the shadow called them back into his soul.

"Choose whichever room you like."

Seemingly satisfied, Snuggle scampered away to explore the house. The shadow, meanwhile, followed an instinct and went into the kitchen.

There, he halted in confusion.

‘Why did I come here?'

The shadow had not eaten anything since the dawn of time, and Snuggle was a doll — even if there was a Transcendent soul within it, she still couldn't consume food. Needless to say, there was no food to be cooked in the ancient manor, anyway.

The shadow frowned.

‘I guess treating a guest to some food is just a habit I picked up in my countless lives.'

Tatal used to steal the offerings from his altar, as well. So, it felt strange not to offer Snuggle anything to eat.

Shaking his head, he returned to the foyer.

“Shadow! I'll take the master bedroom!"

A squeaky voice resounded from somewhere deeper in the manor. The shadow shrugged, indifferent to her choice. And that was how his kingdom got a second resident.

As far as residents went, Snuggle was clearly a failure — she did not pay any tax, went around brazenly illuminating the peaceful darkness, and was surprisingly loud despite her small stature.

Still, the shadow somehow found himself enjoying her company.

It was not unpleasant, at least.

So... perhaps that was fun.

Snuggle spent the first few days recovering from her wounds and replenishing her essence. Then, she went to explore the city. After that was done, she began slowly and carefully scouting out the surrounding lands, observing the Nightmare Creature that populated them from a distance.

The more she learned, the more dismayed she became.

“Another Tyrant... what the heck? Is this place really hell? No, there would be an abundance of Devils in hell, so if anything, this place is worse..."

After a while, feeling curious, the shadow finally asked:

“That day when you fought the Great Beast. How did you do it?"

Snuggle stared at him in confusion.

"Did what?"

The shadow sighed.

“I saw it. You weakened the sea of Corruption in his soul — you destroyed some of it, even. I've never seen anything like it."

After hesitating for a moment, he added:

“Destroying Corruption is the domain of death. It should be impossible to cleanse a living creature of Corruption without killing it."

He should know. After all, he was an emissary of death.

The little doll tilted her head a little.

“Oh, that? Well, it's simple. That's my Aspect."

The shadow frowned.

“Only humans have Aspects. You are not a human; you are a soul."

Snuggle raised her chin haughtily.

“So what? I'm a human soul!"

Then, she scaled the leg of a table he was sitting at like an experienced alpinist and sat down, her legs hanging from the edge.

"My Dormant Ability allows my soul to wander as a free spirit and animate various things. My Awakened Ability allows me to heal my own soul. My Ascended Ability allows me to infuse others with my essence to heal or empower them."

The shadow studied the radiant soul that shone within Snuggle.

‘The unusual potency of her essence must be the result of an Attribute, then — or even several of them, including a Divine Lineage. Quite a powerful combination.'

“What about your Transcendent Ability?"

Snuggle coughed in embarrassment.

“Oh... my Transformation, you mean? Well, it's very beautiful and splendid! It gives me a corporeal form. A very beautiful, very magnificent form! Way more majestic and impressive than this doll. However, I can only heal souls, not flesh... so, I don't use it often in this dire place."

She sighed, her shoulders falling.

“Plus, I have misplaced my real body. So, I don't even know how my Transformation would work if I were whole."

The shadow raised an eyebrow. From the sound of it, Snuggle had misplaced her real body some time ago — before she became a Transcendent, at least.

However, that was not very important to him.

“That still doesn't explain how you were able to destroy Corruption."

Snuggle raised her little hands and waved them in front of her beady eyes. The shadow observed her strange antics in silence.

“What are you doing?"

She lowered her hands.

“I'm blinking in confusion!"

The shadow took a deep breath, suppressing the desire to palm his face.

‘Right. She doesn't have eyelids, so why not?'

"What is so confusing about my question?"

Snuggle beamed.

“Well, didn't I already say it? I heal souls!"

He frowned, still unable to understand. Noticing his confusion, the little doll explained:

“Corruption infects souls, does it not? So I can heal souls from that infection, as well."

The shadow stared at her silently.

‘Corruption... is an infection.'

Her explanation was far too simple, but it made a strange kind of sense.

Corruption was indeed an unnatural state. It was the result of foreign influence — that of the Void — twisting and changing the souls of those who were born from the Flame. So, destroying Corruption could indeed be seen as restoring souls to their intended shape. Or, in other words, healing them.

Destruction, restoration... the words were different, but they meant the same thing.

It was a miraculous power, no doubt — especially considering how potent the essence of the radiant soul was, as well as the fact that it was infused with the Flame of Divinity. That attribute, after all, was the antithesis of the Void, and therefore of Corruption.

And since the wandering soul could heal itself, as well, she had to possess a truly fearsome resistance to being Corrupted. Which was not to say that she was completely immune to it. Even the shadow, who was far more powerful than her and a Shadow Creature to boot, was not immune to Corruption. There was no one in the world who could resist it fully — not even the gods...

No. There was one being.

Wasn't there?

“Anyway, why are you asking?"

The shadow shifted slightly, then looked at Snuggle.

“No reason. I was just curious, since I've never seen anything like it before... and I've seen a great deal of things."

He remained silent for a moment, then asked:

“So what are your plans? What do you want to achieve?"

The little doll had been cautiously exploring the outside world, so it seemed that she still harbored a desire to leave — or wanted to make sure that she had a way out, at least.

Snuggle looked away and swung her little feet a few times, in no hurry to answer. Eventually, she shrugged with a smile.

“I am not sure. All this time, I was just trying to survive. But... that's enough of a goal, I think."

She looked at him, her smile widening a little.

“That's because someone will come to rescue me, eventually. I just need to stay alive long enough for that person not to have wasted his time. He'd be quite disappointed to find me dead."

The shadow did not say anything, staring into the distance.

Somehow, an old memory surfaced from the depths of his mind.

He remembered a harrowing abyss full of impenetrable darkness, a narrow cliff, and a lantern that hung from the crossguard of a shattered sword.

And old bones illuminated by the light of the lantern, lying lonesomely amidst the darkness.

He sighed, not knowing why.

After remaining silent for a while, the shadow said:

"I hope you won't have to wait long."

--- Chapter 3193 ---

Days turned into weeks, and weeks turned into months.

It didn't take the transient soul long to fully recover from her wounds. However, even after she mended herself and replenished her essence, the little doll did not seem in a hurry to leave the lightless kingdom that belonged to the shadow — she cautiously scouted its surroundings, but made no effort to venture into the wide world beyond.

That was probably because she was scared. Snuggle maintained a cheerful attitude, but the shadow could tell that there was a deep well of darker emotions hidden behind her bright surface. It was easy to understand why — she had not encased herself in an inescapable crystal without a reason, after all.

An unknown number of years had passed in the real world, but for Snuggle, those events had happened mere days ago. So, it was no surprise that she was in no hurry to embark on another traumatic adventure.

She did not have a good reason to, anyway, from what the shadow could tell. The wandering soul seemed convinced that someone would come to find her, one day in the future — she believed in that person with all her heart, not allowing even the smallest measure of doubt to creep into her thoughts.

And if that was true, then all she had to do was stay alive and wait. The shadow had frightened her at the beginning, but now, she seemed to find his company reassuring. There was no place safer than his kingdom anywhere in this realm — or any mortal realm, perhaps. So why would she leave?

The shadow did not mind her company.

His slow and uneventful existence did not change much. He was still vast and devoid of desire, his consciousness sprawled across the silent reaches of his dark kingdom — devoid of life, devoid of light, populated by no one except a legion of quiet shades.

It was just that now, there was also a little doll living among the shades as well.

The shadow maintained a human incarnation to keep her company, finding her antics a refreshing distraction from the crushing weight of eternity. He did not do much and did not speak often, but the transient soul did enough of that for both of them.

Somehow he even doubted that she knew how to keep quiet. The little doll was a constant source of noise, not to mention light.

The shadow simply kept calling her Snuggle. She did not seem to mind — and despite the nascent bond of trust between them, she did not seem in a hurry to share her true name with him either.

Names had power, after all, and especially so True Names. In the hands of a powerful sorcerer, they could become one's doom... and in the hands of a being such as the shadow, they could become a beacon for the deadly weapon of his Will.

The wandering soul did not seem aware of what the Will was, but she knew enough to keep her True Name a secret. That suited the shadow fine, since he would feel awkward calling the little doll anything but Snuggle anyway.

Snuggle, meanwhile, developed an extremely bizarre habit...

She began talking to the shades.

As the two of them walked the streets of the lifeless city, she was like a squeaky fountain of greetings.

"Oh, hello there, Mr. Miller!"

"Fancy meeting you here, Madam Sash!" "Handsome Guard? What are you doing here? That is not your usual patrol route!" “Lady Hairdo! How was your day?"

The shade of a mature matron with a complicated headdress just gazed at her silently. Snuggle smiled.

“Just as usual, then! Well, I won't keep you. Let's catch up later!"

The shadow stared at Snuggle in utter incomprehension, wondering if she had lost her mind.

Noticing his stare, she glanced in his direction and asked:

"What?"

The shadow lingered a few moments.

"I just can't fathom why you would talk to them."

Snuggle shrugged.

“Why not? Who knows, perhaps they'll respond one day.’

The shadow frowned in confusion.

"They won't. Even if they could, what do you think they would say?"

Snuggle raised one of her hands and supported her chin, contemplating the answer seriously.

Then, she said:

“Something like ‘Oh, gods! A talking doll! Run for your lives!'?"

The shadow blinked a couple of times.

He stared at the little doll, then at the shades that surrounded them.

Eventually, he nodded.

“A reasonable answer."

Snuggle exploded with laughter and scampered forward, forcing him to keep pace.

Eventually, it seemed like she knew everyone in the city. Snuggle spent quite some time observing the lives of the silent shades, asking the shadows questions about their actions from time to time. She was especially interested in the Transcendent shades — there were only a few of them in his kingdom, all holding important posts. The lord of the city, the high priest, the shaman...

Snuggle was fascinated by each one.

"Transcendent humans... three of them, no less! People like them were only a theoretical existence back home. And these ones conquered Transcendence naturally. What an achievement!"

She sighed.

“I wonder what their Aspects were..."

The shadow studied her for a moment.

“Aren't you a Transcendent human, as well? Or a soul of one, at least."

Snuggle nodded.

"Yeah. But I only became Transcendent after ending up here. It just sort of happened as I was trying to survive the collapse of the First Kingdom. Things got pretty ugly when various priests and nobles began fighting for control... being a mere Ascended did not seem like enough, so I had to step up my game."

The shadow looked at her with a dubious expression.

"Countless people survived the fall of the First Kingdom, and most of them were mundane, not Ascended.”

Snuggle laughed awkwardly.

"Yeah, but... how do I say it... most humans don't feel an overwhelming compulsion to poke their noses into other people's business, unlike me. What, did you think I would stand by and do nothing while those priests and nobles were rampaging, committing vile deeds left and right?"

The shadow shrugged.

"I'd think so, yes."

Snuggle scoffed.

“Didn't you annihilate this entire city because of one human sacrifice?"

The shadow did not know what to answer. Eventually, he simply said:

"I did."

More time passed as he and Snuggle slowly got used to each other. By now, the shadow wasn't even surprised by her conversations with the shades, seeing it as something normal.

And that, in turn, pushed him to pay more attention to the shades himself.

The more he studied the shades, the heavier his heart became...

It was the weight of what he had done, catching up with him slowly.

One day, as they took a walk along the outer edges of the city, Snuggle suddenly asked, her squeaky voice cautious:

“Hey, Shadow, don't you... don't you regret it at all?"

Her gaze was directed at the shades of the farmers pretending to tend to the fields beyond.

The shadow hesitated.

Did he regret it? He wasn't sure. He wasn't sure that he knew what regret was, or if he was capable of feeling it still.

He saw life and death differently from mortals, as well.

Eventually, he said:

“I don't regret anything. Regret... is meaningless. It is a desire aimed at the past, and therefore doomed to stay forever unfulfilled."

However, after saying that, he lingered for a moment and added:

"But... when I look at the future, I do feel reluctant to do anything similar ever again. That is the closest thing to regret I know."

Snuggle sighed and turned away from the fields.

"So you do think about the future as well, sometimes."

The shadow raised an eyebrow.

"Of course, I do."

He thought about the future all the time. Mostly, he thought about how there was always a future, for him — for someone who was denied the right to end and become a thing of the past.

The thought made him feel tired.

Snuggle looked up at him and asked, her usual bright tone returning:

"So, is there something you want to do in the future? Something you desire?"

The shadow smiled.

“Something I desire?"

He lingered for a moment, then shook his head.

“Not really. I don't have any desires left, I think."

Snuggle shook her head.

“No, no, that's not true! You just said that you don't want to slaughter cities anymore. That's a desire, as well! So think deep. Think well! If nothing held you back, what would you want to do?"

The shadow would prefer not to answer, but something compelled him to respond anyway.

He looked at the shades that pretended to tend the fields, contemplating.

A sense of placid melancholy slowly settled in his heart.

Eventually, he said:

“Well... actually, I guess there is one thing.”

Snuggle tugged at the hem of his tunic.

"What is it? Come on, tell me!"

He sighed.

“You see... I am a creature of death. All the things I kill become a part of me. So, in a sense, my existence is like a dam that blocks the entrance to the Shadow Realm. Because of me, countless shadows are doomed to never reach the Realm of Death — to stay within me forever. They are like a deep and dark lake, its surface still and unmoving."

The shadow fell silent for a moment.

"A long time ago, I had a friend. She was a mortal woman, and I didn't want to part with her — so, I offered to make her a part of my soul. But she refused... she said that such an existence would be terribly sad. So, she's gone, and we will never meet again."

Snuggle studied him, then asked in her small, squeaky voice:

"So you want to meet your friend?"

The shadow shook his head.

“No. It's impossible. Even if I live forever, I will never see her again. However... I destroyed this city because I was angry, and I was angry because its people had desecrated her memory."

He looked at his shades, his gaze hiding a hint of despondency.

“But wasn't the act of destroying this city a desecration of her memory, as well? And wouldn't the act of keeping these countless shadows trapped within me, forever, make her terribly sad?"

The shadow smiled wistfully.

"I cannot meet my friend again, because she is in the past. I can't bring the city back to life, either. However... I can still set these shades free, somehow. That is the only thing I can do that belongs to the future."

Snuggle tilted her head a little.

"You want to liberate your shades? Let's do it, then! What's stopping you?"

The shadow looked down, taken aback.

He was just thinking aloud. In truth, he had never contemplated releasing his shades seriously before.

How would he even do it?

After a while, he shrugged.

“I don't really know how to set them free. I can consume them... but then they'll still be a part of me. I would have to deliver them to the Shadow Realm, I guess — let Shadow God deal with it."

Snuggle gulped, but then seemed to find her courage again.

“Well, so what? If that is your only desire, let's go knock on Shadow God's door! Let's come and say — here, these are your clients. Sign for delivery!"

The shadow stared at her, baffled.

“It's... not that easy."

Snuggle waved her hands in the air.

“Why not?"

He didn't know what to answer.

“Well, first of all... I don't even know how to get to the Shadow Realm. We'd need a map, or better yet, a guide. Someone who knows the mortal realms well and can lead us to the Hollow Mountains."

The shadow frowned.

Even if they did get to the Hollow Mountains, they would have to brave the Underworld and the Abyss. And then, they would enter the soul of Shadow God, which was not something the shadow really wanted to do.

But perhaps, maybe...

Perhaps if he met Shadow God, he could receive some answers too.

Still, the very idea was crazy.

Leaving his peaceful kingdom? Plunging into the endless chaos of the mortal realms? Braving unknown dangers and willingly entering the Shadow Realm?

Why would he ever want to do that? Looking at Snuggle, the shadow sighed.

"Listen. You don't seem to realize, but the world out there is full of things that even I, a Supreme Titan, can't handle easily. There are powerful Creatures of Corruption, ancient deities, beings of the Flame that can rend me to shreds with a thought, and all kinds of horrors. And let's not forget people! People are the..."

But before he could finish, a stifled hiss suddenly escaped from his mouth.

That was because some distance away, the peaceful silence of his kingdom was suddenly torn apart by a blinding explosion of pale, ethereal light.

The darkness that had shrouded this land for countless years was banished, and a small portion of the city was suddenly revealed under the night sky.

Moonlight poured from the dark heavens like a waterfall, painting the lightless landscape in pale silver.

‘What the hell?'

The shadow turned in that direction, suppressing the searing pain. He frowned.

‘Who dares?’

Snuggle spun, as well.

It was in that moment that a youthful, arrogant voice reached them from the distance.

"Come out and face me, creature!"

The shadow frowned, and then let out a heavy sigh.

‘Damnation.’

It seemed that the Age of Heroes had descended upon his lands, after all.

Some human fool had finally decided to come and bother him.

“Today is the day you die!"

And that fool was an especially obnoxious one, it seemed.

‘Just what kind of idiot would attack me in my own domain?'

As the shadow grimaced and leaned down to pick up Snuggle, the wind carried the voice of the supposed hero to them once more.

"...Because today is the day that you met me, the Crimson Beast of Twilight!"

As if that was not enough, the uninvited fool added:

"The greatest — and most handsome — hero in all mortal realms!"

--- Chapter 3194 ---

Putting Snuggle into a pocket, the shadow clasped his hand behind his back and headed in the direction from which the voice was resounding. Soon enough, he reached the plaza at the edge of the city, where the northbound road turned into its main street.

There, in front of the open city gate, he saw a figure painted in shades of pale silver by the pouring moonlight.

In front of him stood a human youth. The stranger was dressed in dashing, albeit somewhat dusty, robes of pure silk — his garment must have been quite lavish once, but now, the luxurious scarlet dye had faded, and the embroidered hems were frayed. His skin was pale and smooth, and his black hair glistened in the moonlight like onyx.

There was a crescent moon mark on his forehead, and below it, two clear eyes were burning with righteous fury, imbuing his adolescent face with a hint of noble dignity. The shadow sighed inwardly.

‘Another child...’

Despite his youth, the fool who had wandered into his kingdom this time was a Transcendent Beast, no different from Snuggle. In fact, his soul gave off the scent of divinity as well — he had to be a descendant of one of the great gods, without a doubt. This was the Age of Heroes, after all, and there were plenty of them running around.

In fact...
