The shadow felt that the human youth looked strangely familiar. He just couldn't quite place the young man, lost in the boundless ocean of his memories.

So, instead, the shadow simply said:

"Greetings."

Hearing his voice, the youth did a double take and turned to look at him in surprise. After studying the shadow in confusion for a few moments, he suddenly beamed.

“Well met, stranger! What luck, to find a fellow wanderer in this desolate land. However, take heed — a terrifying monster is rumored to dwell in this cursed ruin. I plan to challenge and slay it, so you'd best take cover until the dust settles. We'll savor fine wine and trade stories after I return victorious!"

The shadow stared at the youth, confused. Snuggle, meanwhile, peeked out of his pocket. Looking just as baffled, she glanced at the uninvited guest, remained silent for a moment, and then whispered:

"Is he a fool?"

The shadow did not respond immediately.

‘I mean... that's self-evident.'

He gave her a subtle nod, then followed an impulse and asked:

"A terrifying monster?"

The youth threw a tense look into the darkness, then sighed.

“Indeed! You might not know, but this land was prosperous once, populated by enlightened humans. But then, one day centuries ago, all communications with them ceased. When the merchants arrived to trade as usual, all they found was a dead city shrouded by eternal darkness. And, what's worse... something dwelled in the heart of the city."

He grimaced with disdain.

"It was a vicious, ghastly abomination! The one I came here to kill."

The shadow tilted his head a little.

“Really? What kind of abomination?"

The youth looked hesitant for a moment.

"Well... no one knows for sure, and the legends people of the surrounding realms tell all differ. Some describe it as a giant beast with seven heads and the tail of a beaver, some say that it looks like a human with the head of a mountain goat. In any case, it's extremely hideous, grotesque, and unsightly! That's why it lives in darkness, afraid to see its own face."

He sighed.

“That creature is not only extremely abhorrent and revolting, though, it is also extremely powerful. It subjugated all the people of this land and turned them into its servants. Now, those poor souls live in the darkness, having long ceased being human. So, I — the legendary hero, Noctis — came to cleanse this land of Corruption. I came to banish the darkness and return this land to the light of the Moon!"

The shadow studied him for a moment, then threw a furtive glance at Snuggle. Perhaps she knew what he was supposed to do.

But Snuggle just raised her hands and shook her head, similarly stumped.

The shadow sighed.

Standing at the edge of light, he said:

“Oh. I see. However, you are not entirely correct."

The youth raised an eyebrow.

"I'm not? What do you mean, stranger?"

The shadow nodded.

“You see, I never subjugated the people of this city. I merely killed them all. I killed all the beasts, insects, and Creatures of Corruption as well. So... it is not as though I have something against humans in particular. Even if they are the most bothersome bunch."

The youth laughed.

“Well said!"

But then, he froze.

“Uhm... wait. What did you just say, stranger? Did you say... that you were the one who killed these people?"

He stared at the shadow again, a clear expression of incomprehension on his face. Then, he chuckled nervously.

“Don't jest. You are clearly a human... a gentleman of refined upbringing, by the look of it. Even if you do, regrettably, suffer from a lack of taste and seem to be in the habit of wearing drab colors, that's no reason to bring yourself down!"

The shadow blinked a couple of times.

"I just look like a human for the sake of convenience. Would you prefer I take the shape of a giant beast with seven heads and the tail of a beaver? Or should I simply change my head for that of a mountain goat? It's no bother, really. Just say the word."

The youth hiccuped.

"No, no... what are you talking about? The creature that dwells in this land is... is..."

He had already looked pale in the moonlight, but now, his face seemed ghostly white.

The shadow shrugged.

"Is me. Welcome to my kingdom, young Noctis... Crimson Beast of Twilight, was it? Didn't you say that I should come and face you? Since today is the day I die. So, here I am."

The youth studied him for a few moments, then composed himself and forced out an arrogant laugh.

“I see. So the monster who caused the ruin of this city is none other than you! You... uh... what should I call you?"

The shadow shrugged.

"Call me Shadow."

The youth scoffed.

“You vile shadow! As I was saying... I came here to slay you! So, prepare to die!"

The shadow studied him with a dubious expression. The youth was putting on a brave face, but he clearly seemed unnerved. And why wouldn't he be? The shadow was truly an unnerving existence.

Noctis had a reason to be confident in his prowess, perhaps. He was a Transcendent — even if it looked like he had only reached Transcendence recently — and a descendant of one of the great gods to boot. He had also reached this place alone, braving the wilderness beyond.

Even if he had been lucky to avoid the most powerful abominations that dwelled there, he still had to have fought quite a few of them, and yet, he was unscathed.

However, he clearly had not expected to meet a creature that could take any form it wished, was capable of human speech, and seemed just as intelligent as a human. Beings like that were supremely dangerous. He might have already realized that his opponent was Supreme, as well. It was just that he had not realized that the shadow was a Titan.

But, really...

‘So he wants to kill me?’

He had nothing to worry about.

The shadow nodded.

“Okay."

Noctis stared at him in confusion.

"Huh? What do you mean, okay?"

The shadow shrugged.

"Go on, kill me.”

The human youth frowned, then raised a hand.

“Don't think that I won't!"

The shadow just stared at him.

Nothing happened for a few moments.

So, the shadow spoke with a hint of impatience in his voice:

“Alright? Come on, you may begin."

Noctis hesitated for a bit, then lowered his hand and glanced at the shadow with suspicion.

"What kind of ruse is this? Are you trying to deceive me, creature? Let me tell you — I am the smartest hero in this land! Or any land! The likes of you won't ever be able to outsmart me, so you should just give up the thought right now."

The shadow frowned.

“There is no ruse, young human. In truth, I've longed to die for a long time now... since before the dawn of time, when the gods themselves were young. So, I decided that I might as well let you try. Go on, do your best... your worst? Anyway, strike me down with all your might. I won't resist."

Noctis stared at him in stunned silence. Then, he cursed.

"You are taking all the fun out of it, knave!"

Then, he gritted his teeth.

“But I'll take you up on that offer. So, get ready!"

As the youth raised his hand again, Snuggle suddenly jumped out of the shadow's pocket and swiftly climbed to his shoulder. There, she raised her hands and squeaked:

"Wait! Don't do it, please! If you do, someone is really going to die... and it won't be Shadow!"

The young man lowered his gaze and stared at her.

Then, he somehow paled even more. Noctis opened his mouth, then closed it again.

Then, he suddenly screamed in horror:

“Oh, gods! A talking doll! Shadow, run for your life!"

--- Chapter 3195 ---

‘How did it end up this way?’

The shadow remembered his peaceful past. The tranquil quiet of his lightless kingdom, the uneventful years he had spent slumbering in the darkness...

Now, there was bright light illuminating the vast hall, and not one, but two boisterous voices chasing away the silence.

“Thank the gods... so you're just a disembodied soul, not actually a living doll!"

“Of course. But why are you using informal speech when addressing me?"

"What are you talking about? Look at you. You're so tiny and squeaky!"

“So what?! I might be tiny, but l am a mature, respectable woman! You brat!"

“Who are you calling a brat, pipsqueak? I am Noctis, the Crimson Beast of Twilight. l am a Transcendent hero! I am already nineteen!"

"See! I am... huh, wait, how old am I? Twenty-nine? Yeah, that's right!"

"Oh? Oh... well, sorry then. Auntie."

“Auntie?! Did you just call me an auntie?!"

The shadow sighed heavily.

Currently, they were in the house of the city lord. Snuggle was seated on the table, her chin raised arrogantly. The human youth — Noctis — was sitting on a chair, tied up and unable to move. The ropes that bound him were woven out of shadows, strong enough to hold a Supreme being... so, he wasn't going to cause trouble any time soon.

Or maybe he was. Humans were unpredictable, after all — each possessed a unique Aspect, and if the shadow really wanted to contain one, a simple rope would do him no good. He would have to enchant it, somehow, and that felt like too much effort.

In any case, tying the adolescent Transcendent up was only a temporary measure. The shadow had to figure out what to do with him soon.

‘Should I just kill him?'

There was no reason to, so the shadow knew that he wouldn't. Still, a shadow could dream, right?

‘Maybe he'll just go away on his own...’

The shadow looked at Noctis.

Noctis... did not seem like a problem that would go away on its own.

What was worse, now that a Transcendent human had come to battle him, there would most likely be another, and another, and another... the sphere of human influence was expanding, and the forces of Corruption were slowly dwindling. This distant realm was not so remote anymore.

Another heavy sigh escaped from the shadow's lips.

If he would not kill the human youth, and the youth was not going to go away... then what was there to do? The shadow was a little stumped.

He was a creature of death, after all. All he knew was how to kill; if there was something that had to be resolved peacefully, he was just as powerless as a mundane person.

Luckily, Snuggle was there, and she seemed perfectly suited to solve the problem for him. In fact, even if their conversation sounded like a meaningless exchange of insults, the little doll seemed to be guiding it carefully in some mysterious direction.

“So, Noctis... why did you suddenly decide to come challenge the Shadow, anyway? Even if you are a Transcendent, that seems a little too reckless."

Noctis frowned, then threw a furtive glance at the shadow.

Then, he forced out an arrogant laugh.

“What's so reckless about it? Let me tell you, sister... I have slain plenty of Creatures of Corruption. Among all the heroes in the world, there is hardly anyone more fearsome than I!"

He paused for a moment, his haughty smile dimming slightly.

Noctis remained silent for a short while, then added in a more somber tone:

"Human life is fragile and fleeting. All across the mortal realms, countless people are fighting desperately to survive. There is not enough space for everyone, and not enough food for everyone. Scarcity gives birth to poverty and destitution — two vicious beasts that devour dreams and suffocate joy, turning good people into empty husks."

His expression darkened.

“I mean... have you seen the clothes that poor people wear? Those ugly things are an affront to all that is good in life! And their houses! My noble eyes were not made to look at dusty hovels. And let's not even mention the smell..."

Noctis shuddered, a horrified grimace appearing on his face.

Snuggle stared at him with an indescribable expression.

She did not speak for a few moments, then cleared her throat.

"So... you decided to attack Shadow, a Supreme Titan, because you don't like how poor people smell?"

Noctis looked at the shadow, his eyes widening.

“A what now? A S—supreme... T—titan?"

The shadow smiled politely.

"Indeed."

Noctis stared at him for a moment, then raised his chin.

"Well, so what? I must admit — even I, the great and astonishing Noctis, have not slain a Supreme Titan yet. And I might have expected to find something like a Corrupted Tyrant... perhaps a Great Beast or two... here. But! You refused to battle me, using a cunning trick to restrain me instead. So who's to say that I won't win if we fight?"

He scoffed, then sighed and shook his head.

“But that is not what I mean. Beyond the reaches of this wild realm, humans and the Creatures of Corruption are fighting a war for dominion over the world. Transcendent heroes like me are the champions of humanity. Unlike many, I've lived a life of privilege and abundance — I've never been exposed to the bitterness of destitution, let alone to suffering and tragedy."

Noctis coughed and tried to scratch his nose, but failed — his hands were tied, after all.

“Truth be told, I grew up in a temple of the Moon, my grandmother. Once I came of age and Ascended, I left to wander the world... and once I saw how bitterly humans fought to live, I was rattled. It was only then that I truly understood the lessons that the priests had taught me and my siblings — all those words about duty, courage, and the Path of Ascension. About what those who wield power ought to do. So, I endeavored to distinguish myself, like other heroes had."

He sighed.

“Only, the thing is... as it turned out, it's actually not that easy to distinguish yourself these days. There are already plenty of heroes around, and most of them are older, wiser, and more experienced than me. Plus, the Creatures of Corruption are not endless either — with so many of them already slain, finding a worthy opponent is such a hassle! And lastly, I am a direct descendant of a god."

Noctis flashed them a smile.

“So, the burden of expectations piled onto me is truly great! Almost as great as I am... and I am the greatest there is, of course. As well as the most handsome, gallant, charming, and refined. Not to mention the most humble."

He looked at them with a self-satisfied smile.

"If I want to have a legend or two to my name, killing just any random abomination won't do. I need to accomplish something outstanding!"

The haughty youth cleared his throat.

"That was why I thought to slay the mysterious creature that had been scaring people away from this realm for generations."

The shadow and Snuggle glanced at each other.

After a few moments of awkward silence, the shadow spoke:

“So you just went and challenged this supposedly terrifying creature without learning anything about it first? Weren't you afraid that I will slay you instead?"

Noctis scoffed.

“Slay me? As if! Nothing has managed to slay me yet, and there is a reason for that. In truth, I know a secret heroic technique that makes me all but immortal."

The shadow raised an eyebrow.

"You do?"

The youth nodded with an expression of absolute confidence.

“Of course! It's called running away."

As the shadow and Snuggle stared at him silently, Noctis laughed.

“If an enemy is too strong, running away is always an option. And even if boasting is not something I do often — or ever, really, the refined gentleman that I am — let me tell you one thing. There may be heroes who are older than me, wiser than me, and more famous than me. But there's no one who is better than me at running away! If I say that I am the second most elusive man in the world, no one would dare to say that they're the first!"

The shadow suppressed an exasperated groan.

Snuggle, meanwhile, asked in her squeaky voice:

“Aren't you sitting here tied up right now?"

Noctis looked at the ropes binding him, then glared at the little doll for a split second, and then put on a condescending expression.

“What, these ropes? Ha! I am just tolerating them out of courtesy. If I wanted to, I could give you a slip in an instant. One blink, and I'd be out of this crumbling palace. Another blink, and I'd disappear into the darkness!"

The shadow tilted his head.

“I don't blink, though."

The smile froze on the youth's face.

The shadow, meanwhile, added:

“And the darkness outside is just a part of me. So... where exactly are you going to disappear to?"

Noctis remained silent for a while, then opened his mouth.

Then, he closed it again.

Finally, he said in a small voice:

"Well, anyway. You wouldn't want to offend my grandmother, right? So... let's just forget I ever said anything?"

Snuggle nodded a couple of times.

“Indeed, indeed. We should respect the elders. Oh, by the way..."

Her beady eyes glinted.

"Did you say that you wanted to accomplish something outstanding?"

Her mouth twisted into a smile.

"I have just the thing in mind!"

--- Chapter 3196 ---

Snuggle had, indeed, an outstanding feat in mind.

She wanted Noctis to escort them to the Shadow Realm.

There was some merit to her idea, no doubt. After all, neither of them were familiar with the mortal realms and people who populated them — both the shadow and Snuggle were completely ignorant of their customs and traditions, let alone invisible undercurrents that ruled all human societies. They did not know what roads to take and which places to avoid, so they needed a guide.

Well... the shadow could probably find his way to the Realm of Death on his own, eventually. It was just that he would most likely leave a trail of devastation in his wake, which Snuggle wanted to avoid.

Noctis, meanwhile, was not only knowledgeable about the world outside the shadow's lightless kingdom, but also held quite a lofty status among humans — his fame and background alone could open numerous doors for them. And he would probably know where to go, as well. Traveling with a Supreme Titan to one of the Divine Realms was a journey worthy of becoming a legend, so it was in his own interest too.

There was just one problem...

Noctis glanced at the little doll with a lack of amusement on his youthful face.

"To the Shadow Realm, you say?"

Snuggle nodded with a grin.

"Yeah!"

He hesitated for a moment.

"So you are telling me... to just go die?"

The young man grimaced and glanced at the two of them with dismay.

"Listen, friends, if you want to kill yourself, go ahead and have at it! But what do I have to do with any of this? Leave me out of your peculiar suicide pact, please! I am too young to die! Too gorgeous!"

Snuggle waved a hand in front of her face weakly.

"No, wait, I didn't mean it that way..."

The shadow suppressed a smile.

Going to the Shadow Realm had a distinct meaning in most human languages, and that meaning was, simply put, to die. So, it was no surprise that Noctis misunderstood the little doll.

She groaned.

“I meant it literally! Walk down there! Find the Hollow Mountains, traverse the Underworld, jump into the Abyss, say hi to Shadow God! Then come back and have a party!"

Noctis studied her intently, as if contemplating something.

Eventually, he asked, a hint of interest in his voice:

"Party? What kind of party... wait, no! Who would want to party with you?! You're a disembodied soul! You can't even drink!"

Snuggle scoffed.

"You're too young to drink anyway, brat! What kind of priests raised you?!"

With a sigh, the shadow rose and left them to it. He walked out of the hall and then exited the lord's manor, looking into the vast darkness beyond.

Of course, that dark expanse was nothing but a part of him, so peering into it was no different from peering into himself.

Even if he had left the manor, he was still there, listening to two human youths bicker.

Everything in this kingdom belonged to him, was him — the darkness, the shades crowding the streets, the dark trees swaying in the wind. The forests, the fields. Even the buildings of the ancient city had deteriorated with the passage of time, and were held up by the shadows he commanded.

If he left, all of it would disappear. Everything would simply vanish, as if it had never existed at all.

There would be only a lifeless ruin left. But even that ruin would be reclaimed by life eventually — possibly in a hundred years, or possibly in a thousand; grasses and vines would swallow the weathered stones, burying them in the depths of earth.

This land had been his home and shelter since before the world splintered into innumerable realms. Was he really ready to leave?

All of it... was a little bit too sudden.

The shadow could appear anywhere in his kingdom in the blink of an eye, but he chose to walk along the dark streets, looking around with an expression of melancholy. In truth, this city had never felt like home. There were barely any traces of what he remembered left here — everything had been rebuilt, transformed, and altered. A paved plaza lay where the huts of the nomads had once been raised; the familiar fields had long been swallowed by the city sprawl. An imposing temple towered where a humble shrine had stood, and even the old graves were gone.

So was there really anything holding him back?

From the dawn of time, the shadow had only ever wanted one thing — to exist in peace, which was the closest thing to non-existence he could achieve. And from the dawn of time, true peace had eluded him.

Maybe it was time to give up on his impossible goal.

Before the shadow knew it, his feet brought him to a familiar place. He found himself in front of the old cave where he used to reside... a long time ago.

The city was different, and the land was different as well. But the cave was still the same.

Or so it seemed.

As the shadow entered his old abode, he felt nothing. No comfort, no attachment. Just emptiness.

Tatal was not here anymore, and the sound of her voice would never echo between these stone walls again. The silver bell was not here, either.

Even Snuggle was gone, having become a vessel to a peculiar, wandering soul.

The bell and the doll were the only two things he had ever kept in the cave, so without them, there was nothing left.

‘Must I really leave?'

Turning his head faintly, the shadow observed the innumerable shades that populated his lightless kingdom. They were pretending to be alive to chase away his boredom... but they weren't alive.

He had killed them, and now, he was holding them captive within his soul. Unchanging, uncaring. Utterly quiet. Suddenly, their existence did indeed seem awfully sad.

Just like his own.

The shadow sighed.

‘Shadow God is the god of death, peace, and solace. But... he is also the god of mysteries.'

So perhaps... would he shine light on the mystery of the shadow's peculiar fate?

The shadow left the cave and stopped in front of the altar standing in front of it. There were still human remains lying atop the altar, white bones resting in the darkness, a skull staring at him with reproach in its empty eyes.

He remained in front of the altar for a long time, looking at the old bones.

That was where Snuggle found him, eventually.

“Shadow! Hey, Shadow! Where did you go?"

The shadow let out a sigh and glanced away from the decrepit skeleton, shielding his eyes from the radiance emanating from the little doll.

She climbed the altar, gave the skeleton a wary gaze, and then raised her head to beam at the shadow.

“It's all good! I've convinced him. That kid is a bit of a wastrel, but he has a good heart. And despite how he behaves, he's clever. He'll be a good guide for us."

The shadow gave her a long look. Eventually, a faint smile twisted his lips.

“I never said that I would go with you."

Snuggle raised her chin.

“Hmmph!"

She crossed her arms — which looked a bit comical, considering how short they were — and said:

“I never said that I would go with you, either!"

The little doll turned away defiantly.

“Do you want me to go? Ask first! Say please, pretty please!"

The shadow hesitated for a few seconds, then threw a glance down the mountain, where the dead city lay in the darkness. Eventually, he nodded.

“Will you go to the Shadow Realm with me, Snuggle? Please?"

She turned around and glanced at him and smiled.

"Okay!"

Then, her smile slowly disappeared, and a rare serious expression settled on her crude doll face.

"However, Shadow... I have a condition. You must agree to something first if you want me to accompany you."

He raised an eyebrow.

“What kind of condition?"

Snuggle remained silent for a long while, then said solemnly:

“You must promise not to kill anyone on this journey — or any thing. For as long as we're together."

The shadow stared at her in confusion.

He was a little baffled.

"l am an heir of Death. And you expect me not to kill anything?"

Snuggle nodded seriously.

“Wouldn't things be too easy otherwise? Listen, Shadow — Sister Snuggle will teach you a valuable lesson! Only things that aren't easy are worth a damn, most of the time. So, come on! Promise."

The shadow remained silent for a while. Eventually, he asked with a hint of hesitation:

"Not even Creatures of Corruption?"

Snuggle shrugged.

“Noctis and I will kill the Creatures of Corruption. You just focus on not becoming Corrupted yourself!"

The shadow studied her for a few long seconds, then sighed.

‘What am I getting myself into?’

Walking past the altar — and the bones lying on it — he nodded.

“Alright. I promise."

***

Soon enough, the three of them stood at the edge of the city. Well, Shadow and Noctis were standing, at least — Snuggle was seated comfortably on Shadow's shoulder.

"Are you really ready?"

Shadow closed his eyes for a moment and nodded.

Then, he opened his eyes and absorbed his kingdom into himself.

Suddenly, a terrible wind rose, and the darkness around them seemed to rush like a flood — rush into the depths of his soul, where it had come from.

All across the lightless land, innumerable shades vanished without a trace. The streets of the city were suddenly empty, devoid of the false life that had filled them just a moment ago.

The shadows he had manifested collapsed into their natural form. The trees in the forests and the stalks swaying in the fields disappeared, leaving behind only desolate soil.

The shadow holding up the ancient building vanished as well, and the entire city shuddered. Countless homes collapsed with a thunderous roar, and a billowing cloud of dust rose into the air.

And then, for the first time in innumerable years...

Rays of sunlight fell upon the broken land, shining through the dust as they illuminated the vast ruin.

Shadow studied the forlorn, lifeless scene of the devastated city before him for a long while.

Then, with a sigh, he turned his back on it.

"Let's go."

The twisting roads of the mortal realms awaited...

And somewhere at the end of them, the realm of Shadow God awaited, as well.

--- Chapter 3197 ---

The first few days of their journey were rather uneventful. Before, when Snuggle attempted to leave Shadow's kingdom, she had to battle powerful Creatures of Corruption — but now that Noctis was with them, the path seemed clear.

That was because the young Transcendent had already scouted out the safest route to the mysterious ruins, learning how to sneak past the most fearsome beings populating the realm. He had also slain a few abominations on his way to challenge Shadow, so now they simply needed to retrace his steps.

Shadow was not worried about stumbling into some ancient horror — he was one such horror himself, after all — but even he felt that avoiding them was a better solution. He had promised Snuggle not to kill anything on their journey, after all. Since he did not know what else to do with Creatures of Corruption, the idea of fighting one made him a little bit uncomfortable.

Noctis had indeed proven to be a convenient guide... however, there was something about him that eluded Shadow's grasp. It was a faint sense of familiarity, as if he had met this human youth already, a long time ago, but couldn't quite remember when.

Well, that wasn't surprising.

First of all, Shadow could very well have met Noctis in one of his countless lives — or even several of them. In fact, he vaguely sensed that if he delved into the memories of those of his lives that had been tainted by insidious madness, he would most likely learn more about the fate of Noctis. However, Shadow didn't particularly want to remember madness, so he did not give in to curiosity.

Secondly, Noctis was a descendant of Beast God. So, the sense of familiarity Shadow sensed could simply be explained by the scent of divine blood flowing through the youth's veins.

However, there was a third reason as well. Shadow learned the last reason after finally surrendering to his curiosity and brushing his ghostly fingers across the thread of the young man's fate. He did not peer into it too deeply, unwilling to learn too much, but what he saw surprised him a great deal.

‘What are the chances?'

Shadow was truly stunned.

As it turned out, there was a connection between him and Noctis.

The young man’s father was a demigod born of a union between the avatar of Beast God and a mortal man. His mother, however, was a princess of a prosperous human kingdom — a stunning beauty with fiery red hair. People with red hair were rumored to be descendants of the Fox Tribe, and the princess was no exception. In fact, her bloodline could be traced to an obscure branch of the Fox Tribe that had vanished a long time ago — it was just that neither the princess nor her royal family knew of that connection.

The princess only knew that a distant ancestor of hers was the heroine of a popular folk song — a great shaman who had slain a powerful beast to protect her people myriad years ago.

That shaman was none other than Tatal, and the obscure branch of the Fox Tribe that had disappeared from history was the nomadic people who would eventually become the Shadow Tribe.

Noctis came from the bloodline of one of Tatal's children who had married into faraway lands.

After realizing that fact, Shadow stared at the youth for a long time.

His gaze, it seemed, made Noctis uncomfortable.

"What?"

Noctis raised his chin slightly and forced out a smile.

“Listen... I know that my beauty is peerless and my face is like jade, worth writing a hundred songs about, but surely an ancient being like you wouldn't be mesmerized by it, as well?"

Shadow stared at him for a few more moments, then turned away and grumbled:

"I wouldn't. Why do foxes always get entangled with wolves?"

Even if that fool was Tatal's descendant, he clearly took after Stone Hand. Otherwise, Shadow couldn't explain where his personality had come from.

‘Beast of Twilight... Beast of Twilight...’

Even though Shadow pulled his consciousness away from the human youth's fate, he could still feel its thread trembling, ringing in the vast expanse of eternity.

And even if he didn't want to remember, visions of the past — of the future — still flooded his mind.

Only, this time, the life he saw was not one he had lived personally. It was also far too long, far too vast to remember it all, split between fate and fatelessness, twisted unnaturally, imbued with a strange and impossible duality...

Fragmented memories flashed past his eyes.

He saw a tranquil temple. He saw human cities drowning in the sea of Corruption. He saw Transcendent champions shining like bright flames in that darkness. He was one of these champions, as well — young, brash, full of brazen determination to reshape the world into a more beautiful form.

But he was also full of keen perception and compassion that he hid behind the mask of carefree shallowness. And the more he saw, the more he witnessed, the deeper his heart was cut by the sharp edges of the world.

He saw it all...

The suffering, the fear, the bitter plight of those who were too weak to push away the darkness on their own.

As well as a different kind of darkness that dwelled in their hearts. There was Corruption, and there was corruption — the more he lived, the less he knew which one was worse.

But he still believed in brighter things. He still had hope.

And then, one day, a shining god had asked him to become a chain that bound hope.

He agreed.

What followed next... was madness.

He was mad for a long, long time. Far longer than any mortal was supposed to live. And in his madness, he always asked himself — what was it that the shining god truly expected of him?

Was he supposed to hold hope captive?

Or had he always been meant to set hope free?

The longer he carried out his maddening duty, the better human lives in distant realms seemed to become. The world was not as harsh anymore. There was less suffering, less bitterness, and less fear. It was a different age — a golden age... an age where the darkness of Corruption did not torment humans anymore, leaving them to deal with only human darkness.

He wanted to break the chains of hope and set her — and himself — free. But he was also afraid of what would come next.

He feared that the world would come undone if he did.

But he was mad, after all.

So what did he care about all that? So, in the end, he decided to act.

And he made a deal with a daemon.

"Really, damn it all, by the Moon! How... how did it come to this?!"

Donning a black mantle and a black mask, he stared at his own reflection in dismay. That dastardly daemon!

Why did all these things have to be black? Did daemons have no taste?

He shook his head and groaned. The world had not even ended yet, but the worst possible things were already happening.

His face was hidden behind the mask, and he did not even have his name anymore. That was because his original fate had been discarded, replaced by another, stolen one — the fate that could allow him to die, but also demanded that he live a little bit longer.

“Alright. Let's have fun with all of this, at least..."

He became the High Priest of the Nightmare Spell — a heretic pursued by everyone who worshipped the great gods.

It took a lot of talent and tenacity to stay alive, and it took even more to accomplish his mission. Slowly but surely, his followers spread across existence, carrying the Nightmare Spell with them. He had become Supreme, and just in time as well — before he could even blink, the Doom War was upon them, and existence trembled as countless people were destroyed.

“What a mess..."

It was as if the madness he had kept contained for a thousand years exploded outward, consuming every realm. Hope proved to be quite dangerous, indeed...

As the fires of war consumed more and more people, spreading the faith in the Nightmare Spell became easier and easier. Desperate people were far easier to convince, after all, and he was a very convincing man.

But everything had to come to an end. Eventually, the world itself came to an end, as well.

Myriad people died, and those who survived were being swiftly consumed by Corruption. Even the gods died... even the daemons.

Even the scoundrel who had roped him into wearing all black was gone.

But, funnily enough, even though he wasn't immortal anymore, he still lived.

His spirit had sustained dreadful wounds, and his Domain had been annihilated. His followers had all scattered or perished. His body was ready to crumble, and his soul was tired...

But he was still alive, for now.

He didn't really know what to do.

There was nothing really left to do, anyway. So, out of habit, he decided to set out on one last journey. He decided to bring the Nightmare Spell to those few who were yet to perish on the ruins of the destroyed world.

His feet eventually carried him to a land that was consumed by eternal darkness. There was no sun here, no stars... there was no moon.

He missed the moon the most.

All light was gone, but people still persisted in the darkness, refusing to die. Just like him. So, he helped them fight the terrifying creatures that dwelled in the darkness, offering those who were willing to become carriers of the Nightmare Spell.

Fighting against the darkness to help humans survive...

Ah. It reminded him of his youth.

Only, in the end, the very people he had tried to save betrayed him.

Taking advantage of his weakened state, they imprisoned him in a small cell under a magnificent cathedral, bound him with powerful sorcery, and closed the door shut. He was a heretic, after all, so they did not trust him.

That was why he spent quite a long time in that cell.

It was terribly boring.

Even knowing that he would die here, he didn't mind.

He had lived a long life, after all, a glorious life.

A life full of brightness and splendor.

It was just that...

“That damn daemon... I was fooled in the end, wasn't I?"

He had always considered himself a peerless scoundrel, but that daemon! That knave had truly been without a rival, as far as lies and deception were concerned.

Eventually, he felt seeds of Corruption blooming in his soul. Corruption was everywhere now, and all things fell to it... he was not going to be an exception. However...

"No, no. That just won't do."

He had already been forced to wear all black — that horrible, drab color! — and now, even his soul would become impenetrably dark? How tasteless was that!

Sealed in the darkness, he laughed.

Then, straining his broken body, he traced a few words in the dust.

His final farewell...

Hail Weaver

Demon of Fate

Fistborn of the Forgotten God!

Looking at that final message with satisfaction, he remembered his life.

He remembered the many battles he thought... the many friends he had made along the way, then lost.

The countless pleasures of life that he had experienced.

The beauty of it all.

A sigh escaped from beneath the fearsome mask.

"Ah... I really didn't do too bad, did I?"

This life...

It had been everything he had hoped for.

"Farewell."

With that, he shattered his spirit and extinguished his soul.

--- Chapter 3198 ---

Eventually, they did meet an abomination that Noctis had neither slain nor knew how to avoid. It was a Corrupted Tyrant and its brood — a nest of vile creatures that looked like leaves from afar, only to turn into a cloud of grotesque locusts with razor-sharp wings that blotted out the sky, painting the world in shades of dim emerald.

The Tyrant itself was like a locust queen, its brown carapace resembling a branching reef. When the giant creature moved, it was as if a section of the forest suddenly came alive, gazing at them with chilling malice.

"P—prepare to die, vermin!"

Noctis seemed pale as he faced the vast cloud of abominations. Shadow was not sure why exactly, though — it would be natural to feel a measure of fear in the face of such peril, but it was just as likely that the Transcendent youth simply disliked insects a great deal.

Perhaps it was simply because Noctis seemed at his weakest when the sun was high in the sky.

In any case, Shadow did not count the youth's chances of defeating the Corrupted Tyrant and her swarm high. Dealing with vast swarms of tiny abominations was quite tricky, after all — unless one had a suitable Aspect or an enchanted weapon, the fiercest of warriors could be rendered powerless in a battle like that.

Snuggle did not seem very adept at battling swarms of abominations, either. She could ignite the soul of the Corrupted Tyrant, weakening the creature and making it not much stronger than a Fallen Tyrant would have been... but that wasn't going to help them survive.

However, the Shadow could solve the problem easily.

He could annihilate the entire swarm in an instant by simply willing it to die. Eradicating great numbers of weaker creatures was exactly what he excelled at. He could tear the giant Tyrant to shreds in no more than a few seconds, as well. After all, he excelled at slaying strong creatures too.

But...

He couldn't.

Because he had been foolish enough to promise Snuggle not to kill anything.

‘Hmm... this is a bit problematic.’

Shadow was really not sure what to do.

As he contemplated calmly, the vast cloud of abominations drew closer, the swiftest of them already rushing down from the sky. The lumbering Tyrant was slowly approaching, as well.

Snuggle squealed and hurriedly hid in his pocket. Noctis, meanwhile, trembled and backed away until he was standing directly in front of Shadow, staring at the dim emerald world with apprehension.

"H—hey, Shadow. What do we do?"

He paused for a moment, then forced out a few more words.

"I can probably deal with a third... a half of these abominations! But someone will have to deal with the rest. Then, we can bring down the Tyrant together... right?"

A squeaky voice resounded from Shadow's pocket:

"Right! Go on, then!"

Noctis glanced over his shoulder with a startled expression.

"What do you mean, go on? You go on! Let's go together!"

The locusts had almost reached them by then.

‘What to do, indeed?’

Finally, Shadow came to a conclusion.

‘Right. That is also an option...’

With that, he raised a hand and placed it on the young hero's shoulder.

And then, he pulled the three of them — himself, Noctis, and Snuggle — into the shadows.

A moment later, they stepped out of them hundreds of kilometers away, on the shore of a placid lake.

There was no sign of the swarm of locusts of their enormous queen.

Noctis staggered and looked away in stunned silence.

He blinked a couple of times.

"Huh? Where are we?"

Shadow shrugged.

"Far away."

Noctis stared at him for a short while. Slowly, his face regained some color, and his tense body relaxed.

Then, he said in a tone of reproach.

"Listen, Shadow... we are friends, but don't you have any shame? Stealing my special heroic technique already! I shared it with you in confidence!"

Laughing, Noctis shook his head and let out a relieved sigh while patting his chest.

“What did I tell you? Running away is always an option!"

Shadow nodded seriously.

"Indeed."

He had never had to run away from something before, but that technique was really quite wondrous.

Noctis, meanwhile, inhaled a few times deeply, then froze for a moment.

Then, he glanced at Shadow in confusion.

“So, wait, you can just jump from one place to another in a second?"

Shadow simply nodded.

The corner of the young man's eye twitched.

“Then why, by the Moon, did we spend these past few days walking?! You could have just brought us to where we need to go!"

He glanced down with an aggrieved expression.

“Look at my clothes! They are so dusty! The hems are all frayed! It could all have been avoided!"

Shadow looked at him silently for a while. Eventually, he shrugged.

“I haven't gone on a walk since before silk was invented. So, I thought I should give it a try."

He smiled faintly.

"I quite liked it. I think we should continue walking everywhere."

Hearing his nonchalant voice, Noctis groaned.

***

It wasn't difficult to travel from one realm to another. All Ascended could do so, to a degree, and Transcendent heroes could even carry other living beings with them — not to mention Supremes, who could open towering gates in the fabric of realm boundaries.

Of course, there were always nuances. Each realm was different, for example, and their boundaries were different as well. Some were thin and easily traversed; some were all but impenetrable. The Divine Realms, for example, were almost impossible to enter unless one possessed great power or had the permission of their owners.

But there were mortal realms that were difficult to enter or leave, as well. Some were simply isolated firmly, while in some, the universal laws were twisted in a way that made traversal difficult. Some were simply special, so entering them required a special process.

There was nothing particularly special about the realm Shadow had inhabited except for its remoteness... and yet, they couldn't just leave it freely. In truth, unless one wanted to make a big commotion, they had to traverse the realm boundary in a place where it was especially thin — that was what Transcendent champions of the Age of Heroes did, at least.

Shadow could just tear through the realm boundary directly, but then his entrance would echo in the fabric of reality, attracting all kinds of unnecessary attention. So, he allowed Noctis to lead them to a suitable place.

It took them around a week to make it there. They traveled across the untamed wilderness, sometimes stopping to rest. None of them really needed to sleep, and the darkness of the night was not an obstacle either — Shadow saw perfectly well even at night, Noctis only grew stronger once the sun hid behind the horizon, and Snuggle was a walking source of radiant light.

So, they continued their journey at night as well.

As they walked, Shadow gazed at the starlit sky.

He had spent countless years hiding in his cave, and then a few more centuries in the eternal darkness of his lightless kingdom. So, he had not gazed upon the night sky for a long, long time.

Looking at the stars, Shadow felt an inexplicable wistfulness... a peculiar sense of longing he could not quite explain, but that tore at his heart with sharp edges.

‘I wonder...'

Why did he feel like he had lost something... like something so precious that it could not be described with words had been taken from him?

“Enjoying the beauty of the moon, huh?"

Noctis pushed him with a shoulder and smiled.

Shadow looked at him, then shook his head slowly.

"Not really."

The young man nodded in satisfaction.

"Good. That's my grandma, you know. So stop ogling her!"

Shadow stared at him, baffled by the statement. Snuggle, who sat on his shoulder, turned to look at Noctis as well.

After a while, she asked, her voice full of curiosity:

“Is Beast God really your grandmother?"

Noctis nodded.

“Of course! Not only that, but among all her grandchildren, I am the most outstanding!"

Snuggle lingered for a moment.

“So how does it work? Does she... uh... does the moon descend from the sky to congratulate you on your birthday and give you pocket money? Or something like that?"

Noctis chuckled.

"The moon doesn't descend from the sky."

He remained silent for a while, then sighed.

"Gods are vast. They are too vast to be someone's parents, lovers, or friends. Gods are not something that we mortals can fathom — like the ocean, the great abyss of the night sky, or the very soil we walk upon. But the gods... they are not alien to the desire of all these bonds and emotions, either. That is what I think, at least. So, gods inhabit mortal avatars from time to time."

He smiled.

"The Goddess of the Moon is no different, so she has an avatar as well. Granted, her avatar is a Divine being — and has been Divine for a long, long time. She is not exactly an attentive grandmother, but she used to visit me sometimes, when I was growing up in the temple."

Noctis scratched the back of his head.

“Perhaps once every few years, which must have been like a blink of an eye for her. Those nights were rare and far between, but they were also precious. I remember them fondly, at least."

Snuggle tilted her head a little.

"So... what did she do when she visited? Tempered your spirit? Imparted profound wisdom?"

Noctis looked at her solemnly for a long while, then suddenly exploded with laughter.

"Profound wisdom? Gods, no... that grandmother of mine is more childish than I am! That is how she was with me, at least. I know that she can be terrifying and unfathomable when she wants to, but when she was visiting me in my childhood days, she wanted to be different. She wanted to be in the company of a child, I guess."

Sunny glanced at him, not saying anything. But, in his mind, he remembered the days he had spent with Tatal.

He had not imparted any profound wisdom to that mischievous girl, either.

He had simply enjoyed her company.

But that enjoyment returned to him tenfold as sorrow when they parted, leaving a scar on his heart.

...How many partings had Beast God endured?

How scarred was her heart?

Was that the reason why the gods were growing more and more distant, and was there more to it?

He didn't know.

What he did know, however...

Was that the Goddess of the Moon had not had to bury this grandchild of hers, in the end. Noctis would outlive the great and terrible Beast God, his grandmother.

Almost as if they were nothing but a pair of mortals, and everything happened like it was supposed to happen.

As he was contemplating that, Snuggle studied Noctis for a while, then nodded.

"I see."

Then, she turned her little head and said in a deadpan voice:

“Stop ogling Noctis's grandma, Shadow."

He blinked.

"I wasn't."

"Uh-huh."

"I said I wasn't."

"Yup.

"I really wasn't, though?"

"Well, good then! If you say so... continue the same way!"

--- Chapter 3199 ---

Eventually, they reached a place where the realm boundary was thin. One could not see the boundary or touch it, but those who were powerful enough could sense it — and to Shadow, the boundary here felt as thin as a sheet of paper.

The three of them crossed to the other side without much effort.

Standing on the other side, Shadow inhaled deeply and looked around, feeling somewhat lost. He remembered living in countless realms... he remembered a future where only two realms remained as well, one slowly devouring the other. But, still, this was the first time he had entered an unfamiliar one in this life.

So, he felt strange.

“This one is pretty barren."

Noctis kicked a rock and watched it roll across the dry soil.

"No one really lives here. There used to be some trading outposts here and there before, but after the Shadow people vanished, even those were slowly abandoned."

He glanced at Shadow and smiled.

"I guess we know who's to blame."

Shadow did not react.

All he knew was that their journey would be a long one. Noctis had promised to guide them to the Hollow Mountains, but they would have to cross countless mortal realms to reach them — even for a creature like Shadow, that was not a task that could be accomplished swiftly. Especially because most of the lands they had to traverse were not uninhabited, and troubles could arise at any moment.

“Let's make camp."

They had not rested a lot while traveling across his former realm since it was populated by many powerful abominations, but now, there was no reason to keep the same unforgiving pace.

Raising a hand, Shadow manifested a flawless copy of the city lord's manor in the middle of the desert. Noctis stared at it for a moment, then grinned.

“Traveling with style! I like it!"

This was the first time they stopped to rest for a prolonged period of time. In the end, they stayed in the manor for a few days — Shadow explored the surrounding lands, curious to see how the world had changed in the eons since the divine syzygy had splintered. There was nothing really to see here, but even then, he found the little details of the desolate realm interesting.

Soon, they continued their journey. Since Shadow was in no hurry, it took them almost a month to reach the next point where they could quietly cross to the neighboring realm — mostly because Noctis had gotten lost twice, ending up in the wrong places.

Looking aggrieved, he just shrugged.

"Hey, why are you looking at me like that?! This whole place is one huge desert! How am I supposed to navigate it precisely without any landmarks?"

Shadow just stared at him in confusion.

“Don't you have something like a compass?"

Now, it was Noctis who looked confused.

“What's a compass?"

Shadow frowned.

Indeed, what was a compass? A compass was a device that pointed to the magnetic north. However, magnetic north did not exist in all mortal realms, and many realms had features that would interfere with a compass even if it did. A compass would only be reliable in the Divine Realm of War God, really.

‘Huh.'

Shadow asked:

"Don't you know how to navigate by stars, then?"

Noctis scoffed.

"Why would I? Whose grandson am I, Storm God's?"

Shadow simply lowered his head and stared at Snuggle, who sat comfortably on his shoulder.

Snuggle hid behind his ear.

"What? Why are you looking at me like that?!"

Shadow sighed.

Was it not this brazen doll who had assured him that Noctis would be an excellent guide?

They continued on their way, finding the crossing eventually. In the process, Noctis and Snuggle had to fight more than a few abominations — none of them as powerful as the ones they had encountered in Shadow's own realm, though.

As he watched them fight, he had to reevaluate his opinion of the two. Noctis, despite his careless attitude, was really quite a ferocious fighter — especially at night, when his strength reached its natural peak. He was cunning and determined, as well, slaying his foes with fierce efficiency. It was Snuggle, however, who really surprised Shadow.

Even if she could not do much with her doll body, she still showed hints of being a supremely experienced and seasoned fighter — that was clear from her keen judgment, breadth of knowledge, and the ability to remain calm no matter how dire the situation seemed.

It was as if she had spent her entire life battling Creatures of Corruption, facing new foes every day. Even among people of the Age of Gods, that would have been a rarity — most people only fought deadly battles when trouble came knocking on their door, after all.

That gave Shadow a vague premonition of where the transient soul had come from, but he did not pay it much attention. Instead, he considered other things.

“Snuggle.”

During one of their rest stops, Noctis was happily feasting on the meat of an abomination they had slain, while Snuggle just sat on the sand and looked at the fire. Although her face wasn't very expressive, the little doll still looked a little wistful. Turning her head, she gave Shadow a distracted look.

“What?"

He remained silent for a moment, then said:

“If you want, I can construct a worthy vessel for you. A battle golem built from manifested shadows and infused with Supreme essence, for example. It can have any number of blades and weapons attached to its limbs... or it can be like an abyssal beast, brimming with powerful tendrils and slaying extremities."

He smiled.

“That way, you can participate in the battles directly."

Up until now, Snuggle stayed in the back, using her powers to weaken their enemies and infusing Noctis with her essence to empower him — the young man, meanwhile, was the blade of their small formation.

But if she could join him in melee, things would be much easier.

Snuggle hesitated for a few moments, then slowly shook her head.

“No need."

Shadow was surprised.

"Don't you want to..."

However, he didn't finish the question.

He had assumed that Snuggle would want to be able to kill their enemies better, because wanting to be good at killing was natural for Shadow. However, he had forgotten that other living beings could feel differently.

Snuggle giggled.

“Do I want to be a more efficient killer?"

Shadow just nodded.

She smiled.

“But Shadow, I am already very adept at killing abominations."

The little doll pointed to the carcass of the beast Noctis had dressed and was roasting pieces of.

“It's just that I know the things I'm best at well. What I am best at is scouting, healing, supporting my comrades from the back... and, most of all, staying alive. And if there's a situation where I need to clash with an enemy directly, I can do that too."

She shrugged.

“I just don't use vessels to fight the important battles. My strongest suit is my soul, after all, so if we really are in trouble, I'll just fight as a soul. I can heal myself as a soul, but I can't repair a vessel. So, even if receiving soul damage really hurts, that is what I will do if there's a need.”

Shadow considered her words for a moment, then nodded.

Snuggle, meanwhile, stood up and curtsied.

“Plus... I really like being a doll! Look at me! Am I not cute? Am I not precious?"

She gave him a spin.

Shadow observed her with a dubious look. Had Snuggle... actually seen what Snuggle looked like?

It was the ugliest, crudest doll in the world! Even after Shadow personally patched it up, it still looked as if an abomination had chewed it thoroughly, but then spat it out due to how disgusting the doll tasted.

He cleared his throat.

“You... some may say that you are cute and precious, indeed."

Shadow nodded.

There... that wasn't technically a lie.

At that moment, though, Noctis spat out the meat he had just bitten.

"What are you talking about? This doll is the ugliest one I have ever seen! It looks worse than an abomination. It looks like something an abomination would spit out! Honestly, I've never had nightmares about Creatures of Corruption, but I have dreamed of that thing and woke up in a cold sweat!"

Snuggle looked at the young man with murder in her eyes.

"Oh, really?"

Noctis nodded.

"I mean, why are you asking something so obvious?"

Snuggle sighed.

"Well, if you say so."

Shadow glanced at Noctis and shook his head.

‘So young, so inexperienced...'

That night, the young man's favorite pair of shoes inexplicably fell into the fire and got terribly singed. He mourned it loudly the next morning.

During their next stop, all his food somehow ended up being unbearably salty, forcing him to cough and curse as he begged for someone to bring him water.

Snuggle did, but accidentally, the water had somehow ended up being even saltier...

This continued for quite a while.

By the time they reached the crossing, Noctis looked quite miserable.

He also didn't dare to comment on Snuggle's looks anymore.

After traversing it, they finally reached a realm populated by people. After that, it only took them a few days to travel to the nearest city.

As Noctis approached the city gate with a proud bearing, some of the locals seemed to recognize him.

"Is that... is that the Crimson Beast of Twilight?"

Noctis nodded with satisfaction.

"I guess my fame has spread wide enough. Indeed, it's me, the great and heroic Beast of Twilight. I've been to your city before, strangers... ah, it's good to be back!"

The people stared at him for a few moments in silence.

Then, they turned around and screamed:

"Noctis! It's Noctis! The scoundrel is back, hide your wives! Hide your daughters!"

Noctis blinked a couple of times.

"Huh?"

"Hide your husbands, as well!"

Hidden in Shadow's pocket, Snuggle sighed heavily.

"By the dead gods, this kid..."

--- Chapter 3200 ---

Nocits had boasted about his fame... but by the looks of things, in this town at least, he was more infamous than famous.

Even if he and Shadow were allowed to enter the city gates — the Awakened guards would not have been able to stop a Transcendent, anyway, let alone his mysterious companion — the looks they gave the young man were less than friendly. The citizens did not seem particularly happy to see him, either.

Well... some of them. The others, on the contrary, seemed quite joyous.

“Noctis! Young master! Come inside our establishment!"

"Uh-huh."

"Uh-huh!"

It was as if all the people from the surrounding villages had gathered behind these walls, for some reason, and were now waiting for something.

Not all of them looked lively and happy, either. Many wore anxious expressions, dark circles prominent under their eyes. Some were dressed well, some wore dirty and threadbare clothes. Some resided in pretty homes built of stone, some sheltered in makeshift tents and hovels built in narrow alleys.

“That's peculiar.”

“That's right! And I am better-looking than you, too! Cute and adorable, pretty as a peach!"

“What I meant is that the streets of this city are strangely overcrowded. There is an odd tension in the air, as well. Have you not noticed that?"

Noctis glanced around with a surprised expression, lingered for a short while, then shrugged.

“Now that you mention it, the city does indeed seem more crowded than a few months ago. I have not stayed here long enough to learn all the local customs, though... possibly they have a festival happening soon, or a fair. Possibly it's simply time for local farmers to sell their surplus grain.”

Shadow extended his senses carefully, encompassing the entire city. Some time later, he sighed and shook his head.

It didn't seem like Noctis was correct. Still, if there was something peculiar going on, they would probably hear about it at the inn, where wanderers like them had probably already discussed the same strangeness.

Soon enough, Noctis led them to a respectable inn in the wealthy part of the city — it was a tall building built of stone, its courtyard drowning in the shade cast by towering trees. There was a dining hall, rooms for clients who needed to stay the night, a stable, and even a small stage for musicians and dancers to perform in front of the inn's patrons.

Currently, however, the stage was empty, and only a few people were eating in the dining hall, conversing in whispers.

Since neither Shadow nor Snuggle had any money, Noctis was the one to pay for their accommodations, grumbling under his nose in the process. Soon enough, they descended to the dining hall to satiate the young man's hunger and listen to the gossip.

Sunny stared at the bow] in front of him with a troubled expression, while Noctis attacked his meal like a wolf. A few seconds later, he looked at Shadow and raised an eyebrow.

“What are you doing? Eat!"

"I haven't eaten anything since the dawn of time."

Noctis almost choked.

“What? What's the point of living for eons if you can't enjoy good food?"

“Wait, don't tell me... have you not drunk any wine, either? Or tea?!"

Shadow just nodded, causing the young man to give him a look of devastation. Eventually, Noctis shook his head and returned to his meal.

"Well, eat anyway. It would look quite strange if you just sat there and stared at perfectly good food. You don't want everyone to guess that you are an immortal monster instead of a human, do you?"

Shadow frowned.

At the moment, he was suppressing his presence and containing his Will within himself. So, unless one had especially keen senses and glanced directly at him, he doubted that anyone would think him to be anything but a mundane person — possibly an Awakened, considering his looks.

Not wanting to be recognized as a Supreme Titan, Shadow sighed and picked up the utensils.

Then, he tasted food for the first time in this lifetime.

His eyes ignited as soon as he tasted the first spoonful of the fragrant stew.

Noctis grinned.

"Great, isn't it?"

Shadow lingered for a moment.

"It's... acceptable."

Saying that, he was already bringing another spoonful to his mouth.

And then another, and another.

Sitting in his pocket, Snuggle sighed.

"I miss eating food."

Noctis spared a glance in her direction, remained silent for a moment, then asked:

"Can't you inhabit a living being, though? Then, you can eat again! Or do you only possess creepy dolls?"

Snuggle did not answer for a while.

When she eventually spoke, her squeaky voice was a little solemn:

“I can inhabit living beings. But there's no place for two souls in one vessel, you know? So, I have to destroy the original soul first... which is why I don't take living vessels and only inhabit inanimate objects."

Noctis seemed relieved for a moment, then unnerved for a couple.

Then, he shrugged and turned his attention back to his meal.

"More food for me, then..."

Finally satiated, he leaned back and smiled.

“Ah... it's good to be back in a human city! Now, we can finally rest properly. Take a bath. Sleep on a soft bed. Buy new clothes! Treat our hair with fragrant oils. By the Moon, I can't wait! Let me tell you, nothing can stop me from diving into a lavish bath as soon as we're done here — nothing!"

Shadow lowered his spoon and glanced at him with reproach.

“You just had to say that aloud, huh?"

Noctis raised an eyebrow.

“What's wrong with what I said?"

As soon as he spoke, the doors of the dining hall were pushed open, and a group of soldiers marched inside.

Their leader, a tall man wearing lustrous armor, stopped right in front of their table and stared at Noctis darkly.

After a few seconds of silence, he uttered through gritted teeth:

“Beast of Twilight... our lord wants to have a word. You are cordially invited to visit the stronghold.”

A dark smile twisted the man’s lips.

“I'm afraid we must insist that you come with us immediately.”

--- Chapter 3201 ---

The city was vast and prosperous, built with not only utility in mind, but beauty as well. That was why the city lord's stronghold resembled a temple more than a fortress, with marble pillars supporting carved pediments and exquisite statues watching over the verdant gardens. That was not to say that it wasn't a fortress, though — just from one glance, Shadow could see how easy it was to defend.

The soldiers escorted him and Noctis to the heart of the stronghold, where a great reception hall rested in the shadows, radiant beams of sunlight spilling through high windows.

There, they met a placid man who looked to be in his thirties, wearing a simple white tunic and an azure toga. His auburn hair spilled to his shoulders, supported by a golden band, and his eyes were both enlightened and clear.

Despite how young the man looked, Shadow could feel the weight of wisdom in his gaze — a wisdom that could only be earned by living a long life and experiencing many things. Even without peering into the man's soul, he knew that the lord of the city was a Transcendent who had weathered hundreds of years.

Noctis had called him an old man, after all... granted, all men seemed old to that inexperienced youth.

Speaking of Noctis, the closer they came to the city lord's stronghold, the more nervous he looked. Now that they stood directly in front of the lord, there were beads of sweat rolling down his face.

Despite that, the lord himself seemed calm enough. If anything, his faint smile looked friendly.

And there will never be peace?"

He scoffed.

“Ha! You are being ridiculous. Preposterous! You have lost sight of what it means to be Transcendent, old man."

Arelen studied him for a long while. Eventually, he smiled faintly.

“Of course, there will be peace. In this realm, there will be peace when only one Transcendent rules it. When there is no one left to challenge the ruler’s will, then there'll be peace."

He glanced away and added, his voice distant:

“That was how it has been since the dawn of time. Even the mythical First Kingdom only existed for as long as White Abyss ruled over it like a mortal goddess, unreachable and insurmountable, impossible to challenge or depose. Once their sovereign abandoned the people of the First Kingdom, it was quickly torn apart by the ambitions of powerful men."

Arelen's expression turned solemn.

"The world is changing, young Noctis. Slowly but inevitably, it transforms. Humans were weak and few in number before. We struggled to survive in a world full of Corruption — Awakened warriors were rare, and Ascended champions were like a precious treasure. Each Transcendent was like a living legend. But now... how many of us Transcendent heroes are there? How many powerful abominations remain, and how vast a land do they still control?"

He shook his head.

“Much more than that, now that humanity has accumulated knowledge and gained some strength, Transcendence is not the pinnacle of power anymore. There are already those who defy the heavens to become Supreme... to become sovereigns like those ancient demigods, Kanakht and White Abyss. And hearing of their deeds, which Transcendent doesn't want to attain Supremacy?"

Noctis glared at him with a dark expression. Eventually, he uttered through gritted teeth:

"Is Supremacy so important? So desirable? So alluring that those who are meant to protect humans will gather armies and spill human blood instead?"

The Altar Sage glanced at him with a hint of amusement.

Eventually, he said:

"Of course, it is."

His noble face suddenly seemed older than it was.

"After all, how can we not desire Supremacy? You are kin to Beast God, Noctis, and even if I am merely a distant descendant, there is a drop of divine blood in my veins as well. We live in a world where gods walk the earth. When looking at the gods, how can we not desire to become gods ourselves?"

Arelen glanced away with a wistful expression.

“To live for thousands of years instead of hundreds, or even for eternity. To see our people prosper endlessly. To reach for the heavens and bask in their radiance... to conquer them and sit upon a celestial throne. With no common enemy to stand in our way, with no Creatures of Corruption to threaten our lands, who can resist the call of the heavens, the desire to become immortal?"

Noctis scoffed.

"Immortality does sound like a lot of fun, but not if it's achieved through despicable means. Surely, Lady Irian is not leading her army to your city because she wishes to live forever."

The Altar Sage glanced down.

After a while, he said quietly:

"True. Supremacy, immortality — those are not insignificant, but they are too distant to be the real cause of this calamity. The real reason for this war, young Noctis... is you."

Noctis froze, then raised his eyebrows in disbelief.

"Me? What are you talking about, old man?! How could I have caused a war between you two?"

The Altar Sage smiled sadly.

“Did you not slay the Horror of the Viridian Marsh, that Corrupted Tyrant who had haunted the borders of my and Irian's lands for generations? For centuries, both of us tried and failed to kill it. And yet, all those months ago when you visited my city, young hero, you ventured into the marsh and fought a great battle, ending that abomination's profane existence and slaughtering its brood."

Noctis frowned.

"I did, yes! And let me tell you, it was quite a ghastly experience! But so what?"

Arelen glanced away.

“With the Tyrant gone and its minions either slain or scattered, the miraculously fertile lands near the estuary of the river, as well as precious minerals hidden in the depths of the marsh, were left without a master. Naturally, both Irian and I wanted to lay claim to that land.”

Noctis continued to frown, his expression stormy.

“Couldn't you have split it fairly?"

The Altar Sage smiled.

“I thought we could. But then, before consulting with me and coming to an agreement, Irian sent settlers to establish a settlement in those newly liberated lands. Because her people needed food."

His smile widened a little, becoming somewhat fierce.

“But don't my people need food as well, Beast of Twilight? And those precious minerals, don't my warriors need stronger blades and armor so that they could protect my people, too?"

His smile dimmed.

Arelen remained silent for a long while, then sighed.

"So, I ordered my warriors to raze the settlement and slaughter Irian's people. And now, she's coming to exact her vengeance.”

He pursed his lips, a hint of bitterness finding its way into his placid eyes.

“It seems that without the Creatures of Corruption pressing down on us, this vast realm is too small for both Irian and me. One of us must fall."

Looking at Noctis, he lingered for a moment. As the music grew quiet and the dancers retreated, the Altar Sage said:

"Beast of Twilight. Even if it wasn't your intention, the war between Arelen the Altar Sage and Irian, the Blade of Dawn, is happening in part because of what you've done. So, when she arrives... I want you to help me end the war."

His words were solemn.

“I want you to help me kill Irian, sunder her army, and bring this land to peace."

--- Chapter 3202 ---

“That old fool has lost his mind!"

Having parted with Arelen, Noctis and Shadow had returned to the inn. Noctis had not given the Altar Sage an answer, and the older Transcendent had not insisted on receiving one either — he simply implored the two of them to consider his request. Judging by how angry Noctis was, though, it did not seem like he was inclined to see Arelen's offer in good light.

Noctis stared at him silently, a hint of confusion finding its way into his gaze. Finally, he grimaced.

I don't know... marry and solve their problems in the bedroom! Then, their child would inherit both kingdoms, and everyone can live in peace. The process would be much more enjoyable for all involved parties, needless to say!"

Shadow smiled faintly, as well.

He did not say anything immediately, but then shrugged.

He scratched the back of his head and then added with a hint of enthusiasm in his voice:
