Noctis stared at Shadow for a while. Eventually, he turned to look at Snuggle and shook his head.

"Do me a favor, Snuggle. Remind me never to ask that guy for advice again..."

--- Chapter 3203 ---

In the evening, Noctis was full of dismay and anger.

By the morning, he was in a low and somber mood, savoring tea in the courtyard of the inn with a distant expression on his face. Snuggle was keeping him company, hidden from sight in the draping of his colorful robe — the little doll did not say anything, so Shadow was not sure what her purpose in staying with the youth was.

It was a bit unfamiliar not to feel her tiny weight in his pocket, though... not that he minded.

Surely, he did not mind one bit.

In any case, Shadow had a lot to think about, as well. The conversation with the Altar Sage had stirred his memories, and those memories refused to leave him be. ‘Who doesn't want to be immortal?’ Shadow smiled bitterly.

Among his countless lives, there were some that had been cursed to last forever — even if none did, in the end.

He remembered being a prisoner of the Eternal City, his youthful and flawlessly healthy body infected by the virulent plague of a dead heretic's flesh. Thousands of years of torment, an eternity spent in the darkness of abyssal depths... the pain, the horror, the madness, the collapse of both his spirit and his mind.

He remembered being a Saint whose immortal body became a host for a terrifying vine. That eternity was no less traumatic to recall.

He remembered a shattered skeleton slowly crawling across a sea of obsidian dunes, denied the peaceful embrace of death even after coming uninvited to death's lightless realm.

No matter what kind of immortality Shadow could remember, it was always a curse. And how could it not be?

Death was peace, after all. Death was solace. Those who were refused its grace were doomed to never find either one. Shadow thought about his own endless and unforgiving existence. Wasn't he immortal already? If there was one thing that wielded no power over him, it was time.

However, he was not entirely immune to time, either.

Shadow would not be destroyed by its passage... but he was changing.

He was changing swiftly, in fact.

That was something he had noticed after entering the human city. Ever since meeting Snuggle, and then Noctis... ever since embarking on this misguided journey... he could not quite recognize himself.

Would the Shadow from the past have bothered to hide his identity? To get involved in the tiresome conflict of Transcendent rulers? To explain their schemes to a brash youth, let alone attempt to give that youth advice?

No. The creature Shadow had been would have never come to Arelen’s city, and even if he did, it would not have given that human any time.

But now that Shadow was surrounded by people, exposed to the bright radiance of day, the outer layers of his vast being were dissipating one after another.

What would be revealed when enough of them were gone?

He did not know, and was wary of finding out.

So even if Shadow did not care what would happen to these two Transcendent rulers and their lands, he found himself feeling troubled — no different from Noctis.

It was just that Shadow did not have to do anything, while Noctis had to do a lot.

He had to grow up, come to terms with the nuanced nature of the world, and make a difficult choice — all in the span of several days.

On the first day, Noctis remained in the courtyard of the inn, staring into the distance.

On the second day, he went outside, wandering the streets of the city and looking at the frightened refugees sheltered behind its walls.

On the third day, Noctis wanted to visit the stronghold and confront the Altar Sage... But before he could, war horns bellowed from beyond the city wall, causing a panic among the citizens.

Irian the Blade of Dawn had arrived at the head of her army.

“Damn it! Damn it! Damn it!"

Cursing loudly, Noctis hurriedly put on his outer robes. He even layered colors that weren't complementary, which revealed just how great the turmoil in his heart was.

Observing him, Shadow raised an eyebrow.

"So? Did you decide what to do?"

He was genuinely curious what the youth would choose.

Noctis stared at him for a moment, then cursed under his breath and rushed outside.

"No!"

That was a kind of choice, as well. Opening the gates of the inn, Noctis threw a look over his shoulder and added:

"Let's go take a look first. We can come up with something later."

Shadow lingered for a moment, then shrugged and followed. As he did, a squeaky voice resounded from somewhere down below.

“Wait for me! Wait for me!"

Scurrying across the floorboards, Snuggle jumped clumsily, clutched the hem of his tunic, and climbed up to sit on his shoulder.

There, she huffed while catching her breath — which amused Shadow quite a lot, considering that the little doll did not need to breathe — and pointed forward.

“Let's go! Advance!"

Shadow sighed.

Feeling like a giant who had been turned into a horse by a tiny human, he caught up with Noctis and pulled him into the shadows. A moment later, the three of them appeared on the battlements atop the wall. Arelen's soldiers were already there, hastily preparing for battle, and the Altar Sage himself had just arrived as well. He stood on the ramparts above the city gates, looking at the plain beyond with a composed expression. Winds tussled his auburn hair, and his eyes glistened in the golden light of dawn.

Out there on the field in front of the city, the enemy army had already assembled its ranks. Irian's warriors were far more numerous than the defenders of the city, and looked more seasoned as well.

As for their commander...

While Arelen had the air of a scholar, Irian the Blade of Dawn looked like a sharp weapon forged to cut down enemies on the battlefield.

She was a radiantly beautiful woman of tall stature, lithe and slender like a drawn sword, wearing armor crafted from white scales and polished bronze. In the rays of the rising sun, the bronze elements of her armor blazed with fiery radiance, as did the head of her long spear.

Dismounting from her snow-white warhorse, Irian raised her head and gazed at the gates of the city. Her hazel eyes were like liquid gold, and her hair was like a waterfall of warm sunlight, gathered into a braid and held in place by a bronze diadem.

“Arelen!"

Her voice boomed above the vast field, making the soldiers on the wall tremble.

“I've come to seek justice for the lives of the innocent people you slew!"

Pointing her long spear at the figure of the Altar Sage, Irian gritted her teeth and then shouted:

"Come down and face me, coward! I'll send them off to the Shadow Realm by spilling your blood!"

Arelen studied her silently from the battlements, then smiled.

“Innocent people? Those people were thieves who took that which did not belong to them. Surely, you did not bring your army here because I punished some thieves? Oh, but it looks like you did."

His smile turned cold and merciless.

“If so, why don't you come up and face me here instead?"

Irian glared at him for a moment, then laughed darkly.

“So this is how it is. It seems that you have lost all your shame, Arelen the Altar Sage! Fine, then... let us end this dispute with sharp blades instead of treacherous words. Let us show the gods which one of us deserves to be the last one standing!"

Atop the wall, Noctis clenched his fists.

“These two fools... why are they acting as if lam not even here?"

Shadow shook his head lightly.

"Oh, quite the opposite. They are both painfully aware of you. Irian is putting on a brave face, while Arelen is using the fact that you're on this side of the wall to rattle her."

A disbelieving chuckle escaped from the young hero's lips.

“Wonderful... simply wonderful. So even by doing nothing, I am still being used to bolster one side."

He smiled bitterly and shook his head.

“Ah... when I left the temple, I thought that if I was strong enough, valiant enough, and lucky enough, no enemy would be able to stand in my way. But these few days have taught me a bitter lesson, Shadow. Being strong and brave is great, sure."

His smile became a little mocking, as if he was ashamed of himself.

“But being cunning and devious is far more important. Who knew that sages would be deadlier than warriors? Alas, the word is truly mightier than the sword."

Shadow gave him a look of confusion.

“Well, of course it is. After all, any decent Shaper can turn a swordsman into a bloodstain by simply opening their mouth."

Looking the young Transcendent up and down, he sighed.

“It seems to me that you have chosen the fourth option? You are going to fight Arelen and Irian both?"

Noctis smiled crookedly.

“What's the point? What will happen if I kill both of them? Nothing good..."

He remained silent for a moment, then shook his head with a wistful expression.

“I can't do anything to resolve this situation. The best thing I can do... is do nothing."

Then, he turned and looked Shadow directly in the eye.

For a moment, a hint of hope flashed in his eyes.

“What about you, Shadow? Can you do something?"

Sitting on Shadow's shoulder, Snuggle threw a nervous glance at him.

"No, no... he can't. He promised not to kill anyone!"

Shadow remained silent, looking at Irian's army with a calm expression.

Could he do something?

And if he could, was there a reason to be involved?

Troubled, Shadow looked down.

Slowly, a strange pain permeated his entire being, forcing him to give Noctis an answer. Finally, he sighed.

"Can I? I guess I can."

On the walls of the city, the archers were nocking arrows on the strings of their bows.

Below the walls, on the field, Irian's army was preparing to charge.

The two Transcendents, former comrades, studied each other somberly. They were ready to clash and kill each other, as well. Mere moments remained until the start of the battle.

But before the first arrow pierced the radiance of dawn...

A dreadful roar suddenly split the heavens apart.

The ground quaked, and a cold wind blew

across the battlefield, causing deathly fear to grasp the hearts of mortal warriors with icy claws.

Something far more terrifying than either of the Transcendent rulers was approaching.

--- Chapter 3204 ---

The ground shook, and as a terrifying roar thundered above the two armies, dust spilled from between the great stone blocks that formed the wall. Atop the battlements, many of the soldiers lost their balance and fell, dropping their weapons. Below, on the battlefield, the horses of Irian's cavalry buckled in fear, making the riders curse as they struggled to remain in the saddle.

The infantrymen gripped their weapons, looking around with startled and frightened expressions.

Only a few people remained calm and collected, but even their expressions turned grim.

The Altar Sage, the Blade of Dawn, and the Beast of Twilight — the three Transcendent heroes glanced around, momentarily forgetting about their conflict.

"W—what the hell?"

Noctis peered into the distance, where a gargantuan hill was slowly crumbling. His voice sounded subdued.

Shadow, meanwhile, was leaning leisurely on the wall of a guard tower, his expression just as calm as it had always been.

He shrugged lightly.

“Who knows?"

Irian and Arelen, meanwhile, were observing the calamity with wary gazes. Then, briefly, they glanced at each other. Far away, the hill had collapsed entirely, and something gargantuan, hideous, and malevolent moved slowly in the billowing cloud of dust. Suddenly, the radiant light of dawn grew pale and feeble, and the warmth of early summer turned into a piercing chill...

As though death itself had come to reap the two armies.

A moment later, the soldiers paled and staggered, some of them even fainting — that was because the overwhelming presence of the hidden menace washed over them, followed by the suffocating pressure of a vast and alien Will.

Sitting on Shadow's shoulder, Snuggle turned her head to look at him, then stood up slowly and pulled on his hair.

Her squeaky voice was reduced to a barely audible whisper:

“H—hey! Are you not... overdoing it a little?"

Shadow just smiled faintly.

“Am I? It depends on how strong these mortal heroes are, I suppose."

He spoke quietly enough for Noctis not to hear — the young Transcendent was not listening to Shadow, anyway, his entire attention focused on the immense figure moving slowly under the veil of dust. Finally, the Altar Sage uttered a Verse, and a powerful gale tore apart the cloud of dust, revealing the true form of the unknown creature.

Standing atop the wall, he was the first to behold it. His face paled, and his gaze turned grim.

Out there on the plain in front of the city, a towering abomination was slowly crawling out of the shattered earth. Its body was long and segmented, like that of a centipede, but its head resembled a giant human skull that was missing the lower jaw, with three empty eye sockets that hid impenetrable darkness.

The chitinous carapace of the giant abomination was so black that it seemed to absorb the surrounding light. The enormous skull, however, was vibrantly scarlet, as if it had been bathed in an ocean of human blood until the surface of the ancient bone fully absorbed it.

Finally climbing from the depths of earth, the hideous centipede raised its long neck. Even with most of its body still on the ground, the scarlet skull loomed at least a hundred meters above it, turned in the direction of the city.

The three empty eye sockets of the titanic abomination stared at the three Transcendent heroes, eerily emotionless, the unfathomable pools of darkness hidden within them still and hollow.

What was not still, however, were hundreds of ghastly maws that revealed themselves on the inner side of the creature's belly, gnashing myriads of teeth as they revealed the crimson flesh of the monster. Witnessing the great immensity of the abhorrent creature, the soldiers of Irian's army, who stood between the city and the subterranean horror, took an unconscious step back — in the direction of the wall they had been meant to besiege.

Irian herself seemed rattled, as well. Looking at the eerie scarlet skull, she gripped her spear and whispered in a stunned voice:

"A Great Monster!"

She could not see the soul of the giant creature, of course. But merely by sensing the oppressive power of its presence, as well as the malevolent flavor of its Will, she could make a judgment.

Atop the wall, Arelen wore a grave expression, as well.

Noctis, meanwhile...

Seemed thoroughly appalled.

“A centipede! Ah, eww! Why did it have to be a damn centipede?! I hate them!"

He shuddered, grimacing in utter disgust. Shadow spared him an amused look.

“That's what you worried about?"

He was a little bit hurt.

After all, he had gone into a lot of trouble to create that monster.

The giant Nightmare Creature was not an Nightmare Creature at all. Instead, it was merely a construct woven out of manifested shadows, controlled by his will. Its flesh was equal in toughness to that of a Supreme being, since it was infused with his Supreme essence.

As for the power of its presence and the malevolence of its Will, those were simply the presence and Will of Shadow — a sliver of them, at least — which he revealed when the monster appeared.

Creating such a monstrosity was no easy feat, but not that difficult either. Its carapace, its muscles, its tendons, its fangs, and all the other parts of its enormous body — Shadow manifested them all and then connected them together into a functional organism, breathing a false spark of life into that organism with his nuanced control.

He had even gone into the trouble of changing the color of its bones and its flesh, thinking that showing a creature painted entirely black would put Noctis into a difficult position. The youth had just returned from supposedly vanquishing an unknown horror that dwelled in eternal darkness, after all, so Shadow didn't want anyone to think that the monster followed the Beast of Twilight to this peaceful city from a distant realm.

As for whether Irian and Arelen would believe that the giant centipede was indeed a Creature of Corruption... Shadow did not particularly care. Unlike soul essence, his own was the essence of shadows — so, even if they had means of peering into the souls of living beings, they would not see the familiar silver radiance.

And even if they discerned that something was not quite right, it did not matter. The nature of the monster was not as important as its perceived malice and intent to destroy the city.

"Irian!"

Standing atop the wall, Arelen shouted his adversary's name. The radiant Transcendent who had come to kill him glanced up, and the two seemed to converse silently, their gazes full of concerned wariness.

Then, after exchanging a nod, they both rushed toward the towering creature side by side.

Noctis cursed and leaped down from the wall, as well, dashing to follow them. Moments later, Shadow and Snuggle were left alone among terrified soldiers.

"What the hell did you create, Shadow?"

Snuggle's voice sounded oddly weak. Looking down at her in surprise, Shadow raised an eyebrow.

“What? It's merely a construct."

He paused for a moment, then added with a shrug:

“Actually, I didn't even have to work that hard on it. That thing was already something I had considered creating — back when I was thinking of making a better vessel for you. A battle golem, of sorts."

The little doll trembled and stared at him in dismay.

“T—that? You wanted me — me! — to climb inside that thing? That disgusting, ghastly thing over there?!"

Shadow looked at her in confusion.

“Why? Look at it. It's very sturdy, can move below and above ground really fast, and has a lot of ways to kill enemies. And it is very menacing — instilling the adversary with fear is half the victory, you know."

He scratched the tip of his nose awkwardly.

“Admittedly, it can't fly. Adding a sufficient number of wings introduced too many points of vulnerability to the carapace, so I was left with no choice but to scrap that idea. Still. I think it turned out pretty well."

He smiled proudly.

"I call it... the Giant Red Skull Centipede, Prototype One."

Snuggle groaned and covered her face with a hand.

“Prototype One, he says... gods have mercy, look how proud he is! He's completely serious, too!"

Shadow blinked a couple of times.

"It's a fitting name, though? I don't see the issue."

Perhaps Snuggle was simply too young to appreciate his stellar namingship.

Well... what else would one expect from a doll called Snuggle?

Far in the distance, the giant monster lowered its head and flowed forward like a river of scarlet darkness, moving toward the three Transcendent heroes with terrifying speed, the ground turning into a shredded mess of torn soil and seething mucus wherever it passed.

Shadow sighed.

‘All that work, only for it to be destroyed...’

Even though he had promised Snuggle not to kill anyone and created this construct specifically to be slain by the mortal heroes... he still found himself secretly rooting for the giant centipede.

After all, if its own creator couldn't support this soulless construct, wouldn't it be just too pitiful?

A split second later, on the plain in front of the city, three Transcendent heroes — Arelen the Altar Sage, Irian the Blade of Dawn, and Noctis, the Crimson Beast of Twilight — clashed with the harrowing Nightmare Creature... Giant Red Skull Centipede, Prototype One.

Their battle would become a legend all across the mortal realms in the future, one day soon.

--- Chapter 3206 ---

People had always imagined hell as a place full of fire. But, as it turned out, hell was full of wind and water instead.

NQSC was swallowed by a storm. The sky was obscured by a dark, menacing veil of clouds, and hurricane winds howled as they tore through the crumbled remains of the city barriers and collapsed buildings in the outer rings of the city. Rain fell like a wall, flying sideways from the sheer force of the powerful gale. Flashes of lightning burned the darkness away, and deafening claps of thunder roared high above, as if there was a malevolent, hungry dragon hidden in the storm.

Storms like this one had been happening more and more often over the past four years, eventually fusing into a never-ending deluge of calamity.

Of course, despite all the damage caused by the unceasing natural catastrophes, it was merely a background for the true disaster.

The true disaster was the Nightmare Gates that now surrounded the city like siege towers and the endless swarms of abominations escaping them each day.

The world was truly and utterly ending.

In fact, it was already halfway gone.

It had started slowly, but then proceeded swiftly. There were simply more and more Nightmare Gates, more abominations, and more casualties among the soldiers who desperately protected Earth from being torn apart. Then, pieces of the waking world began fusing with the Dream Realm, adding their weight to its patchwork surface.

Once the two realms became partially fused, the Nightmare Creatures did not need Gates to travel between them anymore. That alone added immense pressure to the strained defenses of humanity, but there was even more damage. A planet was a closed and finely tuned system, after all. Once a hostile mystical realm started taking bites out of it, nature itself went insane, causing rapid and unpredictable changes.

Hence, the storms.

Here in NQSC, at least, it was mainly storms. Elsewhere, it was something else — volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, tsunamis, sharp temperature changes...

It was not all bad, though. Yes, the infusion of alien air had caused the sky above NQSC to go insane... but it was clean air. Even now that the air filtration barriers were breached or collapsed, people were not being poisoned on the street — in fact, they could breathe freely without face masks for the first time in hundreds of years.

Even the end of the world had its perks.

“Move aside, bastards! Let them through! As soon as the rear vehicle clears, close ranks!"

“What are you doing, fool?! This guy is still alive! Drag him back and hand him over to the medics!"

“Report! Left highrise turrets, ammunition spent!"

“Sir! They're coming!"

“Argh, curse it all! Anyone whose armor still has more than thirty percent charge left, advance to the front row!"

“Best seats in the establishment! Let's enjoy the show, gentlemen!"

“Light them up!"

On a street between two battered dormitory towers, the joints of powered armor suits hissed as soldiers unleashed a hail of bullets and explosive rounds into the rushing tide of Nightmare Creatures. Behind them, towering MWPs charged their mass drivers, rising monstrous machine guns to bathe the abominations in lead and tungsten hail. The turrets above the highrises spun, spitting out long streams of tracer rounds.

The roaring salvo of countless shots drowned out the deafening blast of thunder... but it failed to drown out the chilling wails of the rushing Nightmare Creatures.

The soldiers of the first line of defense paled, preparing to deploy their bayonets.

"I... I don't think I like this show, guys!"

“Wow, really?! You don't say!"

“It's about to end, though! At least for us!"

"What a silver lining!"

The soldiers had been fighting the entire day, slowly retreating street by street as the civilians of the breached district were being evacuated deeper into the city. Now, however, it looked like for many of the soldiers, this was going to be the last stand.

Just before the tide of abominations overwhelmed the makeshift defensive position, a swift figure streaked through the air and plummeted into their mass.

“Brace for impact!"

There was a muffled boom.

In the next moment, the entire center of the Nightmare Creature horde was pulverized, hundreds of them dying in an instant. It was difficult to see because of the torrential rain and furious wind, but countless abominations that were close to the figure simply turned into bloody mist, while those that had been further away were merely torn to tiny pieces.

Hide, chitin, flesh, bone — everything was crushed and ground to dust in a split second, as if struck by a celestial hammer, flung outward by a heavy shockwave.

A heartbeat later, lightning illuminated the world, and the startled soldiers saw a blurry streak moving through the swarm of Nightmare Creatures with astonishing speed. Wherever it passed, scores of abominations were severed, beheaded, and split open — as if the binds that held their bodies together were being undone.

One soldier, whose visual acuity was better than most, caught a glimpse of a great zweihander flashing in a magnificent arc.

"It's... it's the Lady of Sorrow!"

"What?! Isn't she a Saint?!"

“Since when is Lady Sorrow in NQSC?!"

“A Saint has descended from the sky... now that's an ending!"

“Stop staring and push forward, fools! Support the lady and her people!"

“Left highrise turrets have finished the reloading sequence!"

“The last convoy has entered the Barrier, sir!"

"Advance!"

The situation on this battlefield had changed in an instant. Lady of Sorrow — Tamar of Clan Sorrow — was one of the youngest Saints of humanity, having conquered her Third Nightmare only recently. However, her fame had been steadily spreading among people even before that, when she was a mere Master. Most of the renowned figures of humanity were affiliated with one of the great powers in one way or another. There were Saints serving one of the two queens, Morgan of Valor or Song Seishan, and those who served Nightwalker and the House of Night. There were some who followed Ananke of Weave or one of the three Supreme protectors of the waking world.

Tamar of Sorrow and her small band of elite warriors, however, were one of the few independent forces that roamed the realms while serving no one. Nobody ever knew where they would pop up, which battlefield she would grace with her presence... wherever it was, however, countless Nightmare Creatures died, and tides of battle were usually reversed.

Invigorated, the soldiers pushed forward, aiming to eliminate the remaining abominations before organizing an orderly retreat.

Tamar, meanwhile, cleaved far into the crumbling horde, moving deeper and deeper like a whirlwind of blood and steel.

[Don't get too excited. Pull back.]

The voice came from a Memory used by members of the Shadow Clan — with this many Gates, technology became more and more unreliable, causing a crisis of command and communication among the soldiers of humanity. Where technology failed, sorcery and Awakened picked up the slack.

In that regard, the Shadow Clan was better off than any other faction.

Tamar smiled grimly.

[Who says that I am excited?]

Finally, she reached the Tyrant who controlled the horde from the rear. Leaping into the air, she stepped on it to change her trajectory and avoid a deadly blow, then did it again to launch herself toward the creature's massive head.

[I am exhausted. I want to lie down. I want to take a hot shower. I want to eat something warm, too...]

The creature's head split apart, a fountain of fetid blood mixing with the falling rain. Tamar landed on the wet asphalt, slid a few dozen meters, and brought herself to a halt by transforming her momentum into a blast of concussive force that tore a hole in the nearest abomination.

[Most of all, I want to get somewhere dry. Damn rain...]

Her Memory spoke again:

[Hey. That was uncalled for.]

In that moment, a powerful gust of wind slammed into Tamar, obscuring her vision with a veil of water.

Half-blinded, she looked around.

‘It is time to pull back, indeed.'

She had performed well in front of the soldiers, but in truth, she was not in good shape. Beneath the armor, her body was bruised and battered, littered with wounds — and beneath them, there were the wounds from the previous battlefield that had been treated, but had not healed fully yet.

Things had been getting worse and worse as of late, and there was no respite in sight. Antarctica had fallen first. By now, it was most likely fully absorbed by the Dream Realm, most of it transported to somewhere beyond the Burned Forest. As such, it had become an open wound in the flesh of Earth, unleashing an endless flood of Nightmare Creatures — that alone would have been enough to overwhelm the remaining Quadrants... if not for Revel and the Shadow Clan.

Somewhere out there, on the unknown northern front of apocalypse, Saint Revel was leading the forces of the Shadow Clan, including the powerful Shadows and the legion of shades their boss had left in her care, against the Barrow Wraiths and countless abominations of the Burned Forest. In fact, she had staged a counteroffensive and invaded the charred Death Zone a couple of years ago.

Because of Revel pulling the attention of all those Nightmare Creatures to the Forgotten Shore, fewer of them were spilling into the waking world.

Still... their number was enough to make the oceans of Earth completely inaccessible. Navigating them had always been perilous, but now, it was pure suicide. Even Saints did not dare to traverse the oceans.

The colonies in South America had been evacuated, but the three remaining Quadrants were completely isolated from each other now. With global infrastructure in tatters, famine had long become a real possibility — even with most population centers possessing robust food self-sustenance systems, those had long been cripplied by the spreading influence of the Call.

In the end, the only thing that was preventing humanity from starving was the Night Garden and its captain, who could both carry people from the waking world to the Dream Realm and bring food from the Dream Realm to the waking world on the way back. Raised by Wolves could help, as well.

It was quite ironic... before, people of the Dream Realm staved off starvation with supplies from Earth, But now, the situation was entirely reversed.

Which was not to say that the people in the Dream Realm knew no hunger. The more the situation in the waking world worsened, the more refugees poured into the human enclaves there. By now, a good one-third of humanity had left its cradle, pushing the population of the Dream Realm well beyond one billion.

And the Dream Realm... the Dream Realm was in no way ready to accept this many people.

Things weren't going well there either, after all.

On Earth, the three remaining Quadrants were under a constant siege, both from beyond and from within. In the Dream Realm, meanwhile, the same was true for the three Domains — even with the Sovereigns leading the battle, humanity was struggling to hold on to its land.

Expanding their reach, of course, had become completely impossible.

The wilderness was too dangerous, and the Citadel Cities weren't made of rubber. By now, every single one of them was overpopulated and suffering from resource shortages.

A few had already been lost.

'We are not dead yet.'

Tamar looked at the ravaged urban landscape in front of her with a grim expression.

They were not dead... but they were certainly dying.

Humanity was like a wounded soldier slowly bleeding out on the ground, hoping that a medic would arrive in time to save them.

It was only that the medics who could save humanity were stuck in a Nightmare.

They had been gone for four years already, and nobody knew when they would come back.

--- Chapter 3207 ---

As Tamar retreated, nimbly dashing through the air when towering carcasses blocked her way, the remains of the horde tried to pursue her. Whenever a Nightmare Creature got too close, a black arrow fell from above, its passage almost invisible in the stormy darkness. The arrows struck the abominations unerringly, pinning them down — however, not a single creature died.

Thinking that Rain was enduring the storm somewhere on the roof made Tamar feel better. After all, there was nothing more sad than being miserable alone... being miserable together with a friend was much better.

‘Damn storm...’

The battle for NQSC had been long and gruelling, but for Tamar, the constant rain and unceasing wind felt more exhausting than endless waves of Nightmare Creatures — which was a bit peculiar, considering that her ancestral Citadel used to stand atop the Weeping Goddess.

Until the King of Nothing destroyed it.

Who would have guessed that she'd be praying for his return one day?

His and that of her boss, of course, as well as the other two Supremes who had challenged the Fifth Nightmare.

[I'm retreating.]

The soldiers almost reached the Barrier. Their retreat was orderly, but just to be safe, the Shadow Clan agents under Tamar's command were covering it. Now, it was time for them to escape as well.

‘How many hours can we rest?'

Revel was in the Dream Realm, tied in a vicious war against the Barrow Wraiths and the horrors of the Burned Forest... for now. Last Tamar heard, something was stirring in the rotten corpse of the dead World Tree — so it was unclear how long the Lightslayer would be able to hold on.

That battlefield was too deadly for most human members of the Shadow Clan, though. So, most of them had been sent to various flashpoints of the apocalypse both in the Dream Realm and on Earth, moving in the shadows and accomplishing tasks that demanded an elite force with a delicate touch.

That was how it had been in the beginning, at least... by now, many of them operated in the open, pretending to be independent Awakened — those who were still alive, of course. Tamar had conquered her Third Nightmare recently and was hurriedly sent to the Northern Quadrant, where Rain was in command.

Despite still being a Master, the Princess of Shadows had become somewhat irreplaceable for their ragtag group of knaves and misfits. Her powers were simply too mystical, while her ability as a sorceress was second to none. So, no one was surprised that she was in charge of Saints despite being of a lower Rank, still.

By now, many of humanity's forces had been pulled to NQSC... but even with all of them fighting desperately to keep the city intact, the Nightmare Creatures were slowly pushing them back.

The outskirts had been swallowed almost a year ago. The outer barriers held out for many months, but were eventually breached and conquered by abominations. Now, the last district in the outer ring of the city was being abandoned... which meant that the defenders were fully retreating behind the Barrier.

The Barrier was something that Nightwalker had created. It was a zone surrounding the inner city where space was so torn and twisted that it had become a demented, deadly labyrinth — if one didn't have a special enchanted token, they could very well become lost there for the rest of their lives.

Or for eternity.

Nightmare Creatures still made their way through, but many of them perished or were weakened in the process. So, while the Barrier was not a panacea, it helped the defenders of the city keep at least the inner districts intact.

The battle for NQSC was tough...

But then again, it was tough everywhere. The entire population of the Eastern Quadrant was locked in a bloody war against the horrors that crawled onto the coast from the depths of the ocean. The Western Quadrant was already being consumed by the Dream Realm, and the situation there was even more desperate than here in the north.

Granted, there were relatively few people left there who had not been evacuated to the Dream Realm already — the Northern Quadrant was slowly and surely becoming the last bastion of humanity on Earth, as well as its final battlefield.

Out there in the Dream Realm, the situation was not much better. Its territory was shifting, new regions appearing in the middle of well-charted lands. As a result, old horrors that had been resting in their lairs for eons were stirring, directing their gazes at the human settlements.

The Stormsea was boiling and seething, rivers of blood flowing into its misty water. Silver Web was still holding, and the city in the delta of the River of Tears was holding as well — but they were under constant siege. The basin of the great river had become one vast battlefield, with isolated Citadel Cities barely holding the Nightmare Creatures at bay.

In the east, the eerie darkness had finally stopped spreading after swallowing half a dozen Citadels. However, nobody knew when it would start moving again. Ravenheart was being besieged by the snow wraiths of the frozen wastelands. Bastion was faring relatively well, but the connection to the northern territories had been cut...

And recently, waves of powerful Nightmare Creatures had begun to flow out from the belt of Death Zones lying between the Godgrave and the Stormsea. Morgan and her warriors took the brunt of that tide of horrors, even if some of it spilled into the basin of the River of Tears as well.

Morgan, Seishan, and Ananke... each of them had battled Cursed Nightmare Creatures in the past four years. For now, they were yet to be defeated, but each of those battles had left scars both on their bodies and on the surface of the Dream Realm itself.

The wardens of the waking world had fared somewhat better, but they were exhausted by the need to both fight endlessly and resist the hostile pressure of the very realm they were trying to protect. Still, their presence was like a ray of hope in the sea of nightmares — every time the soldiers of humanity witnessed Raised By Wolves, Nightingale, or Soul Reaper, their morale soared.

It was just that only one of them could be present in the waking world at a time — they had to take turns entering the battlefield, lest a dire crisis happened when none of them could return. And there were too many battlefields on Earth for one being to be enough, even if that being was Supreme.

"Ready your tokens!"

Tamar was the last to arrive in front of the Barrier, rushing ahead of the pursuing mob of Nightmare Creatures. Several cohorts of the Shadow Clan fighters were already waiting for her there, clad in sleek suits of black armor, armed with both Memories and mundane weapons. Rain had descended from the highrise as well, looking at the turrets the soldiers had to abandon with regret.

Tamar leaned on her zweihander, breathing heavily. All around her, her soldiers pulled the enchanted markers that would allow them to pass the Barrier from beneath their armor.

At that moment, blaring alarms roared all across the city.

Looking at her mechanical watch — a relic that had become priceless ever since humanity began to settle the Dream Realm while the Call began disrupting delicate electronics — she cursed.

‘Moonrise...’

Many terrifying things had happened when the boundary between the waking world and the Dream Realm began to become blurry, but none was more terrifying than what was happening to the Moon.

There had been a saying before that looking at the Moon too closely was perilous. Now, however, it was especially so — somewhere along the way, simply glancing up while the moon was visible in the sky became deadly. Many people had died, many had instantly gone mad, and even more of them had immediately become infected by Corruption.

Those who were mundane were dragged into the First Nightmare, most of them turning into abominations and slaughtering everyone around them. Those who were Awakened simply turned, to a much more devastating effect.

And with every month, the influence of the Moon was only growing more intense, frightening, and malevolent.

Tamar was a Saint, and the sky above NQSC was obscured by heavy clouds. Still, she lowered her gaze.

At that moment, another flash of lightning illuminated the word, and Rain pulled back the hood of her black raincoat to look up. Her expression did not seem good. Knowing that her friend often sensed things that other people couldn't, Tamar tensed.

"What?"

Rain hesitated for a moment, then gritted her teeth and pointed at the sky. Tamar hesitated, then glanced at the seething mass of storm clouds above them.

There, hidden by the hurricane, something gargantuan was moving between the bolts of lightning. In fact, it seemed as if the heavens had gone mad, attacking the titanic form in berserk fury. Dozens, then hundreds of twisting eclectic arcs struck the colossal shadow as it slowly revealed itself.

The brilliance of myriad bolts of lightning illuminated the world like a pale sun.

Tamar paled.

A moment later, the Night Garden revealed itself from the storm.

The great ship had descended below the stormclouds, revealing its battered form to the people sheltered in the city. Its size was so immense that it was difficult to fathom, wreathed in lightning and glowing with residual energy.

And, at the moment, another form — one infinitely vast, grotesque, and repulsive — was wrapped around the ship's hull, straining to crush it.

Tamar couldn't see the upper part of the giant Nightmare Creature, but each of its tattered wings was large enough to cover an entire district of the city. One was severed and charred; the other was clawing at the Mainmast Pagoda of the living ship with giant, curving talons.

Myriad arrows streaked from the deck of the Night Garden to pierce its body, and enormous cannons roared one after another, each taking out huge chunks of flesh from its belly. An enormous figure woven out of starlight was rending the creature's back... but even with all these efforts, it didn't seem to be on the threshold of death yet.

Tamar took an involuntary step back.

"What... what the hell is this?"

A Titan? A Cursed Nightmare Creature?

"We need to get behind the Barrier."

Rain's voice sounded calm, but Tamar knew her well enough to recognize an underlying layer of trepidation.

She glanced at her friend with a silent question.

Rain pulled the barrier token out and turned back.

"It's falling. It's going to impact somewhere beyond the city... but close. So, we need to run. What are you standing around for, guys?! Run, run, run!"

Throwing one last look at the Night Garden, Tamar gritted her teeth and dove into the Barrier.

Behind her, Nightmare Creatures were flooding the ravaged street like a grotesque river.

A bolt of lightning flashed, and a deafening thunderclap shook the world.

Another day of the apocalypse was coming to an end.

--- Chapter 3208 ---

‘Curse it all!'

As the wind howled and the endless bolts of lightning scorched the sky, a ferocious mass of dark clouds churning like a celestial ocean, the Night Garden plummeted toward the ground. At first, Nightwalker simply meant to descend below the clouds to shield his warriors from the rising moon — but now, the living ship was wounded too severely to be controlled, and its fall had become unstoppable.

Of course, the titanic creature holding it in a crushing grip was not helping the situation either.

The hull of the great vessel was slowly devouring its flesh, but the damn abomination was too vast and too powerful — there were fractures slowly appearing on the miraculous wood already, and the damage being dealt to the Night Garden was far beyond what the living ship could return.

Usually, slamming into the ground would not have been a major concern. However, with the ship already damaged, a collision could very well become catastrophic — not to mention that the impact would devastate countless districts of NQSC.

The Night Garden was a dozen kilometers from stern to bow, after all, and its mass was incalculable. The speed of its fall looked deceptively tame because of its size, but in truth, it was dire.

Nightwalker couldn't right the ship with the damn Titan weighing it down, though. Sinking his colossal, ethereal fangs into the flesh of the monster, he tore off an enormous chunk of flesh and bellowed, his eerie voice drowning out the deafening roars of the storm.

His Transcendent form, the Starbeast, was uncanny and immensely powerful. However, one thing it did not possess was vocal cords capable of human speech... it was alright, though. Because Aether could understand him.

So, what Nightwalker was relaying to his warriors was quite simple:

“Aether! Concentrate on its right shoulder joint! Take its remaining wing off!"

Almost immediately, the soldiers below rushed to turn the cannons. Some were crawling across the deck, dazed by the terrifying presence of the Titan... some were dead, having been turned into bloody stains. But no one had abandoned their duty. Nightwalker's Saints were all going all out to free their ship from the abomination’s grasp, as well.

But it was not going to be enough.

Perched on the creature's endless back and rending it to shreds with his ethereal fangs, Nightwalker could see the ground clearly. The devastated landscape of the abandoned battlefield beyond the walls of NQSC was drawing closer and closer.

They were not going to kill the Titan in time. They were not even going to sever its one remaining wing in time.

Even with Nightwalker expanding space to extend the calamitous fall, it was not enough — the world he was trying to reshape with his Will was permeated by the Will of the colossal Nightmare Creature, after all, slowing him down.

"Goddammit!"

Looking up, Nightwalker hesitated for a moment, then turned into a torrent of starlight and flashed toward the scarred and battered Mainmast Pagoda. Once inside, he slid across the floor of the runic hall and jumped to his feet, bending space to enter the runic circle in one step.

There, Naeve was standing on one knee, blood streaming down his face. The runic hall had sustained severe damage, but luckily enough, the circle itself was intact — steering the living ship without it was not impossible, but quite difficult.

"Grab the rails!"

Nightwalker's voice boomed across the entire main deck of the titanic vessel, sending the soldiers scurrying to grab something as if their lives depended on it. The Night Garden was supposed to keep them firmly standing on the deck no matter what maneuvers its helmsman had in mind, but with how damaged it was, there was no telling what would happen.

There was nothing to grab onto in the runic hall, though, so Naeve simply grabbed onto the belt of Nightwalker's armor.

The Night Garden careened, its bow moments away from crashing into the ground...

But just before it could, an enormous fissure opened in the fabric of reality, revealing an endless black void that was illuminated by countless stars and dreamlike nebulas.

The bow of the living ship plunged into the Dream Gate, which had opened parallel to the ground. The colossal fissure swallowed the entire great length of the Night Garden — from the runic hall, it looked as if they were falling into the starlit sky.

Then, the Mainmast Pagoda crossed the Dream Gate, as well.

A moment later, Nightwalker was blinded by brilliant light.

He was assaulted by unbearable heat.

The howling cacophony of the endless storm disappeared, replaced by a deafening litany of countless monstrous wails.

When Nightwalker's eyes adjusted to the light, what he saw...

Was a world on fire.

The Night Garden had exited the Dream Gate upside-down, momentum taking it higher into the azure sky. It was already spinning to right itself, but for now, all Nightwalker could see was the ground — the vast expanse of a sandy desert, all of it drowning in an ocean of silver flame. Myriads of Nightmare Creatures were moving in that flame, the black fractures of Nightmare Gates towering above them like dark pillars.

The air was full of winged abominations as well, all of them fusing into a harrowing swarm. Far in the distance, a battered city was unleashing a hail of explosive rounds into the swarm, streams of tracer rounds twisting like radiant snakes.

The terrifying sight was like a scene from hell... but it wasn't some distant inferno. The Night Garden gave Nightwalker the ability to open his Dream Gate between two points in the same realm, and that was what he had done, bringing his ship to the Western Quadrant.

They were currently in the Sahara Desert, where the forces of humanity were fighting a desperate battle against the advancing tide of abominations.

The hull of the Night Garden cracked precariously as the Titan tightened its coils, and since the titanic ship appeared right in the middle of a great swarm of winged abominations, those monsters were shifting their attention to its vast expanse as well. Nightwalker gritted his teeth.

“All battle crew below Transcendent Rank! Kill the vermin! Don't let a single bastard land!"

As the Night Garden spun, aligning its main mast with the boundless sky above, the soldiers let go of the rails and unleashed a squall of attacks at the churning swarm. The Saints, meanwhile, kept attacking the Titan. Nightwalker swayed as the colossal creature's claws tore into the Mainmast Pagoda, then cursed and gazed at the swarming sky outside...

And there, he saw what he was looking for, moving like an annihilating shadow in the endless mass of abominations.

A great dragon with scales the color of the midnight sky was reigning terror in the sky above the ocean of flames, carving a path of destruction through the swarm. As Nightwalker watched, its enormous maw opened, and a haunting song resounded above the endless battlefield.

In the next moment, a blinding pillar of silver flame incinerated countless Nightmare Creatures, plunging toward the ground and cleaving a deadly path through the horde of abominations attacking the city.

Thousands of them were slaughtered in an instant, and more still perished as the dragon moved its head, sending the beam of silver death rolling across the desert. The sand boiled, turning into molten lava and flowing like a fiery sea.

Even if the dragon was too far for Nightwalker to see its eyes, he suddenly felt a heavy gaze crushing into him.

Smiling crookedly, he waved and then pointed to the enormous Titan strangling the ship.

The dragon studied him for a few moments and then changed course, moving swiftly in the direction of the Night Garden. Nightwalker let out a tired sigh, then laughed.

"Damn it. Is his shift not over yet? I hoped to meet one of the young ladies instead..."

Then, he helped Naeve to his feet, patted him on the shoulder, and turned into a stream of starlight again.

By the time Kai arrived, he was already rending the Titan's flesh. The Starbeast attacked the colossal abomination from the left, while the dragon descended upon it from the right like a dark mass of celestial fury.

Soon enough, rivers of blood flowed onto the deck of the Night Garden.

...An hour later, the Titan was dead. The swarm of winged abominations had been repelled, and the horde of Nightmare Creatures on the ground had turned to ash. The enemy was not defeated, but it was pushed back, for now — for a few days, or perhaps hours.

Or perhaps even minutes.

In the endless chaos of the end of days, nobody could say for sure.

Nightwalker was inspecting the damage when Kai landed on the bloody deck beside him, having already assumed his human form. The young man looked quite stunning, but also tired and grim — there were bruises under his eyes, and his skin was smeared with soot and dried blood.

Looking around, he grimaced.

“How bad is it?"

Nightwalker cursed.

“Quite bad. The Night Garden is grievously wounded... I think I'll need to spend at least a few weeks at the wharf Lady Ananke built."

Needless to say, with the Night Garden disappearing for several weeks, the situation in the waking world was bound to turn from bad to worse.

Kai sighed.

"Effie can cover for some of it... I'll talk to her."

Then, he closed his eyes for a moment, suppressing a groan.

When he opened them again, Nightwalker could already see that their conversation would be cut short.

Kai took a step back and nodded.

“I cannot stay any longer. Do not linger either — stay safe."

Saying that, Kai threw one last look at the devastated deck of the Night Garden and pulled himself across the realm boundary.

A few heartbeats later, the unbearable strike of the vast desert, a great swath of it turned to glass, was replaced by unbearable cold. The winds howled, throwing sharp ice crystals into his face. The air smelled of blood and ash, and he was plunged into the clamor of battle once more.

Kai sighed and looked ahead.

In front of him were the spires of the Jade Palace, and beyond them, on the plain below the mountains, a great blizzard was devouring the world. He could see the shapes of countless snow wraiths moving under the cover of the blizzard, and the banners of Seishan's legion fluttering in the wind like a river of blood.

With his miraculous sight, he saw it all — Seishan and her sisters, their Transcendent champions, Ascended officers, Awakened soldiers, Beastmaster's thralls shielding the humans with their bodies, countless Echoes throwing themselves into the mass of enemies, the Ravenous Fiend moving through the blizzard like an obliterating mountain of fire and steel...

Mundane soldiers were manning the fortifications that protected the city, and more Awakened were bracing themselves as the towering, churning white wall of the blizzard drew closer to the vast expanse of scarlet fields.

He also saw three colossal shapes moving far in the distance, guiding the blizzard like profane shepherds. Each of them was tall enough to dwarf mountains and eerie enough to make even his blood run cold. Kai inhaled deeply and summoned his bow.

“It just never ends, does it?"

He nocked an arrow and launched himself into the swirling snow.

Then again, perhaps it was good that the battle never ended.

Life was war, after all.

The day all fighting ceased would be the day all humans were gone.

For now, though, they were still here.

They were still fighting.

--- Chapter 3209 ---

A carriage was rolling down a forest road, pulled by a black steed. Its curtains were closed, and there was no sound coming from the interior. There was a young man sitting on the coachman’s bench, holding the reins with a steady hand. His skin was like porcelain, and his eyes were like glistening onyx; with nothing but rustling trees in sight, he seemed to be enjoying a moment of peace.

That peace did not last long, though. Suddenly, one of the trees fell across the road, barring the path of a carriage, and a ragtag crowd of armed men burst from the underbrush to surround it.

"Well, well, well... what do we have here?"

Their leader was a towering man with a bushy beard, wearing makeshift leather armor. Resting a monstrous cleaver on his shoulder, he gave the gilded ornaments of the carriage a look of avarice and then shifted his menacing gaze to the coachman.

"Hey there, little friend. Where are you heading?"

A sinister grin split his face apart.

The coachman scratched the tip of his nose awkwardly and remained silent for a few moments. Eventually, he sighed and said:

“To be honest, I am heading to the Shadow Realm."

The bandits exploded with laughter. Their leader, too, was amused by the answer.

“Prepared to die? Ha! It seems you've recognized me, the Forest King — the butcher of men, Ascended Cleaver! Ah, but do not worry. I am not at all as bloodthirsty as stories tell."

He chuckled menacingly.

"Tell you what. Give us the horse, the carriage, all the money you have, and your clothes. Then, after we dragged your master from the carriage and stripped them of all earthly possessions... if you kill your master with your own two hands, we will spare your life and allow you to join us!"

The coachman looked at him with a hint of confusion in his black eyes.

After a short while, he decided to clarify.

“Just to be sure. You want me and the person in the carriage to fight to the death... naked?"

The leader of the bandits — the self-proclaimed Forest King, Cleaver, blinked a couple of times. He glanced back at his subordinates, who were giving him weird glances, then coughed.

“On second thought, you can strip naked after you've killed them."

The coachman frowned slightly.

“Won't I be one of you guys by then? Why would I strip naked?"

The towering bandit sighed.

"Are you giving us money or not? I've already decided to cut off your tongue, smartass, but you can still make it out of here alive."

The coachman waved a hand.

"No, no... you can have my money."

With that, he pulled out a small pouch, untied it, and shook it a few times. A dozen or so coins poured into his palm, some of them glistening gold. The eyes of the bandits shone when they saw it.

Before the coachman could hand them the money, though, there was the sound of something falling inside the carriage, followed by the clinking of bottles and a low, tortured groan.

Then, one of the curtains was pulled back, and a devilishly handsome young man with a crescent moon mark on his forehead emerged, hanging out of the window.

He seemed to be in his early twenties. His eyes were bloodshot, and he looked extremely miserable, as if suffering from a dreadful hangover.

The bandits who stood close to the carriage paled and took a step back, pinching their noses. The stench of alcohol was almost unbearable.

The young man looked at the scene in front of him with blurry eyes. Then, he seemed to regain a sliver of awareness.

Looking at the Forest King and the coachman, who froze with a pile of coins in his hand, the young man rubbed his eyes. Then, he studied them for a few more moments and let out a startled chuckle.

"Who are these clowns, Shadow?"

His eyes widened.

“Wait... are we getting robbed? We are actually getting robbed?!"

The coachman nodded.

"That's pretty evident."

The young man stared at him in utter disbelief.

"And you are actually giving them the money?!"

The coachman shrugged.

“I don't really need money. They seem to have more use for it.”

His supposed master scoffed.

Then, his gaze suddenly turned sharp.

"Wait... is this one of your sick games? It is, isn't it?!"

He shuddered, then looked at the bandits with a strange expression.

Cleaver could have sworn that it was... pity.

“It's not. Really."

The young master opened the door of the carriage and stumbled out of it, making the bandits grimace and take another step back.

“As if I'd believe that!"

At that point, Cleaver's patience ran out.

"Hey, bastards! I don't think you two are taking this situation seriously enough! I am going to cut off your limbs, make you eat them, and then skin you alive! I'll mince your bodies into tiny pieces and feed you to the dogs!"

He huffed angrily, but then hesitated for a moment.

Finally, he asked in a lower tone:

“But just in case... what do you mean by sick games? What sick things can this little brat be guilty of?"

The young master rolled his eyes.

"Don't get me started!"

Looking at the coachman with resentful eyes, he spat.

"If I were you, I'd apologize and run away. No, better walk away slowly! Don't make sudden moves... don't provoke him! He made an oath not to kill anyone!"

The bandit leader tilted his head in confusion.

“Wait, isn't that good news for me? Here I was, feeling a little apprehensive. But if he can't even kill anyone, then there's nothing to fear?"

The young master shook his head energetically, then paled and grabbed it, letting out another groan.

“No, no... that just shows how uncultured you are, with no foresight! You'd think that if a person can't kill you, you are safe. But it's the opposite! Just because he can't kill you doesn't mean that he can't make you wish you were dead!"

He leaned tiredly on the carriage.

“Like that time we passed through a sinful city stricken by a mystical plague. That guy found the Spirit Rat responsible for the plague, and, well... I had never seen a rat shedding tears before, let alone a Sacred Rat. But that one! That one was crying and rubbing its little paws together, as if begging to be killed. Actually, there were a myriad of them, and they all begged at the same time."

The bandit leader blinked.

The young master wasn't done, though.

“Or that other time, during the Divine Vigil... all the heroes of the mortal realms gathered to send War God's avatar on her way, and a few Supremes came as well. That sick bastard developed a dislike for the Second Wandering Archon, so he challenged the poor man to a debate and argued with him for seven days straight. On the seventh day, the Archon spat blood and collapsed, his hair turning white, tears flowing out of his eyes like ceaseless rivers. His Domain completely collapsed! I hear he hasn't uttered a word since."

The bandit scratched the back of his head.

“The Second Wandering Archon? No way. That elder withstood two blows from the Demon of Dread once..."

The young master scoffed.

“The Demon of Dread?! Let me tell you about dread, fool! Once, we met an arrogant Spirit who ravaged a realm over a perceived slight. That guy over there couldn't kill it, so instead, he broke its body, shattered its soul, and extinguished its spirit — not enough for that unfortunate deity to die, but just shy of it. Spirits are pretty hardy, though. So, he waited for that one to heal... then repeated the whole thing, ten times in a row. And he had no plans of stopping, either! Eventually, the High Priest of Heart God's cult had to arrive and personally plead for their Spirit."

The bandit leader waited for a few moments, then asked cautiously:

“Well? And what happened then?"

The young master groaned and covered his face with a palm.

"The Heart God's cult has a new High Priest now. The old one retired and became a hermit... after he regained the ability to walk without crutches, that is. He still screams in his sleep, though!"

The coachman gave him a gloomy look.

"I did spare the Spirit though, didn't I?"

The bandit leader studied the two of them silently for a while, then growled and pointed his enormous cleaver at the young master.

“Who do you take me for, noble scum?! A complete idiot?! Sacred Beasts, Supreme monarchs, Spirits, and High Priests?! What kind of human is capable of facing them in a fight, let alone surviving it?! And what, that bastard is serving as a coachman?! Who are you then, a god's avatar?! Let me guess, that horse is a Sacred Beast as well!"

The young master spared him a pitying glance, then sighed and shook his head.

"You made three mistakes, blockhead."

He pointed at the horse.

"First, this is not a horse. This is a mass of shadows shaped to look like a horse. Why? I have no idea. That guy just seems to like black horses, for some reason."

Then, he pointed to himself.

"Second, I am not a god's avatar. I am merely a god's grandson. Her favorite grandson, of course! But still, not an avatar."

Finally, he pointed to the coachman.

"And finally... that thing is not a human. It's a Supreme Titan created by the God of Death to punish all living things. It's just pretending to be human because... well, I don't know. He's just perverted that way, I guess."

The bandit leader scoffed and stared at them with murder in his eyes, clearly unconvinced.

But then, his eyes shifted slightly toward the black horse.

At some point in time, the horse's silhouette had grown strangely vague, and wisps of ethereal black smoke were drifting from its mouth.

The horse slowly lost its shape, like a melting candle. And beneath that deceptive shape, he saw...

A terrified scream resounded in the forest, sending a flock of birds flying in fright.

"R-run! Run!"

Dropping his cleaver, the bandit leader turned around and dashed away, his eyes full of primal horror. His subordinates were of lesser Ranks, so they weren't quite as fast — still, in just a few moments, all of them disappeared into the forest.

Several black tentacles shot from the shapeless mass of shadows.

Instead of pursuing the bandits, though, they simply grabbed the tree barring the road and flung it aside.

A heartbeat later, there was a normal black horse in front of the carriage once again, nibbling docilely on the fallen leaves. Shadow sighed and dropped the coins back into the purse.

“I only got into a spat with that Spirit because you kept threatening to fight it yourself, you know. So... that was unfair."

Noctis waved a hand and climbed back into the carriage.

"Whatever. I am hungover... wake me up when we're there."

Closing the door, he lowered the curtains. Shadow nudged the horse, and the carriage continued to roll forward.

A few minutes later, Snuggle climbed out of his pocket and jumped down to the bench, sitting beside him.

She pretended to yawn.

"See? That's progress! You didn't even want to kill them, did you?"

Shadow spared her a glance.

“Wrong. I did want to kill them."

He leaned back and looked into the depths of the forest with a wistful expression.

“This time, they stumbled onto us. Who will be their victim the next time? Someone weaker than I am, no doubt. How many people will lose their lives because I spared these few?"

He shrugged with a detached smile.

“Not that I care. It's just for the sake of the argument... mercy is not always a virtue, Snuggle.”

The little doll stared at him for a while, then shook her head.

“This is not to save other lives, though. It's to save yours."

Shadow laughed.

"I am neither truly alive nor something that can die. So saving me from death is a misguided endeavor."

Snuggle studied him some more, then looked away dejectedly.

Soon enough, they reached their destination.

Up ahead, the forest receded, making space for a vast expanse of emerald grass. In the distance, golden fields stretched as far as the eye could see.

The air was permeated by a sense of bliss and tranquility.

The dirt road turned into one cobbled with stone, and the carriage rolled through a beautiful stone arch.

At the top of the arch, a few runes were carved into the white stone...

They read:

Kingdom of Hope.

--- Chapter 3210 ---

The carriage crossed the arch and continued on its way. Shadow's expression did not change, but he turned his head slightly, looking north.

Their long journey across the mortal realms was nearing its end.

It had taken them a few years to reach the Kingdom of Hope — the last mortal realm they had to cross before reaching the Hollow Mountains.

Noctis was not nineteen anymore. His face had lost the last traces of adolescence, and he did not look like a boy now, resembling a man more and more with each day. Snuggle and Shadow, meanwhile, remained the same... at least outwardly.

In truth, many things had happened during their journey, so neither of them was the same.

Even if Shadow did not want to, he had allowed himself to be pulled deeper into the whirlpool of humanity. After meeting countless people and witnessing their lives, often becoming an unwilling participant in their joys and conflicts, he had no choice but to become painted in similar hues. He was now much more human than he had been or ever wished to be.

Snuggle seemed to have changed the least. She had grown more comfortable with her Transcendent powers, learning more about her Aspect and its depths — but apart from that, the little doll was just as cheerful and clumsy as before.

It was just that now there was a dark undertone hidden behind her brightness, even more so than there had been in the past.

That was because now that they had spent so much time together, both Shadow and Snuggle had an inkling of who the other one was. It was just that nothing good could come from knowing the truth, so both of them avoided broaching the subject, even in their thoughts.

There were enough things happening every day to keep them occupied, anyway.

In hindsight, meeting Noctis had been a blessing. If Shadow and Snuggle — an ancient Titan and a homeless soul occupying a child's doll — ventured into the cauldron of the mortal realms alone, they would have probably left a trail of ruin and devastation in their wake, eventually attracting the attention of beings who were too powerful even for Shadow to face.

He was not the most sociable of creatures, after all. Even if he did not want to get entangled with the world, the world rarely left him a chance to stay detached from it, and since Shadow wasn't really familiar with such concepts as humility, fear, and knowing when to shut up, things were bound to get complicated when the world came knocking.

His propensity to always tell the truth alone was disastrous.

But with Noctis there to shield Shadow from the countless people and beings they had met on the way, most of their journey had been somewhat smooth. Noctis was not only able to smooth things over, but had also proven himself useful in countless ways, from renting rooms at inns to navigating the complicated web of relationships between the great powers of the mortal realms.

It was just that the young Transcendent's usefulness had its own drawback, as well. There were many things that Shadow would have passed by indifferently, but Noctis refused to.

So... their journey had not been entirely smooth, after all.

In fact, it was full of twists and turns, conflicts and unexpected resolutions. Noctis and Snuggle handled the Creatures of Corruption — those they could handle, at least. Shadow stepped in when things became too perilous.

Like those two Sacred beings Noctis had mentioned. The way he told the tale to the bandits, both of them had been easy prey to Shadow... of course, it wasn't true. In fact, it was the exact opposite of the truth.

After testing himself against these two Sacred beings, Shadow came to the conclusion that while he could handle some, each of such battles would be a matter of life and death. Sacred beings were different from each other, after all. Just like there were people who were weak and people who were paragons of martial skill, Spirits were not created equal either.

Among those who were Supreme, Shadow was like a herald of death. Even if he had promised not to kill, he could still devastate most opponents of his own Rank with relative ease. In a battle against those who were Sacred, however... even if he could hold his own, the outcome was up to luck.

Shadow had a feeling that if he stumbled on a truly powerful Spirit one day, he would be destroyed. Of course, he wasn't really afraid of death.

But every time he had died in the past, he was thrust into a new life.

So if there was something Shadow feared, it was life.

With a sigh, he guided their carriage across a well-maintained stone road. Around them, the tranquil vista of the Kingdom of Hope sprawled toward the horizon. The vast expanse of emerald grass, the golden fields in the distance, the boundless blue sky above — the scene was blissful and picturesque, infused with a feeling of peace.

Among all the places they had visited, this land — a mortal realm ruled by a Divine being — seemed like the safest. From what Shadow had heard, people here thrived. Their lives were not without worries, of course, but far better than in most places.

And yet, Shadow could not help but feel a chill run down his spine.

The moment they entered the Kingdom of Hope, he suddenly felt disturbed and uneasy. Looking at the beautiful landscape around them, all he could hear was the rattling of chains.

All he could think about were memories of madness.

Unable to stop himself, Shadow turned his head and glanced at the carriage, where Noctis was still sleeping off his recent escapade.

Shadow's expression darkened.

Just at that moment, the door of the carriage opened, and Noctis climbed onto the coachman’s bench while yawning.

"I told you to wake me up, did I not?"

“H—hey, watch it!"

In his groggy state, he didn't notice Snuggle and almost sat on her, forcing the little doll to scurry closer to Shadow and give him a resentful look.

“You stink!"

Noctis scoffed.

“So what? You don't have a nose."

Shadow smiled quietly.

Noctis, meanwhile, glanced around with curiosity.

"So this is the Kingdom of Hope."

His eyes glinted with wonder.

"The Demon of Desire has always been fond of humans, but it's still a bit strange, isn't it? For her to establish a kingdom in the mortal realms. I heard she is a wise and benevolent ruler."

He smiled.

“And she invented writing, too!"

His admiring smile widened a little, then suddenly disappeared. Noctis remained silent for a short while, then said with a dark expression on his face:

"Come to think of it, I had to endure all those exhausting reading lessons because of her. Shadow, do you know the horror of having to stay inside and read when the weather outside is perfectly fine? Actually, don't answer. You spent thousands of years in a damp cave. You'd probably love it, lunatic!"

Shadow shrugged.

Noctis sighed heavily, then shivered.

"Still, it's weird. The rest of the daemons are so aloof and terrifying, but the Demon of Desire seems... nice."

Shadow looked at him, then turned his gaze back to the road.

"Really? I think differently."

His faint smile dimmed a little.

"I think she is the most terrifying of them all."

Noctis and Snuggle both glanced at him with surprise.

"Really? Why?"

He did not answer for a while, then leaned back and sighed.

“All things start from desire. And all things bow to desire, as well."

Noctis scoffed.

“Sounds like a lot of rubbish..."

Looking ahead, they could just see the walls of a bustling city. Noctis seemed to liven up, expecting to rest from the road soon.

The closer to the city they got, the more people there were on the road. Carts, carriages, and wagons moved both ways, and from time to time, a horseman would fly by, rushing on some unknown business. There were some traveling on foot, as well — their faces were relaxed and healthy, as if they knew no fear of the Creatures of Corruption.

That, at least, made sense. What kind of Nightmare Creature would be bold enough to enter a land ruled by a Divine Titan?

Noctis seemed more and more pleased. It seemed that he was already imagining the wonders of local cuisine and culture — or maybe he was simply looking forward to curing his hangover with some wine. However, Shadow led their carriage around the city without approaching its gate. Noctis was startled.

“Huh? Wait, where are we going?"

Shadow kept looking ahead.

“There's a place I want to visit."

Despite the protests of the young man, the carriage rolled forward, soon leaving the city behind.

Before too long, towering white walls revealed themselves in front of them once again.

Not too far from the city, a magnificent structure stood under the boundless sky, emanating an overpowering feeling of joy and excitement.

It was a great colosseum built of white stone.

--- Chapter 3211 ---

The coliseum had been built by the Demon of Desire herself, and was called the Theater of Hope. Its walls were white and pristine, as if built from the pure clouds that traveled across the azure sky — however, as Shadow glanced up at the magnificent arches, he couldn't help but imagine them adorned with banners that were as red as blood.

An echo of a distant chant surfaced from his memory:

“Glory! Glory! Glory!"

Shadow winced, feeling a ghostly pain pierce his chest. A moment later, the ghastly vision was gone, and the pain was gone as well.

There was indeed an exuberant chant resounding from within the great theater, but it had nothing to do with glory. Instead, the jubilant voices of a vast crowd were calling for the performers to enter the stage.

It seemed that a play was about to begin — Shadow and his companions had arrived just in time.

“I've heard so many stories about the Theater of Hope! They say that there is nothing like it in the world.”

Noctis grinned, clearly excited.

Snuggle seemed quite curious, as well. Shadow lingered for a moment, then said in a calm tone:

“Then what are we waiting for?"

Leaving the carriage below the walls of the great theater, they paid a small fee and entered. Inside, a vast arena was surrounded by soaring rows of stone benches, all of them filled by expectant spectators. Sunshine poured from above, reflecting from white stone and creating a beautiful, dreamlike atmosphere.

The sounds of laughter and excited chatter washed over Shadow and his companions, making them feel a bit of warm anticipation as well.

Even Shadow, who was rarely enthusiastic about anything, felt like he was looking forward to the play.

He frowned, then shivered slightly.

‘Such potent sorcery...’

Indeed, that feeling of anticipation was not entirely his own. Looking around, he noticed shallow channels carved into the stone throughout the great theater. The entire enormous coliseum was one vast runic array — Shadow could not quite discern its purpose yet, but it seemed to enhance the emotions of people gathered inside.

The sorcery of the Theater of Hope was truly astonishing... and terrifying. It wasn't easy to affect the heart of a Supreme Titan, and yet that was exactly what had happened — without him noticing, no less.

Noctis had said that the Demon of Desire was nice, but Shadow felt nothing but cold dread when thinking about her.

His companions, however, succumbed to the atmosphere of her theater easily, igniting with excitement.

“Shadow! Let's go find a good seat!"

Hearing Snuggle's squeaky voice, Shadow pulled himself out of his short reverie and went to do just that. Soon enough, the three of them were seated in one of the higher rows of the Theater of Hope — Shadow and Noctis resting on the benches, Snuggle sitting on one of Shadow's shoulders.

The vast arena was below them. It was circular, and at its center stood the stage.

“Look, look! It's starting!"

Snuggle pulled at Shadow's hair to make him pay attention, which only made him wince.

There was movement in the arena, indeed.

As if out of nowhere, a tall figure appeared on the stage, wearing a white robe and a smiling mask. The audience exploded with excited shouts, while the figure — the leader of the chorus, coryphaeus — bowed and performed a few movements of a simple, elegant dance.

When the audience grew quiet, a booming voice resounded from beneath the smiling mask. The Theater of Hope was vast, and yet Shadow could hear each word clearly, as if the coryphaeus was standing directly in front of him. It was partially due to the unique acoustics of the theater, and partially due to the actor's masterful delivery.

The play began.

At first, Shadow was only mildly interested in the story. But as it progressed, told by the masked actors and the chorus, he felt himself being drawn into it. The singing of the chorus and the voices of the actors fused with the unique sorcery of the Theater of Hope, creating an unforgettable mixture.

The story of the play was one he knew, but not in detail.

It was the story of the beautiful and enigmatic ruler of a mystical land of ash and snow... the Jade Queen.

At the start of the play, the Jade Queen was a young and innocent monster. She was born in the crystalline darkness and spent her days enthusiastically searching for miraculous nectar. Then, however, her beauty and innocence caught the eye of the Demon of Dread, who was passing by during his journey to the mortal realms. Bored, the Demon of Dread decided to become the young monster's teacher. The first act of the play was light and comedic in tone, describing the many clashes between the terrifying daemon's desire to make the Jade Queen into a proper young lady and her mischievous, inhuman nature. Eventually, the Jade Queen learned how to speak the human language and Transcended, gaining a Transformation Ability — it was just that since she was a creature, and not a human, her Transformation Ability worked the other way around and allowed her to become one.
