At the end of the first act, the Demon of Dread whispered something into her ear — he taught her a terrible truth that no one else knew, causing the end of the Jade Queen's childhood.

Shadow had an inkling of what that truth was, but the playwright didn't. So, the play never stated it either.

‘I wonder how much of what is shown in the play is true.'

In the second act, the Jade Queen had already become a young woman. She was now a ruler of a distant, mystical realm — wise and enlightened, but also willful, capricious, and at times downright sinister. Nevertheless, the news of her enchanting beauty and profound wisdom spread far and wide, stirring the hearts of many heroes.

Many suitors arrived to pursue her. Some failed to cross the great bridge leading to her Jade Palace, some made it through and were welcomed in her court, but ultimately refused. Some harbored impure thoughts and were punished for their vices in ghastly, horrible ways. Eventually, the Jade Queen grew tired of these advances and issued a challenge to all the mortal realms. If someone could solve her riddle, she would fulfill any wish that person had. After the second act ended, Shadow found himself unable to decide whether the Jade Queen was a benevolent being or a creature full of malice. She was endearing and tantalizing, no doubt... her wisdom and insight were unrivaled. But what was hidden behind the jade mask?

What did the Jade Queen desire? What did she fear? Everyone knew of her, but no one seemed to care who she was.

Maybe that was the purpose of the deadly riddle — not to find a worthy consort among the sea of suitors, but to find someone who could share the heavy burden of forbidden knowledge she carried in her heart.

The third act showed the gathering of guests who arrived in hopes of solving the riddle and receiving a wish from the beautiful, frightening Jade Queen. The tone of the third act was not at all comedic, but Noctis spent its entirety laughing... that was because there were many familiar faces among the Jade Queen's guests.

"By the moon... aren't they the pompous brothers, sons of Sun God? They visited the temple once. I stole the older one's sword!"

“Ah, the Mason! That Transcendent uncle is such a bore. Actually, the priests who raised me were all over him, forgetting all shame. That is because nobody can build a temple more magnificent than those built by him — he built one for Sun God, War God, Storm God, Heart God... so, they couldn't endure the thought that grandma doesn't have one as well! I swear, if he put just a fraction of the time he spends on building things into fighting Creatures of Corruption, he'd be Supreme a long time ago.”

"Wait, is that supposed to be... me?! What the hell, I never went to find the Jade Queen! I was a toddler when this gathering happened, damn it!"

Shadow spared him a casual glance and smiled.

Indeed, many heroes gathered to solve the Jade Queen's riddle. In fact, not all of them wanted to become her consort — some were simply attracted by the promise of a wish being fulfilled. There were not that many Supremes in the world, after all, not to mention Supremes favored by one of the great and terrible daemons. So, a promise made by the Jade Queen was worth a lot. None of the illustrious heroes managed to solve the riddle, though. The warriors failed, and the sages failed as well.

In the end, a figure wearing tattered rags emerged from the crowd of guests, the eyes of her mask covered by a dirty blindfold. She was a mad oracle from a distant land — a land where people did not worship gods, and built temples to fate instead.

The great heroes treated her with contempt, but the Jade Queen seemed amused. So, she asked the oracle the same question:

“What is the heaviest thing in the world?"

The mad oracle laughed bitterly and then answered, pointing at her unseeing eyes.

"It's knowledge."

And thus, the riddle was solved.

The play ended with the chorus singing about enlightenment and knowledge, praising the wise queen and the learned oracle.

The audience seemed to be greatly satisfied, exploding with applause and whistles.

Shadow, however, thought that the ending of the play was quite strange.

Neither the Jade Queen nor the blind oracle seemed that fond of the truths they bore, so why would the playwright paint pursuit of knowledge as a noble virtue? Trying to attach a didactic moral to the story only seemed forced and patronizing.

More than that, where was the real ending? What was the wish of the blind oracle, and did the Jade Queen make it come true? Surely, that mad oracle wasn't aiming to become the beautiful queen's consort...

‘What a strange play.’

Shadow sighed and shook his head.

Even if he did not like the ending, the experience of watching a play in the Theater of Hope was truly wondrous. The songs of the chorus, the dancing, the twists and turns of the story... he was swept up by the blazing emotions of the crowd, feeling more joyful and exhilarated than ever before.

In this life, at least.

And while none of the spectators could perceive it, Shadow had learned quite a lot about the sorcery of Hope, as well.

--- Chapter 3212 ---

In Shadow's memories, the Theater of Hope was a ghastly place.

Many of his lives had ended here — some succumbing to terrible wounds in the cages below the arena, some on its blood-red surface. His blood and the jubilation of the frenzied crowd fueled the sorcery of the great coliseum, so he had assumed that it was a sinister and malevolent kind of magic. However, now that he had witnessed the Theater of Hope in its original state, he realized that he was wrong.

It wasn't the deaths of caged slaves that fueled the sorcery that the Demon of Desire had created, and neither was it their blood. Instead, it was the spectators.

Their emotions, to be precise.

As Shadow observed the play, he saw torrents of soul essence flowing through the vast runes carved into the white stone of Hope's coliseum. The source of that soul essence was the jubilant crowd — the more excited and exhilarated the audience members were, the more essence there was. Enthralled by the singing of the chorus and the powerful voices of the actors, they fueled the theater.

However, they did not fuel it with their own soul essence. Shadow did not know how, but it was their emotions themselves that were transformed into mystical energy... truly, a sorcery worthy of one of the daemons.

The source of the soul essence was interesting. Far more interesting, however, was the target of the vast enchantment. Shadow was not powerful or knowledgeable enough to discern the secrets of divine sorcery, but he did manage to glean its core purpose.

The smaller measure of the powerful enchantment was channeled back into the great theater, enhancing the enjoyment of the crowd, making it more susceptible to the mundane power of the engaging performance.

A far greater measure, however, was channeled directly into the depths of the Kingdom of Hope, nourishing it. Shadow was not sure what exact form that nourishment took, but he was certain that the Theater of Hope was nurturing and protecting this land.

It was rather ingenious.

In the hands of the Demon of Desire, the great theater was a joyous and benevolent force that benefitted the people of her kingdom.

In the hands of those who would come after her... it would become the monstrous Red Colosseum, a blood-soaked altar of War. Which was not to say that the Red Colosseum did not benefit people. It was just that its power would serve a far more malevolent purpose in the hands of its future owner.

"That was great, wasn't it?"

Noctis seemed satisfied, at least.

"Now that's culture... ah, the costumes, the poetry! Simply marvelous."

The young Transcendent grinned.

"Even if the mask they used to portray me is not nearly handsome enough! But, oh well. Is there even an artisan in the world who can capture my dashing visage?"

Snuggle gave him a sideways glance.

“The better question is if there is an actor in the world who can portray your vanity..."

Shadow smiled faintly, but he was only listening to them half-heartedly. As they left the great theater, he could not help but look at its pristine white walls.

Once again, his memories were stirring, and he felt powerless to resist them.

He remembered one of his past lives — a fierce and defiant life painted in shades of red.

In that life... he was a girl whom nobody loved.

She was born in the slums of a prosperous city. Her father did not care enough to name her, vanishing into the dark alleys. Her mother saw her as a burden and abandoned her on the dirty streets. The people who saw her were only full of irritation and anger. From those times, all she remembered was hunger and loneliness... and scorn.

Luckily, she was born with hair of a color that was unusual in these parts. Orphaned girls with red hair were often entrusted to an ancient order of female warriors, and while her hair was chestnut, someone decided that it was close enough. So, she was brought to a temple instead of starving or freezing to death on the streets. She was too young to understand what a warrior was or who the gods were — all she knew was that she was warm in the temple, and the adults gave her food for free.

In the temple, she was not alone anymore. She was even given a name.

Life in the temple was not easy. The girls adopted by the priestesses underwent grueling training and thorough education. Those who showed promise were given more attention; those who fell short were raised to be temple slaves or cast out.

Some died.

She did not want to die, but she did not mind becoming a slave. If anything, the girls who had been deemed unworthy of becoming warriors led a much easier life... and yet, she trained harder than anyone else.

That was because, even if she did not understand it clearly, she wanted attention. There were many orphans like her, after all, but only a few priestesses who trained them. Their time was a treasure that was difficult to win.

Attention was not love, but back then, she did not understand the difference. Even if the former tasted hollow, she wanted it all the same. And so, she strived to be the best. She wasn't the strongest among the girls in the temple, and she wasn't the fastest. She wasn't even the smartest... but there was one thing that separated her from the rest. It was that she never gave up.

No matter how painful or difficult, she always pushed forward. Every time she fell, she got up. She endured the bruises, the callouses, the bloodstains. She walked forward, one step at a time.

After a while, she grew stronger, faster, and smarter. As the number of girls on the training field dwindled, her dedication never waned. Soon enough, none of them could defeat her... and that was why they treated her coldly, just like everyone else had.

But she had talent, it seemed.

In fact, her talent was monstrous.

At ten, she slew her first Beast.

At twelve, she learned how to sense soul essence.

At fourteen, she Awakened.

At sixteen, full of vitality and delicate beauty of youth, she unsealed her Aspect. None of the Awakened priestesses in the temple could defeat her anymore.

That was when everything changed. The priestesses who had been cold and distant before slowly started to treat her with warmth and affection. Her fellow disciples, who had always been hostile and unfriendly, were suddenly nice and attentive.

She was happy...

For a while.

But then, things began to turn for the worse.

The priestesses never left her alone, often quarreling among each other about who would spend time with her. Their attention, which she had always desired, became burdensome instead of sweet.

The other young disciples were worse. Their eyes, their smiles, their voices... all of it began to unnerve her. They were too intense, too possessive.

Almost obsessed.

It wasn't long before blood was spilled.

That was how she discovered her Flaw — her cruel, bitter Flaw.

It was that people could not help but love her.

The more time they spent with her, the greater their love became, the more they desired to never be apart from her.

To always be with her... to possess her. That longing eventually drove them mad. Some lasted longer, while some surrendered almost immediately. But in the end, they all succumbed.

Needless to say, that caused quite a problem for the temple.

...At seventeen, she was sent to war.

Now a true War Maiden, having given the oath, she entered the battlefield as a priestess of War God. Things were easier on the battlefield, because no one lived long enough to become infatuated with her. There was blood, there were torn bodies, there were screams of agony and death. There were young soldiers calling for their mothers.

She did not call, because she did not remember hers.

Her world became painted red.

She was cut, battered, and broken. She was pierced by sharp blades and mauled by sharp claws. She fell into dirt and rose from piles of bodies. She learned horror, sorrow, and triumph.

And she never gave up.

Her enemies died. Her comrades died, as well. Those who survived... she kept a distance from them, knowing that they would slowly become enthralled otherwise.

She was lonely.

One war ended, and another started. She traveled from one battlefield to another, undefeated, growing stronger. Growing fearsome. Slowly, her fame spread, and people began to seek her out — not because of her beauty, but because of her strength. Because they wanted her to fight for them. But even bathed in their attention, in their desire, she still felt alienated. There was an invisible wall between her and everyone else.

In her journeys, there was only one being who kept her company.

There was only one being whom she never had to abandon, and who never died.

Who was always by her side.

It was her goddess... the Goddess of War.

Finally, turning twenty, she realized a simple truth.

It was that War God was her mother, her sister, and her companion.

For as long as War God existed, she would never be alone.

She would always be loved.

--- Chapter 3213 ---

Life was war, and war was everywhere in the tumultuous ocean of the mortal realms. Now that generations of valiant heroes had pushed the previous rulers of the mundane world back and civilization had blossomed, Creatures of Corruption hid in the dark corners of existence and remote lands. Even if they had not disappeared altogether, many people went their entire lives without meeting one.

And without the Creatures of Corruption, those same heroes who had fought them turned their gazes to each other.

Cities grew and turned into kingdoms; the borders of the kingdoms pressed against each other, and conflicts abounded. More than that, exalted champions rose to the throne of Supremacy from time to time — and every time a new Supreme was crowned, they had to establish a Domain. Old borders collapsed, and new ones were established. The balance of power in the mortal realms was disturbed, and a devastating wave of change rolled outward across the world, reaching even those realms that were far apart from the rising Domains.

So, war was common.

And a priestess of War always had somewhere to go.

Released from the torment of solitude, she was unbound. She had been too young and too naive when she gave the oath and became a War Maiden — but after maturing and treading the red mud of blood-soaked battlefields, she finally understood its tenets. She finally fathomed the true essence of War and learned true devotion. Her goddess was the goddess of war... but ultimately, she was the goddess of life.

War was life, and life always triumphed. It always persevered, it always endured. It never gave up.

Just like her.

So, what she truly worshipped was life.

And there was nowhere one could experience life sharper or more desperately than on a battlefield — surrounded by death, only the width of a blade away from falling into its dark embrace.

Now that she was twenty and already an Ascended, having devoted herself to her goddess, she finally felt like herself. She felt as if it was only now that she gained the ability to think for herself and make her own decisions... to be her own person.

She wasn't a novice among the War Maidens anymore, either, and as such was afforded authority. One of the privileges she gained was the right to lead younger sisters into battle; the other was to decide which battlefield to enter on her own.

Each War Maiden had her own way of choosing where to worship their goddess, and for which side to fight. Some fought for those who seemed to have a nobler cause; some fought for those who had more valor. Some pursued opportunities to witness specific stratagems or test themselves against outstanding warriors.

For her, the choice was simple. She always went where the drums of war roared the loudest, joining the fiercest of battles to fight for the weakest side. Her goal was always to cut down the strongest adversaries while ensuring that as many of her comrades as possible survived. She was often grievously wounded, but never defeated — wherever she went, blood flowed like a river, but she never drowned in its tide.

She witnessed the ugliest side of humanity. She witnessed the most beautiful expressions of human goodness, as well. She witnessed life in all its brilliant glory — from the darkest hues of despair and sorrow to the radiant joy of devotion and hope.

She fought men. She fought Creatures of Corruption.

She watched, she learned... she grew.

At twenty-six, she became a Transcendent. Soon, there was an army following her. Her name was renowned across all mortal realms, and her fame continued to rise.

But the desire of those who wanted to claim her continued to grow, as well, as did their power. They came to break her and force her to submit, to make her their own...

She faced and killed them all.

Eventually, she grew tired of bloodshed. And so, for a while, she retreated from the world, returning to the temple that had nurtured her — there, she took charge of raising a new generation of War Maidens, treating the orphaned girls as her own daughters.

Some of them were motivated. Some of them were lazy. Some of them were strong and talented, while some were weak and unsuited for combat. But still, she loved them all. Even if she had to keep her distance to spare them the curse of her Flaw, she made sure to give each one as much attention as she could.

She was gentler than the priestesses who had raised her... perhaps that was her sin. The goal of all War Maidens was to reforge themselves in the image of the goddess they worshiped. That goddess was a goddess of war, but she was also the goddess of life — and life had to be nurtured.

So, during her stay at the temple, she sometimes allowed herself to think that she was growing closer to War God. That she understood the depths of the boundless love her goddess had for all humans, and especially for War Maidens like her. Eventually, the girls she raised Awakened and left to seek their own devotion. A new generation came to replace them, and she grew to love them as well... but nothing could compare to the bond she felt to her first pupils, and she missed them dearly.

Even if they did not miss her in turn.

The world outside the temple was in turmoil. A new Supreme had recently risen from the clamor of the battlefield and carved out a small empire for himself. His conquest ended swiftly, and he led his warriors home to consolidate and stabilize his Domain.

However, not all of his subjects were satisfied by the promise of peace. Some had greater ambition... some still lusted for blood. His own son slew him and became the new ruler, attaining Supremacy through an act of defiant patricide — and once he began his own conquest, bloodshed never stopped.

His armies spread across the mortal realms like a steel plague, and no one could stop him. One kingdom fell after another, and so did the Supreme rulers of humanity. Eventually, only a few remained, and people began to whisper that the coming of the Second Kingdom was not far away — a kingdom that would unite all humans. A kingdom of blood, a kingdom of murder... a kingdom devoted to nothing but slaying steel.

That was until one of her pupils — her most cherished daughter — led an army of mercenaries to stand in his way.

The news of her death reached the temple long after she perished. The girl had defeated the insurmountable Steel Horde and caused the collapse of the tyrant's Domain. However, in the process, she broke the covenant between her and her goddess... and, as a result, she was cast into the cruelest hell.

On the day the news arrived, the priestesses in the temple were dismayed and angered. Their eyes were full of fury — a War Maiden was meant to die before breaking her oaths, after all. The black sheep of their order had brought them unspeakable shame. However, she felt no fury and no contempt. All she felt was pain and sorrow.

At night, she walked to look at the starlit sky, wondering about the girl she had lost. Had her last moments been painful? Had she suffered? Had she died all alone, surrounded by indifference and scorn?

On that night... she doubted her goddess for the first time.

Soon, she left the temple and returned to the battlefield. The world had descended into chaos after the collapse of the Steel Empire, with countless warlords fighting over its pieces. The Creatures of Corruption raised their monstrous heads and crawled out of the darkness, using the turmoil to reap a rich harvest of human souls.

Rumors were that a new avatar of War God had been born recently somewhere in the mortal realms, and many people believed that an era of bloodshed would begin to welcome the young dragon into the world.

Her life was not much different from how it had been before, when she was younger — and yet, it felt different. Before, she had wandered from one battlefield to another with a sense of purpose. Now, she was simply drifting from one war to another, unbalanced... directionless. Her power was greater than it had ever been, and yet, she felt powerless.

The ancient order of the War Maidens was slowly becoming a vestige of the past, as well. Too many of them had died, and too few were willing to give the oath — the cult of War God was shifting to the worship of a new incarnation of their deity, after all. Those who followed War wanted to submit to the Dragon and serve a living deity, not remake themselves in the image of a distant god.

By then, she had become the greatest warrior of their order, and one with the most prestige as well.

That was when Sun God approached her, beseeching her to become one of Hope's wardens.

“Among the heroes of humanity, I am neither the strongest nor the swiftest. I am not the wisest of us, either. So why me?"

The avatar of the radiant god remained silent for a long while, then answered in an inscrutable voice.

His answer was simple:

"Because you never give up."

She agreed.

And so, her fate was plucked from the great tapestry and twisted into an endless loop. Taking the remaining War Maidens and those warriors who followed her, she embarked on a journey to the shattered Kingdom of Hope.

She left the world behind.

There, she met the other Chain Lords. The noble Sevirax and his virtuous brother, the enigmatic Saint of Shadows, the aloof oracle who built a temple to the Goddess of the Black Skies in the north, the compassionate and benevolent Aidre... and the eccentric sorcerer, Noctis, as well.

For a while, they performed their duty flawlessly. Outside, the Empire of War expanded through conquest, seamlessly incorporating new lands into its fold. But there was no war in the Kingdom of Hope... there was only time.

Time flowed. People grew old and decrepit, then died. Soon, there was no one left who had known her as she had been before... the priestesses who had raised her were long gone, and her sisters from the temple were gone as well. Even the girls she had nurtured and trained disappeared in the jaws of time, only her memory of them remaining.

She missed them... but she missed the one who had broken the oath the most.

She often went to pray in front of the statue of War God. However, her prayers weren't full of devotion. At times, they were close to sacrilege instead.

"Why did you abandon her?"

"Why was she punished?"

"Didn't you love her?"

"Didn't your heart bleed while she suffered?"

“Mine does..."

She didn't understand why her goddess had been so cruel. She didn't understand how one could love someone, and yet cast their torn and bleeding soul into the depths of hell.

Until, one day, she did.

She understood that gods were different from mortals... and so was their love. So, there was no point in trying to understand it at all.

She laughed bitterly.

She grew despondent.

She allowed herself to question things that she had considered sacred.

During one of the gatherings among the seven immortals, the Beast of Twilight imbibed too much spirit wine, as he always did. The atmosphere was informal, and conversation flowed naturally.

And so, she asked.

“Why do you think the Lord of Light entrusted the keys to Hope's prison to us? Did he want us to protect them? Or did he want us to use them?"

The eccentric immortal gave her a confused, dazed look.

"What do you mean, fair maiden? He told us to never let her escape. Surely, that is what he wants."

She smiled faintly.

Perhaps she had drunk too much wine, as well.

His answer was reasonable. But was it really so simple?

She shook her head and reached for her cup.

“The gods are not like us. Never trust the gods, Noctis..."

He didn't seem to hear her, shifting his attention to Lady Aidre of the Heart God's Grove.

The Crimson Beast of Twilight did not pay much attention to their idle chatter, but she couldn't forget.

More time passed, and the world outside fell under the control of the Dragon. And she... she grew tired of her duty. She grew tired of doubt.

She grew tired of her endless life, which was senseless.

She was immortal, after all, so she did not have to struggle to stay alive. There was no war in her life anymore... but there was no peace, either. So, she was neither truly alive nor dead. Everything was meaningless, and she was just stuck in the middle, year after year, burning with a flame that could never go out.

And with each year, that simple question tormented her more and more...

Was their duty to keep Hope imprisoned, or to set her free?

What was Sun God's will, really?

She agonized about it over and over, endlessly. She searched for an answer, but was unable to find it.

Until she realized that the question itself was wrong.

The truth was...

What did she care about Sun God's will? Why was it the will of the gods that mattered?

It didn't.

The only thing that mattered was her will, as well as that of the other Chain Lords. They held the keys to Hope's prison, after all.

So the real question was not what Sun God desired. It was what she desired.

And what she desired... was to free Hope, to give Hope back to the world.

And to herself.

She wanted to be alive again. She wanted to struggle and strive again. She wanted to fight for something that was not meaningless again... to give it her all and walk forward until, one day, she fell short. Until she was defeated and lost her life. She wanted to die.

But fulfilling her desire was not easy.

There were seven Chain Lords, after all, and each of them was both immensely powerful and immortal. She only had one of the seven knives, so she couldn't set Hope free herself — and the others would never agree to betray the order of Sun God.

One day, she was resting in the inner sanctum of the Chalice Temple. In front of her was a stone table, and on its surface stood seven dominoes. She studied them intently, as she did every day for a long, long time.

Finally, she raised a hand and pushed one of the dominoes, watching the rest fall.

A sad smile illuminated her breathtaking, enchantingly radiant face.

The next day, she abandoned her oath and betrayed the War Maidens — she committed a sin that could not be forgiven. Naturally, the other priestesses were not inclined to forgive her. She fought them all — those who were Transcendent or Ascended — killing some and crippling others.

Then, she took her soldiers and left to settle in the west.

Soon after that, she came to push her first domino.

She killed Aidre and burned the sacred grove of Heart God, retrieving the wooden knife that carried her fate.

The other Chain Lords protested, and Noctis came to destroy her.

His wrath shook the heavens, but without the wooden knife, there was little he could do. In the end, seething with hatred, he retreated. The other immortals had no choice but to accept her cruel act, as well. They continued to carry out their duty as Hope's shackles.

But it was already too late.

Because now, there was a crack in the walls of Hope's cage. And through that crack, her influence slowly seeped into the ruins of her once-resplendent kingdom.

Hope slowly drove them all mad.

The noble Sevirax became a horrid, man-devouring monster. His valiant brother became a demented wraith locked inside a molten tomb. The One in the North grew increasingly detached and indifferent, caring not to be alive. The Saint of Shadows stole his fate and killed himself, departing for the Shadow Realm. The Child of the Moon became decadent and unbridled, increasingly manic.

All of them had fallen.

She had fallen, as well.

The descendants of her once-noble warriors degenerated into insane, blood-addled butchers. The pristine Theater of Hope turned into a ghastly sacrificial altar to a misguided facsimile of War. Everything that had been sacred was desecrated, and everything that had been good became foul.

And she... she had gone mad.

At times, she struggled to remember her reasons. Her thoughts twisted, and she became cruel and uncaring. She might have changed her mind a few times...

But it was already too late.

Because once the first domino fell, the rest could not be stopped.

She waited, and waited, and waited...

For someone to win the wooden knife and drive it into her heart.

Countless years passed.

Until, finally, the time arrived for the last domino to topple.

The one who ended it all was Noctis, the Crimson Beast of Twilight. He killed the Sun Prince... he killed the Ivory Lord, Sevirax, as well.

And he defeated her.

Now, finally! Finally! After all these years, after all this torment...

It was her turn to die.

However, fate was not that kind.

And the Beast of Twilight was not that kind, either.

Just when the glorious promise of death was right in front of her, he refused her its embrace.

He chose to sentence her to eternal agony instead.

Trapped in the ruins of a beautiful vessel, her body consumed by a profane vine, she experienced unimaginable pain, indescribable agony. The intolerable bitterness of having no choice but to live, live, live...

Live forever.

Until she outlived everyone... even her beloved goddess. Until she was left utterly, unfathomably alone.

There was only one thing left for her — an eternal, everlasting struggle.

An endless war against the seeds of Corruption that kept blooming in her torn and bleeding soul.

And so, she fought. She endured. She persevered.

Until the entire world was consumed by a hideous tide of nightmares, turning into the cruelest of hells. Until thousands upon thousands of years passed...

Everything was consumed by Corruption. But she wasn't. She alone remained pure.

Because even if there was no hope in the world anymore...

She never gave up.

--- Chapter 3214 ---

Shadow surfaced from the deep pool of memories, feeling a peculiar melancholy. He was not someone to be consumed by emotion, but at the moment, there was a dull ache in his chest. Everything he saw made him feel mournful.

The beauty of the Kingdom of Hope, the majesty of the great theater... and young Noctis.

It was hard to imagine that all these things were fated to become a desolate ruin. The kingdom of Hope would become a shattered land of bloodshed and madness, her pristine white theater would become a ghastly slaughterhouse, and Noctis... Noctis would become one of the chains that bound the Demon of Desire.

Until he was bound and driven mad by eternity, choosing to break her chains. Shadow lowered his gaze.

‘Knowledge... is indeed the heaviest thing in the world.'

A quiet sigh escaped from his lips.

Noctis and Snuggle, meanwhile, were still discussing the play. However, their conversations slowly shifted to the deity who had built it.

"Do you think we will meet her? The Demon of Desire?"

Snuggle scoffed.

"Do you think a goddess is so easy to meet? She is not your grandma, you know! Why would she deign to grace us with her presence?"

Noctis pointed to Shadow.

"Isn't he a Supreme Titan? Do you think a goddess wouldn't know that someone like him entered her kingdom, or that his presence was important enough to go take a look?"

He turned his head.

"Tell her, Shadow! I bet we will be invited to dine at her palace."

Shadow shrugged lightly.

"Well, I don't know. I doubt it."

He lingered for a moment, then added:

"Also, Hope doesn't have a palace. She has a tower."

Noctis grinned.

"Same thing!"

The young man seemed excited at the prospect of meeting one of the mythical daemons — despite the fact that people generally feared them, usually far more than the gods. Shadow, however, was not too keen on meeting any deities.

The prospect of meeting Shadow God alone filled him with trepidation.

He wasn't even sure what he was afraid of. Was it being destroyed and sent back into the ocean of endless lives?

Or having his hopes crushed?

He didn't know.

Soon, they returned to the city and found an acceptable inn. The sun was already rolling toward the horizon by then, and night was approaching. Tomorrow, they were going to continue their journey — but tonight, they could simply rest and enjoy each other's company.

The conversation was not flowing, though. Perhaps it was because they knew that there were not a lot of nights like this one left for them, now that they had reached the Kingdom of Hope.

Eventually, Noctis sighed.

“So, what is our plan?"

Shadow remained silent for a short while.

"There shouldn't be many problems in a kingdom ruled by a daemon. There will be no Creatures of Corruption to stand in our way, no warring heroes, and no rampaging Spirits to hinder us — no problem that you'll insist that we solve before leaving. So, we can simply head directly north and find a place to cross to the Hollow Mountains."

Noctis looked at him with a concerned expression.

He did not have to say anything for Shadow to understand what he felt.

Years ago, Noctis had agreed to be their guide on the way to the Hollow Mountains. He had entertained an ambition to follow them into the Shadow Realm, as well... but, in truth, that was no place for the young Transcendent.

In fact, even the Hollow Mountains themselves were far more than what he could handle. Shadow was not even sure that Snuggle could endure the boundless expanse of nothingness, albeit he was inclined to believe that she could.

Noctis, however... was too young, too untested. As a hero of a divine bloodline, he had achieved Transcendence quite easily — and precisely because he had not struggled enough yet, his claim to existence was tenuous. He didn't even know himself yet, so could he sustain his sense of self in the chilling white mist of the Hollow Mountains?

Unlikely.

That meant that once they reached the Hollow Mountains, they would part ways. Noctis would stay behind, free to live his life as he wanted and continue pursuing excitement and glory. Shadow and Snuggle would continue forward, searching for a way to enter the Underworld.

Needless to say, the young man was disheartened.

Shadow could not say that they had gotten particularly close, but they were not strangers by now, either. As for Noctis and Snuggle — despite their constant bickering, they had long become dear friends. More than that, they were comrades, having fought against countless Creatures of Corruption side by side.

Snuggle sighed.

“Hey, why the long face? It's not like we'll never see each other again."

She giggled.

"After all, Shadow and I are merely going to the Shadow Realm. What's so scary about visiting the Realm of Death? We'll just stay for a bit and come back."

Noctis looked at her in dismay.

"What kind of preposterous..."

Then, however, he fell silent and stared at her for a few moments.

A faint smile appeared on his face.

"Then again, knowing you, maybe that is exactly what is going to happen."

With a chuckle, Noctis leaned back and studied the strange pair — the man with onyx eyes who wasn't human at all, and a little doll wearing an exquisitely sewn black dress who actually harbored a human soul. He waved to the waiter.

“Good man! More wine. Tonight is a special night, so bring us your best."

Noctis sighed.

“Back when I ran away from the temple... I mean, solemnly departed the temple to bring honor to my name... who knew that I would end up this way?"

He shook his head.

“I went to that mythical realm of yours to slay a powerful Creature of Corruption, but ended up becoming an errand boy for a taciturn Supreme Titan. Strangely enough, though, as an errand boy... I fought and killed more terrifying abominations than any other Transcendent did in these past few years, each of them more terrifying than the previous one. And since the two of you do not like attention, everyone seems to believe that it was the Crimson Beast of Twilight alone who caused all that chaos."

Noctis chuckled.

"Look! It's Noctis, the hero who defeated the Rat. By the gods! It's the Beast of Twilight, who beheaded the Great Demon of the Thousand Steps! Oh my, isn't that Noctis, who obliterated the Devouring Tyrant and its myriad of abominable minions? He's the one who killed the Red Skull Centipede! Who dueled the Transcendent Prince to a stalemate! Who destroyed the Hidden Stronghold and cut down the Bandit King!"

His expression lacked amusement, but there was a smile on his lips.

Snuggle frowned.

“What are you complaining about? Isn't that what you wanted? To earn a name for yourself and have minstrels sing songs about your astonishing deeds?"

Noctis hesitated, then shrugged.

"True, that is what I wanted. I was impatient to prove myself, to let the world know who I am... ah, but somewhere along the way, I seem to have lost that desire."

His smile disappeared slowly.

“I am not that same youth anymore, after all. We've been to so many places and seen so many things. The ghastly piles of corpses left in the wake of that Sacred Rat's plague; the gaunt faces of starving children who could not get any food because that damn Great Demon ruined the fields and killed all the merchants. The pitiful ruins of the city devoured by the minions of that Corrupted Tyrant, with no flesh left on the bones of its murdered inhabitants. The monstrous arrogance of Transcendent rulers and those who harbored ambition to rule in their place... and so much more."

Noctis looked at Shadow and Snuggle silently for a while, then shook his head.

“Nobody sings about that side of legends. For every name that is known, there is a myriad that disappears forever from the pages of history. So... no, I don't really care about being renowned and famous anymore. I just want to slay Creatures of Corruption and make the lives of all humans a little better. And that is why..."

He sighed.

“That is why even if you were willing to take me with you on a legendary journey to the Shadow Realm, I would have refused.”

Noctis smiled sadly.

"There are no humans in the Underworld, after all. There's none in the Shadow Realm, either. So, there is nothing for me to do there. My duty — the duty of an Awakened champion — lies here, in the mortal realms."

Finally, the waiter brought the wine to their table. Noctis poured it into three cups and picked up one of them.

"It just saddens me that we won't be together anymore. Not because I was able to ride on Shadow's shoulders to fame and glory, but because... we are friends."

He laughed.

"You were good friends to me, Snuggle and Shadow. I don't think I'll ever meet friends as good as you. So, thank you."

With that, he brought his hands together and gave them a bow. Then, he raised his cup and emptied it in one go.

Shadow hesitated for a moment, then picked up his cup as well.

He smiled faintly.

“There is no need to thank us. Just... make sure that you are a good friend to someone in the future, as well."

With that, he drank his wine.

The wine was sweet, and yet it left a bitter aftertaste on his tongue.

Snuggle grasped her cup with both hands and strained a little to raise it a few centimeters above the table.

She remained silent for a moment, her expression solemn.

Then, she glared at Noctis and said with a deep scowl.

“What am I supposed to do with this, you fool? I don't have a mouth! I can't drink wine!"

Noctis laughed.

Shadow chuckled, as well.

They spent a few more hours chatting and laughing, remembering all the adventures they had experienced during their journey.

That night, when Noctis was already asleep and Snuggle was resting quietly, Shadow sensed something and looked out of the window.

Then, taking a step, he traveled dozens of miles and appeared in front of an old statue depicting the Goddess of War — her primal avatar, who held a spear in one hand and a bleeding human heart in the other.

There was a vague figure standing beneath the statue, wearing a pristine white dress. In the darkness of the night, it was difficult to make out her features... or perhaps her face was simply woven out of night, too sacred and miraculous to be witnessed by mortal eyes.

Shadow hesitated for a moment, then bowed slightly.

“This humble shadow greets Hope, the Demon of Desire... daughter of the Forgotten God."

--- Chapter 3215 ---

Shadow remained motionless, studying the Demon of Desire with a sense of trepidation.

Most of his senses were useless, as if Hope wasn't there at all. That was because she was suppressing her presence, sparing the world the unfathomable burden of her resplendent divinity — she was known to be a patron of humans, after all. If Hope did not hide her true splendor, merely being near her would have crushed mundane souls. So, Shadow could only see her.

Even then, her figure was nebulous. All he saw was an elegant white dress outlining the shape of a graceful figure, and yet somehow, it felt as if there was nothing beneath the soft fabric at all.

It felt as if the white fabric hid a cosmic infinity, a vast abyss woven out of purest darkness, purest light, and then shaped carelessly to resemble a human.

He shivered, overwhelmed by her breathtaking radiance.

He shuddered, overcome by an alien sense of revulsion.

He felt compelled to fall to his knees in blind worship. He felt his heart drowning in terror, barely suppressing an impulse to flee.

Every emotion, every desire, every passion he had known and tried to forget suddenly ignited with an insurmountable intensity, setting his lightless soul aflame.

Shadow gritted his teeth and suppressed these frenzied flames, pacifying his soul. Just as he did, a voice that sounded like the wind that blew between distant stars and the sound of myriad prayers resounded in the still darkness of the night.

That voice was the most radiant sound he had ever heard, but also the most harrowing.

"You shouldn't exist."

Shadow trembled.

Hope simply shared her thought, but even if she did not put any intent into her words, the world shifted slightly, reshaping itself to fit them. He felt his existence growing a little more vague than it had been before, and had to call upon his Will to solidify it. Only then did Shadow have a chance to consider Hope's words.

‘I.. shouldn't exist?'

It seemed he and the Demon of Desire shared the same thought. Shadow was tired of his endless existence, after all.

Still...

What exactly did she mean by that?

"Why should I not exist?"

Hope stood beneath the statue of War God. The statue was illuminated by starlight, while Hope's silhouette was drowning in darkness.

Her nebulous voice resounded again, making the Shadow shiver.

“Because you are not allowed to exist."

Taking a step forward, she seemed to study him for a moment.

Then, an ethereal chuckle echoed in the wind.

“And you do not wish to exist, either."

Her words sounded certain, but carried a subtle hint of a question.

Shadow frowned, feeling lost. When he sensed the ethereal but irresistible call, he knew that the Demon of Desire had summoned him. But now that he faced her, it was difficult to understand why.

Perhaps it was idle curiosity, no more.

As he considered what to say, Hope turned slightly, looking north.

“The Shadow Realm... that is what you desire?"

Shadow flinched, feeling like his soul was laid bare in front of her. He hesitated for a moment, then bowed.

“Yes, indeed. That is why I entered your kingdom, my lady. I am merely a traveler passing through."

Hope remained motionless, her face still hidden from view. Yet, Shadow felt as if he glimpsed a subtle smile woven out of starlight, glinting in the strange darkness that his sight could not pierce.

“Little shadow, you seem to have forgotten who you are. Do you not wish to remember? If so, I will respect your desire."

Suddenly, she was standing just a step away from Shadow, peering into the depths of his being. He felt impossibly small under her gaze... but strangely enough, her attention was not overbearing and crushing. Instead, it was gentle and soothing as a cool spring.

"But are you sure that you want to face a god? Gods are the reason you are not meant to exist, after all.”

Shadow trembled, but forced himself to remain still. He did not really understand what the Demon of Desire meant... but it seemed that she meant him no harm, at least.

As for her question...

Shadow’s lips slowly twisted into a crooked smile.

“And yet they are the reason I do exist. So, I think gods owe me an explanation."

A gust of wind blew across the world, and the tip of War God's spear seemed to glisten in the starlight. Hope's laughter resounded in the darkness, pleasing like the murmur of a clear brook.

"If so, I will not stop you. Go, little shadow... you have my blessing. May it help your wishes come true."

As those words settled in the silence of the night, Shadow felt the world shifting once again, obeying the radiant daemon. Hope's curiosity seemed to be sated. Sparing him one last glance, she turned, as if wanting to leave.

"Wait!"

Shadow himself was surprised by his impulsive call. He froze, startled by the sound of his own voice, as well as by the indescribable longing that awoke in his soul when I saw her leave.

Hope did linger for a moment.

He struggled to contain himself for a moment, then asked in a tense, trembling voice:

"Why... why are you here? Why do you live among humans? Why did you build a kingdom for them, and why do you protect them from the harshness of the world?"

He did not understand. He could not understand. Even if Shadow was not a god, he had experienced what being worshipped like a god felt like. How deeply it hurt, how inescapable the pain of knowing humans was.

How distasteful human natures were. Whatever he had experienced, Hope would have experienced a thousandfold.

So why would she subject herself to this hideousness, to this torment?

Hope hesitated for a brief moment, then answered in her nebulous, spellbinding voice:

"Because I am lonely."

Turning to Shadow, she laughed quietly.

“All of us are. Isn't that why you are here? Mirage has her illusions; Rime has her flowers. Ariel has his queen, while Nether has his goddess. But I only have humans. I love humans, because they are children of the Flame... and therefore, my children as well."

Shadow shook his head in dismay.

Usually, his emotions would not have been so unbridled — but in the presence of Hope, it was impossible to be insincere.

So, he could not stop himself from objecting.

"But they are so fleeting. As soon as you allow them into your heart, they are gone, leaving you bleeding. How do you save yourself from having to suffer?"

Hope remained motionless.

Her answer was gentle, as if she was explaining something obvious to a naive child.

"I simply suffer."

She seemed to smile.

“Why would I save myself from sorrow? When I am happy, I savor joy. When I am heartbroken, I savor sorrow. One cannot exist without the other, so only those who know sorrow can experience joy. Little shadow... do you wish to live in a world devoid of happiness?"

Shadow hesitated, then shook his head slowly.

Hope nodded.

“Then do not save yourself from sorrow."

He gritted his teeth, raising his chin in defiance.

“Then what about fury? Human hearts are so hideous, so vile. The crimes they commit are abhorrent; and what is worse, they will commit them in your name. They will desecrate everything that is holy and spoil everything that is pure... there is no end to their ambition, their lust, their greed! When you see all the dirty, dark desires that hide in their hearts, don't you want to erase them from existence and be spared their depravity?"

The Demon of Desire gazed at him with an emotion that resembled pity.

"Your two friends, the young wolf pup and the lost soul... are they hideous? Are they vile? Do you feel fury when you are with them, and do you want to erase them from existence?"

Shadow hesitated, then slowly shook his head.

Hope seemed to smile.

“Humans and gods... all of us are creatures of Desire. Some desires are noble, some are banal, some are twisted and vile. Such is the world. Humans are no different from gods, and gods are no different from humans. If I were to be furious with humans, shouldn't I feel the same fury toward the gods?"

She shook her head slightly.

“Above all of it, there is choice. Some make the choice to be vile, while some make the choice to be noble. That is what separates us, beings of the Flame — of Desire — from those who have become Corrupted. Because Corruption is the thief of choice."

As the stars glistened in the distant sky, Hope shifted, enjoying the warm breeze.

“But not all beings of the Flame are afforded the privilege of making choices, or even knowing that there is a choice. So, all I want to do is help humans learn what they are choosing and help them be in a position to choose. Then, most of them will make the most radiant choices..."

As the warm breeze reached Shadow, she seemed to smile.

"...That is my hope."

Shadow stared at her, motionless.

Wasn't she saying that she could tolerate the darker side of humanity... for no other reason than that she desired them to choose light?

Because she simply wanted to?

What kind of answer was that?!

Shadow gritted his teeth and then uttered:

“But those humans! Even if gods can endure living in their company, can they endure living alongside gods? Can they survive in the shadow of divinity, doomed to always be lesser, to know that all the things they desire and can never possess belong to someone else?"

Hope studied him silently for a long while. Eventually, she turned to leave.

"Then what about us, little shadow? You and I... don't we exist in the shadow of divinity, knowing that all the things we desire belong to someone else?"

As her nebulous figure disappeared like a fleeting dream, the last echo of her voice caressed his ear like a soothing whisper:

“Don't we daemons live alongside the gods? If we can, why can't humans?"

A moment later, it was as if she had never been in front of him at all.

Shadow was left alone, standing beneath the statue of War God.

Looking at the bleeding human heart she held in her hand.

He remained silent for a long while, staring at the sharp spear held in the statue's other hand.

Eventually, he asked quietly:

"Can we?"

--- Chapter 3216 ---

In the morning, Snuggle and Noctis woke up as if nothing had happened. Listening to their bickering, Shadow did not show that he had conversed with a deity while they slept, either.

He was generally quiet and reserved, so they did not notice his inner turmoil... Noctis did not, at least. Snuggle might have sensed something, but tactfully chose to play along with his silence.

A myriad of thoughts swarmed in Shadow's head.

Had he met a god before?

Across his countless lives, he must have. Yet at the moment, he did not remember — perhaps he had not, after all. The only image in his mind was the harrowing scene of Beast God devouring a Void Creature.

He had been far, far away from that titanic clash, though. Both of those beings were simply so colossal that they could be seen from a vast distance. If Shadow had been any closer, he would have been obliterated by the violent horror of the divine confrontation.

The daemons were not equal to the great gods, but by now, they were Divine. So, for Shadow, meeting Hope was no different from facing true divinity for the first time. Needless to say, she had not disappointed his expectations.

Even if Hope had been suppressing her deific presence to the point that it was all but impossible to sense her existence, her visage had still left a profound impression on Shadow. He could not even describe the feeling she had invoked in him... it was simply too compelling, too poignant. Unknowable.

And he was a vast being on the precipice of becoming a deity himself, at that. Shadow could not even imagine the awe those lesser than him would feel in her presence. Perhaps that was why she concealed it and obscured her visage — because she wanted those whom she met to feel emotions other than awe. To look past her divinity and see her instead.

Unlike Shadow, who hid because he didn't want to be seen.

Beyond the shock of witnessing the Demon of Desire, though, were the words that she had spoken.

Shadow was surprised to learn that Hope was such an... optimist.

Perhaps there was a seed of profound wisdom in what she had told him, but he felt reluctant to accept it. That was because Hope did not know the future — but he did. She had told him that if daemons could live alongside the gods, then humans could too. And yet, all of existence was doomed to be destroyed in a war between the gods and the daemons.

Didn't that make Hope's conviction misguided and naive?

As Shadow and his companions departed from the inn and left the city, Shadow contemplated deeply.

‘No... perhaps not.'

Hope did not strike Shadow as someone who could be naive, let alone misguided. So perhaps what she meant was not that the daemons and the gods were coexisting splendidly, so humans could too. Because they were all the same. Because they were all children of the Flame.

Perhaps what she truly meant had to do with everything she had said before.

Perhaps it was that daemons had a choice, just like humans... just like the gods.

And that she hoped they would choose wisely.

...However, in the end, her hope was destined to be crushed.

It was destined to be crushed by Nether, the Demon of Choice.

Who chose war.

As Shadow was jostled lightly on the coachman's bench, he sighed.

‘Well. It's not like that has anything to do with me.'

Shadow seemed like a vast and unfathomable being to someone like Noctis or Snuggle. But to beings like Hope or the great gods, he was no more than a little, transient shadow.

Gods were great, but Shadow was small. He had no business concerning himself with the fate of the gods and the choices of daemons. All he wanted to do was keep a promise he should have given a dear friend, but never had — and then, perhaps, find a way to end his tedious existence.

‘It is quite ironic, isn't it?'

The Demon of Desire, who called herself Hope, was destined to have her hopes crushed.

And Shadow, a creature of death, wanted to die but did not know how.

‘We really are quite a pair.'

Perhaps that was why he had sensed a hint of affection in the way Hope spoke to him.

“What are you thinking about, Shadow?"

Snuggle's squeaky voice pulled him out of his contemplation.

Pulling slightly on the reins of their horse, Shadow smiled faintly and shook his head.

"I was wondering if the Demon of Desire likes me."

Both Noctis and Snuggle stared at him, their mouths agape — one of their mouths, at least.

In the end, Noctis exhaled slowly and gave him a thumbs up.

His hand seemed to be trembling.

"Please forgive me, Brother Shadow. I did not know that you are a man of great ambition. This junior still has a lot to learn... I've never even dared to think about aiming that high..."

Snuggle seemed to have regained her composure, as well. She looked at him tearfully.

“Our Shadow is all grown up! He likes girls now... well, primordial deities, at least..."

Shadow sighed.

“You two are fools."

Snuggle giggled, while Noctis exploded with laughter.

"That we are, that we are..."

Their journey north was uneventful.

There were no powerful Creatures of Corruption in the Kingdom of Hope. There were no Transcendent warriors searching for trouble or rampaging Spirits, either. The roads were well-maintained, and the weather was gentle. Their carriage rolled forward at a steady pace, devouring mile after mile.

Without having to hurry, they reached the northernmost edges of the Kingdom of Hope in a few weeks. Those weeks were blissful and carefree, full of nothing but leisure — none of them spoke about the inevitable parting, which was drawing near. In the end, however, that day still arrived. The carriage stopped near a vast meadow, a modest mountain chain looming far in the distance. A warm breeze blew across the meadow, making the grass ripple like the waves of an emerald sea. The sun was shining high in the sky, and there was no cloud in sight to obscure it.

It was only when they alighted from the carriage and gazed at the horizon that Noctis finally lost his smile, looking ahead with a dejected expression.

Snuggle remained silent for a while, then tentatively pulled on the hem of his colorful robe.

“I meant it. There is no need to feel sad. We will definitely meet again, someday."

Noctis stared into the distance, his face solemn.

Eventually, he shook his head.

“No, it's not that. I just... realized something only now. When it's already too late."

Shadow and Snuggle looked at him quietly, giving the young man time to speak.

After a while, Noctis let out a long sigh.

“I realized that once Shadow leaves..."

His face hardened.

"This damn horse will disappear. So I'll have to either abandon this wonderful carriage or pull it myself. By the Moon! What a travesty!"

As he looked at the luxurious carriage, his expression turned mournful.

His lips even quivered a little.

Shadow stared at him for a bit, then patted him on the shoulder.

"Stay strong.”

Snuggle nodded seriously.

“Our thoughts will be with you. You can endure!"

Noctis looked down, hiding a smile.

When he looked up, however, there were traces of genuine sadness in his eyes.

“What are you doing? Go. We have already said everything that needed to be said... trying to pull off an emotional farewell will only be awkward. It's been a pleasure traveling with you, friends. But there are countless other pleasures to be enjoyed in the world, and I am off to enjoy them all by myself. If anything, you are the one who should wallow in sadness and envy."

Shadow smiled faintly.

"Perhaps we will."

Then, he looked back at the radiant vista of the Kingdom of Hope.

"So, what are your plans? Are you going to stay here for a while and explore Hope's domain?"

Noctis shook his head slowly.

"No. You saw it yourself — there are no dreadful abominations or bloodthirsty villains in the Kingdom of Hope. I am not needed here. So, I'll go someplace where a fool like me can be of use."

He sighed, then beamed them a smile.

"I'll go be a hero... no different from all the other Transcendent heroes, but far more handsome and with better style. Be prepared! You may hear about my incredible deeds and astonishing looks even in the Shadow Realm."

He hesitated for a moment.

“But what about you? Are you sure that you want to continue forward? The Hollow Mountains, the Underworld, and the Realm of Death itself... as far as itineraries go, that one sounds like a real drag. You might want to consider a better pastime."

Shadow chuckled.

“We'll be fine. I've been to all those places before, I think... a long time ago. We'll manage."

Noctis studied him for a long while, then nodded.

"In that case, go. I wish you luck on your journey. And now that I think about it..."

He fell silent for a brief moment, then nodded decisively.

"I think I'll drag that carriage to the nearest settlement, after all. Surely, I'll be able to buy a horse there! Luxurious coaches like this one don't just grow on trees, you know."

Shadow smiled.

“It depends on the tree, I guess."

As he turned to face the distant mountains, Snuggle climbed to Noctis's shoulder and hugged him tightly. She whispered something into his ear, causing him to laugh, then jumped down and scampered over to Shadow.

Picking her up, he prepared to cross the realm boundary and enter the Hollow Mountains.

The last leg of their journey awaited ahead. Just before the pull of a different realm grasped him, Shadow turned his head and looked at the young man who stood behind them.

"Noctis..."

Shadow lingered for a moment, struggling with something, and then finally said:

"Do not let yourself be bound, Noctis. Wolves... are meant to be free."

In the next moment, the warmth of the Kingdom of Hope disappeared, replaced by a chilling cold.

The radiant vista of the emerald meadow was gone, as well.

Instead, Shadow and Snuggle were surrounded by swirling white fog, unable to see anything.

As if nothing existed in the world anymore, except for the two of them — and the endless expanse of swirling mist.

--- Chapter 3217 ---

Shadow walked through the white mist, feeling his self being slowly eroded and erased.

Nothingness was truly fearsome. All beings were equal in front of it — the gods, the people... even the terrifying creatures of the Void. Shadow did not know for sure, but he suspected that even the Flame itself was not immune to the subtle, insidious tides of nothingness.

He knew only one force that was indifferent to nothing...

It was fate.

Fate cared not for the white mist, just as it did not care to be burned by the Flame or tainted by the Void. So, Shadow assumed that beings with a strong fate were better suited to endure the eroding influence of the white mist.

There weren't many beings like that, though. Those who did exist all possessed a True Name, which was both an expression of their fate and a unique descriptor that distinguished them as individuals in its great tapestry.

There were myriad swords in the world, after all, but only one Excalibur. Excalibur was a sword, but not all swords were Excalibur. That was both the reason and the consequence of that singular sword's uniqueness.

‘Actually, there might have been two Excaliburs.'

Even assaulted by the mist, Shadow smiled faintly.

In any case, the mist eroded one's very existence, and to repel it, they had to tether themselves to reality — or rather, to fate. The easiest way to do so would be to concentrate on their True Name, which already served as an anchor of one's self.

The stupidest thing one could do was enter the white mist without a True Name and with only a tenuous connection to fate. Shadow did not know if such fools truly existed, but if they did, he struggled to imagine the sheer magnitude of their stupidity.

As for Shadow himself...

Did he possess a True Name?

He wasn't sure. He did, most likely, but did not care to remember. What complicated the matter even more was that he remembered myriad lives, and in many of those lives, he had been someone with a True Name. From that perspective, he had numerous True Names... but were those names truly his?

Shadow did not know.

Therefore, he had expected to suffer quite a lot in the white mist.

But, to his surprise, he was faring quite well. Nothingness had some effect on him, but it was minimal — not nearly enough to deal serious damage to his existence in a short span of time.

Perhaps it was because he carried the memories of myriad lives, and was therefore tethered to reality by myriad connections. Perhaps it was simply because his being was too vast, and erasing it from existence was no easy task.

But, most likely... it was because his fate was quite strong. His connection to fate had to be truly exceptional to explain why the white mist seemed so powerless to destroy him, though.

Shadow frowned, disturbed by that possibility.

It was still a relief to know that he did not have to worry about himself too much.

However, Shadow was concerned about Snuggle.

At the moment, she was hiding in his pocket, and he was covering the pocket with a hand in a protective gesture. Despite that, the radiant soul hidden in the little doll was being assaulted by the power of nothingness, too.

Snuggle was resisting the white mist surprisingly well.

Even if she had never shared her True Name with Shadow, she surely possessed one. Her sense of self seemed to be crystal-clear and as strong as a glistening diamond. Most of all, her desire to exist and attachment to the world were like a blazing flame that burned with daunting intensity.

Snuggle was unwilling to disappear, so she clung to existence with a desperate determination.

As Shadow observed, he could even sense Snuggle use her Will clumsily to reinforce her connection to reality. She was unable to sense the Will or consciously manipulate it, so it was merely an instinctual response... still, few Transcendents would have been able to achieve the same result.

All living beings possessed the Will, and all living beings used it to some degree before becoming Supreme. However, only Supremes were able to perceive the Will and wield it with intent. It wasn't that strange that Snuggle could subconsciously rally a few wisps of her Will as a Transcendent, and it wouldn't have mattered too much if not for the peculiar nature of that Will.

Her Will was not especially tyrannical or potent, but it was exceptionally pure. Infused with a firm determination to stay alive, it protected her from the eroding influence of nothingness quite well.

It was enough for Shadow not to worry about her in the short term, at least. Still, he had to hurry if he didn't want to lose his little companion, so Shadow hurried his steps.

"Shadow..."

Snuggle's squeaky voice was weak and trembling.

“This place is terrible."

He smiled faintly.

If she was in the mood to complain, things weren't too bad yet.

“Naturally. Of all the terrible places, this might just be the worst."

After a few moments of silence, Snuggle mumbled quietly:

"I am glad Noctis did not come..."

She did not speak for a while after that, then asked in a curious tone.

"What is the second-worst place you've been to?"

Shadow's smile widened a little.

"Well. It is probably where we are heading next — the Underworld.”

Snuggle groaned in dismay.

Shadow stopped for a moment, looking around with a wary expression, then made a turn and continued walking through the swirling fog.

A short while later, he asked:

“What about you? What's the second-worst place you have visited?"

Snuggle sighed.

"Easy answer..."

She trembled in his pocket, as if overcome by dread, then said gravely:

"Middle school."

Shadow chuckled.

The sound of his quiet laughter was suffocated by the mist, disappearing as if it had never existed.

"Really? What kind of terrifying realm is that?"

He continued chatting with her, using his voice and their conversation to anchor her in reality a little more.

At the same time, though, Shadow was concentrating on his senses.

It wasn't easy to find his way in the sea of nothingness, and it was even harder still to avoid things that hid in the white mist. The Hollow Mountains were home to few Creatures of Corruption, but every Nightmare Creature that could endure living in the white mist was bound to be terrifyingly powerful.

The Creatures of Corruption were not the true peril hiding in this eerie land, though. It was the beings born from the mist that Shadow was truly wary of.

He wasn't the Demon of Imagination, after all, so he had no way of dealing with them. All he could do if they ever encountered one was turn around and run — but even then, running from a Creature of Nothingness was an act of acknowledging its existence. And acknowledging those things was no different from making them stronger.

It was quite a pity, therefore, that all of Shadow's senses were useless here in the Hollow Mountains. Surrounded by nothing, he couldn't sense anything.

None of his five senses were of much use, and his shadow sense stayed quiet as well. So, all he could follow was his intuition. Luckily, his intuition was abnormally potent.

As Shadow explored it, he came to the conclusion that what he assumed to be intuition was, in fact, an innate ability to sense the minuscule vibrations of the Strings of Fate.

He had known about his affinity to fate, but he had never been forced to face it.

Here in the Hollow Mountains, all of his other senses were cut off. More than that, only now that he had lost it, Shadow realized how deep his connection to the world ran.

All those myriad years spent in a state of fusion with the lands surrounding his cave had left a mark on him. Now, wherever Shadow went, his vast being was deeply connected to the world around him, brushing against the fabric of universal laws governing it.

Since it had become natural for him, he had never been consciously aware of that connection. But now that the white mist replaced the world and the connection was cut, he realized its absence.

People were not usually aware of their breathing, after all. It was only when they consciously decided to concentrate on it or when their air supply disappeared that they realized the fact that their lungs had been contracting and expanding all along.

‘Curious.'

Now that Shadow felt disconnected from the world, he was only connected to one thing — fate.

Fate loomed above him like a gargantuan monster, unfathomable and endless in its eldritch immensity.

Shadow was daunted by its scale, but also confused as to why he was able to sense fate so easily.

Despite his confusion, he did not mind using that inexplicable connection to his advantage.

Following his intuition, Shadow traveled deeper into the Hollow Mountains, eventually reaching a deep gorge between two towering, jagged peaks.

The gorge had appeared when one of Beast God's harrowing fangs tore the molten fabric of the world, so it was frighteningly deep.

Shivering slightly at the memory of how the Hollow Mountains had been born, Shadow summoned a pair of raven-black wings and glided to the bottom of the gorge.

There, a deep fissure ran through the weathered rock, nestling with impenetrable darkness.

"W—what's that?"

Snuggle's voice sounded a little timid.

Shadow sighed.

"This is where the Void Creature's blood flowed into the depths of the world, a long time ago."

It was an entrance into the Underworld.

Now, all Shadow had to do was take a step forward and plunge into the darkness.

--- Chapter 3218 ---

The Underworld and its eternal darkness were terrifying... but they were not nearly as terrifying as the endless expanse of white mist above the mountains.

And yet, Shadow disliked the Underworld much more.

The white mist robbed him of his senses and quietly eroded the very foundations of his existence. True darkness merely robbed him of his senses, so in theory, Shadow should have felt better once he and Snuggle escaped the white mist and dove into the depths of the Underworld. But in practice, it was quite the opposite.

Shadow felt deeply uncomfortable.

Maybe it was because the mist was a natural force — a literal manifestation of absolute absence — while true darkness felt... alive. Not only did it feel like a living being, but like a being that was a natural predator of shadows.

Shadow felt like he marched into the belly of a hungry beast of his own volition.

"What... is up... with this creepy place?"

Snuggle's squeaky voice broke the silence, and a moment later, her small figure ignited with a brilliant radiance, chasing away the darkness.

Even if her light only illuminated a small area — far smaller than it usually did — Shadow immediately felt a little better.

He lingered for a moment, then glanced at a radiant doll who stood on his shoulder.

"This is the Underworld, where elemental darkness dwells. Most people have never encountered it, so they mistake shadows, which are the absence of light, for true darkness. However, true darkness is not an absence — it is a presence. It is an element opposite to light, and therefore an enemy of shadows."

Snuggle scratched her head.

"Ah, I remember. It was born from the blood of a Void Being. No wonder it's so creepy."

She hesitated for a moment before asking:

“So, what kind of dangers can we expect to meet in the Underworld?"

Shadow had to consider his response for some time.

Indeed, what kind of creatures populated the Underworld in this era?

The Stone Saints would only be created many centuries later, so there was no civilization in the Underworld at the moment. Nether might have explored this dark realm already, but had he claimed it as his own?

Shadow was not sure. He couldn't quite remember when the Demon of Destiny was supposed to have a falling out with Storm God, go to war with her realm, and then retreat into the Underworld to sulk in solitude. Even if their spat had already happened, the Underworld was vast. Chances were, they would not encounter Nether.

That only left the original inhabitants of the Realm of Darkness.

He sighed.

“There are probably some Creatures of Corruption hiding in the darkness. There are probably Creatures of Darkness here, as well. The former are quite dangerous, while the latter... are not necessarily hostile, but will undoubtedly try to kill the two of us in particular."

Snuggle turned to him in dismay.

“What? Why us in particular?"

Shadow gave her a sideways glance.

"You're a walking lamp, and I'm a shadow. There are two kinds of beings that Creatures of Darkness will attack on sight, and we're both. Do you really need to ask?"

Snuggle tilted her head.

Currently, they were standing in a cave that wasn't that different from the one Shadow had inhabited for countless years — apart from being filled with true darkness, of course. Further away, the walls of the cave narrowed into a natural passage that was only wide enough for one person to walk through, as long as their shoulders weren't too wide.

Shadow did not really want to push through that narrow passage, but he had no choice. Letting out a sigh, he walked forward.

This time, he had entered the Underworld from the bottom of a deep gorge, at least, as opposed to from the peak of a hollow mountain. So, they were going to reach the middle stratum of the dark realm directly, perhaps even the lowest stratum, without having to descend from great heights.

“How are we going to survive all those terrible creatures, though?"

Snuggle did not sound very confident.

"I mean... don't get me wrong! Even if Noctis is not here, I can still fight off plenty of abominations! But I am only a Transcendent, after all. More than that, I've only been a Transcendent for a few years... so if something truly ghastly attacks us, we'd better run!"

Shadow smiled.

"Don't worry. I know this place like the back of my hand. Even if my powers are suppressed by true darkness, I'll still be able to run."

He wasn't lying. There were many ways for Shadow to traverse the Underworld — he could transform himself into a creature full of light, for example. However, he hoped that there would be no need for that.

He indeed knew the Underworld well, including how to get to where they were going while avoiding the most hazardous places. That was because among his myriad lives, there had been lives spent in this eerie darkness, as well.

In Shadow's mind, there were scattered fragments of memories that belonged to one of Nether's children — one of his favorite creations, at that, who had eventually become known as the Prince of Darkness.

As one of the Princes of the Underworld, the Prince of Darkness had been a member of the first generation of his people — those like him had been created by the Demon of Destiny himself, as opposed to being born from unions among the Stone Saints. Therefore, he had witnessed the Underworld as it had been before the Stone Saint civilization blossomed in its depths. Even if Shadow remembered only fragments of that life now, it was still enough to build a detailed map of the Underworld in his mind.

He knew all the paths and treacherous depths. He knew which parts of the great rivers could be navigated, and which were no different from a death sentence. He knew where their tributaries flowed, and how to reach them.

Most of all, he knew how to reach the Abyss while avoiding the truly dreadful Creatures of Corruption who dwelled in the darkness. By the time Stone Saints spread across the Underworld, most of those abominations were long gone, having been slain by Nether — but the stories of his countless battles were like myths to his children, the battlefields treated as sacred sites.

By knowing where those sacred sites would one day be in the future, Shadow could infer where the powerful Creatures of Corruption dwelled at the moment.

And whatever he did not remember or had never known could be made up for by his mystical intuition.

If not...

Shadow gazed into the impenetrable darkness with a calm expression.

If he failed to avoid danger, he would destroy danger.

So what if true darkness was a natural predator of shadows? He was not powerless in its embrace, either. A true shadow was never powerless, because it was shapeless. A shapeless being could take any shape it needed, and kill any enemy it wanted. Predator, prey... both were the same in the face of death.

It was just that Shadow had promised not to kill anything.

Feeling his chest and back scrape against the walls of the narrow passage, he sighed.

‘I guess I can let those things escape alive...'

Soon, the passage widened. Not long after that, they entered an unfathomably large cavern.

Snuggle's light did not reach far, and Shadow's senses were suppressed by true darkness. So, neither of them could tell just how vast the cavern was — however, both of them felt that it could swallow entire kingdoms, or maybe even mortal realms. Snuggle suddenly seemed hesitant.

“Hey, Shadow... just how big is the Underworld?"

He shrugged. When his shoulder moved, the little doll had to spin her arms in the air to keep her balance, then quickly grabbed his ear for support.

Shadow grimaced.

“The Underworld is truly immense. There is a reason why the Hollow Mountains can be entered from so many mortal realms, after all — they stretch far and wide, and therefore, the Underworld does too. It might even be bigger than some of the Divine Realms."

Snuggle coughed.

"And your powers are suppressed here, right? So, what... are we going to just walk to the Abyss? How far is that? And how long will it take us to get there on foot... won't our feet fall off?!"

Shadow spared her an amused glance.

“First of all... am I not the only one who does the walking? For someone who lazes about on my shoulder, you sure have a lot of complaints."
