Continuing forward, he shook his head.

"And no, we are not going to walk all the way to our destination. There is a much faster way. Hopefully, we can finish this journey in a few weeks... a month or two, at most."

Just as he said that, a distant sound reached them — it was the murmur of flowing water. Not long after that, they reached the shore of a small river.

In the soft radiance emanating from Snuggle, silver reflections danced on its surface. The water was cold and deep, its depths as dark as the world beyond the small circle of light.

Shadow remained motionless for a few moments, then sighed and manifested the few shadows sheltered by the light into the shape of a simple gondola. Stepping into it, he put Snuggle down on the forward bench and picked up the oar.

Then, he leaned down and pushed their modest boat off the shore.

As the slow current pulled it into the darkness, Shadow straightened and inhaled deeply.

The end of their journey felt so close.

--- Chapter 3219 ---

A black gondola moved across dark waters. There was a little doll sitting at its bow, her clumsy figure shining with a soft radiance that reflected from the surface of the river. At the stern, a young man with porcelain skin and lightless eyes held the oar, guiding the boat forward with smooth motions.

All around them, there was only darkness. The silence of this dark world was broken only by the soft splashing of water and the steady murmur of the flowing river, creating a peaceful, but ominous atmosphere.

For some reason, Shadow felt an impulse to hum a peculiar song.

However, he held himself back.

After a while, however, he spoke softly:

"I think I met a man once. That man was nothing but a broken skeleton, but he could still talk and sing."

Snuggle turned to look at him, a confused expression on her face.

“A singing skeleton? What about him?"

Shadow hesitated for a moment.

"That man was the worst man to have ever lived."

Snuggle tilted her head a little, struggling to understand what Shadow was talking about. Her little face was not very expressive, but still, he could just hear what she wanted to say...

What the hell are you saying?

Something like that.

He smiled faintly.

He wasn't quite sure himself.

"It's true. From the day the world was created until the day it was destroyed, no one had caused more suffering and devastation than that heartless man. Perhaps that was why Shadow God cursed him, taking his death away. Even when the man became a broken skeleton, he still couldn't die."

Shadow remained silent for a while and then sighed.

"Just like me. So, I wonder sometimes... what crime did I commit to end up the same way? Was it worse than what that man had done?"

He glanced down, feeling lost in his endless memories.

“Maybe that broken skeleton I remember is me."

Snuggle stared at him for a long time, then chuckled suddenly.

“Shadow... do you even have a skeleton? Aren't you a formless ocean of sentient darkness under that shell of yours?"

He gave her an offended glance.

“Of course, I have a skeleton. In fact, I have several skeletons."

Snuggle laughed.

“See! By that logic, you'd be a group of broken skeletons, so that inferior man who only had one cannot be you."

Shadow lingered for a bit, then nodded with a slight smile.

"Your argument is quite reasonable."

Snuggle grinned.

"Naturally! I am nothing if not reasonable. Someone has to be, after all."

She sighed heavily, as if lamenting the sheer lack of reason all her companions seem to share.

One was an ancient Titan who had all the common sense of a primordial natural disaster, and the other one was Noctis.

"Ah, woe is me! I really suffered a lot!"

Shadow smiled, then glanced ahead. His expression turned a little troubled.

"You'd better prepare. There is another one nearby."

As if in response to his words, the sound of a loud splash reached them from somewhere far ahead. Snuggle covered her face for a moment, then jumped off the bench and scurried over to Shadow.

Looking up at him, she said:

“You... you watch over my precious vessel well this time! Understand?!"

Shadow frowned.

“When have I ever not watched it well?"

Snuggle stared at him in dismay.

"W—what?! Do... do you have any shame? The last time I returned, I was soaking wet! Do you think it's pleasant for a doll to be wet? Huh?"

Shadow considered his answer for a few seconds.

“I wouldn't know. And no, I don't have any shame. Why would I care to have something like that?"

Wasn't shame something only humans felt? He paused for a moment.

"In any case, that was your own fault. Try not to rock the boat so much this time."

Snuggle glared at him some more, then humphed.

"Look away!"

Shadow obediently turned his head, gazing at the dark waters.

A few seconds after he did, he heard a soft thump — that was the sound of Snuggle falling lifelessly to the floor of the boat.

Of course, she wasn't dead. It was just that the transient soul who inhabited the little doll had left its clumsy vessel — as soon as she did, intense radiance chased away the darkness, illuminating more of the dark river.

Snuggle had to abandon her corporeal vessel because there was a Creature of Corruption approaching their boat, and she had to fight it.

It had already been a week since they entered the Underworld. In that time, Shadow had steered them away from truly perilous abominations, but he couldn't avoid all threats — the Underworld was a realm that had never surrendered to the champions of the Age of Heroes, after all.

There were no humans here, since no human tribe would be foolish enough to try settling this lightless subterranean world. There were no Creatures of the Flame, either. So, no one had ever waged war against the ancient horrors who populated the endless ocean of elemental darkness, and therefore, all those horrors remained.

More than that, many Creatures of Corruption had made their way to the Underworld as humanity's sphere of influence slowly spread. In the future, Nether would cleanse this lightless realm to proclaim his ownership over it — but before that happened, the Underworld was no different from hell.

That was why Snuggle had to clash with powerful abominations from time to time. Of course, that was her own fault, since she was the one who had forbidden Shadow from killing. In the past, she and Noctis had managed quite well, but now that he was gone, there was no one for the little doll to support from the rear.

She had to face abominations alone and slay them all by herself.

And for that, she had to abandon her vessel and assume her Transcendent form.

A few moments later, Shadow felt the boat sway lightly, as if suddenly carrying more weight. He waited a while longer and turned around.

His expression was a little complicated. Snuggle — the doll — was lying motionlessly at the bottom of the boat, devoid of its usual liveliness. Above her, meanwhile, stood a young woman in a suit of intricately forged armor, a brilliant radiance emanating from her exquisite figure.

Behind her, two beautiful white wings opened, as if wanting to embrace the world. The young woman's hair fell like a waterfall of glistening black silk, and her skin was as fair as fresh snow. Her eyes were like sparkling jewels, and the corners of her rosy lips were naturally upturned, making it seem like she was always smiling. Her features were not ravishing, but they were soft and enchanting, giving her breathtaking beauty a pure and innocent kind of sheen.

In fact... she was so lovely and charming that even Shadow felt awkward looking at her for too long. In his memories, he had seen all kinds of astonishing beauties, but Snuggle's natural charm made almost all of them seem dull in comparison.

After witnessing Snuggle's Transcendent form for the first time, Shadow had realized why she had never used it before. He had assumed that she simply wanted Noctis to handle all the direct clashes, but now, he strongly suspected that she simply did not want Noctis to see her in that form. Otherwise, the young and hot-blooded Beast of Twilight would have been instantly smitten and utterly enamored, making their long journey together quite difficult to endure.

As for Shadow himself, he wasn't really affected. In fact, he slightly disliked Snuggle's Transcendent form.

After all, Snuggle was Snuggle. She was a clumsy doll, and quite possibly the ugliest doll in the world as well... seeing her like that, tall and beautiful enough to put deities to shame, felt incredibly wrong.

Snuggle smiled radiantly, two charming dimples appearing on her cheeks.

"What? Have you been left speechless by my peerless beauty?"

Shadow stared at her nonchalantly, then shook his head.

"I like you better when you're ugly."

He was being honest, of course.

Snuggle blinked a couple of times, then laughed.

"I'm never ugly, though? I am always adorable. So, keep my adorable vessel dry this time!"

With that, she turned back and leapt into the air. Her beautiful white wings propelled her into the darkness, and she shot forward like a ray of sunshine.

Before she left, she infused the black gondola with a bit of her essence, so Shadow was not left in complete darkness. He saw a long spear weave itself into existence in her hand.

Shadow glanced at the sparks of light that swiftly formed the shaft and the head of an enchanted spear.

Those sparks were the reason he had to look away every time Snuggle assumed her Transcendent form. Her armor was woven out of light, as well.

Seeing the sparks of light made him frown.

Far in the distance, a gargantuan maw broke the surface of water, and a monstrous head rose above the river. The creature had no eyes, and its skin was smooth like black stone. Its maw brimmed with dreadful teeth, and there was an undulating forest of revolting pseudopodia moving above its lips.

As it rose higher, a glimpse of a monstrous body was revealed, brimming with a chaotic mess of bony limbs.

It was a Great Beast.

'If it's a Great Beast, there's no reason to worry.'

Snuggle was not the most powerful Transcendent Shadow had ever seen, but she was powerful. More than that, she was meticulous, supremely skilled, and seasoned, her combat intelligence sharper than the deadliest of blades.

Most of all, she was the bane of Creatures of Corruption.

If Snuggle were to face a Supreme Beast, Shadow would be worried. But in a battle against an abomination of the Great Rank, he did not have to feel too tense.

And indeed — just a few seconds later, a blinding beam of light tore the darkness and pierced the abomination's head. That was Snuggle's spear, thrown by her steady hand from up high.

The wound it delivered to the Great Beast was not too serious... but wounding the enemy was not Snuggle's goal. What she wanted to deliver was not a wound — it was her radiant essence.

Once the grotesque creature was infused with her essence, its rotten soul was caught aflame. Great swathes of the appalling darkness melted as it strained to devour the blessed fire, and the abominations let out a horrid, chilling wail.

It did not die, and it was not cleansed of Corruption either. However, it was weakened, becoming no stronger than an abomination of the Corrupted Rank would have been.

That was when Snuggle plummeted from the darkness above it, aiming to press her attack.

Her weapon of choice was a spear, but she was a proficient archer as well, using arrows and evasion when the enemy was too strong. Finally, she also wielded a beautiful saber, summoning it when the spear was too long or had already been thrown.

All of her weapons were enchanted, even if none of them were too powerful...

None of the Transcendent champions of the Age of Heroes could boast about having that many sorcerous items.

Shadow sighed.

Just then, a tall wave that had been raised by the clash between Snuggle and the Great Beast reached the gondola, rocking it violently. Shadow easily kept his balance. However, some water splashed into the boat.

He froze, and then slowly looked down. Snuggle — the doll — lay helplessly in a puddle, her raggedy body quickly absorbing the glistening water.

Shadow closed his eyes tightly and let out another, heavier sigh.

"...Damnation."

--- Chapter 3220 ---

It didn't take Snuggle long to slay the Great Beast. The hideous creature drifted in the current, its blood spilling into the depths of the river and spreading across its surface like virulent blight — not only was it a fatal poison, but also highly corrosive, forcing Shadow to reinforce their boat with his Will.

The transient soul, meanwhile, returned and hid itself inside the little doll once again — that way, she did not need to continue expending her essence. The doll stirred and threw an accusing glare at Shadow.

"What is this?! Why am I in a puddle again?!"

Shadow coughed awkwardly.

“Well. You see. There was a wave..."

As he defended himself, the gondola continued rushing downriver.

The tributary they were braving eventually merged with one of the great rivers of the Underworld. The great river was far more hazardous, so Snuggle had to work harder to keep them safe. On more than one occasion, she received grievous wounds — luckily, since she could mend her own soul, her life was not in danger.

Nevertheless, Shadow had to involve himself in the battles soon enough.

He still held himself back from killing their foes. Instead, Shadow restrained them, while Snuggle delivered lethal blows. After a while, her enchanted weapons proved too weak to harm the ghastly dwellers of the Underworld, so he crafted her a suit of armor and a set of weapons out of shadows. Even then, she couldn't kill some of their enemies, merely managing to drive them away.

Snuggle could wield the weapons Shadow had forged for her. However, she could not waste time on donning the suit of armor every time there was a threat — so, Shadow enchanted both the weapons and the armor to function in a similar fashion to her original arsenal.

It was surprisingly easy. Shadow might not have remembered or cared to remember all of his past lives, but his hands did. Just like the day he had mended the little doll and sewn her a dress, a needle that glowed with ethereal golden light appeared in his hand, while the other wove strings of inky-black essence with elegant ease.

Shadow was mildly surprised by his skill. Snuggle, meanwhile, was too giddy about her new armaments to pay his sorcery much attention.

More time passed. They traveled across the Underworld, getting closer and closer to their goal.

Until, finally, they reached it.

As Shadow guided the gondola to shore and dismissed it, both he and Snuggle looked ahead. Nothing but darkness surrounded them, with only a small circle of light keeping it at bay. Neither could see what lay ahead, but they could hear a distant, penetrating hum.

Shadow knew that it was the sound of the great waterfall that fell into the Abyss.

He also knew that in front of them was a colossal cavern with mountain-like stalagmites rising from the white mist that swirled above the rushing water, and similarly titanic stalactites hanging from the distant ceiling.

The Stone Saints did not exist yet, so their radiant city had not been built in this cavern. And judging by the lack of lights in the distance, Nether's stronghold was not hovering at the edge of the Abyss, either. So, the Demon of Destiny had not established his laboratory here yet, after all.

Shadow vaguely remembered an Unholy horror that was chained by true darkness in the depths of the Abyss... or rather, would be chained there in the distant future. At the moment, the Abyss was free of its profane presence — he was quite confident that it was, at least.

That was because that horror festered from the remains of a nephilim that had fallen in the last battle of the final war, leading the Demon Legion to breach the Abyss and besiege Death. That apocalyptic battle had not arrived yet, so the nephilim was still alive, residing somewhere else in the Underworld.

All Shadow had to be wary of was the true darkness.

He inhaled deeply, then looked at Snuggle.

"It will be faster to move if both of us can fly. I think you should assume your Transcendent form now."

Snuggle, who was standing on his shoulder, looked at him nervously and then jumped into his pocket. As the little doll stumped there, the radiant soul emerged, illuminating the darkness.

Soon enough, the winged radiance was standing by his side, the pristine white feathers of her wings contrasting sharply against her intricate black armor.

Her expression was tense, and it seemed that, for once, she was in no mood for carefree banter.

"So... we're close?"

Shadow lingered for a moment, then nodded.

“Very close. Follow me."

With that, he summoned a pair of raven-black wings and soared into the air. They traveled forward cautiously, moving from one stalagmite to the other.

And as they did...

Shadow's thoughts turned more and more somber.

This journey of theirs had been... pleasant. He had allowed himself to drift in the current, following his companions passively.

He did not bother to think about too many things, least of all those of them that were important.

Asa result, he had enjoyed his time in the mortal realms. The world was vast and full of beauty. He was curious about great many things and had explored them with interest. He had tasted human food and grew familiar with human customs. Most of all, he had enjoyed the company of his two fellow travelers, Snuggle and Noctis.

But he had only been able to enjoy all those things because their journey had a time limit.

Now, the journey was coming to an end. And so, Shadow couldn't close his eyes to the truth he had been irresponsibly ignoring for so long anymore.

As they drew closer to the terrifying drop from the middle to the lower stratum of the Underworld, where the edge of the Abyss lay, the hum of the great waterfall grew louder. He could already smell the water vapor in the air... at the same time, the darkness around them somehow started to feel deeper, colder, more impenetrable. The soft radiance emanating from Snuggle's winged figure did not change, but the circle of light created by it grew narrower. Her expression was tense now, as well, her face slowly turning paler.

Shadow's expression, meanwhile, was solemn.

What was he really doing?

Snuggle was under the impression that they were traveling to the Shadow Realm to help him let go of an old regret... and perhaps find a way to embrace life, as well. Shadow wasn't really sure, but he knew that she wanted to help him, somehow — granted, her impression of what his needs were differed from his own.

Still, she saw the world in brighter hues. To her, it always seemed that the rays of sunshine were just beyond the horizon.

And knowing that, he had been deceiving her all along.

In truth, Shadow’s goal was far darker. Yes, he wanted to live up to Tatal's impression of him and set the shadows contained within his soul free. But what he truly wanted to find in the Realm of Death... was Shadow God.

Shadow wanted that nebulous god, who was supposedly his creator, to explain the mystery of his existence. To tell him why it couldn't end.

..But that was a lie, as well.

He was going to the Shadow Realm to find Death.

What Shadow truly wanted was for Shadow God to grant him peace.

‘Ah, peace...’

Wasn't it a wonderful thought, to find peace at long last?

It was.

But...

Where did it leave Snuggle?

Flying ahead of her, Shadow could not help but grit his teeth slightly.

What would happen if the two of them faced Shadow God, and she heard her friend's request?

What would happen if Shadow God refused to grant it?

...What would happen if Shadow God agreed?

Shadow felt a heavy burden settle on his heart.

No, that burden had been there for a long time. But he did not know if it was the worst of what he could be forced to endure, because on the other side of these questions were a few others, which were just as heavy — if not more.

What would happen to Snuggle if she did not follow Shadow into the Realm of Death?

In this nightmarish world, she could only endure because she had hope. Hope burned in her heart, shining brighter than the divine radiance of her wondrous soul. But just like the hope of the Demon of Desire, hers was destined to be shattered and crushed.

It was just that Hope's fall still loomed in the dark, tempestuous future.

The hope that kept Snuggle going, on the contrary, had already been shattered in the lightless expanse of the past.

She just did not know it yet.

So... wouldn't it be better for this radiant, transient soul to follow Shadow into the Realm of Death?

Death was far more merciful than hopelessness, after all.

And Shadow was a creature of Death.

As they approached the last of the towering stalagmites and rested briefly on its surface, high above the bottomless void of the Abyss, he looked at the radiant figure standing with her back to him and closed his eyes for a moment.

A heavy thought surfaced in his mind.

‘Was that what Hope meant?’

It seemed that even a forsaken creature like him had the privilege... or the curse... of having to make choices.

--- Chapter 3221 ---

Shadow and Snuggle glided down to the precipice of the abyss, enveloped by the roaring of the great waterfall. Clouds of water vapor shone in luminous radiance like nebulas woven out of myriads of diamonds, and beyond them, the cold darkness of the Underworld stretched endlessly. Eventually, they reached a shelf of rugged rock that protruded from the roaring wall of falling water. It tapered to a point, hanging above the abyss like a narrow cliff.

Below them was the Abyss.

Shadow walked to the tip of the shelf, looking into the darkness below with a distant expression. Snuggle followed carefully, trying to steady her footsteps on the slippery rocks, and stopped just behind him.

Looking down into the unfathomable darkness, she shivered.

"So, what? Do we just... jump down?"

Shadow remained silent for a few seconds, then shrugged.

"I am not sure. I have never dove into the Abyss before."

He studied the darkness.

The dreadful prisoner of the Abyss was not there. As for the Creature of Darkness that was meant to bind it... he wasn't sure. It had not haunted them on the journey through the Underworld, at least. Possibly it had not been born yet; possibly it already existed, but had not been reared by Nether to become as vast as it would be one day. Maybe it was simply uninterested and hid itself in the depths of the Abyss, or didn't dare to leave it because Shadow God still ruled his realm far below.

In any case, Snuggle was more or less correct. If they wanted to brave the Abyss and enter the Shadow Realm through one of the cracks created in its walls by Rime, the Demon of Repose, all they could do was take a leap of faith.

But...

Did they want to?

Shadow did. He was not sure if he wanted Snuggle to follow him, though.

And he had to make his choice now. Shadow remained motionless for a long while, staring into the darkness. His mind was too restless and crowded, brimming with a screaming legion of memories. It was difficult to remember who he was, who he was meant to be, let alone form cohesive thoughts and decide something so vital, so important... so irrevocable.

A thousand images flashed in his mind, forcing him to grit his teeth.

But then, suddenly, he grasped the only correct thought in this sea of fragmented memories.

Once he realized the essence of that one right argument, the screaming rending his mind apart settled, and he let out a quiet sigh.

That truth he realized was very easy...

It was that the difficult choice haunting him was not his to make, to begin with.

What right did he have to decide for Snuggle?

She had to make that choice herself.

It was just that before making it, she had to know what she was choosing.

Shadow threw one last glance into the darkness, then took a deep breath and turned his back to it.

He glanced at Snuggle, who seemed to read something from his expression.

Her brow furrowed faintly.

“What? Why are you looking at me like that?"

Shadow lingered for a moment, gathering his thoughts.

He had to face the truth... and even if the truth was cruel, this lost soul had to face it, as well.

Knowledge was the heaviest thing in the world, but there was a reason why myriad men had pursued it desperately despite knowing the cost. It was because knowledge was precious, as well. It was the origin of all power.

And in this dire world, who dared to exist without power?

He sighed deeply.

"It is because I have to tell you something.”

Shadow paused for a moment, then smiled faintly.

His smile carried a subtle hint of wistfulness.

“Once I reach the Shadow Realm... I don't think I will be coming back, Snuggle."

She blinked.

“Huh? What do you mean?"

Shadow shook his head lightly.

“What did you think? It is not easy to escape the Shadow Realm. Very few beings ever achieved that feat... and I never intended to follow in their footsteps, to begin with."

Snuggle frowned.

“Wait a minute. What are you saying? Why would you want to stay in such a dreary place?"

Shadow smiled sadly.

"Why would one want to stay in the Realm of Death, Snuggle?"

He glanced down at the head of the little doll sticking out of his pocket.

The winged woman standing in front of him, meanwhile, glanced at him with a stunned expression.

"C... come on, Shadow! Stop joking around."

He sighed and glanced away.

After remaining silent for a few long minutes, Shadow lowered his head and said:

“Back then... didn't I tell you why I wanted to come to the Shadow Realm? It was because I wanted to set the shadows trapped in my soul free. Because a friend had once told me that their existence was awfully sad."

He faced Snuggle, her bright radiance reflecting in his lightless eyes.

“But am I not the same, Snuggle? How am I different from those lost, pitiful shades?"

He shook his head.

"I am tired of this place... of this vicious, never-ending nightmare. I have lived myriad lives, and all of them were full of nothing but horror and strife, ending violently. Agony, torment, madness, and death — those are the things I know best. They are the only things I know, and I've had enough of them."

Shadow inhaled deeply, settling his mind.

"So, I will go to the Realm of Death in search of Shadow God's mercy. I will cross the Abyss to find peace within him."

He remained silent for a moment, then looked Snuggle directly in the eye.

Shadow exhaled slowly.

Then, he said softly:

“And I want you to come with me."

Snuggle took a step back, looking at him in disbelief.

A baffled smile appeared on her lips.

“Are you seriously asking me to... die together?"

Shadow did not look away, but his expression changed subtly, a sense of tired melancholy reflecting in his eyes.

"Yes, I am. If... if you want to."

A startled scoff escaped from Snuggle's mouth.

She studied Shadow for a while, her brow creased by a scowl. Then, with an angry smile, she asked:

“Why would I want to die, Shadow?"

But he just continued to look at her silently. Eventually, he said:

“You know why."

Snuggle's frown deepened, and she took a step back.

"No... no, I don't. I cannot die. I have to wait for the person who will come to find me. I have to return to the people who are waiting for me. There are so many things that I want! That I haven't had the chance to experience yet! What... what nonsense are you spouting?!"

Shadow did not answer for a long while, feeling a peculiar pain permeate his entire being.

In the end, he sighed.

"Smile of Heaven... that is your True Name, isn't it?"

Snuggle... Smile of Heaven... froze.

"H—how... how do you know it?"

Shadow smiled sadly.

“Because among the myriad nightmares I've lived, there were countless nightmares about the dark future you come from."

She stared at him with a pale face, her eyes suddenly full of fear.

She shook her head slowly, taking another step back.

“No... no, you can't be a challenger. You can't be. I don't know you."

Shadow glanced down, at the weathered rocks under their feet.

He remembered standing on this narrow ledge once, in one of his myriad lives.

In the distant future.

He took a deep breath, then stilled his expression and looked at the radiant woman in front of him.

He was about to do the cruelest thing he had done.

He was going to be truthful, for once. Shadow spoke, his voice resounding in the darkness:

“No one is coming to find you, Smile of Heaven. The man you are waiting for died a long time ago, alone and surrounded by darkness. The people you called friends are all gone. Your father, your mother... the entire Immortal Flame clan you knew. None of it remains."

Shadow paused for a moment.

“You do have a daughter, but she is a stranger."

Smile of Heaven suddenly let out a stifled laugh.

“A daughter? I am pretty sure I would remember having a daughter!"

He simply glanced at her, his expression aloof.

"Not if she was born of your body after you abandoned it."

Smile of Heaven fell silent, staring at him with her large, glistening eyes.

A peculiar, indescribable expression settled on her pale face.

There was only silence between them until she broke in a quiet, trembling voice:

"You're lying."

She forced out a smile.

"You're an awful liar."

Shadow met her gaze, then sighed.

He wished that he was.

“I never lie."

Her words fell like the blade of a guillotine.

"There is nothing waiting for you in that world. There is nothing holding you in this one, either. The future only hides sorrow, pain, and rage. So..."

Shadow glanced at Smile of Heaven.

"Come with me. Let us leave this cursed place behind... together."

Smile of Heaven studied him for a long time, her eyes full of dark intensity.

Eventually, however, a concerned, but calm expression settled on her face.

She inhaled deeply, then let out a long sigh. When she glanced at him again, her gaze was steady.

"No."

Smile of Heaven closed her eyes for a moment.

"Come with me instead, Shadow. So what if this world is cursed? We can heal it. Even if we lose people we love... we can make sure that the rest don't have to. We can conquer this nightmare — we can conquer all nightmares. So, please. Let's stay alive together!"

Shadow remained silent for a while, then slowly shook his head.

Smile of Heaven opened her mouth, as if wanting to say something else, to convince him... but then closed it. She must have noticed from his expression that there was nothing she could say that would change his mind.

Her face fell.

She did not speak for some time, then sighed heavily.

When she glanced at Shadow again, there was a familiar smile on her lips... even if her eyes were mournful.

Still, Smile of Heaven smiled.

"Then... please forgive me, Shadow. But I will have to refuse."

Her lips shook.

“You'll have to meet Shadow God alone. I know you want to find peace, and I can't really imagine what you've been through. So I hope that you find what you seek. But I..."

She composed herself and faced him firmly.

"I am not ready to give up yet. I don't want to.”

Then, she suddenly chuckled.

“After all, according to you, I have a daughter somewhere out there. She's probably awfully angry at me for leaving her alone and going missing for so long. So, at the very least, I have to let her properly berate me."

With that, Smile of Heaven glanced at him with pain in her bright eyes, then turned back and took a step away.

Shadow raised his hand, as if reaching for her.

"Wait!"

His hand hovered in the air, not daring to move further.

Smile of Heaven paused for a moment, but did not look back.

He gritted his teeth.

"The Underworld is so dangerous. How are you going to escape it?!"

She seemed to have smiled.

“Did you forget? I am great at hiding, escaping, and staying alive. When we first met, I even managed to escape you for a while. So I'll find a way out of this place, as well."

Smile of Heaven continued walking.

“You'll think that I am cursing you, Shadow... but I hope that we meet again, one day."

The sound of her quiet, wistful laughter was drowned by the roar of the waterfall.

"When we do... be prepared to receive an earful... goodbye!"

A moment later, her light was almost gone. Shadow knew that in just a few heartbeats, he would be left in complete darkness.

In a world devoid of light.

Before that happened, however, all emotion left his face, and he glanced to the side.

He called for someone whom he hardly remembered, but knew all too well.

In that instant, a dark figure rose from his shadow.

It was a graceful woman woven from darkness, her nebulous face hidden behind a veil. Clad in light armor, she seemed more like a dancer than a warrior... and yet, her presence was unmistakably that of a slayer — of a ruthless predator who had killed countless prey.

When she appeared, the air suddenly turned colder, as if turned frigid by the presence of death.

Even Shadow shivered faintly.

As two lifeless black eyes stared at him with no emotion, he sighed.

It seemed that there had been a demon like that in his soul all along, as well.

Turning to look at the disappearing figure of Smile of Heaven, he said quietly:

"Go. Protect her. Stay with her... don't let her die."

That was the last thing he could do for his lovely companion.

The graceful shadow studied him emotionlessly for a few seconds, then turned away and disappeared into the darkness.

And just like that, finally...

Shadow was left completely, utterly alone. With a sigh, he reached into a pocket and pulled a little doll out of it.

By then, he was surrounded by true darkness, blinded and unable to see its ugly face.

Shadow turned to the Abyss.

"It's just you and me now, Snuggle. Shall we go knock on Death's door?"

His quiet voice was swallowed by darkness, and the doll didn't answer.

Closing his eyes, Shadow took a step forward and fell.

--- Chapter 3222 ---

A figure fell from the lightless sky, streaking across its dark expanse like a star woven out of impenetrable darkness. It collided with a towering dune of obsidian dust and obliterated it, sending countless tons of black sand into the air.

As a billowing black cloud spread, swallowing a vast swath of the desolate land, the roar of the terrible impact rolled outward.

Soon enough, however, there was silence once more.

The billowing dust slowly settled, revealing a shallow crater. Shadow was lying there, his body battered and covered in dreadful wounds.

Nevertheless, not a single drop of blood seeped from them into the obsidian dust. He exhaled slowly.

As several sparks of light drifted from his body into the dark aether, he rose to his feet, swaying lightly, and glanced around. Before him lay the endless expanse of the Shadow Realm.

A sea of black dunes rested in the darkness, the tenebrous sky illuminated by the distant radiance of wandering essence storms. Here and there, dark figures could be seen, walking across the desolate wasteland in a single direction.

Those were the shadows of the dead, venturing on their last journey.

As they walked, the Shadow Realm slowly destroyed them — still, the shadows persisted, as if overcome by an insurmountable determination to come as close to the heart of this lightless land as they could.

Shadow remained motionless for a while, contemplating.

It was amusing that he did not feel the same compulsion... and bitter, as well. After all, it was another reminder that he was refused the inalienable right that all other beings seemed to enjoy.

‘I am here.'

He had finally reached the Shadow Realm. Shadow had wondered about what it would feel like once or twice... he had even entertained the idea that entering the realm of Shadow God would feel like returning home.

But he felt nothing.

Nothing except for the pain in his battered body.

The Abyss had not been kind to him. There, blinded and robbed of his senses, he fell for what felt like an eternity — at some point, the concept of time itself seemed to lose meaning, and all that remained was the feeling of plummeting endlessly.

That and the feeling of not being alone in the darkness.

Shadow still did not know what he had encountered in the Abyss, but he knew that the force he had endured — a being, perhaps, or a legion of beings — was hostile. He had been attacked viciously, an invisible power trying to pull him apart, to drain him, to devour the essence of his being completely.

There, in the Abyss, he had no choice but to hide within his corporeal vessel, not daring to unleash his true self into the jaws of darkness.

However, his human body was not weak. Shadow had fought fiercely, overcome by a ferocious malice. He did not truly realize how straining the promise given to Snuggle... to Smile of Heaven... had been. But now that he was released from its shackles, it was as if the deadly intent that he had been suppressing for so long broke free all at once, igniting him with murderous wrath.

In the end, he had survived Abyss — even if he did not know if that was because of his will to endure or by pure luck.

And now, he was here, in the realm of Shadow God.

Shadow inhaled deeply.

He remained still for a while, gazing at the dark landscape of the Realm of Death, then walked forward.

He walked and walked. Sometimes, he walked alone. At other times, the shadows of the dead kept him company.

But after a while, none of them remained, erased from existence by the mercy of Shadow God — only swirls of radiant sparks rose into the dark skies, soon disappearing from view.

Eventually, Shadow found himself entirely alone.

As far as he could see, not a single shadow remained. Behind him was the vast expanse of obsidian dunes; in front of him, a titanic mountain chain seemed to rise from the ground in the distance.

Finally, he stopped and glanced down, his mangled face full of grim exhaustion.

With a heavy sigh, Shadow lowered himself to the ground and sat cross-legged. Pulling the little doll out of his pocket, he placed it carefully on the sand beside him.

Then, he gazed into the distance.

He remembered the past... not the endless fragments of his myriad past lives, but the long years of this one. He remembered the time when the world was young. He remembered the tranquility of the primal realm around him. He remembered the little girl who had once come to his cave, full of unabashed enthusiasm and passion for life. He remembered saying goodbye to the old woman the girl had become, as well.

Smile of Heaven, Noctis... even Hope.

Compared to the rest, this particular life seemed especially bittersweet. But at the moment, he felt like it had been a little bit sweeter than bitter.

‘Ah... I've lived too long.’

Shadow inhaled deeply, then looked at the ugly doll that sat motionlessly beside him.

"...Don't be sad anymore."

With that, he reached deep into his soul and called all the shadows trapped there forth. In the next moment, it was as if an ocean of darkness escaped from his small figure, devouring the sands around him. Then, countless figures rose from it, all looking at him silently.

Some of them were small. Some of them were gargantuan. Some were human, while some were monstrous. So many of them... He saw many familiar faces.

The old slaver was there. The broad-shouldered slave was there, as well. The righteous king who had succumbed to doubt gazed at him with five blind eyes. The doubt that had consumed him was there too, its wings obscuring the sky.

The cursed legionnaires of the Forgotten Shore rested under the branches of a colossal tree. A ghostly flower made of silk drifted in the currents of wind. A man who looked like a king stood side by side with a radiant woman whose face bore a striking resemblance to him, both devoid of emotion.

The people of the Shadow Tribe tribe were there, as well, looking at him with a silent accusation.

And so... So many more.

Shadow could feel a subtle, insurmountable connection between him and these shades. Because they belonged to him. Because they were a part of his Domain.

...But he did not want to be their master anymore.

With a sigh, he smiled faintly.

"Go on. Find peace. Be free."

With that, he reached into his soul and broke the connection.

It hurt him terribly, so much so that he barely suppressed a scream.

The shades did not move.

They remained motionless, still staring at him.

But soon, more and more sparks began to rise above the vast sea of their dark figures. There was a handful at first, then a hundred. The world, which had been drowning in darkness, was suddenly illuminated by a radiant light.

And then, the radiance became blinding. Suddenly, the darkness was vanquished, and Shadow found himself in a world filled with nothing but brilliant light. Countless shades around him melted slowly in that light, and a whirlwind of sparks erupted into the dark heavens of the Realm of Death.

As his eyes widened, Shadow looked into the light in wonder.

‘How radiant...’

Finally, after eons spent in the darkness, he found himself surrounded by light.

The wind grew stronger, turning into a hurricane. And the great mass of soul essence unleashed by the destruction of the legion of shades expanded, becoming an essence storm.

Hidden in the heart of the storm, Shadow felt his flesh being eroded by its ferocious power. It was as if each of the many sparks was a tiny blade that cut him, tearing his skin away, erasing his flesh little by little.

But Shadow did not move, even when his bones were revealed in the dreadful wounds. He only lowered his hand to protect the little doll from the rage of the devastating storm.

He continued to stare into the light, mesmerized by it.

Around him, the shades collapsed one after another, turning into torrents of essence. More and more of them were gone. Hundreds, thousands... too many to count. Until only one of them remained.

It was the shade of the lonely priestess of War who did not know how to give up.

She gazed at Shadow, her tattered figure slowly dissipating into the light.

Shadow gazed at her, as well.

By then, half of his face was gone, revealing the white skull hidden beneath.

He remembered that woman's life.

A soft, mournful smile twisted what remained of his lips.

"It's alright. You've endured enough... you can rest now. Farewell."

The tattered shade looked at him one last time.

And then, finally, she turned into a whirlwind of essence, soaring high into the sky.

Disappearing forever.

Shadow glanced down, then suddenly laughed.

There was no joy in his laughter, only envy.

“This... this is the mercy of Shadow!"

The hurricane winds roared, drowning out his voice. Carried by the wind, the gargantuan storm moved on, leaving to roam the desolate expanse of the Shadow Realm. The light grew dimmer soon.

And then, darkness crept to surround Shadow once more.

‘They are gone.'

At that moment, Shadow felt it...

He felt that he could have absorbed the shades instead of setting them free. And that consuming his Domain could have made him far stronger.

But by now, he was old and wise enough to know that not all power was a blessing. There were crossroads and dead ends even on the Path of Ascension... and those who chose the wrong turn would only end up damned.

Shadow had set his shades free, as Tatal would have wanted. He expected to feel weak and empty... but, strangely enough, it was the opposite.

He felt free, too.

"It's done, then."

A heavy sigh escaped from his lips. Grimacing, Shadow raised his head and looked into the distance.

There, far away...

The blinding radiance he had summoned into the world seemed to have attracted someone's attention.

The titanic mountain chain that loomed in the distance moved. At first, Shadow thought that his senses were playing a trick on him, but there was no mistake — the black ridges seemed to flow like a river, and the entire mountain chain was slithering across the sea of obsidian dunes, dwarfing them.

Then, a part of it rose, disappearing into the darkness above.

It was only then that Shadow recognized the mountain chain for what it was...

An inconceivable, unfathomably colossal serpent whose obsidian body must have coiled around the entire world. Shuddering, he instinctively reeled back and glanced up.

A serpentine head slowly revealed itself from the darkness above him, obscuring the sky. Its size defied reason, and Shadow could not judge it correctly due to the fact that the magnitude of its terrifying visage distorted perspective.

All he knew was that he could not move under the gaze of its lightless, still, unfathomable black eyes.

But then, he gritted his teeth in anger. Forcing himself to move, Shadow rose to his feet, staggered, then righted himself and met the colossal serpent's gaze with defiance.

A burning sensation boiled in his heart.

"Why?"

He clenched his fists.

"Why?!"

Shadow pointed an accusatory finger at Shadow God.

“Why have you forsaken me?! What terrible crime did I commit to deserve this?! Live, live, live... why is everyone allowed the solace of death, but I am not?!"

Burning with anger, he screamed:

“Weren't you supposed to welcome all, bring peace to all?! Well, here I am! Where is my solace, where is my peace?!?! Give it to me! I demand it!"

His voice fell, and he lowered his head tiredly.

Shadow sighed.

“I am so tired. I can't endure it anymore. Why can't I die? Please, Death... show me mercy."

The titanic serpent gazed at him silently. Then, from all around him, a horrible hiss suddenly resounded, penetrating the darkest depths of his soul and making his spirit shudder in dread.

"Do you really want to die?"

The serpent lowered its head, as if wanting to study Shadow more closely.

He straightened, trying not to tremble as he met the god's gaze.

Shadow could almost see his mutilated, pale reflection in the great serpent's lightless, colossal eyes.

Then, the hiss resounded again from the darkness, as if the world itself was speaking.

“I can grant your request, child. You simply have to say it..."

The colossal serpent remained motionless.

"Say that you truly want to die. Say it aloud. Then, I shall grant you peace."

Shadow froze for a moment, stunned... overjoyed.

‘Is that all?"

Suddenly, his heart ignited with exhilaration. With a tentative, feeble hope. Finally! After all these years, his prayers would be answered.

He would finally be able to die.

All he had to do was proclaim it.

Shadow's eyes widened, and he opened his mouth.

...However, no sound came from it.

‘W-what?'

He froze, failing to understand what was happening. He tried to speak again, but no words came out of his mouth.

It was as if something was preventing him from speaking.

'N—no...'

A strange, familiar pain slowly permeated his being.

The more Shadow tried to speak, the more pain he felt.

"No! No!’

He raged against the pain, forcing himself to speak — to say it. To prove to Shadow God that what he wanted the most in the world was to die.

‘I do! I want to! Please!’

But no matter how hard Shadow tried, no sound came out of his mouth.

In the end, blinded by pain, he staggered and fell to his knees.

‘Say it! Say it!"

His tongue refused to listen, and his lips remained sealed.

The colossal serpent studied him for a while longer.

And then, silently, it began to withdraw into the darkness.

‘No!'

A tortured groan escaped from Shadow's lips.

But by then, Shadow God had already turned away.

His horrible hiss resounded once more:

"Death cannot die, child. Didn't you want to spite us all?"

Soon, the serpent's head disappeared into the darkness. The mountain chain flowed like an oceanic tide, receding.

An echo of the horrible hiss was carried by the wind.

“Do not waste my blessing.”

In the end, Shadow was left alone, kneeling on the obsidian sand. The land around him was desolate and empty.

He bent over, pressing his forehead against the ground.

‘No, no, no...'

"No!"

His shout was not answered.

Shadow remained motionless for a long while.

Then, a bitter, indescribable laughter resounded in the silence.

Shadow laughed, and laughed, and laughed, burning tears flowing from his eyes.

None of his questions had been answered. None of his prayers had been answered, either.

He had come from far away to find Death, but even then, Death refused him.

There was no peace. There was no solace. No hope remained, no salvation.

Why couldn't he just say what Shadow God had told him to say?

That was the most painful part of it all, the most bitter!

Shadow had not been able to say anything... because he couldn't lie.

And even if he had not known it before, somewhere deep down, a tiny and unknown part of him still wanted to live.

It refused to die.

‘Ah...’

He couldn't stop laughing.

Truth... was so cruel.

--- Chapter 3223 ---

Time flowed.

The Flame continued to wane. The Flame continued to fuel itself and burn brighter. In the world outside the desolate expanse of the Shadow Realm, the Age of Heroes flashed with brilliant intensity and slowly drew to an end. Humanity had risen from its humble beginnings, pushing away the darkness of Corruption and conquering the world.

The Kingdom of Hope was swallowed by the light of Sun God and crumbled. The Demon of Desire used the last of her strength to bind the fragments of her shattered kingdom and keep them from plummeting into the ocean of fire, saving those few of her subjects who had survived the calamity. Thus, a new era began... the Golden Age, the Age of Humans.

The gods had already been growing more and more withdrawn from the affairs of mortals. But now, they grew entirely distant. Even the Spirits had become a rare sight, most of them having left for the Divine Realms.

The daemons all but vanished, each obsessed with their own endeavors.

In the void left by the missing divinity, only one god remained — War God, the patron deity of humanity. His avatar still dwelled among humans, ruling the ever-expanding Empire of War. Its legions spread across myriad realms, slowly subjugating them one by one.

But in time, even War God became an unseen presence in his militant empire. In the early years of his reign, the Dragon ruled it personally, establishing laws and leading the conquest — as time went, though, he appeared rarer and rarer, until the War Empire fell almost entirely into the hands of his Sacred emissaries and Supreme priests.

Centuries passed.

In the shattered land that was once known as the Kingdom of Hope, floating islands rested above the dark abyss of celestial flames, connected to each other by enormous chains. This land was ruled by the immortal Chain Lords, who had been personally chosen by Sun God to guard the prison of the Demon of Desire.

At the heart of the Kingdom of Hope, a beautiful city built of white stone sprawled across many islands. It had grown around the cage where Hope was imprisoned — her former stronghold, the Ivory Tower. The chief among her wardens was the ruler of the city, Sun God's own descendant, Lord Sevras — the ivory dragon, Sevirax.

Sevirax was a dutiful warden, so nothing could get past him to enter the Ivory Tower, where Hope was chained.

It was no surprise, then, that the King of Nothing made his way into the great pagoda without ever being seen.

Inside, the breathtaking silhouette of the fallen daemon was kneeling on the floor, caught and immobilized by unbreakable chains. The sight was almost too radiant to endure, too tragic to tolerate.

Mordret hid in the reflections, observing Hope with an aloof detachment.

Waiting.

Eventually, Hope let out an almost inaudible sigh.

Her head shifted slightly, causing the chains to rattle and draw taut, pulling it back.

But Hope endured, looking at the light pouring into the great hall of the Ivory Tower through tall windows.

“You don't have to hide."

Her voice was quiet and subtle, sounding like the rustle of falling leaves.

There was silence for a long while, and then a tall figure was suddenly standing some distance from her, having appeared out of nowhere.

It was a man with strange, mirror-like eyes and a cold expression.

When the Demon of Desire reflected in his eyes, he shivered slightly.

Hope seemed to smile.

"It has been a while since I entertained a guest.”

Her dying voice was no different from the whisper of receding waves.

Mordret lingered for a while, then said evenly:

“I came uninvited, so I hardly constitute a guest.”

Finally, Hope couldn't endure the pull of the chains anymore — or perhaps did not wish to endure it — and her head turned back to its original position.

Her gaze was now directed at the gates of the Ivory Tower, which were destined to remain shut for as long as she looked at them, longing to be free.

“Has my sister sent you? It does not seem like her."

Mordret smiled faintly, then walked to stand in front of Hope once more and shook his head.

“Nobody sent me."

It was easy to imagine why Hope would assume that he was a messenger of Mirage, the Demon of Imagination. His nature was similar to that of the remainder, after all — of the reflections that populated the Great Mirror, who had been created by Mirage. Hope looked at him with curiosity.

After a while, she asked:

“How has the world outside changed?"

Mordret was a little surprised by the question.

He sat on the floor, studied the chained daemon for a few moments, and shrugged.

"It is pretty much the same, I guess."

Then, after some contemplation, he added:

"The gods rarely show themselves to humans now. The daemons have scattered, each pursuing their own ambition. Mirage has withdrawn into her mirror, living out one fantasy after another; Repose has built a city devoid of death in the depths of the Black Skies, populating it with those who earned her favor. Nether has retreated into the Underworld, where he is trying to create something that he is not supposed to create. Ariel is building something in the desert, from what I've heard."

Hope asked:

“What about Weaver? And that child?"

Mordret raised an eyebrow.

“Who can know what Weaver is up to? I certainly don't. I don't know what child you are talking about, either. If you mean Oblivion... I feel like I knew something, but now, I don't remember."

He looked away and sighed.

“It is the Age of Humans out there now. Some call it the Golden Age. The Creatures of Corruption are hard to meet these days, even if they are not entirely extinct. War God's avatar is the only divine authority that remains in the mortal realms, and his empire is steadily spreading. That is about it."

Hope exhaled slowly.

“What about me? Do humans remember me?"

Mordret tilted his head a little.

“They do, of course. They remember you as a villainous spirit who grew prideful and was punished by the gods... a cautionary tale to teach children the perils of arrogance."

He shook his head with a hint of disdain.

“They are still enamored with the sorcery you taught them, though, as well as with everything else you gave them. Their Golden Age would not have been possible without writing, but only a few bother to remember that."

Hope smiled.

“That's good, then. They're using my gifts well."

Mordret looked at her, a hint of surprise surfacing in his mirror-like eyes.

He remained silent for a long while, then sighed.

His gaze grew distant once again.

“I still understand so little.”

Mordret lowered his gaze to the floor, looking slightly dejected.

“I spent countless years living among humans, you know? Observing them patiently. Their hopes, their passions... their fears and sorrows. An eternity spent as a silent observer. At times, I even forgot who I was, confusing myself with the people whose eyes I was using as shelter. But even after all these years, I still fail to understand the world. The truth still eludes me.”

He smiled bitterly.

"I died once while attempting Apotheosis. I thought that this time, I would do it the right way... that after I fathom the depths of humanity, I will be able to leave it behind and become a deity. But I only feel more lost. I don't even know what the purpose of this Nightmare is, let alone how to escape it."

Hope looked at him quietly.

Then, her voice resounded in the great hall again:

“Of course you are lost. After all, a passive observer can never become a god... you've been walking the wrong path this whole time."

Saying that, she chuckled suddenly.

“Not that I know a lot about Apotheosis. I was born a Spirit, no less."

Mordret gazed at her silently.

Eventually, he nodded.

“That was my conclusion as well. So, I ceased my attempts to understand humans and attempted to understand the gods."

His expression darkened slightly.

“But... perhaps because my mind has been painted in the hues of humanity, the conclusion I made after observing deities was nothing like what I had expected."

Hearing that, Hope seemed curious.

“What conclusion was that?"

Mordret faced her and remained silent for a long while.

In the end, he said in an even, calm tone:

"It is that gods should not exist. Their very existence is poison."

But then, he sighed.

“But what can I do? I cannot erase all gods from existence. More than that, the only sure way for me to escape is to become a deity myself. It seems that I have arrived at another dead end."

He contemplated for a while, then smiled ominously.

"So, eventually, I came up with a third plan."

Hope did not seem surprised by his sinister tone.

"Oh?"

Mordret nodded.

"You see, when I was younger, I once harbored an ambition to destroy your soul and take your divine body as my vessel. I am not sure if I could have killed you then, even if you were bound and severely weakened... but I am not the same Awakened youth anymore. I've grown much more powerful, and my bloodline has revealed much more of its latent potential."

He studied Hope with a cold gaze.

"I think... perhaps I can manage that feat now. Killing a god and stealing their body should be helpful if one wants to undergo Apotheosis, don't you think?"

Hope remained silent for a while, then asked:

“Is that why you came? To kill me?"

Mordret remained silent.

Then, he suddenly looked away and laughed bitterly.

"No. I did contemplate killing you, but now I've changed my mind."

His bitter smile slowly drained from his face, and finally, he sighed.

“After all, can godhood really be stolen? Even if it can, it doesn't change anything. The fact of the matter is that I have never taken someone's body... the very idea revolts me. Plus, you have never offended or harmed me, so what reason do I have to kill you?"

A joyless smile illuminated his face.

"I came here merely out of a sense of nostalgia. Meeting you now, face-to-face... feels like a kind of closure. Besides, I don't really have anywhere else to go. I am at another dead end."

Hope gazed at him for a long while.

After the silence between them stretched, she asked:

"Then, do you want a suggestion?"

Mordret raised an eyebrow.

Hope laughed.

“Stay here with me. Keep me company."

Then, she looked down.

“My brother should be somewhere below right now. This island and the one he created are connected by a portal. While you are here, you can try spying on him as well...”

--- Chapter 3224 ---

Time passed.

Time passed as the world moved along the predictable path.

The gods were distant; the people were mortal.

The Empire of War continued to grow, poised to devour all mortal realms one day. And what would happen next?

Nobody knew.

Some believed that the endless conquest would end, ushering in an era of harmony and peace — on that day, the Empire of War would become the Empire of Life.

Most, however, held a different belief.

They believed that once all mortal realms were conquered, the Dragon would lead his triumphant warriors as they ascended to the heavens to wage a glorious war of conquest against the Divine Realms as well.

But no one truly knew, since no one could know the future.

Except for those who could.

There were prophets among mortal men. Some, like the sybils, heard the voices of the gods. Some were sensitive to the torrents of fate. Some had gleaned the secrets of the world, and could therefore predict the movements of its parts.

The most famous of the seers was rumored to be the Oracle of Theta, who ruled a distant realm. The peculiar people of that peaceful realm did not bow to the gods — instead, they worshipped fate itself. The Oracle was shrouded in mystery, since they had only ever spoken to the supplicants through the mouths of their three disciples, the priestesses of fate.

So, many believed that the Oracle did not exist and was a mere myth.

If the Oracle did exist, though...

They would have known that even if nobody had realized it yet, the winds of change were already blowing across the mortal realms, and a terrible storm was brewing. The first thunderclap of the calamitous storm was ready to shake the world.

On a day like any other, two messengers arrived beneath two thrones.

One of them had crossed the great bridge and knelt in front of the pristine white gates of the Jade Palace, enduring the bitter cold in silence. Soon, the gates opened, and he was invited into the beautiful depths of the Queen's court.

After receiving the hospitality of the Jade Court, washing himself in a crystal pool, and enjoying a lavish meal, he was ushered into a great hall. There, a white throne towered above the floor, illuminated by torrents of light that poured through the translucent walls.

A young woman sat on the throne, her mesmerizing features caught between adolescence and adulthood. She wore a simple tunic of white silk, and her eyes were like two radiant pools of molten gold, glistening with mischievous sparks. Despite her breathtaking beauty and young age, something about her was eerily inhuman, deeply sinister, making the man shiver and lower his gaze.

Noticing his trepidation, she smiled. The twist of her crimson lips was indescribably alluring, and her golden eyes were full of mirth.

Standing up from the throne, the woman walked down the steps barefoot and stopped in front of the man. He did not dare to look at her — in fact, he shut his eyes tightly, terrified to catch a glimpse of her tunic's hem.

“Well? I was told you have a message for me."

The sound of her voice was enchanting. The man drew a deep breath, then nodded carefully.

"Yes, Your Majesty."

The young woman — the gorgeous monster, Jade Queen — seemed to have run out of patience.

“Let's hear it then!"

The man lowered his head and exhaled slowly.

“The message is this, my lady..."

He fell silent, as if gathering his courage. Eventually, he bit his lip and shouted:

"It's time! Pay up."

After that, there were a few gasps, and then a long silence.

The maids and the courtiers of the Jade Palace froze, shocked by the sacrilege. Their faces turned pale, and they threw frightened gazes at their queen.

The man did not see their reactions, though, since he still had his eyes closed. He tensed, feeling cold sweat rolling down his face.

The Jade Queen did not say anything, either.

After a few seconds, however, she suddenly exploded with laughter.

Her laughter was pure and melodious like the sweetest of songs.

Eventually, she forced out a few words through laughter:

“Ah, that heartless woman... did she finally remember that I exist? After ignoring me for centuries. Took her long enough!"

Turning away, she climbed the steps and sat back on her throne.

Looking at the trembling man with a fond smile, she hesitated a little, then said generously:

"I've decided not to eat you."

Then, she leaned forward a little.

"What else did she say?"

...On the same day, the capital of the War Empire was shaken by a tremor. It was a vast city that sprawled under the azure sky, climbing the slopes of seven tall hills. At the heart of it, an imposing tower soared into the air, its tip almost touching the clouds. The Dragon was said to rest on the top of the tower, observing his empire from its great height.

The tower itself was the Temple of War, and in front of its empty throne, a young man was sitting on the stone steps, looking down at the prayer hall with a heavy gaze. The man was handsome and broad-shouldered, his face seemingly chiseled from the finest marble. If anyone were to sculpt the ideal of masculine beauty, they would fail to create a statue more striking than this man — his features were clean and severe, and his scarlet eyes were full of cold will.

Most of all, he possessed a chilling presence. A presence that was ferocious like a beast and cold like forged steel, full of both triumph and bitterness, inevitable and insurmountable, impossible to overcome. If not for the fact that the man was suppressing it, everyone who faced him would have been crushed or driven to their knees.

It was as if he was surrounded by a ghostly song of war horns and the clangor of countless blades, by the inescapable scent of blood and deafening wails of sorrow... But also by the essence of pride, courage, and unbreakable willpower.

He was the Son of the Dragon, the Child of War, the most heroic warrior of the Empire and the commander of its endless legions. He was the Spirit of Victory.

A moment ago, the Spirit of Victory watched as the gates of the Temple were thrown open, and an uninvited guest entered the prayer hall.

The guest was a Transcendent knight wearing lustrous armor, his gaze clear and undaunted, utterly devoid of fear or reverence.

As if he was not bothered by the fact that he was standing in front of a god.

The priests in the hall — all seasoned warriors and veterans of myriad campaigns — glanced at the intruder with deadly animosity. If not for the Child of War, who silently commanded them to stand down, they would have already torn the intruder apart.

After all, no one had ever dared to act so brazenly in the Temple.

But the Spirit of Victory wanted to hear what the man had to say.

More than that, he had sensed a subtle strangeness about this unexpected visitor. He knew that the knight was not what he seemed.

Stopping beneath the throne, the knight bowed slightly.

“l am Gilead, the Summer Knight. I bring a message to the rulers of the Empire."

The Spirit of Victory studied him silently. He felt a deep history etched into the spirit of this knight. countless battles, myriad triumphs — far more than any of the Transcendent champions of the Empire could boast of... and very few defeats. Which should have been impossible.

There were simply not enough battles in the world that the Empire was not involved in, and a warrior of such storied excellence would not have remained unknown.

The Spirit of Victory felt an emotion he had long forgotten.

Was it confusion? Was it excitement?

He was not sure, but he wanted to find out.

“Who sent the message?"

His voice resounded in the prayer hall like the call for battle.

The knight who had called himself Gilead lingered for a moment, then answered calmly:

"It was sent by the Oracle of Theta."

Theta...

The Spirit of Victory knew of that realm, of course, just like he knew of all other realms. It was a distant land, a peaceful land... and insignificant land. A land that lacked strong warriors, but was known for its art, culture, philosophy, and learned people.

Despite its remoteness and weakness, goods from Theta were popular in the Empire, as were its people — the nobles competed for who could hire a Thetian tutor for their children, while Thetian courtesans, while few, were famed for their beauty and artistic skill.

That feeble realm had not been conquered yet, but its fall into the hands of the Empire was only a matter of time. The campaign would not be long or difficult, either — while it could offer the warriors of the Empire riches, it could not offer them glory. Theta remained independent, for now, only because it was so remote.

Well, and of course... there was the Oracle. There were very few Supremes who had not bowed to the Empire left in the world, and the Oracle was one of the few.

Even if her kingdom was weak and feeble, she still deserved some respect.

The Spirit of Victory nodded.

"I will receive the message."

The man who had called himself Gilead bowed again, and then pulled a sealed scroll from his armor. An attendant took the scroll and ascended the steps of the altar, offering it respectfully to his god.

The Spirit of Victory broke the seal and unfurled the scroll, reading its contents quietly.

Then, his face was suddenly split by a smile. Throwing his head back, he laughed.

The priests were startled by the sound, since they had never heard him laugh before — even though some of them had served the Child of War for centuries. There was only one sentence on the scroll, written in the runes of an ancient language. The runes read:

“The Kingdom of Theta declares war on the Empire."

--- Chapter 3225 ---

Months before, the Oracle of Thetis had issued a summons to the rulers and champions of the peaceful kingdom.

Soon enough, they gathered in the inner sanctum of the Temple of Fate, where three priestesses sat behind the veil.

One of them was a young girl, one was a mature woman, and one so old that she seemed like a crumbling statue made of sand.

All three were blind, and yet they saw more than any mortal could.

They were the voices of the Oracle, after all.

The king — a man with wise eyes who had the bearing of a scholar — bowed reverently before the priestesses, and then knelt.

“We have received the summons. What message does the Oracle have?"

Behind him were the most prominent people of Thetis — warriors, ship-builders, philosophers, artisans, and more.

The priestesses spoke, their voices effortlessly intertwining to create a peculiar, melodious sound — as though it was fate itself speaking, not merely three mortal women.

“The Oracle has shared two truths."

“The Oracle is leaving."

"Prepare for war."

The king froze, shocked by the two revelations. He did not know which one had shocked him most — the fact that the Oracle, who had been the Supreme patron of Thetis since the day of its creation, was leaving... or that they had to steel themselves for war.

Behind him, the sanctum exploded with a hum of voices.

Glancing over his shoulder, the king frowned.

"Silence!"

The the rest obeyed his command, allowing silence to return.

Exhaling slowly, he turned around to the thin veil that obscured the figures of the three priestesses.

He had never been a fearful man, but now, he felt the need to gather his courage before asking the next question:

“What... what does it mean? What war?"

After a long pause, a childish voice spoke:

"It is the war against War."

The king flinched.

‘War... against War?’

His expression turned ugly.

One did not need to guess in order to understand the meaning of this revelation. It meant that the Empire of War, which had been devouring realm after realm somewhere far away, had finally set its sights on Thetis. The king was dismayed, since no one had expected that to happen so soon — at the current rate of expansion, the Empire was not poised to reach them until centuries later.

Even then, most believed either that the war would never happen or that they would be able to reach a peaceful resolution. Fate had other plans, it seemed.

But if that was true, then didn't they need the Oracle more desperately than ever before?

The king closed his eyes for a moment.

“Then why did the Oracle leave?"

A mature voice responded him a moment later:

"She left to ensure that we win."

An old, feeble voice added:

"She left to gather allies that will save Thetis."

The king was a pious man. How could he not be? The Oracle, despite her nebulous nature, had been the guardian of Thetis for centuries — in fact, numerous believed that Thetis would not have existed without her, since this land used to be tainted by a harrowing plague of spreading Corruption once. Therefore, the Oracle was beloved and revered by her people.

And yet, for the first time in his life, he could not help but doubt her words.

The king believed that the Oracle had left in search of help, hoping to enlist the aid of powerful allies.

But he doubted that there were beings powerful enough to repel the Empire of War anywhere in the mortal realms. Trembling, he gritted his teeth and asked:

“What allies does the Oracle seek? Who can save Thetis from the clutches of the Empire, and how vast an army would they need to assemble in order to face the endless legions of War?"

Once again, the three priestesses responded.

“The Oracle does not seek an army."

"The Oracle seeks champions."

“She only seeks four."

There was a hum of voices behind the king. This time, he did not silence his people. Instead, confused and wary, he asked:

“Only four champions? How can this be?! Who are these four heroes then, those who can defeat War?"

There was a long stretch of silence.

Then, the childish voice spoke:

“One Who Brings Light, the Tyrant of Compassion, the Eternal Flame, the First Ruler... the nephilim, White Abyss."

The mature voice continued:

"The Shattered One, He Who Observes, the Companion of Hope... the mirror wraith, King of Nothing.”

The old voice was next.

“The Blessed of Dread, the Truth Keeper, the Lady of Sin... the gorgeous monster, Jade Queen."

And finally, all three voices resounded together, sending shivers running down the king's spine.

“The Rightful Heir of Death, the Bastard Son of Fate, the Apostle of Ruin... the shadow, Lost from Light!"
