“By the Moon..."

On a cloudless night, a startled voice resounded on the upper floor of the Ivory Tower.

The full moon was traveling across the velvet sky, and its silver light spilled into the spacious chamber. The figure of a man was outlined by the light, his long hair tied carelessly by a ribbon. There was a miserable expression on his face.

The man was miserable because he was wearing black, and he had been forced to wear black because, tonight, his mission was to sneak into the Ivory Tower.

No matter how he loathed his current garment, none of his usual clothes were suitable for creeping in the darkness of the night.

Hence, the black attire.

At the moment, however, Noctis all but forgot about his misery.

‘I know that I am mad — the maddest man in all of the Kingdom of Hope, no less! — but am I that mad?'

No, his eyes were not deceiving him.

“So there's indeed someone living in the Ivory Tower..."

The traces of a person inhabiting the chamber were subtle, but unmistakable. Noctis glanced around in bewilderment, then walked over to the stairs and descended to the floor below.

There, the traces were not even subtle anymore.

Everywhere he glanced, peculiar things were scattered on the floor. Sheets of paper covered with peculiar letters he did not know; shards of broken mirrors and mysterious instruments. There were even broken dolls the size of adult humans and intricate porcelain limbs, as well as numerous items he would struggle to describe, let alone identify.

Looking at the mess, Noctis was dismayed. He felt like his title as the maddest man in all of the Kingdom of Hope was under threat.

“Is anyone here?"

He did not bother lowering his voice, so it echoed wildly between the stone walls. There were a few seconds of silence. Then, an ominous voice resounded from behind him.

“What if nobody is here?"

Noctis spun around, staring at the man in front of him.

Then, he grinned.

"My, my! Greetings, friend. Oh, but I must say — I like you a lot!"

In fact, even though they had just met, Noctis had to admit that he liked this man more than almost anyone he had seen before.

That was because the man had peculiar, mirror-like eyes. When Noctis glanced at him, he saw his own reflection. Two of them, no less!

What was there not to like?

“Allow me to introduce myself, friend. I am Noctis, the Crimson Beast of Twilight — the greatest sorcerer and handsomest man in all of the Kingdom of Hope."

The man studied him with an indifferent expression.

"You are one of the Chain Lords."

As he said that, a dreadful malice flashed in his mirror-like eyes.

Noctis grinned.

“Indeed, I am. Therefore... you know what that means, don't you? I am immortal, so trying to kill me would be a tiring and senseless feat."

The man tilted his head a little.

"Well, I don't know... there are fates far worse than death, after all. Being immortal won't save you from those."

Noctis's grin turned a little forced.

“Why are we talking about such unpleasant things? In any case, I have already introduced myself. Won't you return the favor, friend? I feel like I am at a disadvantage."

The man remained silent, studying him emotionlessly.

Noctis coughed.

"On second thought, no need! I already know who you are. You are the King of Nothing, aren't you?"

Finally, the man showed a reaction. The mask of indifference slipped from his face, and he pierced Noctis with an intense gaze.

“How do you know that?"

Exposed to his eerie presence, Noctis let out a nervous laugh.

“Well, it's actually a funny story...”

He hesitated for a moment, then sighed.

“I have this friend, you see. Her name is Nem — although most people know her simply as the One in the North. Nem fares from a faraway land, where she was a priestess once. That land always has three priestesses — a girl, a woman, and an old hag. Once the girl matures, she replaces the woman, who takes the place of the old hag after the old hag dies."

The King of Nothing blinked, confused.

“Can you get to the point?"

Noctis gave him a resentful glance.

“l am getting there! Anyway, all three priestesses serve the Oracle, and Nem was the Oracle's personal disciple — she was rescued by her and raised as her own. But, for whatever reason, Nem did not replace the older priestess when time came. Instead, she left the temple to wander the mortal realms, slaying Creatures of Corruption until her fame was almost — but not quite, naturally — as immense as mine. That was when Sun God got us both, and we became immortal."

The King of Nothing frowned.

“You don't sound very fond of Sun God, and neither do you seem to enjoy your immortality. Why did you agree to become a Chain Lord, then?"

Noctis laughed.

"Me? Well, that is because I am the most agreeable man in the world, naturally!"

But then, he glanced at the King of Nothing with a hint of wistfulness.

“To tell you the truth, a friend once warned me against doing such stupid things. But when push came to shove... I figured that if I didn't agree, some other fool would. And that poor fool would not be nearly as radiant or gorgeous as me, so how would they endure the weight of eternity that had been meant for me?"

There was a dark depth to his voice, as if he was not telling everything. However, a moment later, Noctis was smiling again.

“Well, anyway! We seem to have steered away from the core of this riveting conversation. The point is... recently, Nem received a message from her beloved teacher and mother figure, the Oracle. The Oracle asked her to pass you a message, and since I had some gambling debt... I mean, since I am known for being very generous — the most generous man in all of the Kingdom of Hope, no less! — she asked me to do it in her stead. So, here I am."

His smile grew into a grin, and Noctis glanced at the King of Nothing with contentment.

The King of Nothing sighed.

"The Oracle, you say. So, what does she want this time?"

Noctis cleared his throat.

"To tell you the truth, friend, I don't quite understand the message myself. It is this — come and pay respect to the Queen."

The King of Nothing frowned, then turned and glanced west.

“Ravenheart..."

Then, he chuckled chillingly.

“l am sorry to disappoint you, but I am quite comfortable right here. So, tell your friend that I refuse."

Noctis blinked a couple of times.

"Amazing. She truly is the Oracle!"

Mordret's frown returned.

“What do you mean?"

Noctis shook his head.

"No, it's just that I wasn't entirely honest. The message was actually a bit longer — the Oracle knew exactly how you would respond, so she instructed Nem to deliver the second part of the message after you refused the first."

The King of Nothing sighed and fell silent. Eventually, he said:

“Go on, then. Tell me the second part."

Noctis shrugged.

“She said to tell you that she knows how to end the nightmare."

He paused for a moment, then said compassionately:

“Are you having trouble with sleep, friend? Have you tried... drinking? I find that getting lethally drunk helps one fall asleep splendidly!"

The King of Nothing did not answer, but turned to look west once more.

His expression was grim.

After remaining silent for a long while, he cursed.

“Damn it... why can't I ever say no to her?"

--- Chapter 3226 ---

Sometime before the day the Oracle spoke to her people, far away...

There was a land shrouded in fog, with tall evergreen trees rising from it as black masts tinged with an emerald hue. The silence of the misty forest was broken only by the cawing of crows... that was because the grotesque creatures that dwelled in the fog moved noiselessly, hidden in its cold embrace.

Until the silence was shattered by the sound of battle.

Far away, in the depths of the forest, there was an overgrown ruin. The ruin was vast, as if it had been a prosperous city once. If one looked closely enough, they could still discern the shapes of man-made structures buried under layers of moss.

There was an imposing city wall, now breached and crumbled. The field of tall mounds had been streets and houses once. The stronghold at the heart of the city was now a misshapen hill, and there were innumerable human bones hidden beneath the roots of soaring pines that stood like gravestones above the ruin.

There was a place, though, that the trees and the moss seemed reluctant to approach. That peculiar island of desolation revealed the true face of the ruined city — the fractured cobblestones, the stone buildings turned into piles of rubble, the grotesque skeletons littering the ground like a white pallisade... the gentle slopes of the shallow crater hidden in the fog.

Soon, the cawing of the crows grew deafening, and innumerable black streaks fell from the sky, assembling into a human form.

A few seconds later, there was a tall man standing in the fog, wearing a dark military coat and gazing ahead with a grim expression. His gaunt face betrayed his age, but his hair was as black as raven feathers. Drops of blood were still falling from his gloved fingers.

The man remained motionless for a few seconds, then walked forward.

He walked past the collapsed building, navigating his way between the skeletal carcasses of dead abominations. The closer he got to the crater, the more grotesque remains he encountered. Passing them with unhurried steps, he reached the crater.

The fog obscured what was hidden at its bottom, but he could see gigantic bones protruding above the slope. A truly monstrous creature must have perished here... or possibly it had perished trying to get to the heart of the crater, where he was headed as well.

The man moved down the slope. He walked along the towering bones, circling around them from time to time. The bones created an eerie maze, but he did not seem bothered.

Soon enough, he was close enough to the bottom of the crater to almost see what was hidden in the fog.

Before he could take another step, however, he felt a cold blade touching the side of his neck.

The man stopped.

Without looking back or changing expression, he said in an aloof, grating voice:

“Don't get cute with me, creature."

There was no response, but the blade pressed deeper, and a drop of blood rolled down his neck.

The man smiled darkly.

“Your master's friend sent me — the blind seer. I am here to help."

The sharp blade remained motionless for a few seconds, then disappeared.

Not long after, a nebulous figure shrouded in wisps of ghostly black smoke revealed itself from the fog. Beneath the smoke, the graceful silhouette of a slender woman could be gleaned, moving with the poised elegance of a dancer.

When the man glanced at the shadowy figure, he could not help but feel a chill run down his spine — even if he had long forgotten the meaning of fear, his body still responded to the presence of an absolute predator.

His brief smile disappeared like a fleeting dream.

“You must be the one they call Slayer."

Instead of responding, the woman studied him for a moment, then turned away and walked into the fog.

The man followed.

Soon, the fog around them changed, as if infused by a soft radiance. Then, rays of radiant light shone through it, illuminating the world — before too long, it was as if the sinister shadow and the gaunt man were walking through a celestial haze.

A vague form revealed itself in the radiance ahead of them.

Taking a few more steps, the man stopped and glanced up.

In front of them was the source of the radiance — it was a towering crystal, its depths hiding the unclear silhouette of a winged woman.

The man studied the crystal for a bit, then looked at the silent shadow.

Eventually, he sighed.

“Might as well get comfortable. It will take me a long while."

With that, he pulled something from the inner pocket of his coat — it was a papyrus scroll covered in an intricate weave of runes. Unfurling it, the man pulled a knife from the sheath on his belt and crouched, tracing the first rune in the soil.

The shadow observed him with cold indifference.

Hours later — or possibly days — the man was done with his task. A complicated runic circle surrounded the crystal, shimmering with its own pale light. He straightened and sheathed his knife, then studied the circle for a while.

Eventually, the man shrugged.

“Looks faithful enough. But what do I know? Sorcery has never been one of my talents."

He paused for a moment and then added in his hoarse, grating voice:

"One way to find out."

With that, the man pressed his hand against a particular rune and poured his essence into the circle.

The lines etched into the ground swelled with light, producing a wavering hum. The hum grew louder and louder, coming in waves — eventually, the man grimaced and covered his ears.

Soon, the sound became loud enough to be deafening, and each of its peaks was like a devastating shockwave. Any mundane human would have already been reduced to a bloody pile, but the man endured. The fog was torn apart and dispelled, allowing sunlight to shine upon the bottom of the crater for the first time in countless years.

Finally, the crystal responded.

Its surface rippled as if made of water, then shifted, forming peculiar geometrical shapes.

A moment later, the crystal exploded into a myriad of radiant shards.

The winged figure trapped within fell to its knees and drew a stifled breath — at the same time, the runic circle dimmed, and the harrowing hum grew quiet.

The man glanced at the scroll in his hand with a hint of amusement.

"It actually worked, huh?"

Then, he glanced at the young woman who had been trapped in the crystal.

His stern expression softened for a moment, while his cold eyes revealed complicated emotions.

The young woman, meanwhile, finally caught her breath and stood up with a stagger. She glanced around tensely, her gaze finally stopping at the gaunt man.

She seemed confused for a moment. Then, her eyes widened, and an expression of shock appeared on her face.

Taking a step forward, the woman asked:

"M—master Cor? Is that you?"

The man smiled wistfully.

“Actually, it's Saint Cor now."

She froze for a moment, glancing at the sinister shadow standing beside him, then gazed at the ruins.

A hint of sorrow flashed in her eyes, but then she shook her head and turned around to the man — Saint Cor, Wake of Ruin.

“Are you... are you a challenger in this Nightmare, as well?"

He shook his head simply.

"No. I am dead."

Noticing her confused expression, Cor added in a neutral tone:

"One of the new Supremes has an Ability that allows her to manifest memories — the mundane kind. So, that is what I am. The memory of a dead man."

He shrugged.

“It was quite an unusual experience, to find myself in a Nightmare after dying an inglorious death in the Dream Realm. But there was no reason to refuse her request, so I ventured to find you. After all, helping her means helping humanity — it is not too bad, staying useful even as a corpse."

Letting out a sigh, he walked a few steps and sat on a boulder protruding from the ground.

Then, looking at the winged woman, he smiled again — this time, his subtle smile was genuine.

“But you are still alive, girl. You've been alive this whole time... I still can't believe it. I guess it is true what they say about the Immortal Flame — that it can never be extinguished."

Smile of Heaven hesitated for a few long seconds.

Eventually, she asked:

“How... how long has it been since I entered the Nightmare?"

Wake of Ruin shook his head.

“I'm not sure. I have no idea how many years it has been since I died, after all. Back then... my memories at the end are hazy, but I think it was Year 58 of the Nightmare Spell. So, you would have been gone for about thirty years."

The young woman's legs gave out, and she fell heavily to the ground.

He glanced at her evenly.

After remaining silent for a while, Saint Cor said:

"Many things have happened in your absence, and I am sure that you have a lot of questions. But it is not time for answers just yet — in fact, we don't have much time."

His grating voice turned somber.

“Song of the Fallen can manifest her memories, but sustaining a Transcendent draws heavily on her essence. There are a few of us doing her bidding, and gods know how powerful the people she left in the real world are by now. In any case, her resources are strained at the moment... so I will be brief."

Hearing his words, Smile of Heaven flinched.

“Right... essence."

Her own reserves had been frozen inside the crystal, but now that she was free, sustaining her Transcendent form was draining what little essence she had left rapidly.

So, she glanced at Slayer awkwardly.

“Sister... you don't mind, do you?"

Slayer did not respond, but having spent many years in her company, Smile of Heaven could easily discern her meaning.

With that, the winged young woman suddenly turned into a sphere of light. That light then shot forward, entering the Shadow's body.

Slayer's eyes flashed with brilliant radiance for a moment before turning to their usual inky black.

A moment later, she shifted and spoke in a voice that somehow sounded both sweet and sinister:

“I am ready to listen, M... Saint Cor."

He observed her for a moment with an amused expression, then nodded.

“Well, my message is brief. Song of the Fallen wants you to know that if you want to find your daughter, you do not need to conquer this Nightmare."

The face of the sinister Shadow was obscured by a veil, but he could tell that she frowned.

“What... does she mean?"

Wake of Ruin smiled joylessly.

"What else? She means that your daughter is right here in the Nightmare with you."

The Shadow's eyes seemed to widen.

Saint Cor glanced down.

“Of course she is. In any case, Song of the Fallen says that if you want to find her, you need to travel to the ruins of the First Kingdom and convince someone called White Abyss to pay a visit to the Jade Palace. You need to hurry, too, because time is of the essence."

He hesitated for a moment.

"I think I was sent out earlier than Gilead and that dreadful thing she had conjured, but still, be swift."

Smile of Heaven remained silent, contemplating.

‘White Abyss? The queen of the First Kingdom?'

It was a miracle that White Abyss still lived. Convincing that mythical creature of anything seemed like an impossible task, though.

Nevertheless, Smile of Heaven nodded.

"Alright."

Saint Cor sighed.

“Well then... my mission is complete."

He looked at the sinister Shadow in front of him with a hint of poignant emotion in his eyes, then smiled.

"I am glad that you are alive, girl. Truly, I am so happy. This alone makes coming back from the dead worth it."

Then, he inhaled deeply and closed his eyes.

“If you find that child, Changing Star... tell her that I am sorry. And that I tried my best..."

Suddenly, Cor's presence dissipated, and his figure became oddly elusive.

“But most of all, stay alive. Survive this Nightmare, no matter... the cost..."

A moment later, he was gone.

The bottom of the crater was suddenly empty, as if the gaunt old man had not been sitting on a boulder just a second ago.

As if he had been just a memory dispelled by sunlight.

Smile of Heaven sighed heavily and glanced into the distance.

She felt the consciousness of Orphne, whose body she inhabited, move subtly in their shared vessel. Usually, her soul couldn't possess bodies of living things — but Orphne was not alive, and neither did she possess a soul. Instead, she had a shadow.

So, paradoxically, Smile of Heaven was able to use her Supreme body as shelter.

Taking the first step, she answered Saint Cor, even though he was already gone.

“I will."

--- Chapter 3227 ---

Smile of Heaven spent some time wandering the ruins of the overgrown city. It seemed like hundreds of years had passed since she was forced to encase herself inside the crystal for the second time... but to her, the bitter culmination of the battle for the city had happened mere minutes ago.

She had put on a brave face when parting with Shadow — but as soon as she made her way out of the enormous cavern, she nearly broke down. The weight of the truth crushed her like a gravestone, and she spent hours slumped on cold stone, struggling to breathe and drowning in tears.

That was when a stealthy Nightmare Creature attacked Smile of Heaven, catching her unaware, and was struck dead in the air by a black arrow.

That was how Smile of Heaven met Orphne — Slayer — for the first time. Of course, she did not know who Slayer was back then, but it wasn't difficult to figure out who had sent her.

‘Liar...’

Smile of Heaven smiled weakly through the tears.

Shadow pretended to be cold and unfeeling, as if human emotions were beneath him, but he still assigned her a bodyguard before diving into the Abyss... to seek his death, presumably.

With Orphne by her side, finding a way out of the Underworld had not been too difficult. If anything, it was easier than reaching the precipice of the Abyss — the sinister shadow had never promised not to kill anyone, after all. And unlike Shadow, she wasn't going to be convinced to spare someone either.

Traveling through the lower stratum of the Underworld, they eventually escaped into the unbearable heat of a vast desert. The desert was like a nightmare in and of itself, but they escaped its searing embrace as well.

Not long after that, they reached a realm where humans lived.

Smile of Heaven was not sure what to do. She knew that she had to conquer the Nightmare... but that was a tall task. Masters had been the strongest humans of the waking world when she entered the Seed, but in this Nightmare, she found herself hopelessly outclassed, weaker than a worm in the face of terrifying beings of the Age of Gods.

Even discovering the secrets of natural Transcendence and climbing to a higher Rank did not change the situation much — she ended up having to seal herself in stasis as a Transcendent, after all.

Then again, perhaps simply surviving was already an achievement.

It was no surprise. This Nightmare was meant for Supreme beings, and even then not all of them were guaranteed to stay alive.

So... Smile of Heaven did not count her chances of conquering the Nightmare high. She had to find out the core conflict of the Nightmare first, anyway — and at the moment, she had not the slightest clue. She did not even know where to start searching, since the world of this Nightmare was as vast as the true Dream Realm.

Smile of Heaven did not consider surrendering, though.

So what if she did not have any clues? She could find them.

More than that, there were other challengers beside her in the Nightmare now. Shadow was obviously one of them, even if she could not tell if he knew that he was.

‘Gods...'

Having confirmed that Shadow was from the waking world, Smile of Heaven felt both heartbroken and shocked. She was heartbroken because his existence proved that she had been stuck in this Nightmare for a long time — long enough for someone as powerful as him to be nurtured by humanity, at least. She was shocked because of how powerful he was, as well.

Shadow was not a deity, but he might as well have been. To Smile of Heaven, his powers seemed so terrifying as to be miraculous — she could not even begin to guess how they worked, what their limits were, and what kind of trump cards he was hiding.

To think that there were monsters like that wandering the waking world these days...

It was both sobering and reassuring.

In any case, if Shadow was here, there could be other challengers as well.

So, Smile of Heaven set two immediate goals for herself.

One was to search for clues about the pivotal conflict of the Nightmare; the other was to look for traces of other humans from the waking world.

At that time, the Age of Gods was long over, and the world was in the throes of the Age of Heroes. Humans had achieved many victories over the Nightmare Creatures, but not enough of them to make the mortal realms safe. Still, Smile of Heaven was not as powerless anymore — the world was not as dire anymore either, after all.

In fact, even though she had not been one of the frontline fighters of her cohort, she was still far more skilled and deadly than most Transcendent heroes of this forgotten era... if not all of them — simply by the virtue of faring from the dreadful, apocalyptic hellscape of the distant future.

Even if conquering the Nightmare still seemed like an impossible task, she was confident in her ability to achieve her two tasks, at least.

Especially considering that Orphne the Slayer, who had proved to be chillingly lethal, was following her like a shadow. However, Smile of Heaven had failed to account for one fatal variable.

Herself.

Her search had met obstacles from the very beginning — for no other reason than that she was not the kind of person who could pass by those who needed her help, even if they were mere phantoms conjured by the Spell.

Some would call it a weakness, and Smile of Heaven could even agree with them. Nevertheless, she knew that on the day she learned how to walk past human suffering with an indifferent heart, she would cease to be herself.

That day, she would take the first step on the long, irrevocable path to Corruption. So, her search for clues and other challengers was frequently derailed.

There were powerful Nightmare Creatures hunting down people of remote settlements. There were roaming Awakened who had chosen to seek greater power by slaughtering other humans. There was famine and natural disasters, there was conflict and strife...

In the end, Smile of Heaven found that she moved even slower than when she had been with Shadow and Noctis. At the same time, she was growing stronger, tempering herself against the myriad dangers of the never-ending Nightmare.

Years passed, and she wasn't any closer to achieving her goals than she had been after escaping the Underworld.

Then, a few years more.

By then, Smile of Heaven had become somewhat renowned in the mortal realms, joining the pantheon of famed heroes. She might have even become a bit too famous, which only meant that more people looked at her with hope and implored her to help. So... she helped.

Until she crashed into an obstacle that she failed to overcome.

The overgrown ruin of a once-thriving city was a poignant monument to her failure.

It was here that Smile of Heaven and Orphne attempted to repel a horde of Nightmare Creatures and the Corrupted Titan that herded it toward the city. In the end, the battle was lost, and she was driven into a corner.

At the last moment, Smile of Heaven gambled and placed herself into stasis once more.

It was a desperate move, since there was no guarantee that the Titan would not be able to destroy the crystal — just like Shadow had destroyed it once. Even if the enchantment held, there was no guarantee that Smile of Heaven would ever be able to escape it again.

Now that she did...

She felt disoriented.

‘How many years have passed?’

Judging by the state of the ruins, it had been a long time.

The Age of Heroes must have ended by now, which meant that...

Smile of Heavens tried to remember everything she knew about the history of the Dream Realm.

‘It should be the Imperial Era now.'

The War Empire had most likely already been established. In fact, it was probably quite developed now, sprawling across myriad realms.

It did not matter that much, though.

What mattered was that, all of a sudden, Smile of Heaven had found herself one step closer to achieving her two goals.

She had learned about two other challengers from the memory of Saint Cor — one was the mysterious Supreme who had sent him to find her, and the other... the other was Smile of Heaven's mysterious daughter, whom she had never met.

And at least one of them had to know what this strange Nightmare was about.

More than that, with the youngest descendant of the Immortal Flame clan here, Smile of Heaven did not even know what her ultimate goal was now. She had wanted to conquer the Nightmare for many reasons, but the most important of them was to meet her daughter.

Things were happening in the wrong order, making her feel confused.

‘The youngest descendant...’

Smile of Heaven froze suddenly.

‘Wait.'

Was her daughter even the youngest? According to Saint Cor, Smile of Heaven had been absent for at least thirty years. Who knew what had happened in that time?

‘I am... I am not a grandma now, am I?'

Her eyes widened.

Surely, not!

Smile of Heaven had not even known that she was pregnant when departing for America, so how could she suddenly become a grandmother?!

Covering her face with a palm, she took a deep breath.

‘No, what am I even thinking about? That's not important right now!'

She had to find the ruins of the First Kingdom and convince the mythical being, White Abyss, to travel to Ravenheart. Although mortal realms did not correlate to the map of the Dream Realm exactly right, they were situated in relatively the same directions. Combining what she knew of the Dream Realm with what she had learned during her time in the Nightmare...

'The holy city of the First Kingdom should be in one of the Death Zones west of Bastion, below Godgrave.'

Or rather, in one of the mortal realms that would be consumed by those Death Zones in the future.

Smile of Heaven, meanwhile, was currently in the far east.

There was a long road ahead of her... and she had to hurry.

'I'll have to avoid drawing the Empire's attention, as well.'

Getting entangled with the imperials would delay her too much.

With a sigh, Smile of Heaven released control of Slayer's body.

‘Sister Orphne...'

In the next moment, the body moved without her input.

The graceful figure of the malevolent shadow lost its form, expanding and transforming.

Soon, a magnificent black dragon soared into the sky.
